Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor consists of stations $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ connected by segments $J = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$. Each segment $j$ has two tracks: the nominal track (direction-dependent) and the opposite track. A partial blockage disables the nominal track of segment $j^*$ during the disruption time window $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$. Trains may either wait, or **reroute** to the opposite track (single-track operation, bidirectional conflicts must be resolved).

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Trains run according to a scheduled timetable with planned arrival/departure times at each station.
- (A2) Each train $f$ has a finite set of precomputed speed profiles per segment, each characterized by (unimpeded) running time and energy consumption — this linearizes train dynamics (standard discretization assumption).
- (A3) Rerouting to the opposite track is only possible on the disrupted segment and only if the opposite track is not blocked (it is not, since the blockage is partial).
- (A4) Minimum headway times on each track are constant.
- (A5) Dwell times have fixed minimum values; no overtaking within stations except through reordering.
- (A6) Cancellation is allowed with a large penalty (optional binary variable).
- (A7) Energy consumption is linear in the selected speed profile (A2 makes this exact).

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | set of trains, $f \in F$ |
| $J$ | set of segments; $J_f \subseteq J$ segments traversed by train $f$ |
| $S$ | set of stations |
| $P_{fj}$ | set of speed profiles for train $f$ on segment $j$ |
| $r^{nom}_{fjp}$ | running time of train $f$ on segment $j$ with profile $p$ on the nominal track |
| $r^{opp}_{fjp}$ | running time with profile $p$ on the opposite (rerouted) track (includes switch/turnout time) |
| $e_{fjp}$ | energy consumption of profile $p$ |
| $a^{sch}_{fs}, d^{sch}_{fs}$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $f$ at station $s$ |
| $dw^{min}_{fs}$ | minimum dwell time of train $f$ at station $s$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway (time) between trains on the same track of a segment |
| $T^{start}, T^{end}$ | disruption start/end time on segment $j^*$ |
| $M$ | big constant (e.g., horizon length) |
| $w^{d}_{f}, w^{e}, w^{c}$ | weights for delay, energy, cancellation |
| $\sigma_{f}$ | priority weight of train $f$ |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable variables:**
- $a_{fs} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $f$ at station $s$
- $d_{fs} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $f$ at station $s$

**Routing and speed variables:**
- $x_{fjp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $j$
- $y_{fj} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $j$ (only defined for $j = j^*$)
- $z_f \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ is cancelled

**Ordering variables:**
- $\delta_{fgj} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ passes segment $j$ before train $g$ (on the same track), 0 otherwise

**Auxiliary:**
- $u_{fj} \ge 0$: effective running time of train $f$ on segment $j$ (accounts for rerouting)

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total (weighted) delay, energy consumption, and cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{f \in F} \sigma_f w^d_f \left( d_{f,\,dest(f)} - d^{sch}_{f,\,dest(f)} \right) \;+\; w^e \sum_{f \in F} \sum_{j \in J_f} \sum_{p \in P_{fj}} e_{fjp}\, x_{fjp} \;+\; \sum_{f \in F} w^c \sigma_f z_f
$$

*(Assumption A8: delay is measured at the destination; terminal delays are nonnegative by constraint (C2), so no absolute values are needed.)*

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile uniqueness.** Each train picks exactly one profile per segment (unless cancelled):
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{fj}} x_{fjp} = 1 - z_f \qquad \forall f \in F,\; j \in J_f
$$

**(C2) Timetable consistency along the route.** Departure from a station follows arrival plus minimum dwell; arrival at the next station follows departure plus effective running time:
$$
d_{fs} \ge a_{fs} + dw^{min}_{fs} \qquad \forall f,\; s \in S_f \setminus \{dest(f)\}
$$
$$
a_{f,\,next(s)} \ge d_{fs} + u_{fj(s)} - M z_f \qquad \forall f,\; s
$$
where $j(s)$ is the segment following station $s$.

**(C3) Effective running time links routing and speed profiles:**
$$
u_{fj} = \sum_{p \in P_{fj}} \Big( (1 - y_{fj})\, r^{nom}_{fjp} + y_{fj}\, r^{opp}_{fjp} \Big) x_{fjp} \qquad \forall f,\; j \in J_f
$$
*(Linear because $y_{fj}$ and $x_{fjp}$ are both binary and the products $y_{fj} x_{fjp}$ can be linearized, or equivalently written as two sums:*
$$
u_{fj} = \sum_p r^{nom}_{fjp} x_{fjp} + \sum_p (r^{opp}_{fjp} - r^{nom}_{fjp})\, v_{fjp}, \quad v_{fjp} \le x_{fjp},\; v_{fjp} \le y_{fj},\; v_{fjp} \ge x_{fjp} + y_{fj} - 1
$$
*)*

**(C4) Rerouting only on the disrupted segment and within its capacity:**
$$
y_{fj} = 0 \qquad \forall f,\; j \ne j^*
$$

**(C5) Disruption time window.** A train may traverse the blocked nominal track only outside the disruption window; if it passes during the window it must reroute:
$$
d_{f,\,s(j^*)} \ge T^{end} - M\left( y_{fj^*} + z_f \right) \qquad \forall f \text{ with } j^* \in J_f
$$
i.e., to use the nominal track during the window is forbidden: either the train departs after $T^{end}$, or it reroutes ($y_{fj^*}=1$), or it is cancelled.

**(C6) Headway / conflict-free constraints on the nominal track.** For trains $f \ne g$ both using the nominal track of segment $j$ (i.e., not rerouted, not cancelled), enforce minimum headway between consecutive entries, with ordering variable $\delta_{fgj}$:
$$
d_{f,\,s(j)} \ge d_{g,\,s(j)} + h - M\left( 3 - \delta_{fgj} - (1-y_{fj}) - (1-y_{gj}) - (1-z_f) - (1-z_g) \right)
$$
$$
d_{g,\,s(j)} \ge d_{f,\,s(j)} + h - M\left( 2 + \delta_{fgj} - (1-y_{fj}) - (1-y_{gj}) - (1-z_f) - (1-z_g) \right)
$$
*(Big-M form: the headway constraint is active only when both trains use the nominal track and are not cancelled; $\delta_{fgj}$ selects the order.)*

**(C7) Headway on the opposite (rerouted) track.** Analogous constraints for trains using the opposite track, active when $y_{fj} = y_{gj} = 1$:
$$
d_{f,\,s(j)} \ge d_{g,\,s(j)} + h - M\left( 3 - \delta_{fgj} - y_{fj} - y_{gj} - (1-z_f) - (1-z_g) \right)
$$
$$
d_{g,\,s(j)} \ge d_{f,\,s(j)} + h - M\left( 2 + \delta_{fgj} - y_{fj} - y_{gj} - (1-z_f) - (1-z_g) \right)
$$
These constraints resolve the **bidirectional conflicts** on the shared opposite track.

**(C8) Station capacity / no overtaking conflict at stations (optional, per platform):** for trains dwelling simultaneously at station $s$:
$$
a_{fs} \ge d_{gs} + h^{station} - M\,\delta_{fgs}, \qquad
a_{gs} \ge d_{fs} + h^{station} - M(1 - \delta_{fgs}) \qquad \forall f \ne g,\; s
$$

**(C9) Time horizon:**
$$
T^{start} \le a_{fs},\, d_{fs} \le T^{max} \qquad \forall f, s
$$

**(C10) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{fs}, d_{fs}, u_{fj} \ge 0; \quad x_{fjp},\, y_{fj},\, z_f,\, \delta_{fgj} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Integration of TRP and TSMP:** Constraints (C2)–(C3) couple timetable times with speed-profile choice: retiming (changing $a,d$), reordering ($\delta$), rerouting ($y$), and speed profiles ($x$) are decided simultaneously, guaranteeing that the rescheduled timetable is executable at the train-control level.
- **Energy–delay trade-off:** The objective captures the two strategies described in the introduction — accelerating (earlier arrival, higher energy profile) vs. coasting/decelerating (later arrival, lower energy) — through the joint weighting of delays and $e_{fjp} x_{fjp}$.
- **Equivalence note:** As stated in the paper, if the profile sets $P_{fj}$ are generated on a sufficiently fine time discretization, this MILP is equivalent to the exact integrated problem; the decomposition into an IP over train interactions plus per-train plan selection, solved by the adaptive iterative algorithm, is a solution method for this model and does not change its feasible set.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

**Assumptions** (made where information was missing): a double-track line with stations S = {0,…,S̄}, segment set E; a known disruption blocking one track of segment b during window [T_s, T_e]; a finite set P(k,e) of discretized speed profiles per train and segment with fixed running time τ_k,e^p and energy E_k,e^p; trains may be retimed, reordered, rerouted to the opposite track, or cancelled. Big-M relaxation is used for disjunctions.

## Sets and parameters
- K trains; S stations; E segments; P(k,e) speed profiles.
- ā_k,s, d̄_k,s: scheduled arrival/departure times.
- [W_k^in], [W_k^out]: entry/exit time windows.
- d^min, d^max: min/max dwell time; h: headway.
- [T_s, T_e]: disruption window on segment b, direction 0.
- w₁, w₂, w₃: weights on delay, energy, cancellation.

## Variables
- a_{k,s} ≥ 0, d_{k,s} ≥ 0: actual arrival/departure times.
- D_k ≥ 0: delay of train k.
- x_k ∈ {0,1}: cancellation (1 = cancelled).
- y_{k,e,p} ∈ {0,1}: profile p selected for train k on segment e.
- z_{k,e} ∈ {0,1}: rerouting — 1 if train k uses the opposite (diverted) track on segment e.
- o_{k₁,k₂,e,d} ∈ {0,1}: train k₁ precedes k₂ on track d of segment e.
- o^S_{k₁,k₂,s} ∈ {0,1}: ordering of trains at station s.

## Objective
Minimize:

min  w₁ Σ_k D_k + w₂ Σ_k Σ_e Σ_p E_{k,e}^p · y_{k,e,p} + w₃ Σ_k x_k

## Constraints

**Cancellation linkage / entry–exit windows**
1. a_{k,s₀} ≥ W_k^in − M·x_k
2. a_{k,s̄} ≤ W_k^out + M·x_k

**Delay definition (at final station)**
3. D_k ≥ a_{k,s̄} − ā_{k,s̄} − M·x_k
4. D_k ≤ M·(1 − x_k)

**Dwell time bounds** (for all intermediate s):
5. d^min − M·x_k ≤ d_{k,s} − a_{k,s} ≤ d^max + M·x_k

**Speed-profile consistency and selection** (for each segment e = (s, s′)):
6. |a_{k,s′} − d_{k,s} − Σ_p τ_{k,e}^p y_{k,e,p}| ≤ M·x_k  (running time equals the selected profile's time)
7. Σ_p y_{k,e,p} = 1 − x_k  (exactly one profile if not cancelled)

**Disruption / rerouting (segment b)** — if a train uses its own blocked track (z=0), it must traverse the segment entirely before T_s or entirely after T_e; if it is rerouted (z=1), it must traverse entirely within [T_s, T_e]:
8. d_{k,b} ≤ T_s − 1 + M(1−b₁_k) + M·x_k + M·z_{k,b},  a_{k,b′} ≥ T_e + 1 − M(1−b₂_k) − M·x_k − M·z_{k,b},  b₁_k + b₂_k ≥ 1 − x_k − z_{k,b}
9. d_{k,b} ≥ T_s − M(1−b₃_k) − M·x_k − M(1−z_{k,b}),  a_{k,b′} ≤ T_e + M(1−b₄_k) + M·x_k + M(1−z_{k,b}),  b₃_k + b₄_k ≥ z_{k,b} − x_k
   (b₁,…,b₄ auxiliary binaries for the disjunctions)

**Track assignment helpers** (u_{k,e,0} = uses own track, u_{k,e,1} = uses opposite track):
10. u_{k,e,0} = 1 − z_{k,e} − x_k;  u_{k,e,1} = z_{k,e}

**No-overlap / headway on segments** (for all pairs k₁ < k₂, tracks d, segments e, with helper binary B_{k₁k₂,e,d} = u₁·u₂):
11. o_{k₁,k₂,e,d} + o_{k₂,k₁,e,d} = B_{k₁k₂,e,d}
12. a_{k₂,e′} − a_{k₁,e′} ≥ h − M(1 − o_{k₁,k₂,e,d}) − M(1 − B_{k₁k₂,e,d})
13. a_{k₁,e′} − a_{k₂,e′} ≥ h − M(1 − o_{k₂,k₁,e,d}) − M(1 − B_{k₁k₂,e,d})

**Station capacity (no platform overlap, capacity 1)**:
14. o^S_{k₁,k₂,s} + o^S_{k₂,k₁,s} = 2 − x_{k₁} − x_{k₂}
15. a_{k₂,s} − d_{k₁,s} ≥ h − M(1 − o^S_{k₁,k₂,s})
16. a_{k₁,s} − d_{k₂,s} ≥ h − M(1 − o^S_{k₂,k₁,s})

All times continuous and nonnegative; x, y, z, o, o^S, b binary. The model simultaneously yields a conflict-free retimed/reordered/rerouted timetable and a consistent energy-efficient speed profile per train and segment, with cancellation allowed as a last resort at penalty cost.

Text:
# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations (or junctions) indexed along a line. A disruption partially blocks one track of a segment during a known time window. Affected trains may either wait or **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-track operation with bidirectional conflicts). Each train–segment pair has a set of precomputed **speed profiles** with different running times and energy consumptions.

**Assumptions (explicitly stated, as some are not given in the input):**
- (A1) The disruption time window and affected segment are known in advance (deterministic disruption).
- (A2) For each train and each segment, a finite set of feasible speed profiles is precomputed (e.g., by optimal train control), each characterized by running time and traction energy. This linearizes the train dynamics.
- (A3) Rerouting to the opposite track is only allowed within the disruption window and only on the blocked segment; the opposite track then operates as a single bidirectional track (one train at a time).
- (A4) Train order on unaffected segments may be changed (reordering allowed everywhere).
- (A5) Cancellation is not considered (all trains run); extension is straightforward.
- (A6) Headway times are deterministic and constant.
- (A7) Dwell times have minimum (and optionally maximum) values.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, $i \in T$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of stations/junctions, $s = 1,\dots,|S|$ |
| $K$ | set of segments between consecutive stations, $k = (s, s+1)$ |
| $K^*$ | the blocked segment (partial blockage of one track) |
| $P_i$ | set of speed profiles of train $i$ on a segment |
| $D = [\underline{d}, \bar{d}]$ | disruption time window on segment $K^*$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a^{sched}_{i,s}, d^{sched}_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r^{min}_{i,k}, r^{max}_{i,k}$ | min/max running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ |
| $w^{min}_{i,s}, w^{max}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{sec}$ | arrival, departure, and section headways |
| $t^{run}_{i,k,p}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $k$ with profile $p$ |
| $e_{i,k,p}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $k$ with profile $p$ |
| $\tau^{enter}_{i,k}, \tau^{exit}_{i,k}$ | entry/exit conflict-point times offsets of profile $p$ (for headway checks) |
| $M$ | big constant (horizon length) |
| $W$ | weight of total delay in objective |
| $\delta_{i,k,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if profile $p$ of train $i$ on $k$ is compatible with rerouting (i.e., executable on the opposite track) |

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{i,s} \ge 0$ | actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s} \ge 0$ | actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{i,k,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $k$ |
| $y_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** (uses opposite track) on segment $k$ |
| $o_{i,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $k$ in the "forward" direction slot (ordering variable, see C6–C7) |
| $z_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ (reordering) |
| $D^{tot}$ | total delay (auxiliary) |

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay plus energy consumption:

$$
\min \; W \sum_{i \in T} \Big( \underbrace{(a_{i,|S|} - a^{sched}_{i,|S|})}_{\text{terminal delay}} + \sum_{s} (a_{i,s} - a^{sched}_{i,s})^{+} \Big) + \lambda \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{k \in K}\sum_{p \in P_i} e_{i,k,p}\, x_{i,k,p}
$$

Linearized delay: introduce $\Delta_{i,s} \ge 0$ with

$$
\Delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^{sched}_{i,s}, \qquad \Delta_{i,s} \ge 0
$$

so the objective becomes

$$
\min \; W \sum_{i}\sum_{s} \Delta_{i,s} \;+\; \lambda \sum_{i}\sum_{k}\sum_{p} e_{i,k,p}\, x_{i,k,p}
$$

*(Assumption A8: delay is measured against scheduled arrival at each station; weights could be train-specific.)*

## 6. Constraints

**Timetable consistency:**

$$
\text{(C1) } d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\text{(C2) } w^{min}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le w^{max}_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\text{(C3) } a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + \sum_{p \in P_i} t^{run}_{i,k,p}\, x_{i,k,p} \quad \forall i,\; k=(s,s+1)
$$

**Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per train–segment):**

$$
\text{(C4) } \sum_{p \in P_i} x_{i,k,p} = 1 \quad \forall i, k
$$

**Running time bounds (link with profiles):**

$$
\text{(C5) } r^{min}_{i,k} \le \sum_{p} t^{run}_{i,k,p} x_{i,k,p} \le r^{max}_{i,k} \quad \forall i, k
$$

**Rerouting logic (only on blocked segment, only during disruption window):**

$$
\text{(C6) } y_{i,k} = 0 \quad \forall i,\; k \neq K^*
$$
$$
\text{(C7) } a_{i,s} \ge \underline{d}\, y_{i,k} \quad \text{and} \quad d_{i,s+1} \le \bar{d} + M(1 - y_{i,k}) \quad \forall i,\; k = K^* = (s,s+1)
$$

*(a rerouted train must traverse the blocked segment entirely within the disruption window)*

$$
\text{(C8) } x_{i,k,p} \le 1 - y_{i,k} + \delta_{i,k,p} \quad \forall i, k = K^*, p
$$

*(only rerouting-compatible profiles may be used when rerouted)*

**Bidirectional conflict-free operation on the shared (opposite) track:**
For each pair $i \neq j$ and each direction combination, if both trains occupy the single bidirectional track, one must fully exit before the other enters. With entry/exit times

$$
t^{in}_{i,k} = d_{i,s} + \sum_p \tau^{enter}_{i,k,p} x_{i,k,p}, \qquad
t^{out}_{i,k} = d_{i,s} + \sum_p \tau^{exit}_{i,k,p} x_{i,k,p},
$$

the disjunction is linearized with binary $z^{opp}_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$ (1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on the opposite track):

$$
\text{(C9) } t^{out}_{i,k} + h^{sec} \le t^{in}_{j,k} + M(3 - y_{i,k} - y_{j,k} - z^{opp}_{i,j}) \quad \forall i<j,\; k=K^*
$$
$$
\text{(C10) } t^{out}_{j,k} + h^{sec} \le t^{in}_{i,k} + M(2 - y_{i,k} - y_{j,k} + z^{opp}_{i,j}) \quad \forall i<j,\; k=K^*
$$

**Reordering and headways on normal (double-track) operation:**
For each pair $i \neq j$ on segment $k$, ordering variable $z_{i,j,k}$ enforces non-overlap:

$$
\text{(C11) } t^{out}_{i,k} + h^{sec} \le t^{in}_{j,k} + M(1 - z_{i,j,k}) + M\, y_{i,k} + M\, y_{j,k} \quad \forall i \neq j, k
$$
$$
\text{(C12) } t^{out}_{j,k} + h^{sec} \le t^{in}_{i,k} + M\, z_{i,j,k} + M\, y_{i,k} + M\, y_{j,k} \quad \forall i \neq j, k
$$

**Station headways (same direction, per track):**

$$
\text{(C13) } d_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{dep} - M(1 - z_{i,j,k}) \quad \forall i \neq j, k=(s,s+1)
$$
$$
\text{(C14) } a_{i,s+1} \ge a_{j,s+1} + h^{arr} - M\, z_{i,j,k} \quad \forall i \neq j, k=(s,s+1)
$$

**Variable bounds and integrality:**

$$
\text{(C15) } a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0; \quad x_{i,k,p}, y_{i,k}, z_{i,j,k}, z^{opp}_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 7. Remarks

- **Coupling of TRP and TSMP** is achieved through (C3), (C8)–(C10): timetable times depend on the chosen speed profile, and profile choice is restricted by rerouting decisions and conflict constraints — exactly the interdependency highlighted in the problem statement.
- **Big-M disjunctions** (C9)–(C12) model the bidirectional conflicts on the shared track; they are the source of the combinatorial complexity motivating the decomposition into a train-interaction IP and single-train plans (train-plan selection), as described in the paper's solution framework.
- **Equivalence note:** with a sufficiently fine discretization of profiles (interval plans), the plan-selection IP obtained by enumerating feasible single-train plans is equivalent to this MILP.
- **Extensions:** train cancellations (add binary $c_i$ and relax C1–C4), train-specific delay weights, and capacity limits of the opposite track (max number of rerouted trains) can be added without changing the model structure.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Following the described two-stage framework: (i) a **sub-optimal model** solving rerouting and reordering with pair-wise delay variables, and (ii) an **extended global-optimum model** adding delay propagation, followed by rescheduling with fixed routes.

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **A1 (Macroscopic model):** Signals and lower-level resources are neglected; infrastructure is a set of blocks/routes between stations (Cacchiani et al., 2014).
- **A2:** Each train $t$ runs along a fixed sequence of **scheduled points** (stations/passing points) $i \in S_t$; the route choice at each point is a decision variable.
- **A3:** Primary delays $d^{prim}_{t,i}$ are known inputs (from the disturbance forecast).
- **A4:** Minimum headway times between trains on shared/overlapping resources are given constants $h_{t,t',r,r'}$.
- **A5:** Minimum and maximum running and dwell times per train and route are constants.
- **A6:** Trains cannot be overtaken inside a block section unless a reordering decision is explicitly allowed (ordering variables).
- **A7:** Safety-relevant overlaps (Lindenmaier et al., 2022) are modeled as additional headway constraints behind stop signals.
- **A8:** The objective is minimization of total (secondary) delay; energy is not in the objective (consistent with the reference model of Pellegrini et al., 2014).

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $S_t$ | ordered set of scheduled points of train $t$ |
| $R_{t,i}$ | set of admissible routes for train $t$ at point $i$ |
| $O$ | set of ordered train pairs $(t,t')$ sharing at least one resource |
| $d^{prim}_{t,i}$ | primary delay of train $t$ at point $i$ |
| $r^{min}_{t,i,r}, r^{max}_{t,i,r}$ | min/max running time of train $t$ via route $r$ from point $i$ |
| $w^{min}_{t,i}, w^{max}_{t,i}$ | min/max dwell time of train $t$ at point $i$ |
| $h_{t,t',i,i',r,r'}$ | minimum headway between $t$ on route $r$ and $t'$ on route $r'$ |
| $a^{sch}_{t,i}, d^{sch}_{t,i}$ | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $M$ | big constant (big-M) |
| $\Delta$ | dispatching time horizon |

---

## 3. Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{t,i} \in [a^{sch}_{t,i},\, a^{sch}_{t,i}+\Delta]$ — actual arrival time of train $t$ at point $i$
- $d_{t,i} \ge 0$ — total delay of train $t$ at point $i$

**Binary:**
- $x_{t,i,r} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_{t,i}$ at point $i$ (rerouting)
- $y_{t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$ — ordering: 1 if $t$ passes the shared resource before $t'$ (reordering)
- $z_{t,t',i} \in \{0,1\}$ — **pair-wise delay variable** (sub-optimal model): 1 if train $t$ waits for train $t'$ at point $i$

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{i \in S_t} d_{t,i} \tag{1}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Route selection

Each train uses exactly one route per point:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_{t,i}} x_{t,i,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T,\; i \in S_t \tag{2}
$$

### 5.2 Time propagation (running and dwell times)

$$
d_{t,i} - d_{t,i-1} \ge \sum_{r \in R_{t,i}} r^{min}_{t,i,r}\, x_{t,i,r} + w^{min}_{t,i} - \big(d^{sch}_{t,i} - d^{sch}_{t,i-1}\big) \qquad \forall t,\; i \in S_t \setminus \{first\} \tag{3}
$$

$$
d_{t,i} - d_{t,i-1} \le \sum_{r \in R_{t,i}} r^{max}_{t,i,r}\, x_{t,i,r} + w^{max}_{t,i} - \big(d^{sch}_{t,i} - d^{sch}_{t,i-1}\big) \qquad \forall t,\; i \in S_t \setminus \{first\} \tag{4}
$$

Initial delay equals primary delay:

$$
d_{t,i_0} = d^{prim}_{t,i_0} \qquad \forall t,\; i_0 = \text{first point of } S_t \tag{5}
$$

### 5.3 Pair-wise delay interpretation (sub-optimal model, Section 3.1)

The delay of train $t$ at point $i$ is lower-bounded by the delay of the train it waits for (delay propagation **disregarded**):

$$
d_{t,i} \ge d_{t',i'} - M\,(1 - z_{t,t',i}) \qquad \forall (t,t') \in O,\; i \in S_t,\; i' \in S_{t'} \text{ conflicting} \tag{6}
$$

$$
\sum_{t' : (t,t') \in O} z_{t,t',i} \le 1 \qquad \forall t,\; i \in S_t \tag{7}
$$

$$
z_{t,t',i} \le \sum_{r \in R_{t,i}} \sum_{r' \in R_{t',i'}} x_{t,i,r}\, x_{t',i',r'} \quad \text{(linearized as: } z_{t,t',i} \le x_{t,i,r} + x_{t',i',r'} - 1 \text{ for each conflicting pair } (r,r')) \tag{8}
$$

### 5.4 Ordering and headway constraints

For each ordered pair $(t,t') \in O$ sharing resources:

$$
a_{t,i} + \sum_{r,r'} h_{t,t',i,i',r,r'}\, x_{t,i,r}\, x_{t',i',r'} \le a_{t',i'} + M\,(1-y_{t,t'}) \tag{9}
$$

$$
a_{t',i'} + \sum_{r,r'} h_{t',t,i',i,r',r}\, x_{t',i',r'}\, x_{t,i,r} \le a_{t,i} + M\, y_{t,t'} \tag{10}
$$

(Products $x\,x$ are linearized with auxiliary binaries $u_{t,t',i,i',r,r'} \ge x_{t,i,r} + x_{t',i',r'} - 1$.)

Consistency between ordering and pair-wise waiting:

$$
z_{t,t',i} \le 1 - y_{t,t'} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in O \tag{11}
$$

$$
z_{t',t,i'} \le y_{t,t'} \qquad \forall (t,t') \in O \tag{12}
$$

### 5.5 Safety-relevant overlaps (extended rtRTMP, Lindenmaier et al., 2022)

$$
a_{t',i'} \ge a_{t,i} + \omega_{t,t',r,r'} - M\,(2 - x_{t,i,r} - x_{t',i',r'} + y_{t,t'}) \tag{13}
$$

where $\omega_{t,t',r,r'}$ is the clearing time of the overlap behind the stop signal; the symmetric case for $y_{t,t'} = 0$ is analogous.

---

## 6. Extended Model: Global Optimality via Delay Propagation (Section 3.3)

The sub-optimal model is globally optimal **iff** no delay propagation chain exists, i.e., if the pair-wise waiting structure forms no path of length ≥ 2 (optimality condition, Section 3.2). Otherwise, replace (6) with full propagation:

$$
d_{t,i} \ge d_{t',i'} + \big(d^{sch}_{t,i} - d^{sch}_{t',i'}\big) - M\,(1 - z_{t,t',i}) \qquad \forall (t,t') \in O,\; \text{conflicting } (i,i') \tag{14}
$$

so that delays propagate recursively along waiting chains, guaranteeing the global optimum of the original rtRTMP (Pellegrini et al., 2014) with a more favorable computational cost.

---

## 7. Stage 2: Rescheduling with Fixed Routes

Given the solution $(x^*, y^*)$ of Stage 1, solve the original model with:

$$
x_{t,i,r} = x^*_{t,i,r}, \qquad y_{t,t'} = y^*_{t,t'} \quad (\text{optional}) \tag{15}
$$

and objective (1), constraints (2)–(5), (9)–(13), and (14). This yields the final conflict-free timetable with minimal total delay.

---

## 8. Model Summary

- **Type:** MILP, big-M formulation
- **Decision space:** routes ($x$), ordering ($y$), waiting relations ($z$), timing ($a$, $d$)
- **Stage 1:** (1)–(12) — fast, sub-optimal rerouting + reordering
- **Stage 2:** (1)–(5), (9)–(14) with (15) — exact rescheduling; with (14) the two-stage result matches the global optimum of the monolithic rtRTMP.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Physical and Disruption Setting (Assumptions A1–A4)

- **A1.** The line consists of stations **S** connected by segments (inter-station block sections). Segment *(i, i+1)* has two tracks: track 1 (original, direction +) and track 2 (opposite, direction −). Normally each direction uses its own track.
- **A2.** During the disruption window **[T^D_start, T^D_end]**, one track of segment *d* ∈ **S_seg^dis** is blocked. Trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track of segment *d*, sharing it bidirectionally with opposing trains.
- **A3.** Time is discretized into periods t = 1, 2, …, |T| (linearity assumption). All times are integer multiples of the discretization step.
- **A4.** Safety headways are constant: departure–departure h^dd, arrival–arrival h^aa, departure–arrival h^da (or a single uniform headway h).

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **K** | set of trains, indexed k |
| **S** | set of stations, indexed i (line endpoints 1, |S|) |
| **A_k** | ordered set of stations visited by train k |
| **E** | set of directed runs e = (i, j); e ∈ E_k for runs of train k |
| **T** | discretized time horizon {1, …, |T|} |
| **P_e** | feasible speed profiles for run e, indexed p; each has running time r^{ep} ∈ ℤ and energy cost c^{ep} |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| a⁰_{k,i}, d⁰_{k,i} | planned arrival/departure times |
| \bar{a}_{k,i}, \bar{d}_{k,i} | maximum allowable arrival/departure times |
| w_k ≥ 0 | delay weight (priority) of train k |
| D^{arr}_k | scheduled terminal arrival of train k (delay reference) |
| r^{ep}, c^{ep} | running time / energy cost of run e under profile p |
| λ_e | conversion factor from energy to delay cost for run e |
| dw^min_{k,i} | minimum dwell time of train k at station i |
| T^D_s, T^D_e | disruption start/end times |
| M | sufficiently large constant (e.g., |T| + max headway) |
| Q | large cancellation penalty |
| h | safety headway (periods) on the same track resource |

## 4. Decision Variables

**Timetable (integer):** a_{k,i} ∈ ℤ≥0 (arrival), d_{k,i} ∈ ℤ≥0 (departure).

**Route choice (binary):**
- x_k — 1 if train k uses the opposite track on the disrupted segment d (rerouted)
- z_k — 1 if train k is **cancelled**

**Speed-profile selection (binary):** y^{ep}_k — 1 if train k uses profile p on run e.

**Sequencing (binary):**
- σ_{k,l} — 1 if train k departs the shared track before train l (pairs that may share the opposite track)
- u_{k,l} — 1 if train k enters segment e before train l (normal same-direction ordering)
- b_k — 1 if train k traverses segment d on the blocked track *before* the disruption

**Auxiliary:** δ⁺_k, δ⁻_k ≥ 0 with a_{k,|S|} = D^{arr}_k + δ⁺_k − δ⁻_k.

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted terminal delay plus weighted energy consumption plus cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; \sum_{k \in K} w_k\,\delta^+_k \;+\; \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{e \in E_k}\sum_{p \in P_e} \lambda_e\, c^{ep}\, y^{ep}_{k} \;+\; \sum_{k \in K} Q\, z_k
$$

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Timetable consistency

**(C1) Dwell and running-time coupling.** For every train k and consecutive stations i, j = i+1:

$$
d_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i} + dw^{\min}_{k,i} \quad \forall k,\; i \in A_k \setminus\{|S|\}
$$
$$
a_{k,j} - d_{k,i} = \sum_{p \in P_{(i,j)}} r^{(i,j)p}\, y^{(i,j)p}_{k} \quad \forall k,\; (i,j) \in E_k
$$

(speed-profile–timetable coupling: the actual inter-station time *exactly equals* the chosen profile's running time.)

**(C2) Profile uniqueness:**

$$
\sum_{p \in P_e} y^{ep}_{k} = 1 - z_k \quad \forall k,\; e \in E_k
$$

(a cancelled train runs no profiles; C9 sets its times to dummy values.)

**(C3)** Only feasible profiles are enumerated: P_e = {p : r^min_e ≤ r^{ep} ≤ r^max_e}.

### 6.2 Disruption and rerouting

**(C4) Blocked track unusable during the disruption window.** A train keeping the original track must traverse segment d entirely before T^D_s or after T^D_e, via binary b_k:

$$
d_{k,i} \le T^D_s - \sum_p r^{(i,j)p}y^{(i,j)p}_k + M\big(1 - b_k + x_k + z_k\big)
$$
$$
d_{k,i} \ge T^D_e - M\big(b_k + x_k + z_k\big)
$$
$$
b_k + x_k \le 1
$$

(i.e., if x_k = 0 and z_k = 0, the train must either pass before T^D_s (b_k = 1) or enter at/after T^D_e (b_k = 0).)

**(C5) Rerouted trains respect the disruption window on the opposite track.** If x_k = 1, occupancy of the opposite track on segment d must lie within [T^D_s, T^D_e]:

$$
d_{k,i} \ge T^D_s - M\big(2 - x_k - (1-z_k)\big)
$$
$$
d_{k,i} + \sum_p r^{(i,j)p} y^{(i,j)p}_k \le T^D_e + M\big(2 - x_k - (1-z_k)\big)
$$

### 6.3 Bidirectional single-track conflict-free sequencing

**(C6) Non-overlapping occupancy with headway h** on the shared resource, for pairs k < l that may both use it:

$$
a_{k,j} + h \le d_{l,i} + M\big(3 - \sigma_{kl} - x_k - x_l\big)
$$
$$
a_{l,j} + h \le d_{k,i} + M\big(2 - \sigma_{kl} + x_k + x_l\big)
$$

(If both trains actually occupy the shared track, exactly one ordering σ_{kl} is enforced, guaranteeing a gap ≥ h; otherwise relaxed by big-M. Analogous big-M disjunctions cover every pair sharing the physical track.)

### 6.4 Headways on normal (single-direction) segments

**(C7)** For all pairs k < l (not cancelled), on segment e = (i,j):

$$
d_{l,i} \ge d_{k,i} + h - M(1 - u_{kl}) - M z_k - M z_l
$$
$$
d_{k,i} \ge d_{l,i} + h - M\, u_{kl} - M z_k - M z_l
$$
$$
a_{l,j} \ge a_{k,j} + h - M(1 - u_{kl}) - M z_k - M z_l
$$
$$
a_{k,j} \ge a_{l,j} + h - M\, u_{kl} - M z_k - M z_l
$$

(Reordering allowed: u_{kl} selects which train goes first; headways enforced on both entry and exit.)

### 6.5 Horizon, cancellation, and domains

**(C8)** 0 ≤ a_{k,i} ≤ d_{k,i} ≤ \bar{d}_{k,i}, and a_{k,i} ≤ \bar{a}_{k,i} ∀ k, i.

**(C9) Cancellation:** if z_k = 1, times are pushed to the horizon (dummy schedule):

$$
a_{k,i} \ge |T|\, z_k, \qquad d_{k,i} \ge |T|\, z_k \quad \forall k, i
$$

and C2 removes profile assignments, while big-M terms with z_k relax all sequencing constraints.

**(C10)** Optional: fix a_{k,i} = a⁰_{k,i}, d_{k,i} = d⁰_{k,i} for trains/runs not affected by the disruption.

**(C11) Domains:**

$$
a_{k,i}, d_{k,i} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\quad x_k, z_k, y^{ep}_k, \sigma_{kl}, u_{kl}, b_k \in \{0,1\},\quad \delta^\pm_k \ge 0
$$

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Retiming** — integer variables a, d (Assumption A3 keeps the model linear; the discretization step must be at least as fine as the smallest headway).
- **Reordering** — pairwise binary sequencing variables (C6, C7) via big-M disjunctions; order-free conflict resolution.
- **Rerouting** — per-train binary x_k; shared-track usage triggers the bidirectional sequencing constraints (C6), the core of coordinating trains on the single available track.
- **Speed management** — discrete profile choice y^{ep}_k per run, hard-coupled to the timetable by the equality in (C1), so energy-optimal profiles and delays are traded off in one objective.
- **Disruption windows** — enforced via the b_k/x_k big-M structure (C4–C5): the blocked track is unavailable inside [T^D_s, T^D_e], and the opposite track is shared only during that window.
- **Cancellation** — fallback with large penalty Q, consistently deactivated across times, profiles, and sequencing.
- **Objective** — weights delay (priority w_k) against energy (λ_e·c^{ep}), capturing the TRSMP trade-off between punctuality recovery and energy-efficient speed profiles.

**Linearity assumptions:** all constraints are linear in integer/binary variables; headways are constant; profile running times and energy are precomputed constants; energy–time interactions (speed-dependent consumption under delays) are captured through the finite profile menu P_e.

Text:
# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem setting and assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations (or junctions) and segments between them. A partial blockage disables one track of a segment during a known time window; trains may either wait or **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-track operation in the disrupted segment), which requires coordinating bidirectional trains.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Disruption location, affected segment, and time window [T^s, T^e] are known in advance (deterministic disruption).
- (A2) Each train has a finite set of candidate speed profiles per segment, each with fixed running time and energy consumption (precomputed from train dynamics; this keeps the model linear).
- (A3) Dwell times have minimum and maximum values; running times equal the chosen profile's duration.
- (A4) Headway times on segments and at stations are fixed safety separations.
- (A5) Cancellation is allowed with a large penalty (optional; can be removed).
- (A6) Energy consumption is linear in the selected profile (constant per profile).

## 2. Sets and indices

- $I$: trains, $i \in I$; $S$: stations, $s \in S$; $K$: segments, $k \in K$ connecting consecutive stations.
- $P_{ik}$: candidate speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $k$, $p \in P_{ik}$.
- $D$: disruption segment $k^* \in K$; opposite (available) track of $k^*$ usable for rerouting.

## 3. Parameters

- $a^{sch}_{is}, d^{sch}_{is}$: scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{seg}$: minimum headways (arrival, departure, segment running).
- $\underline{w}_{is}, \bar{w}_{is}$: min/max dwell of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $\tau_p$: running time, $e_p$: energy of profile $p$.
- $M$: large constant.
- $w^{delay}, w^{en}, w^{can}$: objective weights.
- $[T^s, T^e]$: disruption time window on segment $k^*$ (one track blocked).

## 4. Variables

- $a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times.
- $x_{ikp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $k$.
- $y_{ik} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $k^*$ on the **opposite** track (reroute).
- $o_{ik} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$ (for $i<j$).
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.

## 5. Objective function

$$\min \; w^{delay}\sum_{i\in I}\Big(\sum_{s\in S}\big[(a_{is}-a^{sch}_{is}) + (d_{is}-d^{sch}_{is})\big]\Big) \;+\; w^{en}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in P_{ik}} e_p\, x_{ikp} \;+\; w^{can}\sum_{i\in I} z_i$$

Delays can be written linearly since $a_{is} \ge a^{sch}_{is}$ is enforced (see below), so no absolute value is needed.

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Profile selection (exactly one running time per segment):**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{ik}} x_{ikp} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, k$$

**(C2) Timetable consistency (running + dwell):**
$$a_{i,s+1} = d_{is} + \sum_{p \in P_{ik}} \tau_p\, x_{ik} + M z_i \qquad \forall i,\; k=(s,s+1)$$
$$\underline{w}_{is} \le d_{is} - a_{is} \le \bar{w}_{is} \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(C3) Delay monotonicity (no early arrivals relative to schedule):**
$$a_{is} \ge a^{sch}_{is}, \quad d_{is} \ge d^{sch}_{is} \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(C4) Segment headway (same track, same direction), for trains $i<j$ both using track $t$:**
$$a_{j,s+1} \ge a_{i,s+1} + h^{seg} - M(1 - o_{ik}) - M(1-y_{ik}) - M z_j \qquad \forall i<j, k$$
$$a_{i,s+1} \ge a_{j,s+1} + h^{seg} - M\, o_{ik} - M(1-y_{ik}) - M z_j \qquad \forall i<j, k$$
(analogous constraints for the opposite track with $y_{ik}=1$).

**(C5) Station headways (departure and arrival separations):**
$$d_{js} \ge d_{is} + h^{dep} - M(1 - o^{dep}_{isj}) \qquad \forall i<j, s$$
$$a_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{arr} - M(1 - o^{arr}_{isj}) \qquad \forall i<j, s$$
with complementary constraints for the reversed order.

**(C6) Disruption window on the blocked track of $k^*$:** a train may use the blocked track only if it fully passes outside $[T^s, T^e]$:
$$a_{i,s+1} \le T^s + M(1 - x_{ik^*p}) \quad \text{or} \quad d_{is} \ge T^e - M(1 - x_{ik^*p})$$
implemented pairwise via binaries $b_{ik^*} \in \{0,1\}$ (before / after disruption):
$$a_{i,s+1} \le T^s + M(1-b_{ik^*}), \qquad d_{is} \ge T^e - M\, b_{ik^*} \qquad \forall i$$

**(C7) Rerouting:** if a train cannot use the blocked track within the window, it must reroute or wait:
$$y_{ik^*} \ge 1 - b_{ik^*} - \sum_p x_{ik^*p}\cdot(\text{delay feasibility}) \quad\Rightarrow\quad \text{enforced by combining (C6) with } y_{ik^*} + b_{ik^*} \ge 1$$

**(C8) Single-track capacity on the reroute (bidirectional conflict resolution):** on the opposite track of $k^*$, trains in both directions must respect headways and cannot occupy simultaneously:
$$a_{j,s+1} \ge a_{i,s+1} + h^{seg} - M(1-o_{ij}) - M(2 - y_{ik^*} - y_{jk^*}) \qquad \forall i<j$$
$$a_{i,s+1} \ge a_{j,s+1} + h^{seg} - M\,o_{ij} - M(2 - y_{ik^*} - y_{jk^*}) \qquad \forall i<j$$
plus analogous constraints for opposite-direction trains sharing the rerouted track (using their respective entry/exit times into segment $k^*$).

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0; \quad x_{ikp}, y_{ik}, o_{ij}, b_{ik}, z_i \in \{0,1\}$$

## 7. Remarks

- The model is a pure MILP: all nonlinearities (min/max, disjunctions) are handled with big-$M$ and auxiliary binaries.
- Constraint (C2) links timetable times to speed profiles, ensuring the rescheduled timetable is executable at the train-control level — the core of the TRSMP integration.
- (C6)–(C8) model the partial blockage: trains either pass before/after the window on the normal track, or reroute onto the opposite track with strict bidirectional conflict resolution.
- As stated in the paper, this MILP can be decomposed into an IP over train interactions plus single-train plans (each plan = a feasible combination of times, route, and profile), with an adaptive iterative refinement of plan granularity; for sufficiently fine plans the IP is equivalent to this MILP.

Text:
Below is the final, self-contained MILP model for the **Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)** under a partial segment blockage, after two rounds of review and refinement.

---

# MILP for the TRSMP: Integrated Timetable Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Blockage

## 1. Assumptions (explicit)

- **A1.** A double-track corridor consists of ordered segments $s \in S$; each segment has two tracks, one per direction ($k \in K = \{own, opp\}$).
- **A2.** One track ($k^{blocked}$) of segment $s^{blocked}$ is unavailable during window $[T^W_{start}, T^W_{end}]$. Trains may reroute onto the opposite track, which is then shared bidirectionally; conflicts are resolved by headway constraints.
- **A3.** Speed profiles are discretized: each profile $p \in P$ has a fixed running time $r_{i,s,p}$ and energy $e_{i,s,p}$, keeping the model linear.
- **A4.** Retiming, reordering, rerouting, and cancellation are decisions. Overtaking occurs only at stations (FIFO within segments).
- **A5.** Trains may never arrive earlier than scheduled (holding is free); standard in HSR rescheduling.
- **A6.** Big-M: $M := T^H + \tau^h$, with $T^H$ the planning horizon and $\tau^h$ the headway — valid since no time variable exceeds $T^H$.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | trains; $S$ ordered segments; $P$ speed profiles; $K=\{own,opp\}$ tracks |
| $s^{blocked}, k^{blocked}$ | disrupted segment and blocked track |
| $r_{i,s,p},\ e_{i,s,p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ for train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $r^{min}_{i,s}, r^{max}_{i,s}$ | admissible running-time bounds |
| $\tau^h$ | minimum headway on a shared track |
| $\tau^{dwell}_{i,s}$ | minimum dwell time |
| $T^{start}_i$ | earliest origin departure of train $i$ |
| $[T^W_{start}, T^W_{end}]$ | disruption window |
| $\pi_i$ | cancellation penalty; $w^t, w^e, w^c$ objective weights |
| $D$ | train pairs $(i,j)$ sharing segments |

## 3. Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $d_{i,s},\ a_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | departure onto / arrival at end of segment $s$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $z_{i,s,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if profile $p$ is used on $(i,s)$ |
| $x^{tr}_{i,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses track $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $g_{i,j,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if both $i$ and $j$ use track $k$ (linearized AND) |
| $y_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $i$ departs onto $s$ before $j$ |
| $u_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ occupies $s^{blocked}$ during the disruption window |

## 4. Objective

$$
\min\; Z = w^t \sum_{i \in I}\left(a_{i,|S|} - T^{start}_i\right)
+ w^e \sum_{i}\sum_{s}\sum_{p} e_{i,s,p}\, z_{i,s,p}
+ w^c \sum_{i} \pi_i c_i
$$

Weighted total travel time (with destination delay implicitly weighted highest via $a_{i,|S|}$), total energy, and cancellation penalties.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Running dynamics (timetable–speed-profile coupling):**
$$a_{i,s} = d_{i,s} + \sum_{p \in P} r_{i,s,p}\, z_{i,s,p} \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(C2) Dwell / chain between consecutive segments:**
$$d_{i,s+1} \ge a_{i,s} + \tau^{dwell}_{i,s+1} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,\ s < |S|$$

**(C3) Earliest departure and no-early-arrival:**
$$d_{i,1} \ge T^{start}_i - M c_i; \qquad a_{i,s} \ge \tau^{sch,arr}_{i,s} - M c_i \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C4) Speed-profile selection:**
$$\sum_{p} z_{i,s,p} = 1 - c_i; \qquad r^{min}_{i,s}(1-c_i) \le \sum_{p} r_{i,s,p} z_{i,s,p} \le r^{max}_{i,s}(1-c_i) \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C5) Track assignment (rerouting):**
$$\sum_{k \in K} x^{tr}_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(C6) Same-track sharing linearization and headways:**
$$g_{i,j,s,k} \le x^{tr}_{i,s,k},\quad g_{i,j,s,k} \le x^{tr}_{j,s,k},\quad g_{i,j,s,k} \ge x^{tr}_{i,s,k} + x^{tr}_{j,s,k} - 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in D, s, k$$
$$a_{i,s} + \tau^h \le d_{j,s} + M(1 - y_{i,j,s}) + M(1 - g_{i,j,s,k}) + M c_i + M c_j$$
$$a_{j,s} + \tau^h \le d_{i,s} + M\,y_{i,j,s} + M(1 - g_{i,j,s,k}) + M c_i + M c_j \qquad \forall (i,j), s, k$$

Headways apply only when both trains use the **same** track ($g=1$); on $s^{blocked}$ both directions are forced onto the single available track (C7–C8), so bidirectional conflicts are handled automatically.

**(C7) Disruption-window occupancy detection (fully linear, with boundary tolerance $\epsilon > 0$):**
$$d_{i,s} \le T^W_{end} + M\,u_{i,s}, \qquad a_{i,s} \ge T^W_{start} - M(1 - u_{i,s})$$
$$d_{i,s} \ge T^W_{end} + \epsilon - M(1 - u_{i,s}), \qquad a_{i,s} \le T^W_{start} - \epsilon + M\,u_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\ s = s^{blocked}$$

These force $u_{i,s}=1$ exactly when $[d_{i,s}, a_{i,s}]$ overlaps the window with positive length; a train arriving exactly at $T^W_{start}$ or departing exactly at $T^W_{end}$ correctly gets $u=0$.

**(C8) Blocked-track prohibition during the window:**
$$x^{tr}_{i,s^{blocked},\,k^{blocked}} \le 1 - u_{i,s^{blocked}} \qquad \forall i$$

**(C9) FIFO ordering consistency (no overtaking within a segment):**
$$y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in D,\ s$$

**(C10) Variable bounds:**
$$0 \le d_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} \le T^H; \quad \text{all binaries} \in \{0,1\}$$

## 6. Key modeling points

- **Integration of TRP and TSMP:** C1 links timetable times directly to the selected speed profile; the objective's energy term captures the time–energy trade-off (accelerate to arrive earlier vs. coast/brake to save energy).
- **Rerouting:** $x^{tr}$ allows using the opposite track; C8 forces rerouted trains onto the shared track during the window, and the $g$-linearization cleanly restricts headways to same-track pairs — resolving bidirectional conflicts linearly.
- **Cancellation:** $c_i$ is a decision variable; $M c_i$ terms deactivate all timing, headway, profile, and track constraints for cancelled trains, whose cost enters via $\pi_i$.
- **Linearity:** all products are binary × parameter; the only binary × binary interaction ($x_i \cdot x_j$) is linearized via $g$.

The model is a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound; the ordering variables $y$ and the $g$-linearization constitute the main combinatorial core, and it serves as the exact monolithic benchmark against which the decomposition-based IP and adaptive iterative algorithm (plan selection over discretized train plans) can be validated for equivalence.

Text:
The best model is Model 2 — it is the most complete and internally consistent formulation, correctly handling retiming, reordering, rerouting, speed-profile selection, and the bidirectional single-track conflict on the blocked segment.

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $i$ |
| $S$ | set of stations $\{S_0, S_1, \dots, S_n\}$, index $s$ |
| $L$ | set of segments (links) between consecutive stations, index $l$; segment $l$ connects $S_l$ and $S_{l+1}$ |
| $P_i$ | set of speed profiles (plans) available to train $i$ on each segment, index $p$ |
| $D$ | disruption window $[T_0, T_1]$; $l^* \in L$ is the partially blocked segment |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $a^{sch}_{i,s},\ d^{sch}_{i,s}$ | scheduled (original) arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ |
| $E_{i,l,p}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $l$ with speed profile $p$ |
| $\tau_{i,l,p}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ with profile $p$ |
| $\underline{\tau}_{i,l},\ \bar{\tau}_{i,l}$ | min/max running time on segment $l$ |
| $\underline{d}_{i,s},\ \bar{d}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{arr},\ h^{dep},\ h^{tr}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, and train–train on a segment |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $H$ | planning horizon length |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{ij,l} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $l$ (pairwise, $i<j$) |
| $x_{i,l} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $i$ uses the **opposite track** on blocked segment $l^*$ during the disruption window |
| $z_{i,l,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | $=1$ if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $l$ |
| $\delta^+_{i,s}, \delta^-_{i,s}$ | continuous $\ge 0$ | positive/negative delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} w_i\left(\delta^+_{i,s} + \delta^-_{i,s}\right)}_{\text{total weighted timetable deviation}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{\lambda \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{l \in L}\sum_{p \in P_i} E_{i,l,p}\, z_{i,l,p}}_{\text{total energy consumption}}
$$

where $\lambda > 0$ converts energy into a unit comparable with delay. Delay definition:

$$
a_{i,s} - a^{sch}_{i,s} = \delta^+_{i,s} - \delta^-_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall s \in S \tag{1}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable feasibility

**Dwell times:**
$$
\underline{d}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \bar{d}_{i,s} \quad \forall i, s \tag{2–3}
$$

**Running time consistency with selected speed profile:**
$$
a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} = \sum_{p \in P_i} \tau_{i,l,p}\, z_{i,l,p} \quad \forall i,\ \forall l = (s, s+1) \tag{4}
$$
$$
\underline{\tau}_{i,l} \le a_{i,s+1} - d_{i,s} \le \bar{\tau}_{i,l} \quad \forall i, l \tag{5}
$$

**Exactly one speed profile per train–segment:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P_i} z_{i,l,p} = 1 \quad \forall i \in T,\ \forall l \in L \tag{6}
$$

### 5.2 Headway and ordering constraints (same track, same direction)

For each segment $l$ and each pair $i < j$:

**Departure headway:**
$$
d_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge h^{dep} - M(1 - y_{ij,l}) \tag{7}
$$
$$
d_{i,s} - d_{j,s} \ge h^{dep} - M\, y_{ij,l} \tag{8}
$$

**Arrival headway:**
$$
a_{j,s+1} - a_{i,s+1} \ge h^{arr} - M(1 - y_{ij,l}) \tag{9}
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} - a_{j,s+1} \ge h^{arr} - M\, y_{ij,l} \tag{10}
$$

(7)–(10) enforce that if $y_{ij,l}=1$, train $i$ enters and leaves segment $l$ at least $h^{dep}$/$h^{arr}$ before train $j$; otherwise the roles are reversed, guaranteeing non-crossing.

### 5.3 Disruption handling on blocked segment $l^*$

**Reroute or wait:** a train whose original schedule would traverse $l^*$ intersecting the disruption window must either (a) reroute to the opposite track ($x_{i,l^*}=1$) or (b) be delayed so it traverses after $T_1$:

$$
a_{i,s^*} \ge T_0 - M(1 - x_{i,l^*}) \quad \forall i \tag{11}
$$
$$
d_{i,s^*+1} \le T_1 + M(1 - x_{i,l^*}) + M\big(1 - \text{overlap}_i\big) \quad \forall i \tag{12}
$$
$$
a_{i,s^*} \ge T_1 - M\, x_{i,l^*} \quad \forall i \tag{13}
$$

where $\text{overlap}_i$ is a precomputed binary parameter indicating whether train $i$'s original passage on $l^*$ intersects $[T_0,T_1]$. Interpretation:
- If $x_{i,l^*}=1$: the train must enter the shared opposite track no earlier than $T_0$ (11) and, if originally scheduled inside the window, must finish by $T_1$ (12).
- If $x_{i,l^*}=0$: the train may only use its own track after the disruption ends (13).

### 5.4 Single-track occupancy on the shared opposite track during disruption

Only one train at a time may occupy the opposite track of $l^*$ within $[T_0, T_1]$. For each pair $i<j$ with $x_{i,l^*} = x_{j,l^*} = 1$:

$$
d_{j,s^*} - a_{i,s^*+1} \ge h^{tr} - M(3 - x_{i,l^*} - x_{j,l^*} - y_{ij,l^*}) \tag{14}
$$
$$
d_{i,s^*} - a_{j,s^*+1} \ge h^{tr} - M(2 - x_{i,l^*} - x_{j,l^*} + y_{ij,l^*}) \tag{15}
$$

If both trains reroute, either $i$ fully precedes $j$ (14 active when $y_{ij,l^*}=1$) or $j$ precedes $i$ (15 active when $y_{ij,l^*}=0$); the segment is occupied exclusively with headway $h^{tr}$.

### 5.5 Time-window / horizon bounds

$$
0 \le a_{i,s} \le H, \qquad 0 \le d_{i,s} \le H \quad \forall i, s \tag{16}
$$
$$
a_{i,S_0} = a^{sch}_{i,S_0} \quad \forall i \tag{17}
$$

(origin times fixed; terminal arrival free within horizon).

### 5.6 Variable domains

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \delta^+_{i,s}, \delta^-_{i,s} \ge 0; \quad y_{ij,l}, x_{i,l}, z_{i,l,p} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Retiming variables** ($a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$): continuous times capturing the rescheduled timetable; delay is measured against the scheduled timetable via (1) with split positive/negative parts so the objective penalizes absolute deviation.
- **Speed profile selection** ($z_{i,l,p}$): each train–segment must pick exactly one discretized driving strategy (6). Each profile fixes the running time (4) and carries a fixed energy cost in the objective — this linearizes the nonlinear train dynamics.
- **Ordering variables** ($y_{ij,l}$): big-$M$ disjunctions (7)–(10) decide the train sequence on each segment and enforce minimum headways, preventing conflicts and overtaking.
- **Rerouting variables** ($x_{i,l}$): model the partial blockage — trains either cross the blocked segment on the opposite track inside the window (subject to exclusive occupancy via (14)–(15)) or wait until the window ends (13).
- **Big-$M$ logic**: $M$ must exceed the horizon $H$; constraints deactivate when the corresponding binary makes the disjunct irrelevant.
- **Objective**: weighted sum of timetable deviation and energy, capturing the delay-vs-energy trade-off — e.g., slower profiles save energy but propagate delay to following trains through the headway constraints.

The model is a pure linear MILP: all nonlinearities (disjunctions, profile choice, track sharing) are linearized via binaries and big-$M$ constraints, and it integrates retiming, reordering, rerouting, and energy-optimal speed selection in a single model for the partial-blockage scenario.

# MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

Below is a complete, self-contained mixed-integer linear programming formulation of the integrated problem, following the problem description. Missing information is filled with reasonable assumptions, marked **[A1], [A2], …**

---

## 1. Physical setting and assumptions

**[A1 – Infrastructure.** The line consists of stations $S=\{0,1,\dots,m\}$ connected by segments $e=0,\dots,m-1$. Each segment has a *normal* track and an *opposite* track; normally each track is used unidirectionally. During a disruption, the normal track of a set of segments $E_D\subseteq E$ is blocked; trains may reroute onto the opposite track, which must then carry bidirectional traffic (one train at a time).

**[A2 – Disruption.** The disruption affects segments in $E_D$ during the known time window $[t^{start},t^{end}]$. At $t^{start}$, trains already occupying the blocked segments are assumed to have exited them (or occupy the opposite track only).

**[A3 – Speed profiles.** For each train $f\in F$ and segment $e$, a finite set $P_{fe}$ of pre-computed speed profiles is given. Each profile $p\in P_{fe}$ has a fixed running (travel) time $\tau_{fe}^{p}$ and energy consumption $\kappa_{fe}^{p}$ (computed offline by optimal train control, so the model remains linear). Train $f$ runs at most at maximum speed on non-disrupted segments and reduced (safe) speed $v^{safe}$ on the opposite (rerouted) track; hence separate profile sets $P_{fe}^{N}$ (normal track) and $P_{fe}^{R}\subseteq P_{fe}$ (rerouted, slower).

**[A4 – Operations.** Trains cannot overtake each other on the same track of a segment (they may overtake in stations). A train may be cancelled at a penalty cost. Headway requirements on segment entry/exit are captured by a minimum separation time $h$ between two successive trains occupying the same resource. Scheduled arrival/departure times $arr^{sched}, dep^{sched}$ and minimum dwell times $dwell_f$ are given.

**[A5 – Objective.** Minimize a weighted sum of (i) total delay to passengers (arrival and departure delays, plus a cancellation penalty) and (ii) total energy consumption, with weights $\alpha,\beta$.

---

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | set of trains (both directions; direction $dir_f\in\{+1,-1\}$) |
| $E$ | set of segments; $E_D\subset E$ disrupted segments |
| $T$ | discrete time horizon $\{0,1,\dots,|T|\}$ |
| $P_{fe}^{N}, P_{fe}^{R}$ | admissible speed profiles of train $f$ on segment $e$ (normal / rerouted) |
| $\tau_{fe}^{p}$ | running time of profile $p$ (discretized in time units) |
| $\kappa_{fe}^{p}$ | energy consumption of profile $p$ |
| $arr_f^{s},dep_f^{s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure of train $f$ at station $s$ |
| $dwell_f$ | minimum dwell time of train $f$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway (time) between trains on a segment |
| $M$ | big-$M$ constant (e.g. $|T|+1$) |
| $w_f^{arr},w_f^{dep},c_f$ | delay weights and cancellation penalty of train $f$ |
| $\alpha,\beta$ | weights for delays vs. energy |
| $[t^{start},t^{end}]$ | disruption time window |

## 3. Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{fes}\in\{0,1\}$ | | train $f$ uses the **normal** track of segment $e$ (from side $s\in\{L,R\}$) |
| $y_{fes}\in\{0,1\}$ | | train $f$ uses the **opposite** (rerouted) track of segment $e$ from side $s$ |
| $u_{fp}\in\{0,1\}$ | | train $f$ uses profile $p$ on its segment (summed over chosen track type; define $u$ per $(f,e,p)$) |
| $a_{fs}\in T$, $d_{fs}\in T$ | | actual arrival / departure time of train $f$ at station $s$ |
| $A_{fs}^{+},D_{fs}^{+}\ge 0$ | | arrival / departure delay at station $s$ |
| $z_{ff'e}\in\{0,1\}$ | | ordering: train $f$ enters segment $e$ before $f'$ (on whatever track each uses) |
| $q_{ffe}\in\{0,1\}$ | | train $f$ enters segment $e$ **before** $f'$ leaves it (no-simultaneous-occupancy indicator) |
| $\gamma_f\in\{0,1\}$ | | train $f$ is cancelled |

Throughout, define $u_{fep}^{N}\in\{0,1\}$ and $u_{fep}^{R}\in\{0,1\}$ as profile-selection variables under normal and rerouted running, respectively; $x,y$ force the corresponding sets.

---

## 4. Objective function

$$
\min \; Z=\alpha\Big(\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{s\in S}\big(w_f^{arr}A_{fs}^{+}+w_f^{dep}D_{fs}^{+}\big)+\sum_{f\in F}c_f\gamma_f\Big)
+\beta\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{N}}\kappa_{fe}^{p}\,u_{fep}^{N}
+\beta\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{e\in E}\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{R}}\kappa_{fe}^{p}\,u_{fep}^{R}.
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route choice — each train traverses each segment exactly once (or is cancelled):**
$$
x_{fes}+y_{fes}=\;1-\gamma_f \qquad \forall f\in F,\; e\in E,\; s\in\{L,R\},
$$
$$
x_{f,e,L}+x_{f,e,R}\le 1,\qquad y_{f,e,L}+y_{f,e,R}\le 1 \qquad \forall f,e
$$
(i.e., exactly one entry side per chosen track; use $s$ fixed to the train's direction side for $x$, and the opposite for $y$).

**(C2) Rerouting only possible during disruption:**
$$
y_{fes}=0 \qquad \forall f,\; e\notin E_D,\; s .
$$

**(C3) Profile selection consistency (running time coupling):**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{N}}u_{fep}^{N}=x_{fes^*},\qquad
\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{R}}u_{fep}^{R}=y_{fes^*}\qquad \forall f,e
$$
with $s^*$ the train's direction side; exactly one profile per chosen track.

**(C4) Timetable consistency (running time from selected profile):**
$$
a_{f,s+1}\;\ge\; d_{f,s}+\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{N}}\tau_{fe}^{p}u_{fep}^{N}
+\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{R}}\tau_{fe}^{p}u_{fep}^{R}\qquad \forall f,\; e=(s,s+1)
$$
$$
a_{f,s-1}\;\ge\; d_{f,s}+\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{N}}\tau_{fe}^{p}u_{fep}^{N}
+\sum_{p\in P_{fe}^{R}}\tau_{fe}^{p}u_{fep}^{R}\qquad \forall f,\; e=(s-1,s)
$$
(according to train direction; equality variants possible if no early running is allowed on a segment).

**(C5) Minimum dwell time:**
$$
d_{fs}-a_{fs}\;\ge\; dwell_f(1-\gamma_f)\qquad \forall f,s.
$$

**(C6) Delay definition (linear, big-$M$):**
$$
a_{fs}-arr_f^{s}\le A_{fs}^{+},\qquad A_{fs}^{+}\ge 0,\qquad A_{fs}^{+}\le M(1-\gamma_f)
$$
$$
d_{fs}-dep_f^{s}\le D_{fs}^{+},\qquad D_{fs}^{+}\ge 0,\qquad D_{fs}^{+}\le M(1-\gamma_f).
$$
(Optionally enforce equality via $A^+ \ge a-arr^{sched}$ if early running must be penalized too.)

**(C7) Disruption window:**
(a) No train may be *inside* a blocked segment on the normal track during $[t^{start},t^{end}]$; with binary occupancy $occ_{fet}\in\{0,1\}$:
$$
occ_{fet}\le x_{fes^*},\qquad
occ_{fet}\ge x_{fes^*} - \big[(a_{f,e^{+}}\le t)\cdot 1 + (t\ge d_{f,e^{-}})\cdot 1\big]_{\text{linearized}},
$$
linearized as: train $f$ occupies segment $e$ at time $t$ iff it has departed the upstream station but not yet arrived downstream:
$$
d_{f,e^{-}}\le t+M(1-occ_{fet}),\qquad a_{f,e^{+}}\ge t+1-M\,occ_{fet},\qquad occ_{fet}\le 1-\gamma_f .
$$
Then:
$$
occ_{fet}=0 \qquad \forall f,\;e\in E_D,\;t\in[t^{start},t^{end}]\ \text{if }x_{fes^*}=1 .
$$
Combined linear form:
$$
occ_{fet}\le 1-x_{fes^*}\quad \text{is unnecessary; instead force }
d_{f,e^{-}}\ge t^{end}-M\,y_{fes^*}\ \text{or } a_{f,e^{+}}\le t^{start}+M\,y_{fes^*},
$$
i.e., a train using the normal track of a blocked segment must fully exit before $t^{start}$ or enter after $t^{end}$:
$$
a_{f,e^{+}}\;\le\; t^{start}+M\,(1-x_{fes^*}) \qquad \text{(before disruption)}, \ \textbf{or}
$$
$$
d_{f,e^{-}}\;\ge\; t^{end}-M\,(1-x_{fes^*}) \qquad \text{(after disruption)}.
$$
These two are combined with binary $b_{fe}\in\{0,1\}$ ("passes before"):
$$
a_{f,e^{+}}\le t^{start}+M(1-x_{fes^*}+b_{fe}),\qquad
d_{f,e^{-}}\ge t^{end}-M(1-x_{fes^*}+1-b_{fe}).
$$

(b) **[A6]** Rerouted trains run at reduced speed: profile sets $P_{fe}^{R}$ already reflect this, enforced via (C3).

**(C8) Segment capacity / no-simultaneous occupancy (shared opposite track).** For every pair of trains $f<f'$ and segment $e$, and any time $t$:
$$
occ_{fet}+occ_{f'et}\le 1 \qquad \forall t
$$
is sufficient for conflict-free bidirectional occupancy of a single track, but it is lifted only when trains use different physical tracks. Define track-identity binary $\rho_{ff'e}=1$ if $f,f'$ use the *same* track of $e$:
$$
\rho_{ff'e}\;\ge\; x_{fes}+x_{f'es}-1,\qquad
\rho_{ff'e}\;\ge\; y_{fes}+y_{f'es}-1 \qquad \forall s\in\{L,R\}
$$
$$
occ_{fet}+occ_{f'et}\le 1+\;(1-\rho_{ff'e}) \qquad \forall t .
$$
Equivalently, an ordering formulation (tighter in practice): for same-track pairs,
$$
d_{f,e^{-}}\;\le\; a_{f',e^{+}} + M(1-q_{ffe})+M(1-\rho_{ff'e}),
$$
$$
d_{f',e^{-}}\;\le\; a_{f,e^{+}} + M\,q_{ffe}+M(1-\rho_{ff'e}).
$$

**(C9) No overtaking on segments (same direction, same track):** for $dir_f=dir_{f'}$:
$$
d_{f,e^{-}}\le d_{f',e^{-}}+M(1-z_{ff'e}),\qquad
d_{f',e^{-}}\le d_{f,e^{-}}+M\,z_{ff'e}
$$
$$
a_{f,e^{+}}\le a_{f',e^{+}}+M(1-z_{ff'e}),\qquad
a_{f',e^{+}}\le a_{f,e^{+}}+M\,z_{ff'e}
$$
i.e., the entry/exit order of two same-direction trains on the same track must coincide; $z$ is inactive if they use different tracks ($+M(1-\rho_{ff'e})$ on each).

**(C10) Minimum headway on segment entry (same track):**
$$
a_{f',e^{+}}\;\ge\; a_{f,e^{+}}+h - M(1-z_{ff'e}) - M(1-\rho_{ff'e}) \qquad \forall f<f',e .
$$

**(C11) Cancellation:** if $\gamma_f=1$, remove all movements:
$$
a_{fs}\le M\,\gamma_f + a^{min},\qquad d_{fs}\le M\,\gamma_f,\qquad
u_{fep}^{N}=0,\; u_{fep}^{R}=0\ \ \forall e,p .
$$

**(C12) Station capacity** **[A7: assumed 2 tracks per station, one per direction, expandable]**: at most one train dwelling/arriving per direction at any time:
$$
\sum_{f:\,dir_f=+1} dw_{fst}\le 1,\qquad \sum_{f:\,dir_f=-1} dw_{fst}\le 1\qquad \forall s,t,
$$
where $dw_{fst}\in\{0,1\}$ indicates train $f$ dwelling at station $s$ at time $t$ (linearized analogously to $occ$).

**(C13) Time windows and bounds:**
$$
0\le a_{fs},\,d_{fs},\,A_{fs}^{+},\,D_{fs}^{+}\le |T| .
$$

---

## 6. Remarks

- **Linearity:** all constraints are linear; nonlinearity is avoided by (i) discretizing the time horizon, (ii) pre-computing speed profiles $\{\tau,\kappa\}$ offline so that the timetable–speed-profile coupling (C3)–(C4) is expressed through binary profile selection only. This is the key modeling device aligning train positions/timings with executable speed profiles.
- **Complexity:** the model is a big-$M$ MILP; the number of binaries grows with $|F|^2|E||T|$ (conflict/ordering constraints), motivating the paper's decomposition into a train-interaction IP and single-train plan-selection problems, with adaptive refinement of profile sets $P_{fe}$ near incumbent solutions and local branching.
- **Equivalence:** with sufficiently fine time discretization and profile enumeration covering all feasible running times between minimum- and maximum-speed running on each track type, the MILP exactly represents the integrated continuous-time problem **[A8]**.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $S=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and segments between consecutive stations. A partial blockage disables one track of a set of segments $D \subset$ segments during a time window $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$. Affected trains may either wait or **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-track operation with bidirectional conflict resolution), and each train selects a **speed profile** per segment, which determines running time and energy consumption.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Trains run according to a given original timetable; all trains are identical in their set of admissible speed profiles per segment.
- (A2) Each segment offers a finite, discretized set of speed profiles $P_{ij}$ (e.g., from a speed-management module); each profile $p$ has a fixed running time $\tau^{p}_{ij}$ and energy $e^{p}_{ij}$. *(Discretization assumption — standard in the literature.)*
- (A3) Rerouting is only possible on blocked segments, only within the disruption window, and only one train at a time may occupy the opposite track.
- (A4) Minimum headway times $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{run}$ are fixed and train-independent.
- (A5) Cancellation is not considered (all trains must run); dwell times are flexible within bounds.
- (A6) Energy consumption is linear in the selected profile (no regenerative braking recovery modeled).

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains; $T_{up}, T_{down}$: direction subsets |
| $L$ | ordered list of segments $(i,j)$ traversed by each train (same physical path) |
| $P_{ij}$ | admissible speed profiles on segment $(i,j)$ |
| $\tau^{p}_{ij}, e^{p}_{ij}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $a^{0}_{i,t}, d^{0}_{i,t}$ | original scheduled arrival/departure of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $\underline{dw}_{i}, \overline{dw}_{i}$ | min/max dwell time at station $i$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{run}$ | headway requirements (arrival, departure, running) |
| $[T^{start}_{ij}, T^{end}_{ij}]$ | disruption window on blocked segment $(i,j)$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $w^{delay}, w^{en}$ | weights for delay and energy in the objective |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,t}, d_{i,t}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | actual arrival / departure time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $x^{p}_{ij,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses profile $p$ on segment $(i,j)$ |
| $y_{ij,t}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ **reroutes** on the opposite track of segment $(i,j)$ |
| $z_{ij,tt'}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | sequencing: 1 if train $t$ enters segment $(i,j)$ before $t'$ |
| $q_{ij,tt'}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | sequencing on the **opposite** (rerouted) track |
| $\delta_{i,t}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | arrival delay of train $t$ at station $i$ |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = w^{delay}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in S}\delta_{i,t} \;+\; w^{en}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{(i,j)\in L}\sum_{p\in P_{ij}} e^{p}_{ij}\, x^{p}_{ij,t}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per segment):**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_{ij}} x^{p}_{ij,t} = 1 \qquad \forall t\in T,\ \forall (i,j)\in L
$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (links timetable and speed profile):**
$$
a_{j,t} \ge d_{i,t} + \sum_{p\in P_{ij}} \tau^{p}_{ij}\, x^{p}_{ij,t} \qquad \forall t,\ \forall (i,j)\in L
$$

**(C3) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\underline{dw}_{i} \le d_{i,t} - a_{i,t} \le \overline{dw}_{i} \qquad \forall t,\ \forall i\in S\setminus\{\text{terminals}\}
$$

**(C4) Delay definition (linear):**
$$
\delta_{i,t} \ge a_{i,t} - a^{0}_{i,t}, \qquad \delta_{i,t}\ge 0 \qquad \forall t,\ \forall i\in S
$$

**(C5) Rerouting only on blocked segments and only during the window:**
$$
y_{ij,t} = 0 \qquad \forall t,\ \forall (i,j)\notin D
$$
$$
d_{i,t} \ge T^{start}_{ij}\, y_{ij,t}, \qquad a_{j,t} \le T^{end}_{ij} + M(1-y_{ij,t}) \qquad \forall t,\ \forall (i,j)\in D
$$

**(C6) Headways on the normal track (same direction), with big-M:**
$$
a_{j,t'} \ge a_{j,t} + h^{run} - M(1-z_{ij,tt'}) - M\,y_{ij,t} - M\,y_{ij,t'} \qquad \forall t<t',\ (i,j)\in L
$$
$$
a_{j,t} \ge a_{j,t'} + h^{run} - M\,z_{ij,tt'} - M\,y_{ij,t} - M\,y_{ij,t'} \qquad \forall t<t',\ (i,j)\in L
$$
Analogous constraints for departure headways $h^{dep}$ at station $i$ and arrival headways $h^{arr}$ at station $j$.

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict resolution on the rerouted (opposite) track:** trains using the opposite track must be mutually exclusive in time (single-track operation):
$$
a_{j,t'} \ge a_{j,t} + h^{run} - M(1-q_{ij,tt'}) - M(1-y_{ij,t}) - M(1-y_{ij,t'}) \qquad \forall t<t',\ (i,j)\in D
$$
$$
a_{j,t} \ge a_{j,t'} + h^{run} - M\,q_{ij,tt'} - M(1-y_{ij,t}) - M(1-y_{ij,t'}) \qquad \forall t<t',\ (i,j)\in D
$$

**(C8) Conflict between opposite-track user and normal-track users (junction conflict):** a train on the opposite track and a train on the normal track of the same segment cannot occupy the shared station throat simultaneously:
$$
a_{j,t'} \ge a_{j,t} + h^{run} - M(1-r_{ij,tt'}) - M\,y_{ij,t'} - M(1-y_{ij,t}) \qquad \forall t<t'
$$
$$
a_{j,t} \ge a_{j,t'} + h^{run} - M\,r_{ij,tt'} - M\,y_{ij,t'} - M(1-y_{ij,t}) \qquad \forall t<t'
$$
with auxiliary binary $r_{ij,tt'}$ (analogous constraints for $y_{ij,t'}=1, y_{ij,t}=0$).

**(C9) Time bounds:**
$$
a_{i,t}, d_{i,t} \in [0, H] \qquad \forall t,\ \forall i\in S
$$
where $H$ is the planning horizon.

**(C10) Variable domains:**
$$
x^{p}_{ij,t},\, y_{ij,t},\, z_{ij,tt'},\, q_{ij,tt'},\, r_{ij,tt'} \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_{i,t}, d_{i,t}, \delta_{i,t} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Integration mechanism:** Constraint (C2) is the coupling between the TRP (timetable variables $a,d$) and the TSMP (profile variables $x$): choosing a faster profile shortens running time and allows earlier arrival but consumes more energy, which is exactly the trade-off captured in the objective.
- **Rerouting:** Variables $y$ activate the single-track regime on blocked segments; constraints (C5)–(C8) guarantee conflict-free bidirectional operation.
- **Equivalence note:** As stated in the paper, with a sufficiently fine discretization of profiles $P_{ij}$ (assumption A2), this MILP is equivalent to the continuous integrated problem; the decomposition into an IP over train interactions plus per-train plan selection is a solution method and does not change the model.

# TRSMP MILP — Model Formulation

## Sets, Indices, Parameters

- **T**: trains, each with direction `dir[t] ∈ {up, down}`, planned timetable `pa[t,s], pd[t,s]`, cancellation penalty `pen[t]`
- **S**: stations; **I**: inter-station segments/runs `i` (station `i` → `i+1`); one disrupted segment `s*` with disruption window `[T0, T1]`
- **K**: candidate speed profiles per run, with running time `RT[t,i,k]` and energy `E[t,i,k]`
- **H**: minimum headway; **M**: big-M; horizon `[0, Tend]`; weights `w1, w2, w3`

**Assumptions:** double-track corridor; during `[T0,T1]` the disrupted segment has only one usable track, so bidirectional trains must be sequenced one-at-a-time or reroute onto the opposite track (allowed only if traversal lies entirely within `[T0,T1]`); speed profiles are discrete (faster ⇒ more energy); cancelled trains consume no resources.

## Variables

- `a[t,s], d[t,s] ≥ 0` — actual arrival / departure times
- `x[t,i,k] ∈ {0,1}` — speed-profile selection
- `y[t] ∈ {0,1}` — rerouting onto opposite track through disrupted segment
- `c[t] ∈ {0,1}` — cancellation
- `o[t1,t2] ∈ {0,1}` — ordering on disrupted segment (t1 before t2)
- `u[t] ∈ {0,1}` — train passes disrupted segment before `T0`
- `delay[t,s] ≥ 0` — arrival delay

## Objective

```
min  Σ_t Σ_s w1·delay[t,s]  +  Σ_t w2·pen[t]·c[t]  +  Σ_t Σ_i Σ_k w3·E[t,i,k]·x[t,i,k]
```

## Constraints

**(C1) Dwell bounds** (relaxed if cancelled):
```
d[t,s] − a[t,s] ≥ dwellMin − M·c[t]
d[t,s] − a[t,s] ≤ dwellMax + M·c[t]        ∀t, s
```

**(C2) Running-time consistency (couples retiming ↔ speed profile):**
```
a[t,i+1] = d[t,i] + Σ_k RT[t,i,k]·x[t,i,k] + ΔRT·y[t]·[i = s*]     ∀t, i
```

**(C3) One profile per run (none if cancelled):**
```
Σ_k x[t,i,k] = 1 − c[t]        ∀t, i
```

**(C4) Cancellation fixes times to plan:**
```
a[t,s] = pa[t,s]  (via |a−pa| ≤ M(1−c[t]))      d[t,s] = pd[t,s] similarly     ∀t, s
```

**(C5) Delay definition:**
```
delay[t,s] ≥ a[t,s] − pa[t,s] − M·c[t],   delay[t,s] ≥ 0        ∀t, s
```

**(C6) Rerouting logic (opposite track only inside disruption window):**
```
d[t,s*] ≥ T0 − M(1−y[t])
a[t,s*+1] ≤ T1 + M(1−y[t])        ∀t
```

**(C7) Blocked-track avoidance (if not rerouted/cancelled, pass either fully before T0 or fully after T1):**
```
a[t,s*+1] ≤ T0 + M(u[t] + y[t] + c[t])
d[t,s*]   ≥ T1 − M(1−u[t] + y[t] + c[t])        ∀t
```

**(C8) Headway on disrupted segment (bidirectional sequencing, big-M disjunction):**
```
a[t1,s*+1] + H ≤ d[t2,s*] + M(1−o[t1,t2]) + M·c[t1] + M·c[t2]
a[t2,s*+1] + H ≤ d[t1,s*] + M·o[t1,t2]     + M·c[t1] + M·c[t2]        ∀ pairs t1<t2
```

**(C9) Headway on normal segments, same-direction pairs** (with auxiliary ordering binaries `oN[t1,t2,i]`):
```
a[t1,i+1] + H ≤ d[t2,i] + M(1−oN[t1,t2,i]) + M·c[t1] + M·c[t2]
a[t2,i+1] + H ≤ d[t1,i] + M·oN[t1,t2,i]     + M·c[t1] + M·c[t2]        ∀ same-dir pairs, i ≠ s*
```

**(C10) Horizon bounds:** `0 ≤ a[t,s], d[t,s] ≤ Tend` for all `t, s`.

The disjunctive constraints (C6–C9) are all linear big-M formulations, so the model is a pure MILP: it simultaneously decides retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed-profile selection, yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable with executable (energy-optimized) speed profiles.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management (TRSMP)

## Sets and Parameters

- **I**: trains (both directions), **S**: stations, **J**: segments (segment j connects station j and j+1), **T**: discretized time horizon, **P**: precomputed speed profiles per (train, segment)
- **J^D**: disrupted segment; disruption window [t₁, t₂]
- **Dir(i)** ∈ {+1, −1}: train direction
- **E_i, L_i**: earliest departure / latest arrival for train i
- **Dwell(s)**: minimum dwell time at station s
- **h**: minimum headway
- **Runtime(i,j,p)**, **Energy(i,j,p)**: running time and energy of profile p
- **SchedArr(i)**: original scheduled arrival; **M**: big-M; **w_d, w_e, w_c**: weights

## Variables

- **xᵃ(i,s,t), xᵈ(i,s,t) ∈ {0,1}**: train i arrives/departs station s at time t
- **a(i,s), d(i,s) ∈ ℤ≥0**: integer arrival/departure times
- **v(i,j,p) ∈ {0,1}**: speed profile selection
- **y(i,j) ∈ {0,1}**: train i reroutes to opposite track on segment j
- **z(i,k,j) ∈ {0,1}**: train i passes segment j before train k
- **b(i,k) ∈ {0,1}**: both trains of an opposite-direction pair share the single track on J^D
- **before(i), after(i) ∈ {0,1}**: train enters disrupted segment before t₁ / after t₂
- **c(i) ∈ {0,1}**: train i is cancelled
- **rt(i,j), en(i,j) ≥ 0**: realized running time / energy; **delay(i) ≥ 0**

## Objective

Minimize weighted total delay + energy + cancellation penalty:

$$\min \; w_d \sum_i delay_i + w_e \sum_i \sum_j en_{ij} + w_c \sum_i c_i$$

## Constraints

**(0) Unique times and linking** (for all i, s):

$$\sum_t x^a_{ist} = 1 - c_i, \quad \sum_t x^d_{ist} = 1 - c_i$$
$$a_{is} = \sum_t t\, x^a_{ist}, \quad d_{is} = \sum_t t\, x^d_{ist}$$

**(1) Timetable consistency** (running time on segment j):

$$a_{i,j+1} \ge d_{ij} + rt_{ij} - M c_i$$

**(2) Minimum dwell** at intermediate stations:

$$d_{is} \ge a_{is} + Dwell_s - M c_i$$

**(3) Time windows**:

$$d_{i0} \ge E_i, \qquad a_{i,|S|} \le L_i + M c_i$$

**(6) Profile linking**:

$$rt_{ij} = \sum_p Runtime_{ijp}\, v_{ijp}, \qquad en_{ij} = \sum_p Energy_{ijp}\, v_{ijp}$$

**(7) Exactly one profile per train–segment**:

$$\sum_p v_{ijp} = 1 - c_i$$

**(4) Headway / conflict-free ordering** (big-M disjunction, for all pairs (i,k), segments j, both non-cancelled):

$$z_{ikj}=1:\quad d_{kj} \ge d_{ij} + rt_{ij} + h - M(1-z_{ikj})$$
$$z_{ikj}=0:\quad d_{ij} \ge d_{kj} + rt_{kj} + h - M z_{ikj}$$

For opposite-direction pairs on normal (non-disrupted) segments these constraints are relaxed (double track, no conflict).

**(4b) Bidirectional conflicts on the disrupted segment** (opposite-direction pairs, j = J^D):

$$b_{ik} \ge y_{ij} + y_{kj} - 1$$
$$d_{kj} \ge d_{ij} + rt_{ij} + h - M(1-z_{ikj}) - M(1-b_{ik})$$
$$d_{ij} \ge d_{kj} + rt_{kj} + h - M z_{ikj} - M(1-b_{ik})$$

**(5) Disruption feasibility** — a train either enters the disrupted segment before the window, after the window, or reroutes:

$$d_{i,J^D} \le t_1 + M(1-before_i), \quad d_{i,J^D} \ge t_1 + 1 - M(1-before_i)$$
$$d_{i,J^D} \ge t_2 - M(1-after_i), \quad d_{i,J^D} \le t_2 - 1 + M(1-after_i)$$
$$before_i + after_i + y_{i,J^D} \ge 1 - c_i$$

**(8) Rerouting restricted to disrupted segment and window**:

$$d_{i,J^D} \ge t_1 - M(1-y_{i,J^D}), \quad d_{i,J^D} \le t_2 + M(1-y_{i,J^D})$$
$$y_{ij} = 0 \quad \forall j \neq J^D$$

**(9) Delay definition**:

$$delay_i \ge a_{i,|S|} - SchedArr_i - M c_i, \quad delay_i \ge 0$$

## Assumptions (made where information was missing)

- Double-track line with unidirectional capacity per track; rerouting only possible on the disrupted segment during the disruption window.
- Speed profiles are precomputed per (train, segment) with fixed runtime and energy; profile selection is the linearized control-level decision.
- Cancellation is allowed at a high penalty; cancelled trains drop all timetable constraints.
- Headway h is uniform for all segments and both same-direction and single-track bidirectional operation.
