Text:
# MILP Model: Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

This model extends the RECIFE-MILP formulation (Pellegrini et al., 2015) with (i) speed profile options per train, (ii) train- and speed-dependent blocking times (brake indication points anywhere on the track), and (iii) a distinction between switch areas and plain track sections.

---

## 1. Assumptions (marked where not given in the text)

- **A1** (assumption): Trains run over a pre-defined route through the network; rerouting is limited to a finite set of alternative routes per train (local rerouting).
- **A2** (assumption): Delays of trains at the network entrance are known (deterministic, real-time setting).
- **A3** (assumption): Speed profiles are discretised into a finite set of options per train per route (e.g., coasting variants); each option defines a fixed running time and a set of speed-dependent blocking times per TTD section.
- **A4** (assumption): Dwell times may be stretched within given bounds; minimum dwell times are respected.
- **A5**: Headway safety is enforced via blocking-time occupancy: two trains may not occupy overlapping blocking times of the same TTD section. Under DTG, the blocking time of a section depends on the train's speed profile (speed-dependent braking/approach distance to the EoA).
- **A6** (assumption): Rolling stock assignments are fixed; no turning constraints are modelled.
- **A7** (assumption): Objective is total (secondary) delay; weights may differ per train class.

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $S$ | set of TTD sections (blocks) |
| $S^{\text{sw}} \subset S$ | switch sections |
| $R_t$ | set of candidate routes for train $t$ |
| $P_{t,r}$ | set of speed-profile options of train $t$ on route $r$ |
| $E_t$ | ordered set of events (passages / entries / exits) of train $t$ |
| $d_t$ | entrance delay of train $t$ (known) |
| $r^{0}_{t,e}$ | scheduled time of event $e$ of train $t$ |
| $w_t$ | delay weight of train $t$ |
| $b^{p}_{t,r,s}$ | blocking time of section $s$ for train $t$, route $r$, profile $p$ (speed-dependent, includes DTG braking distance to EoA) |
| $\underline{d}_s, \bar{d}_s$ | min/max dwell time on section $s$ |
| $\ell_{t,r,s}$ | running time of train $t$, route $r$, profile $p$ on section $s$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $H$ | time horizon |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $y_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ |
| $z_{t,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed-profile option $p$ |
| $x_{t,e} \ge 0$ | actual (scheduled) time of event $e$ of train $t$ |
| $\delta_{t,e} \ge 0$ | delay of event $e$ of train $t$ |
| $\beta_{t,s} \ge 0$ | time at which train $t$ starts occupying section $s$ (blocking-time start) |
| $\gamma_{t,s} \ge 0$ | time at which train $t$ frees section $s$ (blocking-time end) |
| $o_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ passes section $s$ **before** train $j$ (ordering) |
| $c_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i,j$ conflict on $s$ (both use $s$ with overlapping blocking times) |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total (weighted) delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} w_t \sum_{e \in E_t} \delta_{t,e}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route and profile choice — exactly one option per train:**

$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} y_{t,r} = 1 \quad \forall t \in T
$$
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{t,r}} z_{t,p} = y_{t,r} \quad \forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t
$$

**(C2) Entrance delay propagation:**

$$
x_{t,e_0} = r^{0}_{t,e_0} + d_t \quad \forall t \in T,\; e_0 = \text{first event of } t
$$

**(C3) Delay definition:**

$$
\delta_{t,e} \ge x_{t,e} - r^{0}_{t,e} \quad \forall t \in T,\; e \in E_t
$$

**(C4) Running times and dwell times along the route (linearised via big-M on route choice):**

$$
x_{t,e+1} \ge x_{t,e} + \sum_{r \in R_t}\sum_{p \in P_{t,r}} \ell^{p}_{t,r,s(e)} z_{t,p} - M(1-y_{t,r}) \quad \forall t, e
$$

Dwell time bounds at stations:

$$
\underline{d}_s \le x_{t,e_{\text{dep}}} - x_{t,e_{\text{arr}}} \le \bar{d}_s + \delta^{\text{dwell}}_{t,s}
$$

**(C5) Blocking-time start/end under DTG (speed-dependent):**

The blocking time of section $s$ for train $t$ with profile $p$ is:

$$
\beta_{t,s} \ge x_{t,e^{in}_s} - M(1 - z_{t,p}) \quad \forall t, s, p
$$
$$
\gamma_{t,s} \le x_{t,e^{in}_s} + \sum_{p} b^{p}_{t,r,s} z_{t,p} + M(1-y_{t,r}) \quad \forall t, s, r
$$

where $b^{p}_{t,r,s}$ embeds the DTG approach distance: the braking distance from the speed of profile $p$ to the EoA at the entry of the first occupied section ahead — hence $b^p$ grows with speed (speed-dependent separation, A5).

**(C6) Conflict detection (overlap of blocking times):**

$$
\beta_{j,s} - \gamma_{i,s} \le M(1 - o_{ij,s}) \quad \forall i<j,\; s \in S
$$
$$
\beta_{i,s} - \gamma_{j,s} \le M \, o_{ij,s} \quad \forall i<j,\; s \in S
$$

These two constraints enforce: if $o_{ij,s}=1$ (train $i$ first), then train $j$ may only enter after train $i$ has freed the section, and vice versa. Together they forbid overlapping blocking times.

**(C7) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-symmetry):**

$$
o_{ij,s} + o_{ji,s} = 1 \quad \forall i<j,\; s \in S
$$

**(C8) Route consistency on shared resources:** two trains may only be ordered on section $s$ if both actually traverse it:

$$
o_{ij,s} \le y_{i,r} \;\text{ for all } r \ni s, \qquad o_{ij,s} \le y_{j,r} \;\text{ for all } r \ni s
$$

**(C9) Switch exclusivity (stronger than plain sections):** on switch sections $s \in S^{\text{sw}}$, no overlapping occupancy at all, and routes using conflicting switch positions are mutually exclusive:

$$
\gamma_{i,s} \le \beta_{j,s} + M(1-o_{ij,s}) \quad \forall i<j,\; s \in S^{\text{sw}}
$$

**(C10) Time horizon:**

$$
x_{t,e} \le H \quad \forall t, e
$$

---

## 6. Remarks on DTG-specific modelling

- The **brake indication point** is not a fixed signal location: it is implicit in $b^{p}_{t,r,s}$, which contains the speed-dependent approach/braking distance from the profile speed to the EoA (end of TTD section). Different profiles $p$ yield different blocking times, so rescheduling may trade off speed profiles against reordering.
- **Speed profile options** (C1) allow the model to choose slower profiles to avoid conflicts, capturing the interplay between rescheduling and driving style neglected by conventional fixed-block CDR models.
- The model is a MILP: linear objective, continuous timing variables, binary route/profile/ordering variables, big-M linearisations. It can be solved by standard branch-and-bound solvers and compared against the original fixed-block RECIFE-MILP by replacing $b^{p}_{t,r,s}$ with fixed (speed-independent) blocking times.

Text:
# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

A bidirectional double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $S=\{1,\dots,n\}$ and segments between consecutive stations. A disruption partially blocks one track of segment $(s,s+1)$ during time window $[T^{dis}_1, T^{dis}_2]$; trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-track operation) during the window.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Trains run according to a predefined set of precomputed speed profiles per segment, each with a running time and energy consumption (piecewise-linear energy approximation ⇒ linear model).
- (A2) Each train stops at every station (typical of the referenced literature); dwell times have fixed min/max bounds.
- (A3) Disruption start time and duration are known in advance; trains inside the disrupted segment at $T^{dis}_1$ complete their run.
- (A4) Minimum headway is a constant time separation on each track (assumed for tractability; space–time headways are a straightforward extension).
- (A5) Cancellations are not modeled (fixed circulation); delays are measured against the original timetable.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains; $T^+ / T^-$ up/down direction trains |
| $K$ | set of speed profiles per segment $b$, with running time $r^k_b$ and energy $e^k_b$ |
| $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ (original timetable) |
| $h$ | minimum headway; $dw^{min}_s, dw^{max}_s$ | dwell bounds |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $W=[T^{dis}_1,T^{dis}_2]$, blocked track $b^*$ of segment $\sigma$ | disruption data |
| $\omega$ | energy weight (dual objective weighting) |

## 3. Decision Variables

- $A_{i,s} \ge 0$, $D_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times.
- $x_{i,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: speed profile $k$ of train $i$ on segment $b$ is selected.
- $y_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses the **alternative track** on segment $b$ (only meaningful for $b=\sigma$ during the window).
- $o_{i,b}, \bar o_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variables (train $i$ before $j$ on the normal / alternative track of segment $b$).
- $E \ge 0$: total energy consumption.

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay plus energy:

$$\min \; Z=\sum_{i\in T}\Big(\sum_{s\in S}(A_{i,s}-a_{i,s})+\sum_{s\in S}(D_{i,s}-d_{i,s})\Big)+\omega E$$

with $A_{i,s}\ge a_{i-s}$, $D_{i,s}\ge d_{i,s}$ (early arrival absorbed as waiting).

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Timetable structure and dwell times**
$$D_{i,s}-A_{i,s}\ge dw^{min}_s,\qquad D_{i,s}-A_{i,s}\le dw^{max}_s \qquad \forall i,s$$

**(2) Running times coupled to selected speed profiles** (linearization of $x$-weighted running time):
$$A_{i,s+1}-D_{i,s} = \sum_{k\in K} r^k_b\, x_{i,b,k}\quad \forall i,\; b=(s,s+1)$$
$$\sum_{k\in K} x_{i,b,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i,b$$

(If continuous running times are preferred: $A_{i,s+1}-D_{i,s}\ge r^{min}_b + \sum_k (r^k_b - r^{min}_b)x_{i,b,k}$ and $\le r^{max}_b$.)

**(3) Disruption and rerouting feasibility**
$$y_{i,\sigma} = 0 \quad \text{unless } [A_{i,\sigma^{from}}, A_{i,\sigma^{to}}]\cap W\neq\emptyset$$
linearized as:
$$A_{i,\sigma^{to}} \le T^{dis}_1 + M(1-y_{i,\sigma}) - \epsilon,\qquad A_{i,\sigma^{from}} \ge T^{dis}_2 - M y_{i,\sigma}$$
i.e., a train may use the alternative track only if it traverses segment $\sigma$ (partly) within the disruption window; direction trains unaffected by the window use $y_{i,\sigma}=0$. Additionally, on the blocked track:
$$x_{i,\sigma,k}\text{ with entry time in }W \Rightarrow y_{i,\sigma}=1$$

**(4) Track headway / conflict-freedom on segment $b$**

*Same track, same direction* (normal track, both trains not rerouted, or alternative track):
$$A_{j,b^{in}} - A_{i,b^{in}} \ge h - M(1-o_{i,b}) - M y_{j,b} - M(1-y_{i,b}) \quad \forall i<j \text{ (same direction)}$$
$$A_{i,b^{in}} - A_{j,b^{in}} \ge h - M\, o_{i,b} - M y_{j,b} - M(1-y_{i,b})$$
and symmetrically on the alternative track with $(1-y)$ terms. (Entry times $A_{i,b^{in}}$ = departure from upstream station.)

*Opposite directions on the alternative track (single-track operation)*: require full segment occupancy separation, using exit (arrival) times:
$$A_{j,b^{out}} - A_{i,b^{out}} \ge h + r^{min}_b - M(1-\bar o_{i,b}) - M(1-y_{i,b}) - M(1-y_{j,b}) \ \ \forall i\in T^+, j\in T^-$$
$$A_{i,b^{out}} - A_{j,b^{out}} \ge h + r^{min}_b - M\,\bar o_{i,b} - M(1-y_{i,b}) - M(1-y_{j,b})$$

**(5) Station headway (departure/arrival conflicts at shared platforms):**
$$A_{j,s}-A_{i,s}\ge h^{arr} \ \text{or} \ A_{i,s}-A_{j,s}\ge h^{arr}$$
via ordering binaries $u_{i,s}$:
$$A_{j,s}-A_{i,s}\ge h^{arr}-M(1-u_{i,s}),\qquad A_{i,s}-A_{j,s}\ge h^{arr}-M\,u_{i,s}$$

**(6) Energy accounting** (linear, per profile):
$$E = \sum_{i,b} \sum_{k\in K} e^k_b\, x_{i,b,k}$$

**(7) Variable domains**
$$A,D\ge 0;\quad x,y,o,\bar o,u\in\{0,1\}$$

## 6. Notes

- Constraint (2) is the key **coupling** between timetable (TRP) and speed management (TSMP): choosing a faster profile reduces running time (helping delay) but increases energy in (6).
- Constraints (3)–(4) jointly enforce conflict-free bidirectional operation during the disruption window with local rerouting.
- Per the referenced paper, this MILP is equivalently reformulated by enumerating feasible "train plans" (combinations of profile, route, and local time offsets per train) and solving a set-partitioning-style IP: $\min \sum_p c_p z_p$ s.t. headway constraints $\sum_p \alpha_{p,p'} z_p \le 1$, $\sum_p z_p =1$ per train — the decomposition enables the adaptive iterative solution method described in the text.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

- $I$ — set of trains, indexed $i,j$; $I^{up}, I^{dn}$ — up/down trains
- $S_i$ — ordered stations on train $i$'s route; segment $b$ connects $s_b$ and $s_b{+}1$
- $B^*$ — the disrupted segment (one track blocked during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$)
- $P_{i,b}$ — precomputed speed profiles (train plans) for train $i$ on segment $b$

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\bar a_{i,s}, \bar d_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure times |
| $r_{i,b,p}$, $e_{i,b,p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ for train $i$ on $b$ |
| $dw_{i,s}$ | minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_i$, $\gamma_i$ | delay priority weight / cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $\alpha$ | energy cost coefficient |
| $h$ | minimum same-direction headway; $h'$ — headway for opposing movements on a shared track |
| $[T_{start},T_{end}]$ | disruption window on $B^*$ |
| $\underline T_i, \overline T_i, T^{max}$ | earliest departure, latest arrival, horizon; $M$ — big-M ($\ge T^{max}$) |

## 3. Variables

- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0$ — actual arrival/departure times (retiming)
- $\delta_{i,s} \ge 0$ — delay of train $i$ at station $s$
- $z_{i,b,p} \in \{0,1\}$ — speed-profile selection (speed management)
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$ — train $i$ rerouted onto the opposite track of $B^*$ during the window
- $w_i, \tilde w_i \in \{0,1\}$ — train $i$ passes $B^*$ on its normal track before / after the window
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — train $i$ cancelled
- $x_{ij,b} \in \{0,1\}$ — same-direction ordering on segment $b$ ($1$ if $i$ precedes $j$)
- $v_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ — ordering of opposing trains on a shared track of $B^*$

## 4. Objective

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I} w_i \sum_{s\in S_i} \delta_{i,s}}_{\text{weighted delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i\in I}\sum_{b}\sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} e_{i,b,p}\, z_{i,b,p}}_{\text{energy}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I} \gamma_i c_i}_{\text{cancellations}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Profile selection (exactly one plan per train–segment; none if cancelled):**
$$\sum_{p\in P_{i,b}} z_{i,b,p} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall b \in S_i$$

**(2) Timetable–speed-profile coupling (tight, both sides):**
$$a_{i,s_b+1} \ge d_{i,s_b} - M c_i$$
$$a_{i,s_b+1} - d_{i,s_b} \ge \sum_p r_{i,b,p} z_{i,b,p} - M c_i$$
$$a_{i,s_b+1} - d_{i,s_b} \le \sum_p r_{i,b,p} z_{i,b,p} + M c_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall b$$

**(3) Dwell time:**
$$d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} + dw_{i,s} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s \ne \text{terminus}$$

**(4a) Same-direction headway, entry side:** for same-direction $i<j$ on $b$:
$$d_{j,s_b} \ge d_{i,s_b} + h - M(1-x_{ij,b}) - M c_i - M c_j$$
$$d_{i,s_b} \ge d_{j,s_b} + h - M x_{ij,b} - M c_i - M c_j$$

**(4b) Same-direction headway, exit side (block fully protected):**
$$a_{j,s_b+1} \ge a_{i,s_b+1} + h - M(1-x_{ij,b}) - M c_i - M c_j$$
$$a_{i,s_b+1} \ge a_{j,s_b+1} + h - M x_{ij,b} - M c_i - M c_j$$

**(5) Bidirectional exclusion on shared track of $B^*$** (entry side; exit side analogous with $a_{\cdot,s_{B^*}+1}$). Two opposing trains conflict only if they occupy the *same physical track*:

- *Both rerouted* ($y_i=y_j=1$, both on the opposite track):
$$d_{j,s_{B^*}} \ge d_{i,s_{B^*}} + h' - M(2-y_i-y_j) - M(1-v_{ij}) - M c_i - M c_j$$
$$d_{i,s_{B^*}} \ge d_{j,s_{B^*}} + h' - M(2-y_i-y_j) - M v_{ij} - M c_i - M c_j$$
- *Both on normal tracks* ($y_i=y_j=0$, opposing directions on the same physical track):
$$d_{j,s_{B^*}} \ge d_{i,s_{B^*}} + h' - M(y_i+y_j) - M(1-v_{ij}) - M c_i - M c_j$$
$$d_{i,s_{B^*}} \ge d_{j,s_{B^*}} + h' - M(y_i+y_j) - M v_{ij} - M c_i - M c_j$$

If exactly one train is rerouted, the two use different physical tracks and the big-M terms deactivate the constraints.

**(6) Disruption window on $B^*$ — each non-cancelled train chooses exactly one option:**
$$w_i + \tilde w_i + y_i = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i$$
- Pass **before** the window (must fully clear $B^*$ by $T_{start}$):
$$d_{i,s_{B^*}} + \sum_p r_{i,B^*,p} z_{i,B^*,p} \le T_{start} + M(1-w_i) + M c_i$$
- Pass **after** the window:
$$d_{i,s_{B^*}} \ge T_{end} - M(1-\tilde w_i) - M c_i$$
- **Reroute** through the window (occupy $B^*$ entirely within $[T_{start},T_{end}]$):
$$d_{i,s_{B^*}} \ge T_{start} - M(1-y_i) - M c_i$$
$$d_{i,s_{B^*}} + \sum_p r_{i,B^*,p} z_{i,B^*,p} \le T_{end} + M(1-y_i) + M c_i$$

**(7) Delay definition:**
$$\delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - \bar a_{i,s}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \ge 0, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(8) Cancellation logic:** with $c_i=1$, (1) frees profile selection, (2)–(6) are relaxed via $Mc_i$ terms, and additionally:
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(9) Time horizon:**
$$d_{i,s_0} \ge \underline T_i - M c_i, \qquad a_{i,s_{|S_i|-1}} \le \overline T_i + M c_i, \qquad 0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le T^{max}$$

**(10) Domains:**

# MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## Sets and Parameters

- **S** — segments of a double-track corridor (segment *s* connects stations *s* and *s+1*); **s\*** = disrupted segment, blocked during window **[W_start, W_end]**
- **T** — trains, each with fixed direction *d(t) ∈ {up, down}* and route through stations
- **K_t** — discrete speed profiles (train plans) per train/segment, each with running time **r_{t,s,k}** and energy **e_{t,s,k}**
- **A⁰_{t,s}, D⁰_{t,s}** — scheduled arrival/departure times; **dwell_{t,s}** — minimum dwell; **h** — headway; **M** — big-M; **w_t** — delay weight; **P_t** — cancellation penalty; **H** — planning horizon; **B** — discretized time buckets

## Decision Variables

- **x_{t,s,k} ∈ {0,1}** — train *t* uses speed profile *k* on segment *s*
- **A_{t,s}, D_{t,s} ≥ 0** — rescheduled arrival/departure times
- **z_{t,s\*} ∈ {0,1}** — train *t* is rerouted to the opposite track on the disrupted segment
- **o_{t,t'} ∈ {0,1}** — pairwise ordering variable (o = 1 ⟹ *t* passes before *t'*)
- **c_t ∈ {0,1}** — train *t* is cancelled
- **y_{t,s,b} ∈ {0,1}** — train *t* occupies segment *s* in time bucket *b*
- **δ^arr_t, δ^dep_t ≥ 0** — linearized terminal delays

## Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellation cost:

**min** Σ_t w_t (δ^arr_t + δ^dep_t) + Σ_t Σ_s Σ_k e_{t,s,k} x_{t,s,k} + Σ_t P_t c_t

## Constraints

**(C1) Dwell time** (intermediate stations):
D_{t,s} − A_{t,s} ≥ dwell_{t,s} − M·c_t

**(C2) Running time from selected profile:**
D_{t,s+1} − A_{t,s} = Σ_k r_{t,s,k} x_{t,s,k} + M·c_t  ∀ t, s

**(C3) Profile uniqueness (unless cancelled):**
Σ_k x_{t,s,k} = 1 − c_t  ∀ t, s

**(C4) Headway on normal (double-track) segments** — same-direction pairs, big-M disjunction:
- A_{t',s} − A_{t,s} ≥ h − M(1 − o_{t,t'})
- A_{t,s} − A_{t',s} ≥ h − M·o_{t,t'}

**(C5) Single-track non-overlap on disrupted segment s\*** (all train pairs, both directions):
- A_{t',s\*} − D_{t,s\*} ≥ −M(1 − o_{t,t'}) − M·c_t − M·c_{t'}
- A_{t,s\*} − D_{t',s\*} ≥ −M·o_{t,t'} − M·c_t − M·c_{t'}

**(C6) Disruption window / rerouting disjunction** — a train either passes s\* fully within the window or is rerouted:
- A_{t,s\*} ≥ W_start − M·z_{t,s\*} − M·c_t
- D_{t,s\*} ≤ W_end + M·z_{t,s\*} + M·c_t
- z_{t,s\*} ≥ (A_{t,s\*} − W_end)/M and z_{t,s\*} ≥ (W_start − D_{t,s\*})/M (linking)

**(C7) Occupation linking** (bucket *b* overlaps [A, D] iff y = 1), via big-M covering inequalities:
- y_{t,s\*,b} ≥ 1 − (b + |b| − A_{t,s\*})/M
- y_{t,s\*,b} ≥ 1 − (D_{t,s\*} − b)/M
- y_{t,s\*,b} ≤ (D_{t,s\*} − b)/M + (b + |b| − A_{t,s\*})/M

**(C8) Capacity on disrupted segment during window (unidirectional operation):**
Σ_t y_{t,s\*,b} ≤ 1  ∀ b ∈ [W_start, W_end]

**(C9) Delay linearization (epigraph form):**
- δ^arr_t ≥ A_{t,last} − A⁰_{t,last}, δ^arr_t ≥ 0
- δ^dep_t ≥ D_{t,first} − D⁰_{t,first}, δ^dep_t ≥ 0

**(C10) Cancellation relaxes timing:**
A_{t,s} ≤ H(1 − c_t), D_{t,s} ≤ H(1 − c_t)  ∀ t, s

**(C11) Running-time bounds:** r_min ≤ r_{t,s,k} ≤ r_max for all selected profiles (enforced per profile via x).

## Assumptions (made where input was unspecified)

1. Fixed minimum dwell times; dwell may be extended (flexible dwell) if desired by replacing equality with ≥.
2. Speed profiles are pre-enumerated discrete alternatives (train plans) with known running time and energy — consistent with the paper's plan-selection decomposition.
3. Opposite-direction trains use separate tracks on non-disrupted segments; only s\* during the window becomes effectively single-track.
4. Rerouting is only possible on the disrupted segment; rerouted trains may traverse outside the window on the opposite track.
5. Cancellations fully relax a train's timing/profile constraints at penalty P_t.
6. Big-M disjunctions model all ordering/occupancy logic; all constraints are linear.

# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** A double-track high-speed railway line with stations \(S=\{0,\dots,n\}\) and segments between consecutive stations. Each segment has two tracks (one per direction); during the disruption time window \([T_s, T_e]\) one track of a subset \(B\) of segments (the "disruption area") is blocked, so segments in \(B\) are single-tracked in \([T_s,T_e]\) and bidirectional trains must share the remaining track.
- **(A2)** Rerouting is allowed: a train whose direction conflicts with the surviving track on a blocked segment may run on the opposite track during \([T_s,T_e]\), subject to headway conflicts.
- **(A3)** Train dynamics are linearized: each train \(f\) can select among a finite set of precomputed speed profiles per segment. Each profile \(p\) of train \(f\) on segment \(i\) has a fixed running time \(r^{fp}_i\) and energy consumption \(e^{fp}_i\) (precomputed from optimal train control theory, e.g., Howlett et al. 2022). This makes the model fully linear.
- **(A4)** Time is discretized (horizon \(H\)); headway and block-section occupancy constraints are enforced as minimum spacing between trains entering a segment (line capacity in both directions and on the shared open track).
- **(A5)** Cancellation is allowed with a fixed penalty; a cancelled train occupies no resources.
- **(A6)** Dwell times are bounded by minimum and maximum values; departure (arrival) at each station cannot be earlier than scheduled.
- **(A7)** Speed profiles require no coasting-in-block violations: profile running times must be compatible with entry/exit times via linear consistency constraints.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(F\) | set of trains; \(F^{up}, F^{down}\): directions |
| \(I=\{0,\dots,n-1\}\) | segments; \(K=\{0,\dots,n\}\) stations |
| \(P_f\) | set of feasible speed profiles of train \(f\) (over all segments) |
| \(P^{f}_{i}\) | profiles of train \(f\) applicable to segment \(i\) |
| \(r^{fp}_i,\; e^{fp}_i\) | running time (min) and energy (kWh) of profile \(p\), train \(f\), segment \(i\) |
| \(d^{sch}_{fk},\, a^{sch}_{fk}\) | scheduled departure / arrival of train \(f\) at station \(k\) |
| \(\underline{dt}_{fk}, \overline{dt}_{fk}\) | min/max dwell of train \(f\) at station \(k\) |
| \(h_i\) | minimum headway on segment \(i\) (or open track) |
| \(w_f,\; \gamma_e,\; C_f\) | delay weight of train \(f\), energy price, cancellation cost |
| \(M\) | big-M |
| \(\delta^{in}_{f}\) | 1 if train \(f\) enters the disruption area during \([T_s,T_e]\) |

## 3. Decision Variables

- \(a_{fk}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), \(d_{fk}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\): adjusted arrival/departure times of train \(f\) at station \(k\).
- \(x^{fp}_i\in\{0,1\}\): 1 if train \(f\) uses profile \(p\) on segment \(i\).
- \(y^{f\sigma}_i\in\{0,1\}\): 1 if train \(f\) on segment \(i\) uses route \(\sigma\in\{0,1\}\) (0 = own track, 1 = opposite track).
- \(c_f\in\{0,1\}\): 1 if train \(f\) is cancelled.
- \(z^{ff'}_{i}\in\{0,1\}\): sequencing on segment \(i\): 1 if train \(f\) enters segment \(i\) before train \(f'\).
- \(\theta^{f\sigma}_{i}\in\{0,1\}\): 1 if train \(f\), route \(\sigma\), segment \(i\) is traversed during the disruption window.
- \(L_{fk}\ge0\): arrival delay of train \(f\) at station \(k\) (terminal stations).

Derived (linear) quantities: entry time to segment \(i\) for train \(f\): \(t^{in}_{fi}:=d_{f,i}\) (departure from upstream station \(i\)), exit time \(t^{out}_{fi}:=a_{f,i+1}\).

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay plus energy cost plus cancellation penalties:

\[
\min \; Z=\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{k\in K} w_f\, L_{fk} \;+\; \gamma_e \sum_{f\in F}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{p\in P^f_i} e^{fp}_i\, x^{fp}_i \;+\; \sum_{f\in F} C_f\, c_f
\]

with the linear delay definition:

\[
L_{fk}\ \ge\ a_{fk}-a^{sch}_{fk},\qquad L_{fk}\ge 0 \qquad \forall f,\ \forall k\in K
\tag{D}
\]

## 5. Constraints

**Consistency of times with profiles** (uncancelled trains only; \(M(1-c_f)\) relaxation):

\[
a_{f,i+1}-d_{f,i} = \sum_{p\in P^f_i} r^{fp}_i\, x^{fp}_i + \Delta^{run}_{fi}\quad \forall f,\forall i
\tag{1}
\]

where \(\Delta^{run}_{fi}\) is a slack absorbing tolerance, or, more strictly:

\[
a_{f,i+1}-d_{f,i} \ge \sum_{p\in P^f_i} r^{fp}_i x^{fp}_i - M c_f,\qquad
a_{f,i+1}-d_{f,i} \le \sum_{p\in P^f_i} r^{fp}_i x^{fp}_i + M c_f \quad \forall f,i
\tag{1a,1b}
\]

**Profile uniqueness:**

\[
\sum_{p\in P^f_i} x^{fp}_i = 1 - c_f \qquad \forall f,\forall i
\tag{2}
\]

**Schedule adherence (no earliness):**

\[
d_{fk}\ge d^{sch}_{fk}(1-c_f),\qquad a_{fk}\ge a^{sch}_{fk}(1-c_f)\qquad \forall f,k
\tag{3}
\]

**Dwell time bounds:**

\[
\underline{dt}_{fk}(1-c_f)\le d_{fk}-a_{fk}\le \overline{dt}_{fk}(1-c_f)\qquad \forall f,k
\tag{4}
\]

**Running-time consistency with schedule (linking timetabling to dynamics):** scheduled running time \(\rho^{sch}_{fi}=a^{sch}_{f,i+1}-d^{sch}_{f,i}\) admits only profiles with \(r^{fp}_i\) in a suitable range — enforced through \(P^f_i\); in the model this is (1a)–(1b) plus the restriction that selected profiles satisfy \(\sum_p r^{fp}_i x^{fp}_i \le a_{f,i+1}-d_{f,i}+\) maximum dwell extension, which is captured by (1a,1b).

**Disruption blocking of blocked track:** if train \(f\) runs on the blocked track of segment \(i\in B\) (route \(\sigma\) equal to its own direction), it must not be inside the segment during \([T_s,T_e]\):

\[
t^{in}_{fi} \ge T_e - M\big(1-y^{f\sigma}_i + \theta^{f\sigma}_{i}\big),\qquad
t^{out}_{fi} \le T_s + M\big(1-y^{f\sigma}_i + (1-\theta^{f\sigma}_{i})\big)\qquad \forall f,\ \forall i\in B
\tag{5,6}
\]

with indicator linking:

\[
\theta^{f\sigma}_{i} \ge 1-\frac{t^{out}_{fi}-T_s}{M},\qquad
\theta^{f\sigma}_{i} \ge 1-\frac{T_e-t^{in}_{fi}}{M}\qquad \forall f,\sigma,i\in B
\tag{7,8}
\]

(Linear indicator constraints; in a solver they are declared as such, keeping the model MILP.)

**Rerouting availability:** trains may only use the opposite track during the disruption window on blocked segments:

\[
y^{f\sigma}_{i} \le \theta^{f\sigma}_{i} + M\,(1-\mathbb{1}[i\in B])\qquad \forall f,\sigma,i
\tag{9}
\]

**Route–profile consistency:** each train uses exactly one route per segment:

\[
\sum_{\sigma} y^{f\sigma}_i = 1-c_f \qquad \forall f,i
\tag{10}
\]

**Headway / conflict-free operation (unidirectional segment, per route \(\sigma\)):** for every ordered pair \((f,f')\), \(f\neq f'\), using the same track \(\sigma\) of segment \(i\):

\[
t^{in}_{f'i} \ge t^{out}_{fi} + h_i - M(1-z^{ff'}_{i}) - M c_f - M c_{f'}\qquad \forall i,\sigma,\ \forall f<f'
\tag{11}
\]
\[
t^{in}_{fi} \ge t^{out}_{f'i} + h_i - M z^{ff'}_{i} - M c_f - M c_{f'}\qquad \forall i,\sigma,\ \forall f<f'
\tag{12}
\]

i.e., \(z^{ff'}_i=1\) enforces \(f\) before \(f'\); \(z=0\) enforces the reverse. (Segment-level headway \(h_i\) includes block-section travel, assumption A4.)

**Crossing (single-track operation of shared open track during disruption):** for the surviving track of a blocked segment, trains of opposite directions using it must not overlap — (11)–(12) already apply since both use route \(\sigma\); additionally, an explicit no-crossing constraint for opposite-direction trains passing the *whole* disruption area:

\[
\text{if } y^{f\sigma}_{i}\neq y^{f'\sigma}_{i}\text{ for the open track}: \quad
t^{out}_{f,n} \ge t^{in}_{f',0} - M z^{ff'}_{A},\qquad
t^{out}_{f',n} \ge t^{in}_{f,0} - M(1-z^{ff'}_{A})
\tag{13,14}
\]

where \(z^{ff'}_{A}\) orders trains \(f,f'\) over the entire disruption area \(A\subseteq B\).

**Cancellation consistency (no resource use):**

\[
d_{fk},\,a_{fk}\ \ge\ 0,\qquad
a_{f,k} \le M(1-c_f),\quad d_{f,k} \le M(1-c_f)\qquad \forall f,k
\tag{15}
\]

\[
t^{out}_{f,n} \le M(1-c_f)\qquad \forall f
\tag{16}
\]

**Terminal arrival (last station):**

\[
a_{f,n} = d_{f,n-1} + \sum_{p\in P^f_{n-1}} r^{fp}_{n-1} x^{fp}_{n-1} \qquad \forall f
\tag{17}
\]

(consistent with (1)).

**Variable domains:**

\[
a_{fk},d_{fk},L_{fk}\ge 0;\quad x^{fp}_i, y^{f\sigma}_i, c_f, z^{ff'}_i, \theta^{f\sigma}_i\in\{0,1\}
\tag{18}
\]

## 6. Remarks

- **(1a)–(1b)** implement the coupling of the TRP and TSMP: the chosen speed profile's running time must exactly match the timetable running time, guaranteeing control-level feasibility (assumption A3/A7).
- The energy term in \(Z\) lets the model trade off "run fast then dwell" vs. "run slow to arrive on time" — the two strategies with distinct energy consumption mentioned in the introduction.
- Constraints (5)–(9) model the partial blockage with rerouting to the opposite track; (11)–(14) guarantee conflict-free bidirectional operation including headway and crossing constraints.
- The model is a valid MILP (with indicator constraints (7)–(8), which are standard and convertible to big-M form), and matches the paper's description: simultaneous optimization of times, orders, routes, and speed profiles; the decomposition into train plans (IP + single-train plans) referenced in the paper corresponds to enumerating combinations of \((x,y)\) per train and selecting one plan per train in an IP over \(z\)-variables.

**Assumptions recap:** A1 double-track line with partial single-track blockage; A2 rerouting allowed in the disruption window; A3 finite, precomputed, linear speed-profile set; A4 headway-based capacity modeling with discretized time; A5 cancellation allowed at fixed cost; A6 bounded dwell; A7 profile–timetable consistency enforced linearly.

A constraint written once for all members of a set counts once. A constraint that is only described in words is not included. Variable domain declarations alone (such as x binary) are not constraints.
- Linear: false if the expression multiplies or divides decision variables, takes an absolute value, a maximum or minimum, a logical implication or any other nonlinear function of decision variables; otherwise true.

Here is the final model.

# Integrated MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains $i$ |
| $J$ | set of segments $j$ (block between consecutive stations) |
| $J_D \subseteq J$ | disrupted segments (one track blocked during window) |
| $P_{ij}$ | discretized speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $j$ (running time $r_{ijp}$, energy $e_{ijp}$) |
| $Q_j$ | unordered pairs $(i,k),\ i<k$, both traversing segment $j$ |
| $o_i \in \{0,1\}$ | direction of train $i$ (opposing pair: $o_i \neq o_k$) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $r_{ijp},\ e_{ijp}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ (precomputed from train dynamics — keeps model linear) |
| $a_i,\ A_i$ | scheduled corridor-entry time / desired corridor-exit time of train $i$ |
| $t_0,\ T_D$ | disruption start time and duration → window $[t_0,\, t_0+T_D]$ |
| $h^{same}_j,\ h^{opp}_j$ | minimum headways (same direction / full single-track headway) on segment $j$ |
| $\delta^{rer}$ | extra time penalty for using the opposite track (diversion move) |
| $dw_{ij}$ | minimum dwell/wait between consecutive segments |
| $\beta_i,\ w_c,\ w_r,\ \lambda_e$ | weights: train delay, cancellation, rerouting, energy |
| $d^{max}_i$ | maximum admissible delay of train $i$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $\epsilon > 0$ | boundary resolution for window classification |

## 3. Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{ijp}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $j$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ is cancelled |
| $y_{ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on $j$ |
| $b^{bef}_{ij}, b^{in}_{ij}, b^{aft}_{ij}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | exit-time placement of $e_{ij}$ relative to the disruption window |
| $z_{ikj}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | sequencing: 1 ⇒ train $i$ exits segment $j$ before train $k$ |
| $w^{in}_{ikj}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 iff both $i,k$ enter segment $j$ during the window (linearized product) |
| $\tau_{ij}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | realized running time of $i$ on $j$ |
| $e_{ij}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | exit time of train $i$ from segment $j$ |
| $d_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | terminal delay of train $i$ |

## 4. Objective function

$$
\min\; Z=\;
\underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\beta_i\, d_i}_{\text{weighted delay}}
+\underbrace{w_c\sum_{i\in I}c_i}_{\text{cancellations}}
+\underbrace{w_r\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J_D}y_{ij}}_{\text{reroutings}}
+\underbrace{\lambda_e\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{j\in J}\sum_{p\in P_{ij}} e_{ijp}\,x_{ijp}}_{\text{energy}}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed-profile selection (SOS1) and running-time coupling**
$$\sum_{p\in P_{ij}} x_{ijp} = 1-c_i \qquad \forall i,j$$
$$\tau_{ij} = \sum_{p\in P_{ij}} r_{ijp}\,x_{ijp} \qquad \forall i,j$$
A running train selects exactly one profile; its running time becomes the timetable running time — the timetable–speed-profile link. Energy cost enters via the objective.

**(C2) Time propagation**
$$e_{i,\text{first}} \ge a_i + \tau_{i,\text{first}} \qquad \forall i$$
$$e_{ij} \ge e_{i,j-1} + \tau_{ij} + dw_{ij} + \delta^{rer}\,y_{ij} \qquad \forall i,\ j\in J_D;\qquad e_{ij} \ge e_{i,j-1}+\tau_{ij} \ \text{otherwise}$$
Exit = entry + running time (inequality allows waiting at stations; rerouting adds diversion time).

**(C3) Delay definition and bound**
$$d_i \ge e_{i,\text{last}} - A_i,\qquad d_i \ge 0,\qquad d_i \le d^{max}_i \qquad \forall i$$

**(C4) Disruption-window placement (rigorous three-bin encoding)**
$$b^{bef}_{ij}+b^{in}_{ij}+b^{aft}_{ij}=1 \qquad \forall i,\ j\in J_D$$
$$e_{ij}\le t_0-\epsilon+M\,b^{in}_{ij}+M\,b^{aft}_{ij} \qquad \forall i,\ j\in J_D \tag{C4a}$$
$$e_{ij}\ge t_0-M\,b^{bef}_{ij} \tag{C4b}$$
$$e_{ij}\le t_0+T_D+M\,b^{aft}_{ij} \tag{C4c}$$
$$e_{ij}\ge t_0+T_D-M\,b^{bef}_{ij}-M\,b^{in}_{ij} \tag{C4d}$$
The binaries exactly classify whether the train occupies segment $j$ before / during / after the window.

**(C5) Rerouting rule**
$$y_{ij}\le 1-c_i \qquad \forall i,\ j\in J_D;\qquad y_{ij}=0 \ \ \forall j\notin J_D$$
Rerouting (to the surviving opposite track) is allowed only on disrupted segments for running trains.

**(C6) Single-track no-overlap during the window** — for all pairs $(i,k)\in Q_j$, $j\in J_D$ (any directions):
$$e_{ij}+h^{opp}_j \le e_{kj}+M(1-z_{ikj})+M(2-b^{in}_{ij}-b^{in}_{kj})$$
$$e_{kj}+h^{opp}_j \le e_{ij}+M\,z_{ikj}+M(2-b^{in}_{ij}-b^{in}_{kj})$$
If either train is outside the window, the constraint is relaxed; inside the window, all trains share the single available track and must be fully sequenced (meets happen at stations).

**(C7) Linearization of $w^{in}_{ikj}=b^{in}_{ij}\,b^{in}_{kj}$**
$$w^{in}_{ikj}\le b^{in}_{ij},\quad w^{in}_{ikj}\le b^{in}_{kj},\quad w^{in}_{ikj}\ge b^{in}_{ij}+b^{in}_{kj}-1 \qquad \forall (i,k)\in Q_j,\ j\in J_D$$

**(C8) Same-direction headway (standard disjunction, relaxed inside window)**
For pairs $(i,k)\in Q_j$ with $o_i=o_k$:
$$e_{ij}+h^{same}_j \le e_{kj}+M(1-z_{ikj})+M\,w^{in}_{ikj}$$
$$e_{kj}+h^{same}_j \le e_{ij}+M\,z_{ikj}+M\,w^{in}_{ikj}$$
On normal segments (and disrupted segments outside the window), same-direction trains are conflict-free via entry/exit headways; the $w^{in}$ term hands control over to C6 when both trains are inside the window.

**(C9) Rerouting exemption** — a rerouted train uses the free opposite track, so single-track conflicts (C6) need not bind for it:
$$\text{add } M\,y_{ij}\ \text{(and } M\,y_{kj}\text{) to the RHS of the C6 constraints of pair }(i,k).$$
Pairs on disrupted segments where one train is rerouted and the other is not must still respect $h^{opp}$ on the shared track unless both are exempt.

**(C10) Cancellation semantics**
$$e_{ij}\le E^{max}(1-c_i)\ \text{(vacuous when cancelled)},\qquad y_{ij}\le 1-c_i,\qquad x_{ijp}\le 1-c_i \ (\text{via C1})$$
A cancelled train consumes no capacity, selects no profile, and incurs penalty $w_c$ in the objective.

**(C11) Domains**

Text:
Below is the final MILP model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under a partial segment blockage.

---

# MILP for the TRSMP under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and indices
- $I$: trains; $i,j \in I$
- $S = \{0,\dots,m\}$: stations; segments $s \in \{0,\dots,m-1\}$ connect station $s$ and $s+1$
- $d$: the disrupted segment (one track blocked during $[T_1,T_2]$; the opposite track becomes a shared single-track resource)
- $P_i$: set of discretized speed/running-time plans for train $i$ on each segment

## 2. Parameters
- $a^0_{i,s}, d^0_{i,s}$: scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$
- $r_{i,p,s}$, $e_{i,p,s}$: running time and energy of plan $p$ for train $i$ on segment $s$
- $\tau^{min}_{i,s}, \tau^{max}_{i,s}$: dwell bounds at station $s$
- $h^{seg}, h^{st}$: segment and station headways
- $C_s$: station platform capacity; $\delta$: time discretization for occupancy
- $[T_1,T_2]$: disruption window; $T$: planning horizon (big-$M$)
- $\beta_i, \pi_E, \gamma, M_c$: weights for delay, energy, rerouting, cancellation
- $\delta_{i,s} \in \{up, down\}$: scheduled track/direction of train $i$ on segment $s$

## 3. Variables
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times
- $x_{i,p,s} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses plan $p$ on segment $s$
- $y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ rerouted to the opposite track on segment $s$ (fixed $y_{i,s}=0$ for $s \ne d$)
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled
- $o_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ ($i<j$)
- $q_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: trains $i,j$ use the same physical track on segment $s$
- $g_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ traverses segment $d$ overlapping $[T_1,T_2]$
- $b_{i,j,d} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ enters segment $d$ before train $j$
- $\Delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$
- $w_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ dwells at station $s$ during bin $[t\delta,(t+1)\delta)$

## 4. Objective
$$\min \; \sum_{i}\beta_i \sum_{s}\Delta_{i,s} \;+\; \pi_E \sum_{i,s,p} e_{i,p,s}\,x_{i,p,s} \;+\; \gamma \sum_i y_{i,d} \;+\; M_c \sum_i z_i$$

## 5. Constraints

**Plan selection / cancellation**
$$\sum_p x_{i,p,s} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, s \tag{1}$$

**Delay linearization**
$$\Delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^0_{i,s}, \qquad \Delta_{i,s} \ge d_{i,s} - d^0_{i,s}, \qquad \Delta_{i,s} \ge 0 \tag{2}$$

**Running-time propagation (plan-consistent)**
$$d_{i,s} + \sum_p r_{i,p,s}\,x_{i,p,s} \le a_{i,s+1} + T z_i \qquad \forall i, s \tag{3}$$

**Dwell bounds**
$$a_{i,s} + \tau^{min}_{i,s} - Tz_i \le d_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} + \tau^{max}_{i,s} + Tz_i \qquad \forall i,\ s=1,\dots,m-1 \tag{4}$$

**Schedule admissibility (no earlier than scheduled)**
$$a_{i,s} \ge a^0_{i,s} - Tz_i, \qquad d_{i,s} \ge d^0_{i,s} - Tz_i \tag{5}$$

**Disruption closure of the blocked track.** For trains scheduled on the blocked track of segment $d$:
$$a_{i,d+1} \ge T_2 - T\,y_{i,d} - T\,z_i \tag{6}$$
i.e., such a train must reroute, be cancelled, or complete the segment only after $T_2$.

**Rerouting restriction**
$$y_{i,s} = 0 \quad \forall i,\ s \ne d; \qquad y_{i,d} = 0 \ \text{for trains scheduled on the open track} \tag{7}$$

**Same-track indicator $q$ (XOR logic).** With $y_{i,s}=0$ for $s\ne d$:
- Same scheduled direction ($q = 1 \Leftrightarrow y_i = y_j$):
$$q_{i,j,s} \ge 1 - y_{i,s} - y_{j,s},\quad q_{i,j,s} \ge y_{i,s}+y_{j,s}-1,\quad q_{i,j,s} \le 1 - y_{i,s} + y_{j,s},\quad q_{i,j,s} \le 1 + y_{i,s} - y_{j,s}$$
- Opposite scheduled directions ($q = 1 \Leftrightarrow$ exactly one reroutes):
$$q_{i,j,s} \ge y_{i,s}-y_{j,s},\quad q_{i,j,s} \ge y_{j,s}-y_{i,s},\quad q_{i,j,s} \le y_{i,s}+y_{j,s},\quad q_{i,j,s} \le 2 - y_{i,s}-y_{j,s} \tag{8}$$

**Ordering completeness**
$$o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} \ge 1 - z_i - z_j, \qquad o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} \le 1 \qquad \forall i<j,\ s \tag{9}$$

**Same-track headways** (activated only if trains share a track and $i$ precedes $j$):
$$a_{j,s+1} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{seg} - T(2 - o_{i,j,s} - q_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i<j,\ s \tag{10}$$
$$d_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{seg} - T(2 - o_{i,j,s} - q_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i<j,\ s \tag{11}$$

**Station headway**
$$d_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{st} - T(2 - o_{i,j,s} - z_i - z_j) \qquad \forall i<j,\ s \tag{12}$$

**Disruption-window overlap indicator.** Train $i$ overlaps $[T_1,T_2]$ on segment $d$ iff $d_{i,d} < T_2$ **and** $a_{i,d+1} > T_1$:
$$g_i \ge 1 - \frac{T_2 - d_{i,d}}{T}, \qquad g_i \ge 1 - \frac{a_{i,d+1} - T_1}{T} \qquad \forall i \tag{13}$$
(If $d_{i,d} \ge T_2$ the first RHS is $\le 0$; if $d_{i,d} < T_2$ it forces $g_i=1$; symmetrically for the arrival vs. $T_1$.)

**Single-track ordering on segment $d$ during the disruption**
$$b_{i,j,d} + b_{j,i,d} \ge g_i + g_j - 1 - z_i - z_j, \qquad b_{i,j,d} + b_{j,i,d} \le 1 \qquad \forall i<j \tag{14}$$

**Single-track headways** (entry separation and traversal separation):
$$d_{j,d} \ge d_{i,d} + h^{seg} - T(3 - b_{i,j,d} - g_i - g_j) \qquad \forall i \ne j \tag{15}$$
$$a_{j,d+1} \ge a_{i,d+1} + h^{seg} - T(3 - b_{i,j,d} - g_i - g_j) \qquad \forall i \ne j \tag{16}$$

**Station capacity (time-indexed).** $w_{i,s,t}=1$ iff train $i$ is at station $s$ at time $t\delta$:
$$w_{i,s,t} \ge 1 - \frac{a_{i,s} - t\delta}{T} - z_i, \qquad w_{i,s,t} \le \frac{d_{i,s} - t\delta}{T} + z_i \qquad \forall i,s,t \tag{17}$$
$$\sum_i w_{i,s,t} \le C_s \qquad \forall s, t \tag{18}$$

**Domains**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \Delta_{i,s} \in [0,T]; \quad x, y, z, o, q, g, b, w \in \{0,1\} \tag{19}$$

## 6. Assumptions
1. Fixed station sequence per train; no short-turning or extra stops.
2. Only one track of segment $d$ is blocked during $[T_1,T_2]$; the opposite track remains open but becomes a shared bidirectional single-track resource.
3. Speed profiles are discretized into finite plan menus $(r_{i,p,s}, e_{i,p,s})$; rerouted trains use the same plan set (a separate reroute plan set can be substituted without structural change).
4. Headways are constant parameters, independent of the chosen speed plan (conservative).
5. Big-$M$ equals the horizon length $T$, valid since all times lie in $[0,T]$.
6. Cancellation ($z_i=1$) removes all resource consumption and headway interactions via the $z$-terms.
7. Delay is the positive deviation of actual from scheduled times (linearized via $\Delta$); energy is counted only for non-cancelled trains.
8. Rerouting is possible only on the disrupted segment and only for trains scheduled on the blocked track; it is penalized so the model reroutes only when beneficial.

This model jointly optimizes train times (retiming), orders (reordering), routes (rerouting), cancellations, and speed-profile selection, yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable whose timing is directly coupled to executable, energy-aware speed profiles.

# MILP Formulation of the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

**Assumptions (marked as such where not given):**
- (A1) Train set and stop patterns are fixed; dwell times are constants.
- (A2) Each train–segment speed profile is discretized into a finite set of candidate "interval plans," each with fixed running time, energy consumption, and position–time checkpoint bounds.
- (A3) Minimum headways (same-direction and opposite-direction) are constants.
- (A4) Acceleration/deceleration dynamics are embedded in the discretized speed plans.
- (A5) Big-M formulations are used to couple ordering variables with timing constraints.

## Sets and Parameters
- $F$: trains; $S$: stations; $\mathcal{E}$: segments $(i,j)$ between consecutive stations
- $P_{f,e}$: admissible paths (routes) for train $f$ on segment $e$ — normal track, plus the opposite track only if $e$ is in the disruption area
- $K_{f,e}$: candidate speed plans for train $f$ on segment $e$, with running time $r^{e}_{fk}$, energy $E^{e}_{fk}$, and checkpoint bounds $[\ell^{e}_{fk}, \bar{\ell}^{e}_{fk}]$
- $\Delta$: minimum dwell time; $h^{same}, h^{opp}$: minimum headways; $[t_0, t_1]$: disruption time window; $H$: planning horizon
- $\pi^{sched}_{fs}$: scheduled arrival/departure times; $w_d, w_e, w_c$: objective weights (assumed)

## Decision Variables
- $a_{fs} \in [0,H]$, $d_{fs} \in [0,H]$: arrival / departure times (continuous)
- $x_{fep} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses path $p$ on segment $e$
- $y_{fek} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses speed plan $k$ on segment $e$
- $z_{fge} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ precedes train $g$ on segment $e$
- $u_f \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ is cancelled

## Objective Function

$$\min \; w_d \underbrace{\sum_{f \in F}\sum_{s \in S}\big[(a_{fs}-\pi^{arr}_{fs})^+ + (d_{fs}-\pi^{dep}_{fs})^+\big]}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\; w_e \underbrace{\sum_{f \in F}\sum_{e \in \mathcal{E}}\sum_{k \in K_{f,e}} E^{e}_{fk}\, y_{fek}}_{\text{total energy}}
\;+\; w_c \underbrace{\sum_{f \in F} u_f}_{\text{cancellations}}$$

## Constraints

**Timetable consistency (dwell & running times):**
1. $\quad d_{fs} - a_{fs} = \Delta \quad \forall f, s \in \text{intermediate}$ (relaxed by $\pm M u_f$ if cancelled)
2. $\quad a_{f,j} - d_{f,i} = \sum_{k} r^{e}_{fk}\, y_{fek} \quad \forall f, e=(i,j)$ (linearized: $r^{e}_{fk} - M(1-y_{fek}) \le a_{fj}-d_{fi} \le r^{e}_{fk} + M(1-y_{fek})$)

**Route and plan selection:**
3. $\quad \sum_{p \in P_{f,e}} x_{fep} = 1 - u_f \quad \forall f, e$
4. $\quad \sum_{k \in K_{f,e}} y_{fek} = 1 - u_f \quad \forall f, e$

**Rerouting / disruption window:**
5. If normal track of $e$ is blocked: $\; d_{fi} \le t_0 + M(1-x_{fe,N}) + M u_f$ **or** $d_{fi} \ge t_1 - M(1-x_{fe,N}) - M u_f$ (avoid window)
6. Opposite-track path usable only within the window: $\; t_0 - M(1-x_{fe,O}) - Mu_f \le d_{fi} \le t_1 + M(1-x_{fe,O}) + Mu_f$

**Plan–timetable position–time alignment (checkpoints):**
7. $\quad \ell^{e}_{fk} - M(1-y_{fek}) \le a_{fj} - d_{fi} \le \bar{\ell}^{e}_{fk} + M(1-y_{fek}) \quad \forall f, e, k$

**Headway / conflict-free constraints (big-M, ordering via $z$):** for all train pairs $f,g$ on segment $e=(i,j)$, with $z_{fge}=1$ meaning $f$ precedes $g$:
8. $\quad a_{gj} - a_{fj} \ge h^{same} - M(1-z_{fge}) - M(u_f + u_g)$ (arrival–arrival)

Text:
**Selected model: Model 2** — it is the most complete and internally consistent formulation: it cleanly separates timetable, ordering, routing, cancellation and speed-profile decisions, and the running-time linking constraint is the essential device that makes rescheduling and speed management genuinely integrated while keeping the whole model linear.

---

# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

*Partial segment blockage on a double-track high-speed railway corridor with local rerouting onto the opposite track.*

## Sets and Indices

- $T$: set of trains, indexed by $t$
- $S$: set of stations, indexed by $s$ (ordered along the corridor)
- $L$: set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $l$ ($l$ connects $s_l$ and $s_{l+1}$)
- $P$: set of discrete, energy-feasible speed profiles, indexed by $p$
- $R_t$: set of admissible routes for train $t$ (own track vs. opposite track through the disruption window)
- $L^b$: set of blocked segments (partial blockage)
- $D = [t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$: disruption time window

## Parameters

- $a^0_{t,s}, d^0_{t,s}$: original scheduled arrival/departure of train $t$ at station $s$
- $w^{min}_{t,s}, w^{max}_{t,s}$: minimum/maximum dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $h$: minimum headway
- $\alpha_t$: delay weight of train $t$; $\beta$: cancellation penalty; $\gamma$: energy weight
- $E_{t,l,p}$: energy consumption of train $t$ on segment $l$ with profile $p$
- $\tau_{t,l,p}$: running time of train $t$ on segment $l$ with profile $p$
- $M$: sufficiently large constant
- $t^{max}_t$: deadline for train $t$'s terminal arrival

## Decision Variables

- $a_{t,s} \ge 0$, $d_{t,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times (retiming)
- $y_{t,t',l} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ on segment $l$ (reordering)
- $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_t$ (rerouting)
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled
- $z_{t,l,p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ runs segment $l$ with profile $p$ (speed management)
- $o_{t,t',l} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies shared track $l$ before opposing train $t'$
- $u_{t,l} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ occupies blocked segment $l$ during the disruption window

## Objective Function

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} \alpha_t \sum_{s \in S} \left(a_{t,s} - a^0_{t,s}\right)}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\beta \sum_{t \in T} c_t}_{\text{cancellations}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\gamma \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{l \in L}\sum_{p \in P} E_{t,l,p}\, z_{t,l,p}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
$$

*(Linear since $a_{t,s} \ge a^0_{t,s}$ is enforced below, so delay terms are nonnegative.)*

## Constraints

**1. Speed profile assignment** (exactly one profile per train–segment; none if cancelled):
$$\sum_{p \in P} z_{t,l,p} = 1 - c_t \quad \forall t,\; \forall l \in L$$

**2. Running-time consistency** (timetable ↔ speed profile linkage — the core integration):
$$a_{t,s+1} = d_{t,s} + \sum_{p \in P} \tau_{t,l,p}\, z_{t,l,p} \quad \forall t,\; \forall l=(s,s+1)$$

**3. Dwell times:**
$$d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \ge w^{min}_{t,s} (1 - c_t), \qquad d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \le w^{max}_{t,s} + M\, c_t \quad \forall t,s$$

**4. Route assignment:**
$$\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 - c_t \quad \forall t$$

**5. Headway / safety constraints** (same-direction ordering on each segment):
$$d_{t',s} - d_{t,s} \ge h - M(1 - y_{t,t',l}) - M c_{t'} \quad \forall t \ne t',\; l=(s,s+1)$$
$$a_{t,s+1} - a_{t',s+1} \ge h - M(1 - y_{t,t',l}) - M c_{t'} \quad \forall t \ne t',\; l=(s,s+1)$$
with exactly one ordering enforced when both trains run:
$$y_{t,t',l} + y_{t',t,l} \ge 1 - c_t - c_{t'} \quad \forall t < t',\; \forall l$$

**6. Disruption unavailability** (blocked track may not be used during window unless rerouted):
$$a_{t,s+1} \ge t_d^{start} - M(1-u_{t,l}), \qquad d_{t,s} \le t_d^{end} + M(1-u_{t,l}) \quad \forall t,\; l \in L^b$$
$$x_{t,r} \le 1 - u_{t,l} \quad \forall t,\; l \in L^b,\; r \text{ using the blocked track}$$

**7. Bidirectional conflict on the shared single track** (opposing trains within the window):
$$d_{t,s} \ge a_{t',s+1} - M(1 - o_{t,t',l}) - M(c_t + c_{t'}) \quad \forall t < t',\; l \in L^b$$
$$d_{t',s+1} \ge a_{t,s} - M\, o_{t,t',l} - M(c_t + c_{t'}) \quad \forall t < t',\; l \in L^b$$
$$o_{t,t',l} + o_{t',t,l} \ge x_{t,r} + x_{t',r'} - 1 \quad \forall t<t',\; l \in L^b,\; r,r' \text{ using } l \text{ bidirectionally}$$

**8. Cancellation consequences:**
$$a_{t,s} \ge a^0_{t,s} - M c_t, \qquad d_{t,s} \ge d^0_{t,s} - M c_t \quad \forall t,s$$
$$a_{t,|S|} \le t^{max}_t + M c_t \quad \forall t \quad \text{(deadline; cancellations exempt)}$$

**9. Variable domains:**
$$a_{t,s}, d_{t,s} \ge 0; \quad y_{t,t',l},\, x_{t,r},\, c_t,\, z_{t,l,p},\, o_{t,t',l},\, u_{t,l} \in \{0,1\}$$

## Key Assumptions

- The double-track corridor becomes effectively single-track on segment $l^* \in L^b$ during $D$; rerouting sends one direction's trains onto the opposite track, so opposing trains must be sequenced via $o$-variables.
- Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of energy-feasible alternatives per train–segment (standard practice for MILP tractability); each profile has fixed running time $\tau$ and energy $E$.
- Cancelled trains are fully deactivated (no profile, no route, times relaxed) and pay only penalty $\beta$.
- Weights $\alpha_t, \beta, \gamma$ scalarize delay, service reliability and energy into one objective, enabling trade-off analysis.

All constraints are linear in continuous and binary variables, so the model is a valid MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut, and is amenable to the decomposition (train-plan selection) and adaptive iterative refinement schemes mentioned in the introduction.

Below is the final MILP for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under a partial segment blockage.

## Sets and indices
- $i \in I$: trains
- $s \in S_i$: stations visited by train $i$ (ordered $1,\dots,|S_i|$)
- $a \in A$: track segments; segment $a$ connects station $s$ to $s+1$ (write $a = a(i,s)$ for the segment after station $s$)
- $k \in K_a$: parallel tracks on segment $a$ (double track: $K_a=\{1,2\}$)
- $p \in P_{i,a}$: discrete speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $a$, with running time $r_{i,a,p}$ and energy $e_{i,a,p}$
- $a^* \in A$: the partially blocked segment; track 1 of $a^*$ is blocked during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$

## Parameters
- $w_i$: delay weight; $\beta_i$: cancellation cost; $\alpha$: energy cost coefficient
- $h_a$: headway on segment $a$; $d^{min}_{i,s}, d^{max}_{i,s}$: min/max dwell at station $s$
- $T_{start}, T_{end}$: disruption window; $b_i$: minimum traversal time of $a^*$ under disruption
- $H$: planning horizon; $M$: big-M; $\epsilon$: small tolerance
- $\tau^{arr}_{i,s}, \tau^{dep}_{i,s}$: scheduled arrival/departure times

## Decision variables
- $arr_{i,s}, dep_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times
- $x_{i,a,p} \in \{0,1\}$: profile $p$ selected for train $i$ on segment $a$
- $t_{i,a,k} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses track $k$ of segment $a$
- $y_{i,a^*} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ rerouted to the opposite track on $a^*$
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled
- $\gamma_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff $arr_{i,s^*} \le T_{end}$ (enters $a^*$ before window ends; $s^*$ = station preceding $a^*$)
- $\delta_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff $dep_{i,s^*+1} \ge T_{start}$ (leaves $a^*$ at/after window start)
- $o_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff train $i$'s traversal overlaps the window ($o_i = \gamma_i \wedge \delta_i$)
- $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering binary per unordered pair on a segment
- $delay_i \ge 0$: arrival delay of train $i$ at its final station

## Objective
$$\min \; \sum_{i \in I} w_i \, delay_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{a \in A_i}\sum_{p \in P_{i,a}} e_{i,a,p}\, x_{i,a,p} \;+\; \sum_{i \in I} \beta_i z_i$$

## Constraints

**(1) Profile selection and exact run-time coupling** — a running train selects exactly one profile, and the timetable must match it exactly:
$$\sum_{p \in P_{i,a}} x_{i,a,p} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i,\; \forall a \in A_i$$
$$arr_{i,s+1} - dep_{i,s} = \sum_{p \in P_{i,a(i,s)}} r_{i,a,p}\, x_{i,a,p} + M z_i \qquad \forall i,\; \forall s \in S_i \setminus \{|S_i|\}$$

**(2) Disrupted traversal time** — trains overlapping the window need at least $b_i$ on $a^*$:
$$arr_{i,s^*+1} - dep_{i,s^*} \ge b_i - M(1 - o_i) \qquad \forall i$$

**(3) Overlap logic** (exact biconditionals):
$$arr_{i,s^*} \le T_{end} + M(1 - \gamma_i), \qquad arr_{i,s^*} \ge T_{end} + \epsilon - M\gamma_i$$
$$dep_{i,s^*+1} \ge T_{start} - M(1 - \delta_i), \qquad dep_{i,s^*+1} \le T_{start} - \epsilon + M\delta_i$$
$$o_i \le \gamma_i, \quad o_i \le \delta_i, \quad o_i \ge \gamma_i + \delta_i - 1$$

**(4) Track assignment** — each running train gets exactly one track per segment; rerouting only on $a^*$:
$$\sum_{k \in K_a} t_{i,a,k} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, \forall a \in A_i$$
$$t_{i,a,k} = 1\ (\text{planned track}) \;\; \text{and} \;\; t_{i,a,k} = 0 \;\text{otherwise} \qquad \forall i,\; \forall a \ne a^*$$
$$t_{i,a^*,\delta_i} = 1 - y_{i,a^*} - z_i, \qquad t_{i,a^*,3-\delta_i} = y_{i,a^*} \qquad \forall i$$

**(5) Per-track headway** — same-track trains separated by at least $h_a$ (either order):
$$dep_{j,s+1} \ge arr_{i,s+1} + h_a - M(2 - t_{i,a,k} - t_{j,a,k}) - M y_{ij} \qquad \forall i<j \text{ on } a,\; \forall k$$
$$dep_{i,s+1} \ge arr_{j,s+1} + h_a - M(2 - t_{i,a,k} - t_{j,a,k}) - M(1 - y_{ij}) \qquad \forall i<j \text{ on } a,\; \forall k$$

**(6) Sequencing (no overtaking) on the same track**:
$$dep_{j,s+1} \ge dep_{i,s+1} - M(2 - t_{i,a,k} - t_{j,a,k}) - M y_{ij} \qquad \forall i<j,\; \forall k$$
$$dep_{i,s+1} \ge dep_{j,s+1} - M(2 - t_{i,a,k} - t_{j,a,k}) - M(1 - y_{ij}) \qquad \forall i<j,\; \forall k$$

**(7) Dwell times**:
$$dep_{i,s} - arr_{i,s} \ge d^{min}_{i,s} - M z_i, \qquad dep_{i,s} - arr_{i,s} \le d^{max}_{i,s} + M z_i \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(8) Delay accounting**:
$$delay_i \ge arr_{i,|S_i|} - \tau^{arr}_{i,|S_i|}, \qquad delay_i \le arr_{i,|S_i|} - \tau^{arr}_{i,|S_i|} + M z_i \qquad \forall i$$

**(9) Cancellation and horizon**:
$$arr_{i,s} \le H + M z_i, \qquad dep_{i,s} \le H + M z_i \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(10) Domains**:
$$x_{i,a,p},\, t_{i,a,k},\, y_{i,a^*},\, z_i,\, \gamma_i,\, \delta_i,\, o_i,\, y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}; \quad arr_{i,s},\, dep_{i,s},\, delay_i \ge 0$$

## Key modeling points
- **Timetable–profile coupling (1)**: the equality forces the rescheduled running time to exactly realize the selected speed profile, guaranteeing control-level feasibility; energy enters the objective linearly through the same binaries.
- **Rerouting (4)**: $y_{i,a^*}$ lets affected trains divert to the opposite track during the disruption, with track binaries making all resource constraints fully linear.
- **Window overlap (2)–(3)**: $\gamma_i, \delta_i, o_i$ encode interval overlap with exact big-M biconditionals, so the disrupted traversal time applies only to trains actually inside the window.
- **Conflict-free operation (5)–(6)**: headway and no-overtaking constraints activate only when two trains share a track, with ordering binaries resolving the disjunctions.

## Assumptions
1. Speed profiles are precomputed from train dynamics; running time and energy per profile are constants (keeps the model linear).
2. The disruption affects only segment $a^*$ during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$; $b_i$ is a given minimum traversal time under disruption.
3. Headways are uniform per segment and symmetric; no platform-track assignment is modeled (station headways approximate platform conflicts).
4. Cancellation removes the train entirely; its delay contribution is zeroed by (8).
5. $M$ is chosen large enough (e.g., $M = H + \max r$); $\epsilon$ is a small positive tolerance for strict biconditionals.
6. Energy is profile- and segment-dependent only (no regenerative braking sharing between trains).
7. Objective weights $w_i, \alpha, \beta_i$ are exogenous, reflecting operator preferences over delay, energy, and cancellations.

Based on the generated candidates, **Model 3** is the best: it covers all five decision dimensions (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, speed-plan selection), cleanly handles the bidirectional conflict via shared order binaries, explicitly forbids use of the blocked track within the disruption window, and keeps every constraint strictly linear. Here is the final model:

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions and Modeling Setting

- **Corridor**: A single double-track railway corridor with stations (including passing loops) indexed by $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ and track segments between consecutive stations $A = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$. Segment $a$ normally serves direction $d(a)$, one track per direction.
- **Disruption**: A set $D \subseteq A$ of segments has one track blocked during time window $[\,t_0, t_1\,]$. Trains may either wait (remain on their own-direction track, which is idle during $[t_0,t_1]$) or **reroute** onto the opposite (unblocked) track, where they must be interleaved bidirectionally with trains of the opposite direction.
- **Trains**: Set $T$ of trains; each train $i$ has a scheduled direction $dir_i \in \{+, -\}$, an ordered route, and follows the pre-disruption timetable for all activities scheduled before $t_0$ (fixed).
- **Speed plans**: For each train $i$, segment $a$, and route choice $r$, a discrete library $P_{iar}$ of admissible plans $p$ with running time $L_{iarp}$ and energy $E_{iarp}$ (from traction simulation). Exactly one plan is selected.
- **Time**: Continuous time variables on horizon $[0,H]$; headways enforced per track; big-$M$ constant ($M = H$ suffices).
- Each train may be **cancelled**, incurring penalty $\gamma$.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | trains; $dir_i \in \{+, -\}$ |
| $A$ | segments; $S$ stations; $D \subseteq A$ disrupted segments |
| $N_i$, $A_i$ | ordered stations / segments on train $i$'s route |
| $L_{iarp}, E_{iarp}$ | running time / energy of plan $p$ for train $i$, segment $a$, route $r$ |
| $\tau^{arr}_{is}, \tau^{dep}_{is}$ | original timetable arrival/departure |
| $u^{min}_{is}, u^{max}_{is}$ | min/max dwell at station $s$ |
| $h_1, h_b$ | same-direction headway and bidirectional (single-track) headway |
| $K_s$ | station capacity at $s$ |
| $\gamma$, $W$ | cancellation penalty; energy weight |
| $M$ | big-M constant ($M = H$ suffices) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival / departure of train $i$ at station $s \in N_i$ (entry/exit of segment $a$ is $d_{is}$ at the upstream station, $a_{is'}$ at the downstream station).
- $\delta_{is} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $e_i \ge 0$: total energy of train $i$.

**Binary:**
- $x_{iar} \in \{0,1\}$: route choice ($r=1$: keep own track; $r=2$: reroute via opposite track) — only for $a \in D$; fixed $x_{ia1}=1$ otherwise.
- $z_{iarp} \in \{0,1\}$: speed-plan selection, $p \in P_{iar}$.
- $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering — $y_{ij}=1 \Leftrightarrow i$ precedes $j$ on a shared resource ($y_{ji} = 1 - y_{ij}$ for $i<j$).
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ is cancelled.
- $w_{ia} \in \{0,1\}$: auxiliary — train $i$ occupies its own track of segment $a$ *before* $t_0$ (vs. after $t_1$).
- $\phi_{ist} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ occupies station $s$ during time slot $t$ (slot length $\Delta$).

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in N_i} \delta_{is}}_{\text{total delay (primary)}} \;+\; W \sum_{i \in T} e_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T} c_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Running-time consistency and plan selection
For each train $i$ and segment $a$ joining consecutive stations $s, s'$:

$$
d_{is} + \sum_{r}\sum_{p \in P_{iar}} L_{iarp}\,z_{iarp} \;\le\; a_{is'} \qquad \forall i,\; (s,a,s') \in A_i
$$
$$
\sum_{r}\sum_{p \in P_{iar}} z_{iarp} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,\; a \in A_i
$$
$$
z_{iarp} \le x_{iar} \qquad \forall i,\; a \in A_i,\; r,\; p \in P_{iar}
$$

(Cancelled trains select no plan; timing variables are freed via $c_i$ below.)

### (C2) Energy consistency
$$
e_i = \sum_{a \in A_i}\sum_{r}\sum_{p \in P_{iar}} E_{iarp}\, z_{iarp} \qquad \forall i
$$

### (C3) Dwell time bounds
$$
a_{is} + u^{min}_{is} \le d_{is} \le a_{is} + u^{max}_{is} \qquad \forall i,\; s \in N_i
$$

### (C4) Horizon and fixed pre-disruption timetable
$$
\underline{a}_{is} \le a_{is} \le \overline{a}_{is}, \quad \underline{d}_{is} \le d_{is} \le \overline{d}_{is} \le H \qquad \forall i, s
$$
For all events with scheduled time $\le t_0$: $a_{is}=\tau^{arr}_{is}$, $d_{is}=\tau^{dep}_{is}$.

### (C5) Delay definition
$$
\delta_{is} \ge a_{is} - \tau^{arr}_{is}, \qquad \delta_{is} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$

### (C6) Cancellation
$$
a_{is} \le \tau^{arr}_{is} + M(1-c_i), \quad a_{is} \ge \tau^{arr}_{is} - M(1-c_i), \quad \delta_{is} \le M(1-c_i)
$$
(and identically for $d_{is}$) — cancelled trains keep their original (frozen) times, incur zero delay and no resource consumption.

### (C7) Same-track, same-direction headway
Define the route-agreement binary for unordered pair $i,j$ on segment $a$:
$$
\sigma^{a}_{ij} \ge x_{ia1} + x_{ja1} - 1, \qquad \sigma^{a}_{ij} \ge x_{ia2} + x_{ja2} - 1, \qquad \sigma^{a}_{ij}\in\{0,1\}
$$
For every pair $i \ne j$ with $dir_i = dir_j$ (using $y_{ji}=1-y_{ij}$):
$$
d_{ia} + h_1 \le a_{ja} + M\big(3 - y_{ij} - \sigma^a_{ij} - (1-c_j)\big)
$$
$$
d_{ja} + h_1 \le a_{ia} + M\big(2 + y_{ij} - \sigma^a_{ij} - (1-c_i)\big)
$$
Relaxed when a train is cancelled or the trains use different tracks.

### (C8) Bidirectional conflict on the shared track during the disruption
If trains $i$ (direction $+$) and $j$ (direction $-$) both reroute on disrupted segment $a \in D$, they must use the single available track one at a time with headway $h_b$. Define $o^a_{ij} \ge x_{ia2} + x_{ja2} - 1$ ("both reroute"):
$$
d_{ia} + h_b \le a_{ja} + M\big(4 - y_{ij} - \sigma^a_{ij} - o^a_{ij} - (1-c_j)\big)
$$
$$
d_{ja} + h_b \le a_{ia} + M\big(3 + y_{ij} - \sigma^a_{ij} - o^a_{ij} - (1-c_i)\big)
$$
Rerouted entry must fall inside the disruption window:
$$
a_{ia} \ge t_0 - M(1 - x_{ia2}), \qquad a_{ia} \le t_1 + M(1 - x_{ia2})
$$

### (C9) Blocked-track prohibition within $[t_0, t_1]$
A train keeping its own track ($r=1$) on a disrupted segment must enter before $t_0$ or after $t_1$:
$$
a_{ia} \le t_0 + M(1 - x_{ia1}) + M w_{ia}
$$
$$
a_{ia} \ge t_1 - M(1 - x_{ia1}) - M(1 - w_{ia})
$$

### (C10) Station capacity (time-indexed)
$$
\phi_{ist} \ge 1 - \frac{a_{is} - t\Delta}{M} - \frac{d_{is} - t\Delta}{M} \quad \text{(standard big-M linking; exact big-M pairs may be used)}, \qquad \sum_{i}\phi_{ist} \le K_s \quad \forall s, t
$$

### (C11) Domains
$$
a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is}, e_i \ge 0; \qquad x, z, y, \sigma, o, w, \phi, c \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. How the Model Works

- **Retiming**: continuous $a_{is}, d_{is}$ subject only to the fixed pre-disruption timetable (C4), dwell bounds (C3), and running times (C1).
- **Reordering**: pairwise disjunctive binaries $y_{ij}$ shared between same-direction headways (C7) and bidirectional conflicts (C8) — one order decision serves both resource types (job-shop-style).
- **Rerouting**: binaries $x_{ia}$; $\sigma^a_{ij}, o^a_{ij}$ detect track sharing, activating the appropriate disjunction; C9 forbids occupying the blocked track inside $[t_0,t_1]$.
- **Cancellation**: binary $c_i$ removes the train's plan selection (C1), zeroes its delay (C5–C6), and relaxes all pairwise constraints via $(1-c_i)$ terms; penalty $\gamma$ in the objective.
- **Speed management**: one-hot plan selection $z_{iarp}$ couples the discrete plan library to running time (C1) and energy (C2), so the optimizer trades energy against delay through weight $W$.
- **Big-M validity**: $M \ge H + h_b$ is valid since all times lie in $[0,H]$; tighten with segment-specific $M_{ia} = \overline{d}_{ia} - \underline{a}_{ia} + h$.

The model is a complete MILP — linear objective, continuous time/energy variables, and binaries $\{x, z, y, c, w, \phi, \sigma, o\}$ — integrating retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed management in a single formulation solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX).

Text:
# MILP Model: Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

A single bidirectional urban rail line is considered within an MPC framework: at each control step, a finite prediction horizon of time intervals is considered, the MILP below is solved, only the first control actions are applied, and the horizon rolls forward.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Trains run on a double-track line, one direction per track; overtaking is not possible, so train order on each direction is fixed.
- (A2) Time-varying passenger OD demand is approximated as **piecewise constant** over time intervals of equal length.
- (A3) Train composition is chosen from a set of train unit types (e.g., 3-car or 6-car units); a train's capacity equals the sum of its units' capacities.
- (A4) Rolling stock circulation is modeled at the level of train units: units are coupled/decoupled at terminal stations only *(simplifying assumption)*.
- (A5) Dwell time depends linearly on the number of boarding/alighting passengers *(linearization of a typically nonlinear relation)*.
- (A6) Passengers board the first departing train with sufficient remaining capacity (no over-taking of capacity by later demand); leftover passengers wait.
- (A7) All data (running times, minimum headways, demand forecasts) are deterministic over the prediction horizon.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $S = \{1,\dots,N_s\}$ | stations; direction $d \in \{1,2\}$ (1: up, 2: down) |
| $T = \{1,\dots,N_t\}$ | trains (fixed order per direction) |
| $K = \{1,\dots,N_k\}$ | time intervals of length $\Delta$ |
| $U$ | train unit types (e.g., short $s$, long $l$) |
| $F$ | physical train units (rolling stock), with type $u(f)$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,d}$ | minimum running time from station $i$ to $i+1$, direction $d$ |
| $\tau^{\min}, \tau^{\max}$ | min/max dwell time at a station |
| $h^{\min}$ | minimum headway between consecutive trains (arrival/departure) |
| $D^{arr}_{i,k,d}, D^{dep}_{i,k,d}$ | passengers arriving at platform $i$ (direction $d$) wanting to board during interval $k$ |
| $C_u$ | passenger capacity of a unit of type $u$ |
| $c^{op}_u$ | operational cost per interval-km of unit type $u$ |
| $c^{wait}, c^{load}$ | weights for waiting time and crowding |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $H$ | number of time intervals in the prediction horizon (MPC horizon) |

## 4. Decision Variables

**Integer/continuous timetable variables:**
- $a_{i,t,d} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$, direction $d$
- $x_{i,t,d} \ge 0$: departure time of train $t$ at station $i$, direction $d$

**Composition variables (binary):**
- $z_{t,d,u} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ (direction $d$) departs the first station with composition containing type-$u$ units
- $n_{t,d,u} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of type-$u$ units in train $t$
- $y_{i,t,d,f} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $f$ is assigned to train $t$ on the segment departing station $i$, direction $d$

**Passenger variables (continuous $\ge 0$):**
- $w_{i,k,d}$: passengers waiting at station $i$ (dir. $d$) at the start of interval $k$
- $b_{i,k,d}$: passengers boarding trains departing during interval $k$
- $l_{i,k,d}$: passengers left behind by a departing train

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total cost over the prediction horizon:

$$
\min \; J = c^{wait}\sum_{d}\sum_{i}\sum_{k=1}^{H}\Delta\, w_{i,k,d}
\;+\; c^{load}\sum_{d}\sum_{i}\sum_{t}\sum_{k} l_{i,k,d}
\;+\; \sum_{d}\sum_{t}\sum_{u} c^{op}_u\, n_{t,d,u}\, L_d
$$

where $L_d$ is the line length in direction $d$ (operational cost proportional to train composition). *(Weights are assumptions.)*

## 6. Constraints

**Timetable dynamics (running and dwell times):**
$$
x_{i,t,d} \ge a_{i,t,d} \quad \forall i,t,d \tag{1}
$$
$$
x_{i,t,d} - a_{i,t,d} \ge \tau^{\min} + \alpha\,(b_{i,k(t),d} + \lambda\, l_{i,k(t),d}) \quad \forall i,t,d \tag{2}
$$
$$
x_{i,t,d} - a_{i,t,d} \le \tau^{\max} \quad \forall i,t,d \tag{3}
$$
where $k(t)$ is the interval containing departure of train $t$ *(assumption: one train departs per interval per direction; otherwise use a binary train–interval assignment $g_{t,k,d}$ with $\sum_k g_{t,k,d}=1$ and big-M terms)*. $\alpha, \lambda$ are per-passenger dwell-time coefficients.

$$
a_{i+1,t,d} \ge x_{i,t,d} + r_{i,d} \quad \forall i < N_s,\, t,\, d \tag{4}
$$

**Headway (fixed order, single track per direction):**
$$
a_{i+1,t+1,d} - a_{i+1,t,d} \ge h^{\min}, \qquad x_{i,t+1,d} - x_{i,t,d} \ge h^{\min} \quad \forall i,t,d \tag{5}
$$

**Flexible train composition:**
$$
n_{t,d,u} = \sum_{f:\,u(f)=u} y_{N_s,t,d,f} \quad \forall t,d,u \tag{6}
$$
$$
y_{i,t,d,f} \le y_{i-1,t,d,f} \quad \forall i>1,\, t,\, d,\, f \tag{7}
$$
(units may only be decoupled, not added, en route — assumption A4)
$$
\sum_{f} y_{i,t,d,f} \le \bar{n} \quad \forall i,t,d \tag{8}
$$
(maximum train length $\bar{n}$, platform constraint)

**Rolling stock circulation (unit flow conservation at terminals):**
$$
\sum_{t} y_{1,t,1,f} = \sum_{t} y_{N_s,t,2,f} \quad \forall f \tag{9}
$$
$$
\sum_{t} y_{1,t,2,f} = \sum_{t} y_{N_s,t,1,f} \quad \forall f \tag{10}
$$
$$
\sum_{t} y_{1,t,d,f} \le 1 \quad \forall f, d \tag{11}
$$
(each unit used at most once per direction per horizon; turnaround times are embedded in the headway constraints *(simplification)*).

**Passenger flow dynamics (piecewise-constant demand):**
$$
w_{i,k+1,d} = w_{i,k,d} + D^{dep}_{i,k,d} - b_{i,k,d} \quad \forall i,k,d \tag{12}
$$
$$
b_{i,k,d} \le \sum_{t:\, x_{i,t,d}\in[k\Delta,(k+1)\Delta)} \sum_{u} C_u\, n_{t,d,u} - \sum_{k'<k} b_{i,k',d} \tag{13}
$$
(capacity of trains departing in interval $k$ minus passengers already boarded earlier; linearized with train–interval binaries $g_{t,k,d}$ and big-M if needed)
$$
b_{i,k,d} \le w_{i,k,d} \tag{14}
$$
$$
l_{i,k,d} = w_{i,k,d} - b_{i,k,d} \tag{15}
$$

**Terminal conditions / MPC initialization:**
$$
a_{i,t,d},\, x_{i,t,d} \ge a^{meas}_{i,t,d},\, x^{meas}_{i,t,d} \quad \text{(for trains already en route)} \tag{16}
$$
$$
w_{i,1,d} = w^{meas}_{i,d} \tag{17}
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
a,x \ge 0;\quad w,b,l \ge 0;\quad n_{t,d,u}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0};\quad y,z\in\{0,1\}
$$

## 7. Remarks

- Constraints (2) linearize the passenger-dependent dwell time (A5); (6)–(11) couple composition and rolling stock circulation; (12)–(15) propagate piecewise-constant demand with capacity limits.
- In the MPC scheme, the MILP is solved over $H$ intervals each step; integer variables ($n, y, z$) may be fixed by the LSTM predictor, after which the remaining problem is a **linear program** in $(a, x, w, b, l)$ — guaranteeing constraint satisfaction while reducing online computation, as motivated in the paper's learning-based MPC framework.
