Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

Consider a single railway corridor consisting of two stations A and B connected by a double-track segment (track 1 for direction 1 → 2, track 2 for direction 2 → 1). A partial blockage disables track 1 during the time window $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$; during that window trains may only traverse the segment on track 2, i.e., affected trains must **reroute onto the opposite track**, creating bidirectional conflicts.

**Assumptions (made explicit, as some are implicit in the input):**
- (A1) A finite set of pre-generated feasible speed profiles is available for each train and each (train, track, running-time) combination; each profile has a fixed running time and energy consumption (piecewise-linear approximation of train dynamics).
- (A2) Each train may run at most once over the disrupted segment within the planning horizon $[0, T^{max}]$.
- (A3) Dwell times must lie between minimum and maximum dwell times at each station.
- (A4) Safety is enforced by minimum headway times on each track resource (arrival–arrival, departure–departure, arrival–departure headways).
- (A5) If no feasible routing exists within the horizon, a train may be cancelled (with a penalty).
- (A6) All data are deterministic; the disruption time window is known in advance (rolling horizon can be applied otherwise).

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains; $T^{d}_{1}, T^{d}_{2}$: trains of direction 1→2 and 2→1 |
| $P_{it}$ | set of speed profiles for train $i \in T$ on track $t \in \{1,2\}$ |
| $P^k_{it}$ | parameter vector of profile $k$: running time $r^k_{it}$, energy $e^k_{it}$, segment entry speed, etc. |
| $a^{sch}_i, d^{sch}_i$ | scheduled arrival/departure at station B for train $i$ |
| $w^{min}_i, w^{max}_i$ | minimum/maximum dwell time at the upstream station |
| $h^{aa}, h^{dd}, h^{ad}$ | minimum headways (same track) |
| $M$ | big constant (e.g., $T^{max}$) |
| $c^{delay}, c^{energy}, c^{cancel}$ | cost coefficients |
| $L^d$ | unavailability penalty weight for late departure beyond a bound (optional) |

## 3. Decision Variables

- $a_i, d_i \in \mathbb{R}_+$: actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at the stations (departure at A = $d_i$, arrival at B = $a_i$).
- $x_{itk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff train $i$ uses track $t$ with speed profile $k$.
- $y_{it} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff train $i$ runs on track $t$; $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff train $i$ is **cancelled**.
- $\delta^{aa}_{ij}, \delta^{dd}_{ij}, \delta^{ad}_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering binaries for trains $i \neq j$ on the same track ($\delta_{ij}=1$ iff $i$ before $j$).

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay, energy, and cancellation costs:

$$\min \; c^{delay}\sum_{i \in T}\big[(a_i - a^{sch}_i) + (d_i - d^{sch}_i)\big] \;+\; c^{energy}\sum_{i \in T}\sum_{t \in \{1,2\}}\sum_{k \in P_{it}} e^k_{it}\, x_{itk} \;+\; c^{cancel}\sum_{i \in T} z_i$$

(Delays may be split into positive parts via auxiliary variables $a_i, d_i \ge a^{sch}_i$; if early arrivals are allowed with holding, add $d_i \ge a_i$ and dwell constraints below handle the rest.)

## 5. Constraints

**Route and profile selection (exactly one plan or cancellation):**

$$\sum_{t \in \{1,2\}} y_{it} + z_i = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{1}$$

$$y_{it} = \sum_{k \in P_{it}} x_{itk} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; t \in \{1,2\} \tag{2}$$

**Linking timing and speed profiles (coupling TRP ↔ TSMP):** the running time is determined by the chosen profile:

$$a_i \ge d_i + \sum_{t}\sum_{k} r^k_{it}\, x_{itk} - M z_i \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{3}$$

$$a_i \le d_i + \sum_{t}\sum_{k} r^k_{it}\, x_{itk} + M(1 - \sum_{t}\sum_{k} x_{itk}) \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{4}$$

**Disruption (partial blockage):** track 1 is unavailable in $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$; trains entering it in that window must use track 2:

$$d_i \ge T^{start}\, y_{i1} - M(1 - y_{i1}) \qquad \forall i \in T:\; d^{sch}_i < T^{end} \tag{5a}$$

$$d_i + \sum_{k} r^k_{i1} x_{i1k} \le T^{end} + M(1 - y_{i1}) \qquad \forall i \in T \tag{5b}$$

(5a) forbids entering track 1 before the window closes for trains scheduled during the disruption; (5b) forbids still occupying track 1 after the window opens — together trains affected by the window are forced to $y_{i2}=1$ (rerouting).

**Dwell / turnaround times:**

$$w^{min}_i \le d_i - a^{sch}_i \le w^{max}_i \qquad \text{(if station A arrival } a^{sch}_i \text{ given; analogously at B)} \tag{6}$$

**Headway / conflict-free constraints (per track $t$, for all pairs $i,j$ in the same direction and, crucially, opposite directions sharing the rerouted track):**

$$d_i + h^{dd} \le d_j + M(1 - \delta^{dd}_{ij}) + M(2 - y_{it} - y_{jt}) \qquad \forall i<j,\; t \tag{7}$$

$$a_i + h^{aa} \le a_j + M(1 - \delta^{aa}_{ij}) + M(2 - y_{it} - y_{jt}) \qquad \forall i<j,\; t \tag{8}$$

$$d_i + h^{ad} \le a_j + M(1 - \delta^{ad}_{ij}) + M(2 - y_{it} - y_{jt}) \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; t \tag{9}$$

**Ordering consistency (mutual exclusivity):**

$$\delta^{aa}_{ij} + \delta^{aa}_{ji} = 1, \quad \delta^{dd}_{ij} + \delta^{dd}_{ji} = 1 \qquad \forall i<j,\; t \tag{10}$$

$$\delta^{dd}_{ij} \le \delta^{aa}_{ij} \qquad \forall i<j \tag{11}$$

(FIFO consistency: if $i$ departs before $j$, $i$ arrives before $j$ — no overtaking on a single-track segment.)

**Cancellation relaxation:** a cancelled train occupies no resource and incurs no timing:

$$a_i \le T^{max} z_i, \quad d_i \le T^{max} z_i, \quad y_{it} \le 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in T, t \tag{12}$$

**Variable bounds:**

$$0 \le a_i, d_i \le T^{max}; \quad x_{itk}, y_{it}, z_i, \delta^{\cdot}_{ij} \in \{0,1\} \tag{13}$$

## 6. Remarks

- Constraints (3)–(4) are the core **integration** mechanism: they force the timetable times to be *exactly* consistent with the chosen speed profile, guaranteeing that the rescheduled timetable is executable at the train-control level.
- Constraints (5)–(9) jointly handle the **rerouting strategy** and bidirectional conflicts on the shared opposite track during the disruption window.
- The model is linear: nonlinearity of train dynamics is absorbed by the discrete profile sets $P_{it}$ (Assumption A1), in line with the plan-based decomposition mentioned in the text (profile refinement = finer interval plans, with equivalence to the continuous MILP as granularity → 0).

**Missing-data note:** headway values, profile generation details, and cost coefficients were not specified in the input and are treated as parameters to be calibrated from real-world instances (Section 6 of the source text).

**Best model: Model 2** — it is the most complete and internally consistent formulation: it cleanly separates retiming, reordering, rerouting, and speed-profile selection, handles the disruption blockage with explicit early/late indicator binaries, and correctly deactivates headway constraints when trains occupy different tracks (enabling bidirectional sharing during rerouting). Below is the final model.

# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, $i \in I$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, ordered $s = 1, \dots, |S|$ along the corridor |
| $L$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, $l = 1, \dots, |S|-1$; segment $l$ connects stations $l$ and $l+1$ |
| $K = \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ | Tracks per segment (double track, bidirectional) |
| $P$ | Set of speed profiles, $p \in P$ |
| $P_{il}$ | Feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $[T^D_1, T^D_2]$ | Disruption time window |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $w_i$ | Delay weight of train $i$ |
| $c_p$ | Energy consumption of profile $p$ |
| $\tau_p$ | Running time of profile $p$ |
| $a^{0}_i$, $d^{0}_i$ | Original scheduled arrival/departure at the final station |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{run}$ | Minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, running (same track) |
| $d^{min}_s$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $M$ | Big-M constant |
| $\alpha$ | Weight converting energy to time-equivalent cost |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{is} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$
- $\Delta_i \ge 0$: total delay of train $i$ at destination

**Binary:**
- $x_{ilp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $l$
- $y_{ilk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $l$ on track $k$ (1 = original track, 0 = opposite track)
- $z^{arr}_{ijls}, z^{dep}_{ijls} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ arrives/departs at station $s$ before train $j$
- $z^{run}_{ijlk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ enters segment $l$ on track $k$ before train $j$
- $\delta^{early}_{il}, \delta^{late}_{il} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ exits segment $l$ before / enters after the disruption window

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in I} w_i \Delta_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{l \in L} \sum_{p \in P_{il}} c_p \, x_{ilp}
\tag{1}
$$

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable feasibility

Dwell times:
$$
d_{is} - a_{is} \ge d^{min}_s \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S \tag{2}
$$

Running time consistent with chosen speed profile:
$$
a_{i,l+1} - d_{il} \ge \sum_{p \in P_{il}} \tau_p \, x_{ilp} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; l \in L \tag{3}
$$

Profile uniqueness:
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{il}} x_{ilp} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in I,\; l \in L \tag{4}
$$

Delay definition:
$$
\Delta_i \ge a_{i,|S|} - a^{0}_i \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{5}
$$

### 5.2 Rerouting logic

Track choice per train–segment (exactly one track):
$$
y_{il,\text{up}} + y_{il,\text{down}} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in I,\; l \in L \tag{6}
$$

Rerouting only allowed during the disruption window. Let $k^0_{il}$ be the original track of train $i$ on segment $l$ and $\bar{k}$ the opposite:
$$
d_{il} \ge T^D_2 - M(1-\delta^{late}_{il}), \qquad
a_{i,l+1} \le T^D_1 + M(1-\delta^{early}_{il}), \qquad
y_{il\bar{k}} \le \delta^{late}_{il} + \delta^{early}_{il} \quad \forall i,l \tag{7}
$$

### 5.3 Conflict-free occupancy (headways)

For each segment $l$, track $k$, and train pair $i<j$, with entry time $e_{ilk} = d_{il}$ and exit time $q_{ilk} = a_{i,l+1}$:

Running (entry) headway on same track:
$$
e_{jlk} - e_{ilk} \ge h^{run} - M(2 - y_{ilk} - y_{jlk}) - M(1 - z^{run}_{ijlk}) \tag{8a}
$$
$$
e_{ilk} - e_{jlk} \ge h^{run} - M(2 - y_{ilk} - y_{jlk}) - M\, z^{run}_{ijlk} \tag{8b}
$$

Arrival headway at the downstream station:
$$
q_{jlk} - q_{ilk} \ge h^{arr} - M(2 - y_{ilk} - y_{jlk}) - M(1 - z^{arr}_{ijl,l+1}) \tag{9a}
$$
$$
q_{ilk} - q_{jlk} \ge h^{arr} - M(2 - y_{ilk} - y_{jlk}) - M\, z^{arr}_{ijl,l+1} \tag{9b}
$$

Departure headway at the upstream station:
$$
d_{jls} - d_{ils} \ge h^{dep} - M(2 - y_{ilk} - y_{jlk}) - M(1 - z^{dep}_{ijls}), \quad s = l \tag{10a}
$$
$$
d_{ils} - d_{jls} \ge h^{dep} - M(2 - y_{ilk} - y_{jlk}) - M\, z^{dep}_{ijls} \tag{10b}
$$

Constraints (8)–(10) are active only when both trains occupy the same track $k$ (the $M(2-y-y)$ terms deactivate them otherwise, allowing bidirectional sharing of a track by opposite-direction trains).

### 5.4 Disruption blockage

No train may occupy the blocked track $k^B$ of segment $l^B$ during $[T^D_1, T^D_2]$, unless rerouted to the opposite track:
$$
a_{i,l^B+1} \le T^D_1 + M\left(1 - y_{il^B k^B}\right) + M\,\delta^{early}_{il^B} \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{11a}
$$
$$
d_{il^B} \ge T^D_2 - M\left(1 - y_{il^B k^B}\right) - M\,\delta^{late}_{il^B} \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{11b}
$$

If train $i$ stays on the blocked track ($y_{il^B k^B}=1$), it must fully exit the segment before $T^D_1$ ($\delta^{early}=1$) or enter after $T^D_2$ ($\delta^{late}=1$). If rerouted ($y=0$), (11) is relaxed and the train may traverse the opposite track during the window.

### 5.5 Speed-profile–timetable coupling

The running time in (3) couples profiles to arrivals/departures; energy accounting is tied to profile choice via the objective (1). Optionally, an upper bound on running time per profile class:
$$
a_{i,l+1} - d_{il} \le \sum_{p \in P_{il}} \tau^{max}_p \, x_{ilp} \qquad \forall i, l \tag{12}
$$

### 5.6 Variable domains

$$
a_{is}, d_{is}, \Delta_i \ge 0; \quad x_{ilp}, y_{ilk}, z^{arr}_{ijls}, z^{dep}_{ijls}, z^{run}_{ijlk}, \delta^{early}_{il}, \delta^{late}_{il} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Model Explanation

- **Retiming** is captured by continuous $a_{is}, d_{is}$, constrained by dwell (2), running (3), and headway (8)–(10) constraints.
- **Reordering** is captured by the binary sequencing variables $z$, which enforce pairwise conflict-free ordering on each track via big-M disjunctions.
- **Rerouting** is modeled by $y_{ilk}$: during the disruption window, trains on the blocked segment may switch to the opposite track (7), enabling bidirectional operation; headway constraints remain active on whichever track is used.
- **Blockage** (11) forbids occupancy of the blocked track during $[T^D_1, T^D_2]$ unless the train is rerouted.
- **Speed management** selects one discrete profile per train–segment (4); each profile fixes the running time $\tau_p$ and energy $c_p$, coupling rescheduling and speed optimization through (3) and the objective.
- **Objective (1)** balances total weighted delay against total energy consumption, with weight $\alpha$ as the trade-off parameter.

**Assumptions (marked as such):** single blocked segment $l^B$ with one disruption window; precomputed discrete speed profiles per train–segment with fixed running time and energy; fixed train directions with rerouting only on the blocked segment; constant minimum dwell times; time treated continuously (the discretized time-indexed variant can be obtained by discretizing $a, d$).

Text:
# MILP for Real-Time Railway Traffic Management (CDR) under DTG / ETCS L2 Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP-style model. All assumptions not stated in the input are marked **(A)**.

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **(A1)** The network is a set of microscopic track sections *s ∈ S*, partitioned into switch sections *S_sw* and plain (line/station) sections *S_pl = S \ S_sw*. Each section can be occupied by at most one train at a time (TTD section detection).
- **(A2)** Each train *f ∈ F* follows a fixed route through sections *S_f* in a fixed order (local rerouting is neglected; retiming and reordering are decided).
- **(A3)** Each train *f* may run one of a finite set of speed-profile options *p ∈ P_f* between consecutive sections (e.g., coasting vs. full service braking). Each option *p* induces a section running time *r_{f,s,p}* and a **speed- and train-dependent braking/approach time** *b_{f,s,p}* before the End of Authority (EoA) at the next occupied section.
- **(A4)** The blocking time of train *f* on section *s* under profile *p* is
  β_{f,s,p} = σ_{f,s} (setup/switching) + b_{f,s,p} (braking approach, speed-dependent) + r_{f,s,p} (running) + c_{f,s} (clearing).
- **(A5)** A train's EoA ends at the boundary of the next section; the brake indication point (IP) lies anywhere upstream, at distance equal to the absolute braking distance from the EoA — captured by *b_{f,s,p}*.
- **(A6)** Scheduled (undisturbed) entry times *t̂_{f,s}* and scheduled exit/arrival times are known; delays are measured against them.
- **(A7)** A sufficiently large constant *M* and a finite horizon *T* are given.

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *F* | trains; *S* sections; *S_f ⊆ S* sections on route of *f* (ordered) |
| *P_f* | speed-profile options of train *f* |
| *t̂_{f,s}* | scheduled entry time of *f* into *s* |
| *β_{f,s,p}* | blocking time (A4) |
| *d^{min}_{f,s}* | minimum dwell time at station section *s* |
| *τ_s* | extra interlocking/release time for switch section *s* |
| *t^{rel}_f* | release time of train *f* (actual departure from first section) |
| *M, T* | big-M constant, time horizon |

---

## 3. Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *t_{f,s} ∈ [t̂_{f,s}, T]* | actual entry time of train *f* into section *s* |
| *d_f ≥ 0* | final arrival delay of train *f* at destination |
| *x_{f,p} ∈ {0,1}* | 1 if train *f* runs speed-profile option *p* |
| *y_{f,g,s} ∈ {0,1}* | 1 if train *f* enters section *s* before train *g* (for f<g on common sections) |

---

## 4. Objective

Minimise total train delay:

**min**  Z = Σ_{f∈F} d_f

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Profile selection** — exactly one speed profile per train:

  Σ_{p∈P_f} x_{f,p} = 1   ∀ f ∈ F

**(C2) Linearised (profile-dependent) blocking time.** Define auxiliary *B_{f,s} ≥ 0* with:

  B_{f,s} = Σ_{p∈P_f} β_{f,s,p} · x_{f,p}   ∀ f, s ∈ S_f

(Exact equality is linear since β is a constant coefficient.)

**(C3) Release time / initial condition:**

  t_{f,s₁(f)} ≥ t^{rel}_f   ∀ f, s₁(f) = first section of route

**(C4) Running-time precedence within a train's route**, including minimum dwell:

  t_{f,s'} ≥ t_{f,s} + B_{f,s} + d^{min}_{f,s}   ∀ f, ∀ consecutive (s, s') ∈ S_f

Note: using the full blocking time *B_{f,s}* between consecutive sections of the same train enforces that the train's own braking approach and clearing are respected.

**(C5) Mutual exclusion on each section (reordering):** for every pair f < g with s ∈ S_f ∩ S_g:

  t_{g,s} ≥ t_{f,s} + B_{f,s} − M(1 − y_{f,g,s})
  t_{f,s} ≥ t_{g,s} + B_{g,s} − M·y_{f,g,s}

These disjunctive constraints guarantee at most one train occupies section *s* at a time, with the **speed-dependent** blocking time of the preceding train (DTG separation).

**(C6) Consistent ordering across consecutive sections** (no overtaking within a section sequence unless physically possible — **(A2)**):

  y_{f,g,s'} ≤ y_{f,g,s} + (1 − z_{f,g,s'})   for consecutive sections, where z indicates shared route membership; equivalently, if both trains traverse s and s' consecutively:

  y_{f,g,s'} = y_{f,g,s}   ∀ f<g, s,s' consecutive in both routes

**(C7) Switch sections — additional interlocking time** (route setting and locking before entry):

  t_{f,s} ≥ t_{f,s⁻} + τ_s   ∀ f, s ∈ S_sw, s⁻ predecessor of s in S_f

**(C8) Switch sections — no conflicting moves:** if two trains' routes through switch section *s* conflict (opposing directions, **(A2)** provides conflict set *C_s* of incompatible train pairs):

  t_{g,s} ≥ t_{f,s} + B_{f,s} + τ_s − M(1 − y_{f,g,s})   ∀ (f,g) ∈ C_s, f<g
  t_{f,s} ≥ t_{g,s} + B_{g,s} + τ_s − M·y_{f,g,s}   ∀ (f,g) ∈ C_s

**(C9) Delay definition** (against scheduled arrival at destination section s*_f*):

  d_f ≥ t_{f,s*_f} − t̂_{f,s*_f}   ∀ f
  d_f ≥ 0   ∀ f

**(C10) Variable domains:**

  t_{f,s} ∈ [t̂_{f,s}, T];  d_f ∈ ℝ₊;  x_{f,p} ∈ {0,1};  y_{f,g,s} ∈ {0,1}

---

## 6. Remarks

- **DTG-specific feature:** the braking-approach term *b_{f,s,p}* inside β_{f,s,p} makes separation distances speed- and train-dependent, replacing the fixed number of blocks in conventional fixed-block CDR models. Slower profiles ⇒ shorter braking distances ⇒ shorter blocking times, which the model can exploit when retiming.
- **Speed-profile options** (C1)–(C2) allow the rescheduling to trade running time against blocking time, a key degree of freedom under continuous braking-curve supervision.
- With *P_f* a singleton and constant β, the model reduces to the original fixed-block RECIFE-MILP.
- The model is a MILP: linear objective, continuous timing variables, binary profile-selection and ordering variables, big-M disjunctions.

Text:
# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

- **(A1)** A double-track high-speed railway line with stations $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ and segments between consecutive stations. Each segment has one track per direction.
- **(A2)** A partial blockage affects a set of segments $\mathcal{D} \subset$ segments during time window $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$. In $\mathcal{D}$, only one direction may be used at a time; trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-track operation) during the disruption window.
- **(A3)** Train set $\mathcal{K}$; each train $k$ has a fixed stopping pattern, minimum dwell times, minimum/maximum running times per segment, and a scheduled timetable to be recovered.
- **(A4)** Speed profiles are discretized: for each train $k$ and segment $(i,i+1)$, a finite set of pre-computed, dynamically feasible speed profiles $P_{k,i}$ is available (computed offline via optimal control / pseudospectral methods). Each profile $p \in P_{k,i}$ has a fixed running time $r_{k,i}^{p}$ and energy consumption $e_{k,i}^{p}$. *(This discretization keeps the model linear.)*
- **(A5)** Time is discretized into intervals; headway and blocking constraints are enforced via minimum headway times between trains on the same track resource.
- **(A6)** Cancellation of trains is allowed at a large penalty cost.
- **(A7)** Train acceleration/deceleration dynamics are embedded in the pre-computed profiles; hence no nonlinear dynamics appear in the MILP.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{K}$ | set of trains |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | set of stations, segments $(i,i+1)$ for $i \in \{1,\dots,n-1\}$ |
| $\mathcal{D}$ | disrupted segments, with disruption window $[T^{s}, T^{e}]$ |
| $P_{k,i}$ | feasible speed profiles of train $k$ on segment $(i,i+1)$ |
| $r_{k,i}^{p}, e_{k,i}^{p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $\underline{d}_i^k, \bar{d}_i^k$ | min/max dwell time of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway time (same track, same or opposite direction) |
| $a_i^{k,0}, d_i^{k,0}$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $w_k$ | delay weight of train $k$ |
| $M$ | big constant (horizon length) |
| $C$ | cancellation cost |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable variables:**
- $a_i^k \ge 0$: arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$
- $d_i^k \ge 0$: departure time of train $k$ from station $i$

**Routing / speed profile variables:**
- $x_{k,i}^{p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $(i,i+1)$
- $y_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $(i,i+1)$ (only defined for $i$ with segment in or adjacent to $\mathcal{D}$)

**Ordering variables (conflict resolution):**
- $z_{k\ell,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ enters segment $(i,i+1)$ before train $\ell$ (for all pairs sharing a track resource, same or opposite direction)

**Cancellation:**
- $c_k \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ is cancelled

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay plus energy consumption plus cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} w_k \left[ (a_{\sigma(k)}^k - a_{\sigma(k)}^{k,0}) + (d_{\tau(k)}^k - d_{\tau(k)}^{k,0}) \right]}_{\text{terminal delays}}
+ \underbrace{\lambda \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \sum_{i} \sum_{p \in P_{k,i}} e_{k,i}^{p}\, x_{k,i}^{p}}_{\text{energy}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} C\, c_k}_{\text{cancellations}}
$$

where $\sigma(k), \tau(k)$ are the terminal stations of train $k$, and $\lambda$ converts energy into time-equivalent cost. *(Assumption A8: delays measured at terminus only; linearization of $\max\{0,\cdot\}$ shown below.)*

Linearize delays: introduce $D_k \ge 0$ with

$$
D_k \ge a_{\sigma(k)}^k - a_{\sigma(k)}^{k,0}, \qquad D_k \ge d_{\tau(k)}^k - d_{\tau(k)}^{k,0}, \qquad D_k \ge 0
$$

and use $\sum_k w_k D_k$ in the objective.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per train–segment):**
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{k,i}} x_{k,i}^{p} = 1 - c_k \qquad \forall k \in \mathcal{K},\ \forall i
$$

**(C2) Running time consistency (links timetable and speed profiles):**
$$
d_{i+1}^{k} - d_i^{k} \ge \sum_{p \in P_{k,i}} r_{k,i}^{p}\, x_{k,i}^{p} + \underline{d}_{i+1}^{k} \qquad \forall k, i
$$
$$
d_{i+1}^{k} - d_i^{k} \le \sum_{p \in P_{k,i}} r_{k,i}^{p}\, x_{k,i}^{p} + \bar{d}_{i+1}^{k} \qquad \forall k, i
$$

**(C3) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\underline{d}_i^k \le d_i^k - a_i^k \le \bar{d}_i^k \qquad \forall k, i \notin \{\sigma(k), \tau(k)\}
$$

**(C4) Rerouting feasibility — rerouting only allowed during the disruption window and only on affected segments:**
$$
y_{k,i} = 0 \quad \forall k,\ \forall i \notin \mathcal{D}\text{-related segments}
$$
If train $k$ enters disrupted segment $(i,i+1)$ at time $t$ with rerouting, then $t \in [T^s, T^e]$:
$$
d_i^k \ge T^s \cdot y_{k,i} - M(1 - y_{k,i}), \qquad d_i^k \le T^e + M(1 - y_{k,i}) \qquad \forall k,\ i \in \mathcal{D}
$$

*(Assumption A9: rerouted profiles are included in $P_{k,i}$ with possibly different $r, e$; if a train is not rerouted, it must wait until the disruption ends:)*
$$
d_i^k \ge T^e - M\, y_{k,i} \qquad \forall k,\ i \in \mathcal{D} \text{ with } d_i^k < T^e
$$

**(C5) Headway / conflict-free constraints, same direction on same track:**
For trains $k, \ell$ and segment $i$ (not rerouted, i.e., using their own direction track):
$$
d_{i+1}^{\ell} \ge d_i^{k} + h - M(1 - z_{k\ell,i}) - M\, y_{k,i} - M\, y_{\ell,i}
$$
$$
d_{i+1}^{k} \ge d_i^{\ell} + h - M\, z_{k\ell,i} - M\, y_{k,i} - M\, y_{\ell,i}
$$

**(C6) Bidirectional conflict constraints on the shared (opposite) track in disrupted segments:**
For trains $k, \ell$ traveling in **opposite** directions, both potentially rerouted onto the same track of segment $i$:
$$
d_{i+1}^{\ell} \ge d_i^{k} + h - M(1 - z_{k\ell,i}) - M(1 - y_{k,i}) - M(1 - y_{\ell,i})
$$
$$
d_{i+1}^{k} \ge d_i^{\ell} + h - M\, z_{k\ell,i} - M(1 - y_{k,i}) - M(1 - y_{\ell,i})
$$
These constraints ensure only one train occupies the single available track at a time, in either direction.

**(C7) Disruption-window capacity (single-track occupancy during blockage):** For any two trains $k,\ell$ (any directions) entering disrupted segment $i$ during $[T^s,T^e]$:
$$
d_{i+1}^{\ell} \ge d_i^k + h - M(1 - z_{k\ell,i}) - M\,\delta_{k,i} - M\,\delta_{\ell,i}
$$
where $\delta_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates train $k$ occupies segment $i$ within the disruption window (linearized from $d_i^k, d_{i+1}^k$ vs. $T^s, T^e$ with standard big-$M$ constraints).

**(C8) Time horizon:**
$$
0 \le a_i^k \le d_i^k \le M \qquad \forall k, i
$$

**(C9) Cancellation propagation:** if a train is cancelled, all its times are free / it occupies no resources:
$$
a_i^k \le M\, c_k, \quad d_i^k \le M\, c_k \qquad \forall k, i
$$

**(C10) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{k,i}^{p},\ y_{k,i},\ z_{k\ell,i},\ c_k,\ \delta_{k,i} \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_i^k, d_i^k, D_k \ge 0
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Coupling:** Constraints (C2) are the core integration: the chosen speed profile determines the feasible running time, and the rescheduled departure times restrict which profiles are admissible — timetable and speed profiles are decided simultaneously.
- **Rerouting:** Variables $y_{k,i}$ and constraints (C4)–(C7) implement local single-track operation in the disrupted area, with (C6) resolving bidirectional conflicts on the shared track.
- **Equivalence note:** As stated in the paper, with a sufficiently fine discretization of speed-profile intervals (A4), this MILP exactly represents the continuous integrated problem; the decomposition into a train-interaction IP plus single-train plans (train plan selection) is obtained by relaxing (C1)–(C2) into pre-enumerated per-train plans $(\{x_{k,i}^p\}, \{a_i^k, d_i^k\})$ and keeping only the ordering constraints (C5)–(C7) in the IP.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

## Sets and Parameters
- Trains *i* ∈ I, with direction dir(i) ∈ {up, down}
- Stations *s* ∈ S; segments *k* between consecutive stations
- Time instants *t* ∈ T (discretized horizon)
- Speed profiles (i, k, r, p): route r ∈ {0 = normal track, 1 = opposite track (reroute)}, profile p, with running time RT(i,k,r,p) and energy E(i,k,r,p)
- Disrupted segment k*, direction dir*, blocked during window [τ₁, τ₂]
- Minimum dwell δ(i,s), minimum headway h, platform capacity C(s), big-M, weights w_d, w_e, w_c; scheduled terminal arrival A_i

## Variables
- a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} ≥ 0: arrival / departure times
- x_{i,k,r,p} ∈ {0,1}: selection of route r and speed profile p on segment k
- y_{i,k,t} ∈ {0,1}: train i occupies segment k at time t
- z_i ∈ {0,1}: cancellation of train i
- o_{ij,k} ∈ {0,1}: ordering of same-direction trains i, j on segment k
- u_{i,k,1} ∈ {0,1}: rerouting of train i to opposite track on segment k

## Objective
Minimize

  min  w_d · Σ_i (a_{i,S_end} − A_i)  +  w_e · Σ_{i,k,r,p} E(i,k,r,p) · x_{i,k,r,p}  +  w_c · Σ_i z_i

(total weighted terminal delay + energy consumption of chosen speed profiles + cancellation penalties).

## Constraints

**(1) Dwell time:**
d_{i,s} ≥ a_{i,s} + δ(i,s) − M·z_i  ∀i, intermediate s

**(2) Running-time consistency (couples timetable and speed profile):**
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + Σ_{r,p} RT(i,k,r,p)·x_{i,k,r,p} − M·z_i  ∀i, s→s+1
d_{i,s₀} ≥ d⁰_i (earliest departure)

**(3) Exactly one route/profile per segment (or cancellation):**
Σ_{r,p} x_{i,k,r,p} + z_i = 1  ∀i, k

**(4) Occupancy linking (big-M indicator):**
y_{i,k,t} ≥ x_{i,k,r,p} − (d_{i,s} − t)/M − (t − d_{i,s} − RT)/M  ∀i,k,t,(r,p)
y_{i,k,t} ≤ Σ_{r,p} x_{i,k,r,p}  ∀i,k,t

**(5) Headway / conflict-free, same direction:**
y_{i,k,t} + y_{j,k,t} ≤ 1 + Σ_{t'<t} y_{i,k,t'} + Σ_{t'<t} y_{j,k,t'} − 1  ∀ ordered pairs (i,j), k, t
plus ordering consistency: d_{j,s₀} ≥ a_{i,s₀} − M(1 − o_{ij,k}) and symmetric counterpart.

**(6) Bidirectional conflict on rerouted (single-track) segment:**
y_{i,k,t} + y_{j,k,t} ≤ 1  ∀ i, j with dir(i) ≠ dir(j) both traversing k, ∀t

**(7) Disruption:**
y_{i,k*,t} ≤ u_{i,k*,1}  ∀i with dir(i) = dir*, ∀t ∈ [τ₁, τ₂]
x_{i,k*,0,p} ≤ 1 − (Σ_{t∈[τ₁,τ₂]} y_{i,k*,t})/M  (normal-route profiles forbidden while blocked)

**(8) Rerouting only within disruption window:**
u_{i,k,1} ≤ Σ_{t∈[τ₁,τ₂]} y_{i,k,t}

**(9) Horizon bounds:** a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} ≤ |T|

**(10) Station platform capacity:** Σ_i q_{i,s,t} ≤ C(s) ∀s,t, where q_{i,s,t} ∈ {0,1} indicates train i dwelling at station s at time t (linearized occupancy between a_{i,s} and d_{i,s}).

**(11) Cancellation:** y_{i,k,t} ≤ 1 − z_i ∀i,k,t; timetable constraints relaxed via −M·z_i terms.

**(12) Profile feasibility:** x_{i,k,r,p} = 0 if RT(i,k,r,p) ∉ [RT_min, RT_max].

## Assumptions (marked)
- Double-track line with one disrupted segment/direction; rerouting to the opposite track is possible only there and only during [τ₁, τ₂].
- Speed profiles are precomputed feasible (energy-optimal) trajectories per (segment, route, running-time class); the MILP selects among them, keeping the model linear.
- Delay measured at the terminal station; intermediate delays could be added analogously.
- Platform capacity uses explicit occupancy binaries q_{i,s,t} for exactness (the code sketch uses a conservative linear proxy).
- Big-M exceeds the planning horizon; headway enforced via cumulative occupancy and ordering binaries.

This is exactly the integrated TRSMP: timetable variables (a, d), routing/ordering (x, u, o), and speed-profile selection are co-optimized, with constraint (2) providing the timetable–dynamics coupling and constraints (5)–(7) guaranteeing conflict-free bidirectional operation through the disruption area.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Following the described paper, we formulate a complete MILP that decomposes rtRTMP into **rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling**, using **pair-wise delay variables** (train i waits for train j) and optionally propagating delays. The model is inspired by Pellegrini et al. (2014) and the pair-wise reformulation described in the contribution.

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** Macroscopic infrastructure: the network is a set of *routes* (paths through stations/block sections); signals and track circuits are aggregated.
- **(A2)** Each train has a set of feasible routes; exactly one must be selected.
- **(A3)** Minimum running/headway times per route are known constants.
- **(A4)** Primary (initial) delays are known at the time of dispatching; the horizon is finite.
- **(A5)** Trains cannot be cancelled; scheduled stops are fixed.
- **(A6)** Safety is enforced via minimum headway between train occupancies of overlapping routes.
- **(A7)** If delay propagation is considered (global-optimum variant), a train's exit delay includes waiting for other trains (pair-wise terms).

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $i, j$ |
| $R_i$ | set of feasible routes for train $i$, index $r$ |
| $O$ | set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ sharing at least one resource, $i \neq j$ |
| $K$ | set of shared resources (block sections / station areas) |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_i^{init}$ | primary delay of train $i$ [s] |
| $t_i^{sch}$ | scheduled exit time of train $i$ |
| $\rho_{ir}$ | minimum running time of train $i$ on route $r$ |
| $h_{ij}^k$ | minimum headway between trains $i,j$ on resource $k$ |
| $w_{ij}^{max}$ | upper bound on waiting of $i$ for $j$ (horizon-based) |
| $M$ | big-M (horizon length) |
| $\sigma_{ij}$ | = 1 if train $i$ may be reordered before $j$ (0 if fixed order) |

## 4. Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{ir} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | route selection: 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ |
| $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | ordering: 1 if train $i$ passes resource before train $j$ |
| $w_{ij} \ge 0$ | continuous | pair-wise delay: time train $i$ waits for train $j$ |
| $d_i \ge 0$ | continuous | total (secondary) delay of train $i$ |
| $a_i \ge 0$ | continuous | actual exit time of train $i$ |

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} d_i
$$

Optionally with energy term (trade-off, cf. Rao et al. 2013):

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} d_i + \lambda \sum_{i \in T} E_i, \quad E_i = e_i^{run} \cdot \text{(running time)} + e_i^{stop}\cdot(\text{number of speed changes}),
$$

*(assumption A8: linear energy approximation with coefficient $\lambda$; omitted below for clarity).*

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Route selection — exactly one route per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{ir} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C2) Actual exit time (scheduled + primary + secondary delay):**
$$
a_i = t_i^{sch} + d_i^{init} + d_i \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C3) Delay propagation via pair-wise waits (global-optimum variant):**
$$
d_i \ge \sum_{j:\,(j,i)\in O} w_{ij} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$
*(In the sub-optimal pair-wise model, this is replaced by $d_i = \max_j w_{ij}$ via $d_i \ge w_{ij}\ \forall j$, i.e., propagation is neglected — only the largest single wait counts.)*

**(C4) Pair-wise wait activation (big-M):**
$$
w_{ij} \le M \cdot y_{ji} \qquad \forall (i,j) \in O
$$
i.e., $i$ can wait for $j$ only if $j$ goes first.

**(C5) Ordering consistency — anti-symmetry:**
$$
y_{ij} + y_{ji} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j) \in O
$$

**(C6) Fixed order where reordering is not allowed:**
$$
y_{ij} = \sigma_{ij} \qquad \forall (i,j) \in O \text{ with fixed order}
$$

**(C7) Headway / sequencing constraint per shared resource $k$:**

If $i$ precedes $j$ on resource $k$:
$$
a_i + h_{ij}^k \le a_j + M(1 - y_{ij}^k)
$$
$$
a_j + h_{ji}^k \le a_i + M \, y_{ij}^k
$$
where $y_{ij}^k \le \sum_{r \in R_i:\, k \in r} x_{ir}$, $y_{ij}^k \le \sum_{r \in R_j:\, k \in r} x_{jr}$ (resource used only if the corresponding route is chosen).

**(C8) Route-dependent running time (linearization):**
$$
a_i \ge a_i^{entry} + \sum_{r \in R_i} \rho_{ir} x_{ir} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C9) Wait bound:**
$$
w_{ij} \le w_{ij}^{max} \qquad \forall (i,j) \in O
$$

**(C10) Safety-relevant overlaps (margins behind stop signals, cf. Lindenmaier et al. 2022):** for overlapping margin resources, additional headway constraints of form (C7) apply with enlarged $h$.

**(C11) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{ir} \in \{0,1\},\quad y_{ij} \in \{0,1\},\quad w_{ij}, d_i, a_i \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Decomposition (multi-stage framework)

**Stage 1 (Sub-optimal, fast):** Solve the MILP with (C1)–(C7), (C9)–(C11) and the *non-propagating* version of (C3) ($d_i \ge w_{ij}\ \forall j$). Output: fixed routes $x^*$ and optional ordering $y^*$.

**Stage 2 (Rescheduling):** With $x = x^*$ (and optionally $y = y^*$) fixed, solve the full model including propagating (C3) to obtain exact delays $d_i^*$.

**Optimality condition (Section 3.2 of the paper):** Stage 1 is globally optimal iff no train's delay is caused by the *sum* of multiple waits, i.e., $\max_j w_{ij} = \sum_j w_{ij}$ for all $i$ at the optimum; otherwise the extended model with (C3) guarantees the global optimum.

---

## 8. Notes on complexity

- Binary variables: $\sum_i |R_i|$ (routing) + $2|O|$ (ordering).
- The pair-wise reformulation replaces standard absolute delay variables with waiting variables, reducing equivalent integer combinations (cf. Pellegrini et al., 2019), which improves runtime especially in complex scenarios.

# TRSMP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP under Partial Segment Blockage

## Assumptions

- **A1.** Each train $i \in \mathcal{T}$ has a fixed route: an ordered set of segments $\mathcal{K}_i$, where segment $k$ connects stations $s(k) \to s'(k)$.
- **A2.** For each train $i$ and segment $k$, a set of precomputed speed profiles $\mathcal{P}_{ik}$ is given, each with running time $r^p_{ik}$ and energy $e^p_{ik}$; exactly one profile is used (unless the train is cancelled).
- **A3.** A cancelled train ($z_i = 1$) consumes no resources; all its constraints are relaxed via big-M terms.
- **A4.** Delays are measured at reference stations and bounded by $\Delta^{\max}$.
- **A5.** Tight big-M: $M_{ik} = \Delta^{\max} + \max_{p,p'}|r^p_{ik} - r^{p'}_{ik}|$ for propagation; a horizon-based $M$ elsewhere.
- **A6.** The disruption window $[\tau_1, \tau_2]$ and the blocked track $b(k)$ for each $k \in B$ are known and fixed; one track per blocked segment remains available (rerouting target).
- **A7.** Station capacity is enforced pairwise (no two trains dwell simultaneously at a station).

## Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}, \mathcal{K}_i, \mathcal{P}_{ik}$ | trains; segments of train $i$; speed profiles of $(i,k)$ |
| $H^{DD}, H^{AA}, H^{AD}$ | departure–departure, arrival–arrival, arrival–departure headways |
| $r^p_{ik}, e^p_{ik}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ on $(i,k)$ |
| $w_{ik}$ | minimum dwell of train $i$ at $s'(k)$ |
| $\beta_i, c_i, \alpha$ | delay weight, cancellation penalty, energy weight |
| $a^0_{ik}, d^0_{ik}$ | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $\Delta^{\max}, [\tau_1,\tau_2]$ | max delay; disruption window |

## Variables

- $a_{ik}, d_{ik} \ge 0$: actual arrival at $s'(k)$ / departure from $s(k)$
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: cancellation; $u_{ip} \in \{0,1\}$: profile selection
- $x_{ik} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses the rerouted (opposite) track on segment $k$
- $g_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 iff trains $i,j$ use the **same track** on segment $k$
- $y_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$ ($i \ne j$): 1 if $i$ precedes $j$ on segment $k$
- $\delta_i \ge 0$: counted delay of train $i$; $\delta^+_i, \delta^-_i \ge 0$: auxiliaries

## Objective

$$\min \; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \beta_i \delta_i \;+\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} c_i z_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_i} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{ik}} e^p_{ik}\, u_{ip}$$

## Constraints

**(1) Propagation (retiming + speed-profile coupling):**
$$a_{i,s'(k)} \ge d_{i,s(k)} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{ik}} r^p_{ik} u_{ip} - M_{ik} z_i \qquad \forall i,\, k \in \mathcal{K}_i \tag{1}$$

**(2) Delay linearization** (at reference station $\bar{k}(i)$; zero for cancelled trains):
$$\delta_i \ge a_{i,\bar{k}(i)} - a^0_{i,\bar{k}(i)} - \Delta^{\max} z_i \tag{2a}$$
$$\delta_i \ge \delta^+_i - \delta^-_i, \qquad \delta_i \le \delta^+_i + \delta^-_i \tag{2b}$$
$$\delta^+_i \ge a_{i,\bar{k}(i)} - a^0_{i,\bar{k}(i)}, \qquad \delta^-_i \ge a^0_{i,\bar{k}(i)} - a_{i,\bar{k}(i)} \tag{2c}$$

**(3) Dwell times:**
$$d_{i,k+1} \ge a_{i,k} + w_{ik} - M z_i, \qquad d_{i,k+1} \le a_{i,k} + w_{ik} + M z_i \tag{3}$$

**(4) Profile selection:**
$$\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{ik}} u_{ip} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, k \tag{4}$$

**(5) Same-track indicator** (exact XOR linearization, $g_{ijk}=1 \iff x_{ik}=x_{jk}$):
$$g_{ijk} \ge 1 - x_{ik} - x_{jk}, \quad g_{ijk} \ge x_{ik} + x_{jk} - 1, \quad g_{ijk} \le 1 - x_{ik} + x_{jk}, \quad g_{ijk} \le 1 + x_{ik} - x_{jk} \tag{5}$$

**(6) Ordering consistency** ($i<j$, common $k$; relaxed if either train cancelled):
$$y_{ijk} + y_{jik} \ge 1 - (z_i + z_j), \qquad y_{ijk} + y_{jik} \le 1 \tag{6}$$

**(7) Headways** ($i<j$, common $k$; each with symmetric counterpart swapping $i \leftrightarrow j$, $y_{ijk} \leftrightarrow y_{jik}$):
$$d_{j,s(k)} \ge d_{i,s(k)} + H^{DD} - M(1 - y_{ijk}) - M(1 - g_{ijk}) - M(z_i + z_j) \tag{7a}$$
$$a_{j,s'(k)} \ge a_{i,s'(k)} + H^{AA} - M(1 - y_{ijk}) - M(1 - g_{ijk}) - M(z_i + z_j) \tag{7b}$$
$$a_{i,s'(k)} \ge d_{j,s(k)} + H^{AD} - M(1 - y_{ijk}) - M(1 - g_{ijk}) - M(z_i + z_j) \tag{7c}$$

No overtaking within a segment: $y_{ijk}$ fixes the order at both endpoints simultaneously via (6)–(7a)–(7b).

**(8) Pairwise station capacity** (station $s$, pair $i<j$, with station-ordering binary $y_{ij,s}$ as in (6)):
$$a_{i,s} \ge d_{j,s} + \epsilon - M(1 - y_{ji,s}) - M(z_i + z_j), \qquad a_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + \epsilon - M(1 - y_{ij,s}) - M(z_i + z_j) \tag{8}$$

**(9) Reroute availability** (opposite track usable only if not blocked):
$$x_{ik} \le A_{ik} \qquad \forall i,\, k \in B \tag{9}$$

**(10) Disruption window** (train on the blocked track must pass entirely before $\tau_1$ or after $\tau_2$; binary $q_{ik}$ = "pass before $\tau_1$"):
$$d_{i,s(k)} + \sum_p r^p_{ik} u_{ip} \le \tau_1 + M(1 - q_{ik}) + M x_{ik} + M z_i \tag{10a}$$
$$d_{i,s(k)} \ge \tau_2 - M q_{ik} - M x_{ik} - M z_i \qquad \forall i,\, k \in B \text{ with scheduled track} = b(k) \tag{10b}$$

**(11) Domains:**
$$a_{ik}, d_{ik}, \delta_i, \delta^\pm_i \ge 0; \qquad z_i, u_{ip}, x_{ik}, g_{ijk}, y_{ijk} \in \{0,1\} \tag{11}$$

## Key modeling points

- **Retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed-profile selection** are all explicit decisions; the timetable running time in (1) is exactly the selected profile's running time, guaranteeing control-level feasibility.
- **Bidirectional conflicts** on a shared track during single-track operation are handled by the XOR linearization (5) activating headways (7a)–(7c) only when two trains occupy the same track.
- **Disruption handling** (9)–(10) forces affected trains to either reroute to the available opposite track or shift their traversal outside $[\tau_1, \tau_2]$.
- **Tight big-M values** ($M_{ik} = \Delta^{\max} + \max_{p,p'}|r^p_{ik} - r^{p'}_{ik}|$) keep the LP relaxation strong.
- The model is a pure MILP (linear objective and constraints), solvable by branch-and-bound/cut, and is the natural basis for the decomposition into a train-plan selection IP with adaptive plan refinement described in the paper's solution framework.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

Below is the complete linear model (equations only), based on the problem description. Assumptions are marked where information was missing.

## Assumptions
- Double-track corridor with stations `s ∈ S`, segments `e = (s, s+1) ∈ E`; one track per direction.
- Disruption: segment `e*` partially blocked during window `[t0, t1]`; one track unavailable, so trains may reroute to the opposite track, which is then shared bidirectionally with headway separation.
- Speed profiles are discretized into running-time levels `k ∈ K_e` with running time `rt[e,k]` and energy `en[e,k]` (assumption: discrete profile set, as in the paper's "train plans").
- Big-M = planning horizon `H`.

## Sets & Parameters
- `T` trains; `S` stations; `E` segments; `K_e` profiles.
- `a⁰[i,s], d⁰[i,s]`: scheduled arrival/departure; `dw[s]`: min dwell; `h`: min headway; `π_c[i]`: cancellation penalty; `w_d, w_e, w_r`: weights.

## Variables
- `a[i,s], d[i,s] ≥ 0` — actual arrival/departure times.
- `D[i,s] ≥ 0` — arrival delay.
- `y[i,e,k] ∈ {0,1}` — speed profile selection.
- `r[i,e] ∈ {0,1}` — rerouting to opposite track.
- `z[i,e] ∈ {0,1}` — train `i` traverses `e` during disruption window.
- `x[i,j,e] ∈ {0,1}` — ordering (i before j) on segment `e`.
- `u[i,j,e] ∈ {0,1}` — both trains on same physical track.
- `c[i] ∈ {0,1}` — cancellation.

## Objective
```
min  Σ_i Σ_s w_d·D[i,s]  +  w_e·Σ_i Σ_e Σ_k en[e,k]·y[i,e,k]
   +  Σ_i π_c[i]·c[i]  +  w_r·Σ_i Σ_e r[i,e]
```

## Constraints

**(C1) Timetable consistency (running time from selected profile):**
```
a[i,s+1] = d[i,s] + Σ_k rt[e,k]·y[i,e,k]  (± M·c[i])      ∀i, e=(s,s+1)
```

**(C2) Minimum dwell time:**
```
d[i,s] ≥ a[i,s] + dw[s] − M·c[i]                          ∀i, s
```

**(C3) Exactly one speed profile if the train runs:**
```
Σ_k y[i,e,k] = 1 − c[i]                                   ∀i, e
```

**(C4) Cancellation fixes times to schedule:**
```
a[i,s] = a⁰[i,s] ± M·(1−c[i]);   d[i,s] = d⁰[i,s] ± M·(1−c[i])   ∀i,s
```

**(C5) Same-track indicator (linearized |r_i − r_j|):**
```
u[i,j,e] ≤ 1 − c[i],  u[i,j,e] ≤ 1 − c[j]
u[i,j,e] ≥ 1 − c[i] − c[j] − (r[i,e] − r[j,e])
u[i,j,e] ≥ 1 − c[i] − c[j] − (r[j,e] − r[i,e])
x[i,j,e] + x[j,i,e] = u[i,j,e]                            ∀i<j, e
```

**(C6) Headway via big-M ordering (entry = departure upstream, exit = arrival downstream):**
```
d[j,s] ≥ d[i,s] + h − M·(1 − x[i,j,e]) − M·(c[i]+c[j])
a[j,s+1] ≥ a[i,s+1] + h − M·(1 − x[i,j,e]) − M·(c[i]+c[j])   ∀i≠j, e=(s,s+1)
```

**(C7) Disruption-window indicator (z = 1 if entry before t1 possible):**
```
z[i,e] ≥ 1 − (d[i,s] − t0)/H − c[i];   z[i,e] ≤ 1 − c[i]     ∀i, e
```

**(C8) Rerouting only on blocked segment, only during window:**
```
r[i,e] = 0  ∀e ≠ e*;    r[i,e*] ≤ z[i,e*]                 ∀i
```

**(C9) Blocked-track rule:** own-direction trains must wait until `t1` unless rerouted:
```
d[i,s] ≥ t1 − M·r[i,e*] − M·c[i]      ∀i with dir(i) = blocked direction
```

**(C10) Time bounds & earliest origin departure:**
```
0 ≤ a[i,s], d[i,s] ≤ H;   d[i,s_origin] ≥ d⁰[i,s_origin] − M·c[i]
```

**(C11) Delay definition:**
```
D[i,s] ≥ a[i,s] − a⁰[i,s];   D[i,s] ≥ 0                   ∀i, s
```

**(C12) Profile data validity:** `rt_min[e] ≤ rt[e,k] ≤ rt_max[e]` ∀e,k.

**Key modeling logic:** the same-track indicator `u` activates headway constraints only when two trains share a physical track (including both rerouted onto the open track of `e*`); slower speed profiles save energy but increase delay, so the weights `w_d, w_e` balance the time–energy trade-off; rerouting lets trains bypass the blocked track during `[t0,t1]` at the cost of bidirectional conflict resolution via the ordering variables `x`.

Text:
# MILP Model: Conflict Detection and Resolution for Railway Traffic under DTG Signalling

This model extends the RECIFE-MILP formulation (Pellegrini et al., 2015) with speed-profile options and train- and speed-dependent blocking times for distance-to-go (DTG) signalling (ETCS L2 with TTD).

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** The network is a set of TTD sections (blocks); a section can be occupied by at most one train at a time. Sections are either *switch areas* or *plain line/station sections*.
- **(A2)** Each train has a fixed route through the network (local rerouting is modelled by a set of alternative routes per train, chosen by binary variables).
- **(A3)** Each train selects one of a finite set of precomputed speed profiles per route segment; each profile determines a running time and a braking distance (hence blocking time) as a function of the train's speed.
- **(A4)** Blocking times under DTG are computed offline for each (train, section, speed profile) combination and include the speed-dependent approach/braking distance to the end of authority.
- **(A5)** Delays are measured against the published timetable at every scheduled event (passing/arrival times).
- **(A6)** Dwell times may be stretched within given bounds; retiming and reordering are decision variables.
- **(A7)** All data are deterministic; disturbance is given by initial delays of trains entering the area.

---

## 2. Sets and indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $t$ |
| $R_t$ | set of feasible routes for train $t$, index $r$ |
| $S$ | set of TTD sections, index $s$ |
| $S_{tr}$ | ordered sequence of sections of route $r$ of train $t$ |
| $P_{t,s}$ | set of speed-profile options of train $t$ on section $s$, index $p$ |
| $\Omega$ | set of ordered pairs of trains sharing at least one section, $(t_1,t_2)$, $t_1 \neq t_2$ |
| $K$ | set of discrete time steps (horizon), index $k$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a^{ref}_{t,s}$, $d^{ref}_{t,s}$ | scheduled arrival / departure (passing) time of train $t$ at section $s$ ($\infty$ if not scheduled) |
| $D^{in}_t$ | initial delay of train $t$ at the area entrance |
| $\tau^{run}_{t,s,p}$ | running time of train $t$ on section $s$ with speed profile $p$ |
| $\tau^{block}_{t,s,p}$ | **DTG blocking time** of train $t$ on section $s$ with profile $p$, including the speed-dependent braking/approach distance to the EoA |
| $\underline{\tau}^{dwell}_{t,s},\ \bar{\tau}^{dwell}_{t,s}$ | min/max dwell time of train $t$ at station section $s$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant (horizon length) |
| $\sigma_s \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if section $s$ is a switch area |
| $w$ | weight penalising non-preferred speed profiles (energy/comfort proxy) |
| $\delta^{max}$ | maximum admissible dwell stretching |

## 4. Decision variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ |
| $y_{t,s,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ runs profile $p$ on section $s$ |
| $z_{t_1,t_2} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if $t_1$ passes before $t_2$ on their shared sections |
| $d^{arr}_{t,s} \ge 0$, $d^{dep}_{t,s} \ge 0$ | continuous | arrival / departure delay of train $t$ at section $s$ |
| $t^{arr}_{t,s} \ge 0$, $t^{dep}_{t,s} \ge 0$ | continuous | actual arrival / departure time |
| $u_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if the blocking time of train $t$ on section $s$ covers time step $k$ |
| $v_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ occupies section $s$ at time step $k$ |

## 5. Objective function

Minimise total delay plus a penalty on non-preferred (faster/energetic) speed profiles:

$$
\min \; \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s \in S_{t}} \big( d^{arr}_{t,s} + d^{dep}_{t,s} \big) \;+\; w \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{s} \sum_{p \in P_{t,s}} c_{t,s,p}\, y_{t,s,p}
$$

where $c_{t,s,p}$ is the (normalised) cost of profile $p$ relative to the most economical profile.

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Route choice** — exactly one route per train:
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Speed-profile choice** — exactly one profile per (train, section):
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{t,s}} y_{t,s,p} = x_{t,r} \qquad \forall t,\ \forall r \in R_t,\ \forall s \in S_{tr}
$$

**(C3) Initial delay propagation:**
$$
t^{arr}_{t,s_1} = a^{ref}_{t,s_1} + D^{in}_t + d^{arr}_{t,s_1} \qquad \forall t,\ s_1 = \text{first section of } S_{tr}
$$

**(C4) Running-time consistency with chosen profile:**
$$
t^{arr}_{t,s_{i+1}} \ge t^{dep}_{t,s_i} + \sum_{p \in P_{t,s_i}} \tau^{run}_{t,s_i,p}\, y_{t,s_i,p} \qquad \forall t,\ \forall s_i \in S_{tr}
$$

**(C5) Dwell time bounds (station sections):**
$$
\underline{\tau}^{dwell}_{t,s} \le t^{dep}_{t,s} - t^{arr}_{t,s} \le \underline{\tau}^{dwell}_{t,s} + \delta^{max} \qquad \forall t,\ s \text{ station section}
$$

**(C6) Delay definition:**
$$
t^{arr}_{t,s} = a^{ref}_{t,s} + d^{arr}_{t,s}, \qquad t^{dep}_{t,s} = d^{ref}_{t,s} + d^{dep}_{t,s} \qquad \forall t, s
$$

**(C7) Blocking-time coverage (DTG):** the blocking interval of train $t$ on section $s$ starts $\tau^{block}_{t,s,p}$ before its arrival (speed-dependent, DTG brake indication point):
$$
u_{t,s,k} \ge u_{t,s,k+1} \qquad \forall t,s,k
$$
$$
u_{t,s,k} \ge v_{t,s,k}, \qquad
u_{t,s,k} \ge v_{t,s,k+\left\lceil \tau^{block}_{t,s,p}/\Delta \right\rceil} - 1 + y_{t,s,p} \;\; \text{(linearised per profile)}
$$
Concretely, for each profile $p$ and each $k$:
$$
u_{t,s,k} \ge v_{t,s,k'} - (1 - y_{t,s,p}) \qquad \forall k' \in \left[k,\, k + \left\lceil \tau^{block}_{t,s,p}/\Delta \right\rceil\right]
$$
with $\Delta$ the discretisation step.

**(C8) Occupation consistency with running time:**
$$
v_{t,s,k} \ge v_{t,s,k+1}, \qquad
v_{t,s,k} \ge v_{t,s,k'} - (1-y_{t,s,p}) \quad \forall k' \in [k, k+\lceil \tau^{run}_{t,s,p}/\Delta \rceil]
$$

**(C9) Section exclusivity (single occupancy incl. blocking time):**
$$
\sum_{t \in T} u_{t,s,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall s \in S,\ \forall k \in K
$$

**(C10) Ordering on shared sections** (for each pair $(t_1,t_2) \in \Omega$ and each commonly used section $s$):
$$
t^{dep}_{t_1,s} \le t^{arr}_{t_2,s} + M(1 - z_{t_1,t_2})
$$
$$
t^{dep}_{t_2,s} \le t^{arr}_{t_1,s} + M\, z_{t_1,t_2}
$$

**(C11) Consistent ordering across all shared sections** (no overtaking within the pair unless on different routes):
$$
z_{t_1,t_2} + z_{t_2,t_1} = 1 \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in \Omega
$$

**(C12) Switch-area headway:** on switch sections $s$ with $\sigma_s = 1$, conflicting routes may not be simultaneously blocked:
$$
u_{t_1,s,k} + u_{t_2,s,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \text{ with conflicting switch paths},\ \forall k
$$

**(C13) Route–profile linking (big-M):**
$$
t^{arr}_{t,s} \le t^{arr}_{t,s'} + M \quad \text{(sequence feasibility along chosen route)}
$$
and profile variables forced to 0 for sections not on the chosen route:
$$
y_{t,s,p} \le \sum_{r \in R_t:\, s \in S_{tr}} x_{t,r} \qquad \forall t,s,p
$$

**(C14) Variable domains:**
$$
t^{arr}_{t,s}, t^{dep}_{t,s} \ge 0, \quad d^{arr}_{t,s}, d^{dep}_{t,s} \ge 0, \quad x_{t,r}, y_{t,s,p}, z_{t_1,t_2}, u_{t,s,k}, v_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 7. Remarks

- The **DTG-specific feature** is constraint (C7)–(C8) with parameter $\tau^{block}_{t,s,p}$: blocking times depend on the train and the selected speed profile, capturing the speed-dependent braking distance to the end of authority, instead of a fixed number of blocks as in conventional RECIFE-MILP.
- Constraints (C10)–(C12) implement retiming, reordering and local rerouting; (C2), (C4) implement speed-profile selection.
- The model is a standard MILP, solvable by branch-and-bound; the time-indexed variables $u, v$ may be replaced by pairwise big-M headway constraints for efficiency.

# MILP Model: Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Scheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

We consider a double-track urban rail transit line with stations $S = \{1, 2, \dots, |\mathcal{S}|\}$, where trains run in one direction (per track). Time is discretized into intervals of equal length; passenger demand is piecewise constant per interval. Trains may be composed of 1, 2, or 3 train units (flexible composition), and train units must circulate (a train ending its service must be matched to a following service).

**Assumptions (marked where not given in the input):**
- (A1) Single line, one direction modeled; the reverse direction is symmetric.
- (A2) Passenger demand is deterministic and piecewise constant over intervals of length $\Delta$ (as in Liu et al., 2023a).
- (A3) Passengers board the first arriving train with sufficient residual capacity; FIFO boarding.
- (A4) Running times between stations are fixed; only departure times and composition are decision variables (dwell times may be fixed or bounded).
- (A5) No overtaking; train order on the line is fixed.
- (A6) Rolling stock circulation is modeled by binary linkage variables between consecutive train services at the terminal station.
- (A7) The model is solved repeatedly inside an MPC loop over a receding horizon $[t_0, t_0 + H]$.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $i \in \mathcal{N} = \{1,\dots,N\}$ | trains (services) |
| $s \in \mathcal{S} = \{1,\dots,|\mathcal{S}|\}$ | stations |
| $k \in \mathcal{K} = \{1,\dots,K\}$ | time intervals |
| $c \in \mathcal{C} = \{1,2,3\}$ | train composition (number of coupled units) |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d^{arr}_{i,s}$, $d^{dep}_{i,s}$ | nominal arrival/departure times of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_s$ | running time from $s$ to $s+1$ |
| $\underline{h}, \bar{h}$ | minimum/maximum headway at any station [s] |
| $\underline{d}, \bar{d}$ | min/max dwell time at intermediate stations |
| $Q_{s,k}$ | number of passengers arriving at station $s$ during interval $k$ |
| $B_c$ | capacity of a train with composition $c$ (e.g., $B_1 = 800$, $B_2 = 1600$, $B_3 = 2400$) |
| $\gamma_c$ | operational cost of dispatching a train with composition $c$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights for waiting time and deviation from nominal timetable |
| $M$ | number of available train units; $U$ max units coupled |
| $T^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround time at terminal |
| $H$ | MPC prediction horizon |

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $x_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $w_{s,k} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: passengers waiting at station $s$ at the start of interval $k$.
- $b_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: passengers boarding train $i$ at station $s$.
- $l_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: passengers left behind by train $i$ at station $s$.
- $n_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: in-vehicle load of train $i$ on section $(s, s+1)$.

**Integer/Binary:**
- $y_{i,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is dispatched with composition $c$.
- $z_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if the train units of service $i$ are directly reused by the next service $j$ at the terminal (rolling stock circulation link).
- $\delta_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: stop indicator of train $i$ at station $s$ (optional stopping plan).

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total passenger waiting time, timetable deviation, and operational cost:

$$
\min \; J = \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \Delta \, w_{s,k}}_{\text{passenger waiting time}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \left( x_{i,s} - d^{dep}_{i,s} \right)^2}_{\text{deviation (linearized below)}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} \gamma_c \, y_{i,c}}_{\text{operational cost}}
$$

**Linearization of the quadratic deviation term** (assumption A8, standard big-M): introduce $u_{i,s} \ge 0$ and

$$
u_{i,s} \ge x_{i,s} - d^{dep}_{i,s}, \qquad u_{i,s} \ge d^{dep}_{i,s} - x_{i,s},
$$

and replace the deviation term by $\beta \sum_{i,s} u_{i,s}$ (absolute deviation).

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Train order and headway (no overtaking, fixed order):**
$$
x_{i+1,s} - x_{i,s} \ge \underline{h}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{N}\setminus\{N\},\ \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
$$
$$
x_{i+1,s} - x_{i,s} \le \bar{h}, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{N}\setminus\{N\},\ \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

**(C2) Running time dynamics:**
$$
x_{i,s+1} - x_{i,s} \ge r_s + \underline{d}\,\delta_{i,s+1}, \qquad \forall i,\ s < |\mathcal{S}|
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1} - x_{i,s} \le r_s + \bar{d}, \qquad \forall i,\ s < |\mathcal{S}|
$$

**(C3) Stopping plan consistency:**
$$
x_{i,s+1} - x_{i,s} \ge r_s + \underline{d} - M(1 - \delta_{i,s+1}), \qquad \forall i,\ s < |\mathcal{S}|
$$
$$
x_{i,s+1} - x_{i,s} \le r_s + M(1 - \delta_{i,s+1}), \qquad \forall i,\ s < |\mathcal{S}|
$$
$$
\delta_{i,1} = \delta_{i,|\mathcal{S}|} = 1, \qquad \forall i
$$

**(C4) Passenger flow dynamics (waiting-time recursion):**
$$
w_{s,k+1} = w_{s,k} + Q_{s,k} - \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} b_{i,s} \cdot \mathbb{I}\{ x_{i,s} \in [k\Delta, (k{+}1)\Delta) \}, \qquad \forall s, k
$$

To keep linearity, the indicator is replaced by time-indexed boarding variables: define $b_{i,s,k} \ge 0$ (passengers boarding train $i$ at $s$ who arrived during interval $k$), with
$$
b_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} b_{i,s,k}, \qquad b_{i,s,k} \le Q_{s,k}, \qquad \forall i,s,k
$$
and the recursion becomes
$$
w_{s,k+1} = w_{s,k} + Q_{s,k} - \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} b_{i,s,k}, \qquad \forall s,k
$$

**(C5) FIFO boarding order** (passengers at a station board trains in departure order):
$$
b_{i,s,k} \le Q_{s,k} \left( 1 - \sum_{j < i} \frac{b_{j,s,k}}{Q_{s,k} + \epsilon} \right) \;\; \text{(linearized via big-M:)}
$$
$$
b_{i,s,k} \le M_{b}\left(1 - v_{i,s,k}\right), \quad b_{i,s,k} \ge Q_{s,k} - M_b v_{i,s,k}, \quad v_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$
where $v_{i,s,k} = 1$ indicates train $i$ departs within interval $k$:
$$
k\Delta - M(x_{i,s} - k\Delta) \le M v_{i,s,k}, \qquad x_{i,s} - (k{+}1)\Delta \le M(1 - v_{i,s,k})
$$
$$
\sum_{k} v_{i,s,k} = 1, \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C6) Left-behind passengers and capacity:**
$$
l_{i,s} = w_{s,k_i} - b_{i,s} \ge 0, \qquad k_i \text{ = interval of departure of train } i \text{ at } s
$$
$$
n_{i,s} = n_{i,s-1} - b_{i,s-1}^{\text{alight}} + b_{i,s} \le \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} B_c \, y_{i,c}, \qquad \forall i, s
$$
with alighting proportions $b^{\text{alight}}_{i,s} = \rho_s \, n_{i,s-1}$, $\rho_s$ the fixed alighting fraction (A9).

**(C7) Composition selection (exactly one composition per train):**
$$
\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} y_{i,c} = 1, \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{N}
$$

**(C8) Rolling stock circulation (flow conservation of train units):**
$$
\sum_{j > i} z_{i,j} = \sum_{c} c \, y_{i,c} \cdot \eta - \sum_{j < i} \sum_{c} c \, y_{j,c}\,\eta \, z_{j,i} \;\; \text{(linearized as:)}
$$
$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}: j > i} z_{i,j} \le \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} c\, y_{i,c}, \qquad \forall i
$$
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}: i < j} z_{i,j} \le \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} c\, y_{j,c}, \qquad \forall j
$$
Turnaround time feasibility:
$$
x_{j,|\mathcal{S}|} - x_{i,|\mathcal{S}|} \ge T^{turn} - M(1 - z_{i,j}), \qquad \forall i < j
$$
Fleet size limit:
$$
\sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} c \sum_{i \in \mathcal{N}} y_{i,c} \le M \cdot \kappa
$$
where $\kappa$ bounds the number of simultaneous circulations (A10).

**(C9) Horizon and boundary conditions (MPC):**
$$
t_0 \le x_{i,s} \le t_0 + H, \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
x_{i,s} = d^{dep}_{i,s}, \qquad \forall i, s \text{ already departed at } t_0 \text{ (past decisions fixed)}
$$
$$
w_{s,0} = \hat{w}_s(t_0) \quad \text{(measured initial state)}
$$

**(C10) Terminal penalty (MPC stability, A11):**
$$
J \; \text{includes} \; \beta_f \sum_{s} w_{s,K+1}
$$

## 7. Model Summary

- **Continuous variables:** $x_{i,s}$, $b_{i,s,k}$, $w_{s,k}$, $n_{i,s}$, $l_{i,s}$, $u_{i,s}$ — $O(N|\mathcal{S}|K)$.
- **Binary variables:** $y_{i,c}$, $z_{i,j}$, $v_{i,s,k}$, $\delta_{i,s}$ — $O(N|\mathcal{S}|K + N^2)$.
- **Nature:** MILP (all constraints linear; the quadratic deviation is linearized via $u_{i,s}$).

This MILP is solved at each MPC step. In the proposed learning-based framework, presolve techniques prune integer variables, an LSTM predicts the remaining binaries ($y$, $z$, $\delta$), and with integers fixed the model reduces to a linear program (LP) in $(x, b, w, n, l, u)$, which is solved exactly to guarantee constraint satisfaction — combining learning-based speed with optimization-based feasibility.

All three candidate models were generated. Model 2 is the best: it is the most complete and internally consistent MILP — it cleanly couples timetable variables with speed-profile selection, handles bidirectional single-track conflicts with proper big-M disjunctions, restricts rerouting to the disruption window, and includes cancellations and station capacity. Here is the chosen model:

# Integrated MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

- A double-track high-speed line consists of ordered stations `S = {1, 2, …, n}` connected by segments `A = {1, 2, …, n−1}`. Segment `a*` is partially blocked: only one track is usable during the disruption window `[t_s, t_e]`, so trains in that window must share it as a single track (bidirectional operation).
- Each train `f ∈ F` has a scheduled timetable (planned arrival/departure at each station), a direction `dir(f) ∈ {up, down}`, and a set of feasible speed profiles per segment.
- Each speed profile `p ∈ P_{f,a}` for train `f` on segment `a` has a fixed running time `τ_{f,a,p}` and energy consumption `E_{f,a,p}` (pre-computed from train dynamics — this linearizes the speed decision).
- Trains may be retimed, reordered, rerouted to the opposite (free) track in the disrupted segment while it is blocked, or cancelled.
- Minimum headway `h` applies between consecutive trains entering/leaving the same track resource; station capacity `C_i` limits simultaneous occupied tracks; dwell times are bounded.
- All data are deterministic; all constraints are linear (big-M formulation).

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `F` | set of trains, index `f` |
| `S` | stations, index `i` |
| `A` | segments, index `a`; disrupted segment `a*` |
| `P_{f,a}` | feasible speed profiles for train `f` on segment `a`, index `p` |
| `K_i` | station tracks at station `i` |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `d̂_{f,i}`, `â_{f,i}` | scheduled departure / arrival of train `f` at station `i` |
| `dw^min_{f,i}`, `dw^max_{f,i}` | min / max dwell time of `f` at station `i` |
| `τ_{f,a,p}` | running time of profile `p` on segment `a` |
| `E_{f,a,p}` | energy consumption of profile `p` on segment `a` |
| `M` | sufficiently large constant (planning horizon) |
| `h` | minimum headway on a shared track |
| `C_i` | capacity (number of tracks) of station `i` |
| `t_s`, `t_e` | disruption start and end times |
| `w_D`, `w_E` | weights for delay and energy in the objective |
| `T^max` | maximum allowed delay |
| `c^C` | cancellation penalty per train |

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- `a_{f,i} ∈ ℝ₊` : actual arrival time of train `f` at station `i`
- `d_{f,i} ∈ ℝ₊` : actual departure time of train `f` at station `i`
- `D_f ∈ ℝ₊` : total delay of train `f` at its destination

**Binary:**
- `x_{f,a,p} ∈ {0,1}` : 1 if train `f` runs speed profile `p` on segment `a`
- `y_{f,g}^a ∈ {0,1}` : 1 if train `f` precedes train `g` on segment `a` (ordering)
- `z_f^dis ∈ {0,1}` : 1 if train `f` is rerouted to the opposite track through the disrupted segment
- `c_f ∈ {0,1}` : 1 if train `f` is cancelled

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_D \sum_{f \in F} D_f \;+\; w_E \sum_{f \in F} \sum_{a \in A} \sum_{p \in P_{f,a}} E_{f,a,p}\, x_{f,a,p} \;+\; c^C \sum_{f \in F} c_f
$$

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per train–segment):**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{f,a}} x_{f,a,p} = 1 - c_f \qquad \forall f \in F,\; a \in A$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency with chosen profile:**
$$d_{f,i} + \sum_{p} \tau_{f,i,p}\, x_{f,i,p} \le a_{f,i+1} + M c_f \qquad \forall f,\; i = 1,\dots,n-1$$
$$d_{f,i} + \sum_{p} \tau_{f,i,p}\, x_{f,i,p} \ge a_{f,i+1} - M c_f \qquad \forall f,\; i = 1,\dots,n-1$$

**(C3) Dwell time bounds:**
$$dw^min_{f,i} \le d_{f,i} - a_{f,i} \le dw^max_{f,i} \qquad \forall f,\; i \in S \setminus \{\text{origin, destination}\}$$

**(C4) Delay definition (at destination):**
$$D_f \ge a_{f,n} - \hat{a}_{f,n} - M c_f, \qquad D_f \ge 0 \qquad \forall f \in F$$
$$a_{f,n} \le \hat{a}_{f,n} + T^{max} + M c_f \qquad \forall f \in F$$

**(C5) Cancellation consistency (no movement if cancelled):**
$$d_{f,i} \le M c_f + \hat d_{f,i}(1-c_f), \qquad a_{f,i} \le M c_f + \hat a_{f,i}(1-c_f) \qquad \forall f, i$$

**(C6) Segment ordering — same direction (headway on each segment):** for trains `f, g` running in the same direction on segment `a`:
$$d_{g,i} \ge d_{f,i} + \sum_p \tau_{f,a,p} x_{f,a,p} + h - M(1 - y_{f,g}^{a}) - M c_f - M c_g$$
$$d_{f,i} \ge d_{g,i} + \sum_p \tau_{g,a,p} x_{g,a,p} + h - M\, y_{f,g}^{a} - M c_f - M c_g$$
with anti-symmetry:
$$y_{f,g}^{a} + y_{g,f}^{a} = 1 - c_f - c_g \qquad \forall f < g,\; a \in A \;(\text{same direction})$$

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on the disrupted single track (segment `a*` during `[t_s, t_e]`):** for trains `f` (up) and `g` (down) both potentially using the blocked single track, with `i*`, `j*` the entry stations of `a*` for each direction:
$$d_{f,i^*} \ge d_{g,j^*} + \sum_p \tau_{g,a^*,p} x_{g,a^*,p} + h - M(1 - y_{f,g}^{a^*}) - M z_f^{dis} - M z_g^{dis} - M c_f - M c_g$$
$$d_{g,j^*} \ge d_{f,i^*} + \sum_p \tau_{f,a^*,p} x_{f,a^*,p} + h - M\, y_{f,g}^{a^*} - M z_f^{dis} - M z_g^{dis} - M c_f - M c_g$$
If either train is rerouted to the opposite (free) track (`z = 1`), the conflict constraint is relaxed via the `M z` terms.

**(C8) Rerouting validity:** a train may use the opposite track only within the disruption window:
$$d_{f,i^*} \le t_e + M(1 - z_f^{dis}), \qquad d_{f,i^*} \ge t_s - M(1 - z_f^{dis}) \qquad \forall f$$
and rerouting is only possible for trains whose planned track is the blocked one:
$$z_f^{dis} = 0 \quad \text{for trains whose own track remains available (parameter-defined)}$$

**(C9) Trains outside the disruption window** are unconstrained on `a*`: their `y`-variables for `a*` are fixed by preprocessing, or constraints (C7) are relaxed by big-M when both entry times fall outside `[t_s, t_e]`.

**(C10) Station capacity:** with time-indexed occupancy binaries `o_{f,i,t} ∈ {0,1}` (1 if train `f` occupies station `i` during interval `t`):
$$\sum_{f} \sum_{k \in K_i} o_{f,i,t,k} \le C_i \qquad \forall i \in S,\; t$$
linked linearly:
$$o_{f,i,t} \ge 1 - \frac{a_{f,i} - t}{M}, \qquad o_{f,i,t} \ge 1 - \frac{t - d_{f,i}}{M}$$

**(C11) Variable domains:**
$$a_{f,i}, d_{f,i}, D_f \ge 0; \qquad x_{f,a,p},\, y_{f,g}^{a},\, z_f^{dis},\, c_f,\, o_{f,i,t} \in \{0,1\}$$

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Retiming:** continuous variables `a_{f,i}`, `d_{f,i}` allow arbitrary (linear) shifts of the timetable; constraints (C2)–(C3) keep movements physically feasible.
- **Reordering:** binaries `y_{f,g}^a` decide the sequence on each segment; big-M disjunctions (C6)–(C7) enforce headways only for the chosen order. On the disrupted segment, (C7) is the key bidirectional conflict constraint: two opposing trains cannot occupy the single track simultaneously.
- **Rerouting:** `z_f^dis` lets a train use the opposite track during the disruption, deactivating its participation in the single-track conflict (C7), but only if its entry time lies inside the disruption window (C8).
- **Cancellation:** `c_f` removes train `f` (C1, C5) and adds a penalty in the objective.
- **Speed management:** profile binaries `x_{f,a,p}` couple running time (C2) with energy consumption in the objective, allowing slower profiles to save energy at the price of possible delay — the trade-off is balanced by weights `w_D`, `w_E`.
- **Linearity:** all nonlinearities (profile choice, ordering, rerouting) are handled with standard big-M disjunctions, yielding a pure MILP solvable by branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX).

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Sets and Parameters

- **I**: trains; **S** = {1,…,n}: stations; segments s connects stations s and s+1
- **dirs_i** ∈ {+1, −1}: travel direction of train i
- schedArr[i,s], schedDep[i,s]: scheduled times; DwMin/DwMax: dwell bounds
- Disruption: segment b has one track blocked during window [T0, T1]
- **K(i,s)**: precomputed speed profiles (running-time plans) k with running time r_k and energy E_k
- w_i: delay weight; P_i: cancellation penalty; α: energy weight; h_seg, h_dep, h_arr: headways; M: big-M; T: horizon

## Decision Variables

- a[i,s], d[i,s] ≥ 0: arrival/departure times (continuous)
- r[i,s]: running time on segment s, rMin ≤ r[i,s] ≤ rMax
- Del[i,s] ≥ 0: arrival delay
- x[i,s] ∈ {0,1}: uses normal track; y[i,s] ∈ {0,1}: uses rerouted (opposite) track; c[i] ∈ {0,1}: cancelled
- z[i,s,k] ∈ {0,1}: speed plan k selected on segment s
- u[i,j,s], uy[i,j,s], v[i,j,s] ∈ {0,1}: ordering binaries

## Objective

Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellation cost:

min Σ_i Σ_s w_i · Del[i,s] + α · Σ_{i,s,k} E_k · z[i,s,k] + Σ_i P_i · c[i]

## Constraints

**1. Timetable linking** (entry d[i,s], exit a[i,s′], s′ = s + dir_i):
- a[i,s′] = d[i,s] + r[i,s] − M·c[i]

**2. Speed plan selection** (one plan per non-cancelled train, linear running time):
- Σ_k z[i,s,k] = 1 − c[i]
- r[i,s] = Σ_k r_k · z[i,s,k]

**3. Dwell time bounds:**
- DwMin[i,s] − M·c[i] ≤ d[i,s] − a[i,s] ≤ DwMax[i,s] + M·c[i]

**4. Delay definition and recovery lower bound:**
- a[i,s] ≥ schedArr[i,s]
- Del[i,s] ≥ a[i,s] − schedArr[i,s]

**5. Route assignment / rerouting:**
- x[i,s] + y[i,s] + c[i] = 1 for every segment on train i's route
- y[i,s] = 0 if segment s is not disrupted (no rerouting outside the blockage)

**6. Blockage (constraint on disrupted segment b):** with auxiliary binaries before/after:
- exit_time(i,s) ≤ T0 + M(1 − before) + M·c[i]  (traversal fully before window)
- entry_time(i,s) ≥ T1 − M(1 − after) − M·c[i]  (traversal fully after window)
- x[i,s] ≤ before + after + c[i]  (normal track usable only outside the window; otherwise reroute or cancel)

**7. Segment headways (conflict-free on each track):** for trains i, j sharing segment s:
- Normal track: exit_j ≥ exit_i + h_seg − M(3 − u[i,j,s] − x[i,s] − x[j,s])
- exit_i ≥ exit_j + h_seg − M(2 + u[i,j,s] − x[i,s] − x[j,s])
- Opposite track: same disjunction with uy[i,j,s] and y[i,s], y[j,s]

**8. Station sequencing (same direction), pairwise ordering via v[i,j,s]:**
- d[j,s] ≥ d[i,s] + h_dep − M(1 − v)  and  d[i,s] ≥ d[j,s] + h_dep − M·v
- a[j,s] ≥ a[i,s] + h_arr − M(1 − v)  and  a[i,s] ≥ a[j,s] + h_arr − M·v

**9. Horizon:**
- a[i, terminal] ≤ T

**10. Domains:** a, d, r, Del continuous; x, y, c, z, u, uy, v binary. Cancellation (c[i]=1) relaxes all timing constraints via big-M terms, with its cost captured in the objective.

## Assumptions (made where information was missing)

- Running times are restricted to a finite set of precomputed speed profiles per (train, segment) — this makes the train-dynamics coupling linear; energy consumption is a linear function of plan selection.
- Rerouting is allowed only on the disrupted segment; a train traversing the blocked segment during [T0,T1] must use the opposite track, where bidirectional conflicts are resolved by the headway disjunctions.
- Dwell times are bounded between 1 and 5 minutes, and headways are uniform (2 min) — these are illustrative data values.

Below is the final MILP after three refinement rounds (fixing nonlinearity, restoring the disruption-window logic and speed-profile/energy coupling, and cleaning the big-M formulations).

# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains $i$ |
| $J$ | set of track segments $j$; segment $j$ connects stations $s(j)$ and $s(j)+1$ |
| $J^D \subseteq J$ | disrupted segments (only one track usable during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$) |
| $S$ | ordered set of stations |
| $P_{i,j}$ | candidate speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $j$, split into $P^{norm}_{i,j}$ (normal track) and $P^{sing}_{i,j}$ (single available track) |
| $J_i, S_i$ | ordered segments / stations of train $i$'s route |

## 2. Parameters

- $\bar a_{i,s}, \bar d_{i,s}$: scheduled arrival/departure times
- $r_{i,j,p}, e_{i,j,p}$: running time and energy of profile $p$ ($r$ larger for $P^{sing}$)
- $\underline{dw}_{i,s}, \overline{dw}_{i,s}$: dwell bounds; $h_j, h_s$: segment/station headways
- $C_s$: station track capacity; $T_{start}, T_{end}$: disruption window
- $\alpha_i$: delay weight; $\gamma_i$: cancellation penalty; $\beta$: energy price; $M$: big-M; $\varepsilon > 0$ small tolerance

## 3. Variables

- Continuous: $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0$ (actual times); $D_i \ge 0$ (destination delay)
- Binary: $x_{i,j,p}$ (profile choice); $z_i$ (cancellation); $y_{i,j}$ (use single track, $j \in J^D$); $w_{i,j}, p_{i,j}, r_{i,j}$ (disruption-window indicators); $z_{i,i',j}$ (segment ordering); $q_{i,i',s}$ (station overlap)

## 4. Objective

$$\min \; \sum_{i \in I} \alpha_i D_i \;+\; \sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i z_i \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J_i}\sum_{p \in P_{i,j}} e_{i,j,p}\, x_{i,j,p}$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Profile selection / cancellation:**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{i,j}} x_{i,j,p} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, j \in J_i$$

**(C2) Routing–profile consistency** (single-track profiles only if rerouted):
$$\sum_{p \in P^{sing}_{i,j}} x_{i,j,p} \le y_{i,j}, \qquad \sum_{p \in P^{norm}_{i,j}} x_{i,j,p} \le 1 - y_{i,j} \qquad \forall i,\ j \in J^D \cap J_i$$

**(C3) Timing propagation with selected profile:**
$$a_{i,s(j)+1} \ge d_{i,s(j)} + \sum_{p} r_{i,j,p}\, x_{i,j,p} - M z_i \qquad \forall i,\ j \in J_i$$
$$a_{i,s(j)+1} \le d_{i,s(j)} + \sum_{p} r_{i,j,p}\, x_{i,j,p} + M z_i \qquad \forall i,\ j \in J_i$$

**(C4) Dwell bounds** (relaxed if cancelled):
$$d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge \underline{dw}_{i,s} - M z_i, \qquad d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \overline{dw}_{i,s} + M z_i \qquad \forall i, s \in S_i$$

**(C5) Delay definition:**
$$D_i \ge a_{i,s^f_i} - \bar a_{i,s^f_i}, \qquad D_i \ge 0 \qquad \forall i$$

**(C6) Disruption-window indicators** ($j \in J^D \cap J_i$; entry $= d_{i,s(j)}$, exit $= a_{i,s(j)+1}$):
$$d_{i,s(j)} \ge T_{end} - M(1 - p_{i,j}), \qquad d_{i,s(j)} \le T_{end} - \varepsilon + M\, p_{i,j}$$
$$a_{i,s(j)+1} \le T_{start} + M(1 - r_{i,j}), \qquad a_{i,s(j)+1} \ge T_{start} + \varepsilon - M\, r_{i,j}$$
$$w_{i,j} \ge 1 - p_{i,j} - r_{i,j}$$
