**(C7) Routing rule on disrupted segments:**
$$y_{i,j} \le w_{i,j} \qquad \forall i,\ j \in J^D \cap J_i$$
An in-window train ($w_{i,j}=1$) either uses the single track ($y_{i,j}=1$, sequenced one-at-a-time by (C8a)) or keeps its normal track under unidirectional ordering (C8b). Trains with $w_{i,j}=0$ use their normal track with standard same-direction headways only.

**(C8) Conflict-free segment occupancy** (for all pairs $i \ne i'$ on $j$; relaxed by $M z_i$ terms for cancellations):

*(C8a) Single track, both rerouted ($y_{i,j}=y_{i',j}=1$):*
$$d_{i',s(j)} \ge a_{i,s(j)+1} + h_j - M(1 - z_{i,i',j}) - M(2 - y_{i,j} - y_{i',j})$$
$$d_{i,s(j)} \ge a_{i',s(j)+1} + h_j - M\, z_{i,i',j} - M(2 - y_{i,j} - y_{i',j})$$

*(C8b) Normal track during window ($w=1$, $y=0$), unidirectional sharing:*
$$d_{i',s(j)} \ge a_{i,s(j)+1} + h_j - M(1 - z_{i,i',j}) - M(2 - w_{i,j} - w_{i',j}) - M(y_{i,j} + y_{i',j})$$
$$d_{i,s(j)} \ge a_{i',s(j)+1} + h_j - M\, z_{i,i',j} - M(2 - w_{i,j} - w_{i',j}) - M(y_{i,j} + y_{i',j})$$

*(C8c) Outside window ($w=0$), standard same-direction headway (opposite directions on separate tracks need no constraint):*
$$d_{i',s(j)} \ge a_{i,s(j)+1} + h_j - M(1 - z_{i,i',j}) - M(w_{i,j} + w_{i',j}) - M\,\delta^{opp}_{i,i',j}$$
$$d_{i,s(j)} \ge a_{i',s(j)+1} + h_j - M\, z_{i,i',j} - M(w_{i,j} + w_{i',j}) - M\,\delta^{opp}_{i,i',j}$$
where $\delta^{opp}_{i,i',j}$ is a **parameter** equal to 1 iff the trains run in opposite directions (preprocessed; such pairs never share a track outside the window).

**(C9) Station capacity** via pairwise overlap binaries ($q_{i,i',s}=1$ iff train $i$ still dwells when $i'$ arrives):
$$d_{i,s} \le a_{i',s} + M\, q_{i,i',s} \qquad \forall i \ne i',\ s \in S_i \cap S_{i'}$$
$$\sum_{i \ne i'} q_{i,i',s} \le C_s - 1 \qquad \forall i', s \in S_{i'}$$
(Only the implication $d_{i,s} > a_{i',s} \Rightarrow q=1$ is needed; spurious $q=1$ is never beneficial.)

**(C10) Horizon:** $0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le T$ for all $i, s$.

## 6. Explicit Assumptions

1. Fixed station sequence per train (no rerouting via different stations); rerouting means using the opposite track within a segment.
2. Entry/exit of a segment = departure/arrival at its endpoint stations; no mid-segment stops.
3. Single-track profiles have longer running times, capturing the penalty of shared-track operation.
4. Headways are constant parameters; big-M $= T + \max h + 1$ is valid.
5. Cancelled trains consume no capacity, incur penalty $\gamma_i$, and their delay is not counted.
6. Opposite-direction trains on intact double-track segments are conflict-free by infrastructure; only during the window do they share the single track under (C8a).
7. Only destination delay is priced; intermediate delays propagate via (C3)–(C4).

All constraints are linear in continuous and binary variables; the model jointly optimizes retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed-profile selection, yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable with executable, energy-aware speed profiles.

Text:
# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Model (MILP)

Below are the equations of the complete linear model, based on the generated implementation. Assumptions (marked where inferred): double-track line with segments between consecutive stations; one disrupted segment with a known disruption time window [t₁, t₂] blocking one side; a finite set of pre-computed speed profiles per train per segment; big-M = time horizon H.

## Sets
- T — trains; S — stations; L — segments (i,j); P — speed profiles; K — directions/tracks {up, down}

## Parameters
- H (horizon), w_t (delay weight), pen_t (cancellation penalty), dwell_{t,s} (min dwell)
- a⁰_{t,s}, d⁰_{t,s} (scheduled arrival/departure)
- rt^min_{t,l}, rt^max_{t,l} (running time bounds); rt^p_{t,l,p}, e^p_{t,l,p} (profile running time and energy)
- h_arr, h_dep (headways); cap_s (station capacity); ecost (energy cost)
- Disruption: segment l*, window [t₁, t₂], blocked side

## Variables
- a_{t,s}, d_{t,s} ∈ [0, H] — actual arrival/departure times (retiming)
- x_{t,l,p} ∈ {0,1} — speed profile selection
- c_t ∈ {0,1} — train cancellation
- r_t ∈ {0,1} — rerouting to opposite track
- o_{t,l,t',l'} ∈ {0,1} — precedence: train t before t' on segment l
- y_{t,l} ∈ {0,1} — train occupies blocked side during disruption window
- z_{t,s,t',s} ∈ {0,1} — overlap indicator of trains dwelling at station s
- delay_t ≥ 0 — terminal delay of train t

## Objective
Minimize total weighted delay + cancellation penalties + energy cost:

min  Σ_t w_t · delay_t  +  Σ_t pen_t · c_t  +  ecost · Σ_{(t,l,p)} e^p_{t,l,p} · x_{t,l,p}

## Constraints

**(1) Timetable feasibility**
- Dwell: d_{t,s} ≥ a_{t,s} + dwell_{t,s} − H·c_t  ∀(t,s)
- Running time bounds: d_{t,i} + rt^min_{t,l} ≤ a_{t,j} ≤ d_{t,i} + rt^max_{t,l}  ∀(t,l=(i,j)), relaxed by ±H·c_t

**(2) Conflict-free headways (reordering)**
- Departure headway: d_{t',i} ≥ d_{t,i} + h_dep − H·(3 − o_{t,l,t',l'} − (1−c_t) − (1−c_{t'}))  ∀ t<t', same l
- Arrival headway: a_{t',j} ≥ a_{t,j} + h_arr − H·(3 − o_{t,l,t',l'} − (1−c_t) − (1−c_{t'}))  ∀ t<t', same l
- Order antisymmetry: o_{t,l,t',l'} + o_{t',l,t,l'} = 1 − c_t − c_{t'}  ∀ t<t', same l

**(3) Disruption / rerouting constraints**
- Blocked-side usage: y_{t,l*} ≤ r_t  ∀t (only rerouted trains may use the blocked side's track during the window)
- Window-overlap forcing (big-M linearization): y_{t,l*} ≥ 1 − r_t − (t₁ − d_{t,i})/H − (a_{t,j} − t₂)/H − c_t
- Single-track mutual exclusion for rerouted trains on l*: a_{t',j} ≥ d_{t,i} + ε − H·(4 − o_{t,l*,t',l*} − r_t − r_{t'} − (1−c_t) − (1−c_{t'}))  ∀ t<t'

**(4) Speed profile consistency**
- Exactly one profile: Σ_p x_{t,l,p} = 1 − c_t  ∀(t,l)
- Running time equals profile time: a_{t,j} − d_{t,i} = Σ_p rt^p_{t,l,p}·x_{t,l,p}, enforced pairwise via:
  - a_{t,j} − d_{t,i} ≤ rt^p_{t,l,p} + H·(1 − x_{t,l,p}) + H·c_t
  - a_{t,j} − d_{t,i} ≥ rt^p_{t,l,p} − H·(1 − x_{t,l,p}) − H·c_t  ∀(t,l,p)

**(5) Cancellation logic**
- r_t ≤ 1 − c_t (cancelled trains neither run nor reroute); all timing/resource constraints relaxed via H·c_t terms

**(6) Station capacity**
- Overlap definition: z_{t,s,t',s} ≥ 1 − (d_{t',s} − a_{t,s})/H − c_t − c_{t'}  ∀ t<t' stopping at s
- Capacity count: Σ_{t<t'} z_{t,s,t',s} ≤ cap_s·(cap_s − 1)/2  ∀s

**(7) Delay definition & horizon**
- delay_t ≥ a_{t,terminal(t)} − a⁰_{t,terminal(t)} − H·c_t; delay_t ≥ 0
- d_{t,s} ≤ H·(1 − c_t)  ∀(t,s)

**Assumptions made:** fixed train paths/stopping pattern (no full rerouting via alternative stations, only track swap on the disrupted segment); discrete pre-enumerated speed profiles per train-segment (consistent with the paper's train-plan decomposition); headways constant; delay measured at the terminal station; big-M = H.

Text:
# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor consists of stations (or blocks) indexed by $i \in I = \{1,\dots,n\}$ and segments $s \in S = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$ (segment $s$ connects stations $s$ and $s+1$). Trains $j \in J$ are scheduled on a nominal timetable. A partial blockage disables one track of a segment $s \in S^D \subseteq S$ during time window $[T_s^{start}, T_s^{end}]$. Affected trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-track operation) within the window, requiring coordination of bidirectional trains.

**Assumptions (marked where not given in the input):**
- (A1) Each train travels in one direction (up or down) at constant commercial characteristics; trains do not overtake except at stations *(standard assumption)*.
- (A2) Each segment can host at most one train at a time per track; headway times are aggregated into minimum running/dwell/headway times *(as in D'Ariano et al. 2008)*.
- (A3) Speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of precomputed profiles per train and segment, each with fixed running time and energy consumption *(discretization assumption, standard in integrated models, cf. Zhan et al. 2022)*.
- (A4) Disruption start time is known; end time is known (deterministic case).
- (A5) Cancellation is allowed with a fixed penalty *(assumption)*.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $J$ | set of trains; $J^{up}, J^{down}$: directional subsets |
| $I, S$ | stations, segments |
| $S^D$ | disrupted segments; $[T_s^{start}, T_s^{end}]$ disruption window on $s$ |
| $a_{j,i}^{nom}, d_{j,i}^{nom}$ | nominal arrival/departure times of train $j$ at station $i$ |
| $w_i^{min}, w_i^{max}$ | min/max dwell time of train $j$ at station $i$ (assume $w_i^{min}$ uniform, $w_i^{max}$ given) |
| $r_{j,s}^{min}$ | minimum running time of train $j$ on segment $s$ (unblocked track) |
| $h$ | minimum headway time (same track, same/different direction) |
| $K_{j,s}$ | set of admissible speed profiles for train $j$ on segment $s$; profile $k$ has running time $\rho_{j,s}^k$ and energy $e_{j,s}^k$ |
| $M$ | large constant |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | weights for total delay, energy, cancellations |
| $c_j$ | cancellation penalty of train $j$ |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{j,i}, d_{j,i} \in \mathbb{R}_+$ | actual arrival / departure time of $j$ at $i$ |
| $x_{j,s}^k \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $j$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $y_{j,s} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $j$ is rerouted to the opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $z_j \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $j$ is cancelled |
| $\delta_{j,j',s} \in \{0,1\}$ | sequencing: 1 if $j$ enters segment $s$ before $j'$ (same track) |
| $\delta^-_{j,j',s}, \delta^+_{j,j',s} \in \{0,1\}$ | sequencing on the opposite track (used when rerouting) |
| $D_{j,i} \ge 0$ | arrival delay of $j$ at $i$ |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{j\in J}\sum_{i\in I} D_{j,i} \;+\; \beta \sum_{j\in J}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K_{j,s}} e_{j,s}^k\, x_{j,s}^k \;+\; \gamma \sum_{j\in J} c_j z_j
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable consistency (uncancelled trains):** for all $j$, consecutive stations $i, i+1$, segment $s=i$:

$$
d_{j,i} + \sum_{k\in K_{j,s}} \rho_{j,s}^k\, x_{j,s}^k = a_{j,i+1} \quad \forall j,\; s=i
$$

**(C2) Dwell times:**

$$
w_i^{min} \le a_{j,i} - d_{j,i} \le w_i^{max} \quad \forall j, i \quad(\text{linearized with } M(1-z_j) \text{ slack if cancelled})
$$

**(C3) Speed profile selection (exactly one):**

$$
\sum_{k\in K_{j,s}} x_{j,s}^k = 1 - z_j \quad \forall j, s
$$

**(C4) Minimum running time bound (profile feasibility):**

$$
a_{j,i+1} - d_{j,i} \ge \sum_k \rho_{j,s}^k x_{j,s}^k \ge r_{j,s}^{min}
$$

**(C5) Rerouting logic:** rerouting is only possible on disrupted segments and only within the disruption window; a rerouted train must enter segment $s$ inside $[T_s^{start}, T_s^{end}]$:

$$
y_{j,s} \le \mathbb{1}[s \in S^D] \quad \forall j,s
$$
$$
d_{j,i} \ge T_s^{start} - M(1-y_{j,s}), \qquad d_{j,i} \le T_s^{end} + M(1-y_{j,s}) \quad \forall j,\; s=i\in S^D
$$

**(C6) Conflict-freedom on the default track:** for each segment $s$ and pair $j<j'$ (same direction or meeting on default track), enforce headway via big-M disjunctions:

$$
d_{j',i} \ge a_{j,i+1} + h - M(1-\delta_{j,j',s}) - M z_{j'} - M z_j
$$
$$
d_{j,i} \ge a_{j',i+1} + h - M\,\delta_{j,j',s} - M z_{j'} - M z_j
$$

**(C7) Conflict-freedom on the opposite (rerouted) track:** for pairs of trains actually using the opposite track ($y_{j,s}=y_{j',s}=1$):

$$
d_{j',i} \ge a_{j,i+1} + h - M(1-\delta^-_{j,j',s}) - M(1-y_{j,s}) - M(1-y_{j',s})
$$
$$
d_{j,i} \ge a_{j',i+1} + h - M\,\delta^-_{j,j',s} - M(1-y_{j,s}) - M(1-y_{j',s})
$$

**(C8) Disrupted-track closure:** during the window, no train may use the blocked track of $s\in S^D$:

$$
d_{j,i} \ge T_s^{start} - M\, y_{j,s}, \qquad a_{j,i+1} \le T_s^{end} + M\, y_{j,s} \quad \forall j,\; s=i\in S^D
$$

(i.e., trains either complete the segment before the window or reroute).

**(C9) Delay definition:**

$$
D_{j,i} \ge a_{j,i} - a_{j,i}^{nom}, \qquad D_{j,i} \ge 0 \quad \forall j,i
$$

**(C10) Cancellation propagation:** if $z_j = 1$, all times are free (big-M relaxed) and no resources are consumed:

$$
a_{j,i}, d_{j,i} \le M z_j + M(1-z_j)\cdot(\text{bound}), \qquad \delta_{j,j',s}\text{-constraints relaxed by } M z_j, M z_{j'}
$$

**(C11) Station capacity / no overtaking unless scheduled (optional):** at most one train occupying a station track at a time, enforced analogously to (C6) with departure/arrival headways at station $i$.

**(C12) Variable domains:**

$$
a_{j,i}, d_{j,i}, D_{j,i} \ge 0; \quad x_{j,s}^k, y_{j,s}, z_j, \delta_{j,j',s}, \delta^-_{j,j',s} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Coupling of TRP and TSMP** is achieved through (C1)/(C4): the chosen speed profile $k$ determines the actual running time, which must be consistent with the rescheduled arrival/departure times — the timetable is feasible only if an executable profile exists.
- **Rerouting** is modeled by binary $y_{j,s}$ with window constraints (C5), closure constraints (C8), and dedicated conflict constraints (C7) for bidirectional sharing of the open track.
- The model is a valid MILP: all constraints are linear; disjunctions use standard big-$M$.
- As stated in the paper, this MILP can be decomposed into an IP over train interactions and single-train plans (each plan = a feasible combination of times, route and profile per train), with an adaptive iterative refinement of plan granularity; for sufficiently fine plans the IP is equivalent to this MILP.

Below is the final, complete MILP for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under a partial segment blockage, after two rounds of review and refinement.

---

# TRSMP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

## Problem setting and assumptions

- A double-track high-speed corridor with stations $s = 1,\dots,m$; segment $j$ connects stations $j$ and $j+1$, $j \in J = \{1,\dots,m-1\}$.
- During the disruption window $[T_1, T_2]$, segment $j^*$ is partially blocked: only the **up track** remains usable. Down-direction trains traversing $j^*$ during the window must be **rerouted** onto the up track, and all trains sharing a track must be separated by a minimum headway (bidirectional conflict resolution).
- **Assumption (marked):** for each train $i$ and segment $j$, a finite set $P_{i,j}$ of precomputed speed profiles is given, each with running time $r_{i,j,p}$ and energy $E_{i,j,p}$; this keeps the model linear.
- Trains may be retimed, reordered, rerouted (during the window), or cancelled (with penalty).
- All times lie in a horizon $[0, T]$; $M_T = T$ is a valid big-M, with tighter values noted where applicable.

## Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$, $D \subset I$, $U = I \setminus D$ | trains; down-/up-direction trains |
| $P_{i,j}$ | speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $r_{i,j,p},\ E_{i,j,p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $dw^{\min}_{i,s}, dw^{\max}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $a^{sch}_{i,s}, d^{sch}_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure |
| $h_j,\ h^{arr}_s,\ h^{dep}_s$ | segment / station arrival / departure headways |
| $w_i,\ \gamma_i,\ \alpha$ | delay weight, cancellation penalty, energy coefficient |
| $M_W = (T_2 - T_1) + \max_{i,p} r_{i,j^*,p}$ | tight big-M for window constraints |

## Decision variables

- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in [0,T]$: actual arrival/departure times (continuous).
- $e_{i,j}, t_{i,j} \in [0,T]$: entry (departure from station $j$) and exit (arrival at station $j+1$) times on segment $j$.
- $x_{i,j,p} \in \{0,1\}$: profile selection.
- $y_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $j$ (meaningful only for $i \in D$, $j = j^*$).
- $b_{i,j} \in \{0,1\}$: occupancy of segment $j$ overlaps the disruption window.
- $z_{i,k,j} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering on segment $j$ ($=1$ if $i$ exits before $k$ enters).
- $z^{arr}_{i,k,s}, z^{dep}_{i,k,s} \in \{0,1\}$: station ordering variables.
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: cancellation.
- $\delta^{arr}_i, \delta^{dep}_i, \delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: delay variables.

## Objective

$$
\min \;\; \sum_{i \in I} w_i \left(\delta^{arr}_i + \delta^{dep}_i\right)
\;+\; \sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i\, c_i
\;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} \sum_{p \in P_{i,j}} E_{i,j,p}\, x_{i,j,p}
$$

(Weighted delays + cancellation penalties + total energy over **all** segments, including the blocked one.)

## Constraints

**(1) Profile selection** — exactly one speed profile per segment for non-cancelled trains:
$$\sum_{p \in P_{i,j}} x_{i,j,p} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall j \in J$$

**(2) Running-time consistency** (linearized, relaxed if cancelled):
$$t_{i,j} - e_{i,j} - \sum_p r_{i,j,p}\, x_{i,j,p} \le M_T\, c_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall j$$
$$e_{i,j} + \sum_p r_{i,j,p}\, x_{i,j,p} - t_{i,j} \le M_T\, c_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall j$$

**(3) Link to station times:**
$$e_{i,j} = d_{i,j}, \qquad t_{i,j} = a_{i,j+1} \qquad \forall i,\ \forall j \in J$$
Time progression along the route is monotone by construction ($r_{i,j,p} \ge 0$); no extra ordering constraints are needed.

**(4) Dwell times** (intermediate stations):
$$dw^{\min}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le dw^{\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s \in \{2,\dots,m-1\}$$

**(5) Disruption-window crossing indicator** on $j = j^*$ ($b_{i,j}=1 \Leftrightarrow$ occupancy overlaps $[T_1,T_2]$, for non-cancelled trains):
$$e_{i,j} \le T_2 + M_W(1 - b_{i,j}) \qquad \forall i$$
$$t_{i,j} \ge T_1 - M_W(1 - b_{i,j}) \qquad \forall i$$
$$e_{i,j} \ge T_2 - M_W\, b_{i,j} - M_T c_i \qquad \forall i$$
$$t_{i,j} \le T_1 + M_W\, b_{i,j} + M_T c_i \qquad \forall i$$

**(6) Rerouting logic** — down trains crossing the window must use the available (up) track; up trains never reroute:
$$y_{i,j^*} \ge b_{i,j^*} \qquad \forall i \in D$$
$$y_{i,j} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in U,\ \forall j; \quad y_{i,j} = 0 \ \ \forall i \in D,\ j \ne j^*$$

**(7) Track-usage indicators** (affine in $y$, no extra binaries), for $j = j^*$:
$$u^{\text{up}}_{i,j} = \begin{cases} 1 - y_{i,j} & i \in U \\ y_{i,j} & i \in D \end{cases}, \qquad u^{\text{down}}_{i,j} = \begin{cases} y_{i,j} & i \in U \\ 1 - y_{i,j} & i \in D \end{cases}$$
For $j \ne j^*$: $u^{\text{up}}_{i,j} = 1$ if $i \in U$, else $0$ (and vice versa).

**(8) Blocked track unavailable during the window:**
$$u^{\text{down}}_{i,j^*} \le 1 - b_{i,j^*} \qquad \forall i$$
(Together with (6), this forces every train overlapping the window onto the single available track.)

**(9) Occupancy non-overlap with headway** on each track $q$ of each segment $j$ (true interval separation, not just entry times):
$$t_{i,j} + h_j \le e_{k,j} + (T + h_j)\left(3 - u^q_{i,j} - u^q_{k,j} - z_{i,k,j}\right) \qquad \forall i < k,\ \forall j,\ \forall q$$
$$t_{k,j} + h_j \le e_{i,j} + (T + h_j)\left(2 - u^q_{i,j} - u^q_{k,j} + z_{i,k,j}\right) \qquad \forall i < k,\ \forall j,\ \forall q$$
If both trains use track $q$, $z_{i,k,j}=1$ activates the first, $z_{i,k,j}=0$ the second.

**(10) Station headways** (optional), for pairs $i < k$ at station $s$:
$$a_{k,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h^{arr}_s - M_T(1 - z^{arr}_{i,k,s}) - M_T(c_i + c_k)$$
$$a_{i,s} \ge a_{k,s} + h^{arr}_s - M_T\, z^{arr}_{i,k,s} - M_T(c_i + c_k)$$
$$d_{k,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{dep}_s - M_T(1 - z^{dep}_{i,k,s}) - M_T(c_i + c_k)$$
$$d_{i,s} \ge d_{k,s} + h^{dep}_s - M_T\, z^{dep}_{i,k,s} - M_T(c_i + c_k)$$

**(11) Cancellation propagation** — cancelled trains consume no capacity:
$$a_{i,s},\, d_{i,s},\, e_{i,j},\, t_{i,j} \le T(1 - c_i) \qquad \forall i,\ s,\ j$$

**(12) Delay definitions** (nonnegative, so early arrivals are not rewarded):
$$\delta^{arr}_i \ge a_{i,m} - a^{sch}_{i,m}, \qquad \delta^{dep}_i \ge d_{i,1} - d^{sch}_{i,1} \qquad \forall i$$
$$\delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^{sch}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\ s = 2,\dots,m-1 \ \text{(optional)}$$
$$\delta^{arr}_i, \delta^{dep}_i, \delta_{i,s} \ge 0$$

**(13) Horizon and ordering:**
$$0 \le a_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} \le T \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s$$

## How the model captures the problem

- **Retiming/reordering:** continuous $a, d, e, t$ variables plus big-M disjunctions via $z$ allow flexible times and train sequences.
- **Speed management:** constraint (1)–(2) select exactly one profile per segment, fixing running time and energy linearly; the objective trades faster/more energy-hungry profiles against delays.
- **Partial blockage & rerouting:** (5)–(8) detect window-crossing trains and force down trains onto the single available track; (9) sequences **all** trains sharing that track — regardless of direction — by full occupancy intervals with headway $h_j$, guaranteeing conflict-free bidirectional operation.
- **Linearity:** every disjunction is expressed with big-M constants and binaries; track-usage indicators are affine functions of $y_{i,j}$. The model is a pure MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut, and is the basis for the decomposition into a train-plan selection IP with adaptive plan refinement described in the paper's solution framework.

Text:
# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem setting and assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $S=\{0,1,\dots,|S|-1\}$ and segments $E$ between consecutive stations. Each segment $e$ has two directed tracks: the *scheduled* track (per train direction) and the *opposite* track. A partial blockage disables the scheduled track of a set of segments $E^D \subseteq E$ during time window $[T^s, T^e]$. Trains may either wait or **reroute** onto the opposite track (single-file, bidirectional use), with speed limited to $V^{lim}$ there.

**Assumptions (stated explicitly, as information was partially missing):**
- (A1) Trains run on a fixed sequence of stations (no turning-back, no short-turning); each train visits all stations.
- (A2) Each segment is traversed with a single speed profile chosen from a finite, pre-generated set of profiles (discretization of the speed-management problem; each profile is dynamically feasible and satisfies traction/braking limits).
- (A3) A train occupies a segment exclusively (block section principle); headway is enforced by non-overlap of occupancy intervals.
- (A4) Dwell times are bounded, arrival/departure times integer (minutes or seconds).
- (A5) Cancellation is not allowed (fixed demand); if desired, add binary $z_i$ and relax constraints accordingly.
- (A6) The disruption window and affected segments are known deterministically at the start of the recovery horizon $[0,T]$.

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains (both directions); $I^+ , I^-$ trains in the two directions |
| $E$ | segments; $E^D$ blocked segments; $E(e)$ segments on train $i$'s path |
| $P_i$ | set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $e$ |
| $r_{ipe}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $e$ with profile $p$ |
| $\varepsilon_{ipe}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $e$ with profile $p$ |
| $R_{ie}$ | maximum allowed running time on segment $e$ (recovery limit) |
| $\underline d_i,\overline d_i$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ at a station |
| $a_i^0, d_i^0$ | original scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at a station |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ |
| $M$ | big-M (horizon length $T$) |
| $V^{lim}$ | speed limit on the opposite (rerouted) track → profile set restricted to slow profiles $P_i^{slow}$ |

## 3. Decision variables

- $a_{is}, d_{is} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $x_{ipe} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $e$.
- $y_{ie} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** onto the opposite track on segment $e$.
- $\sigma_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable; $\sigma_{ij}=1$ if train $i$ passes (station or segment) before train $j$.
- $u_{ie} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ during the disruption window.

## 4. Model

### Objective

Minimize weighted total delay plus energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I} w_i \sum_{s\in S_i} \big[(a_{is}-a_i^0) + (d_{is}-d_i^0)\big]}_{\text{total (weighted) delay}}
\;+\; \lambda \underbrace{\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{e\in E(i)}\sum_{p\in P_i} \varepsilon_{ipe}\, x_{ipe}}_{\text{total energy}}
$$

with weighting factor $\lambda$ converting kWh into delay-equivalent cost. *(Assumption: linear delay and energy; both terms are linear in the variables.)*

### Constraints

**(C1) Timetable consistency (running and dwell times):**
$$
d_{is} + \sum_{p\in P_i} r_{ip,e(s)} x_{ip,e(s)} = a_{i,s+1} \qquad \forall i,\; s = 0,\dots,|S|-2 \tag{1}
$$
$$
a_{is} + \underline d_i \le d_{is} \le a_{is} + \overline d_i \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S \setminus\{0, |S|-1\} \tag{2}
$$

**(C2) Exactly one speed profile per segment:**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_i} x_{ipe} = 1 \qquad \forall i,\; e \in E(i) \tag{3}
$$

**(C3) Running-time recovery bound:**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_i} r_{ipe}\, x_{ipe} \le R_{ie} \qquad \forall i,\; e\in E(i) \tag{4}
$$

**(C4) Rerouting logic.** If train $i$ uses the opposite track on blocked segment $e$ during the disruption window, only slow profiles are allowed:
$$
y_{ie} \le \sum_{p \in P_i^{slow}} x_{ipe} \qquad \forall i,\; e \in E^D \tag{5}
$$
$$
u_{ie} \ge \frac{a_{i,e^-} - T^e}{M} + \frac{T^s - d_{i,e^+}}{M} - 1,\qquad
u_{ie} \le 1 - \frac{a_{i,e^-} - T^e}{M},\quad
u_{ie} \le 1 - \frac{T^s - d_{i,e^+}}{M} \tag{6}
$$
where $e^-, e^+$ are the stations bounding segment $e$ (i.e., $u_{ie}=1$ iff the traversal overlaps $[T^s,T^e]$). Then:
$$
y_{ie} \ge u_{ie} \qquad \forall i,\; e\in E^D \tag{7}
$$
*(Assumption A: trains whose scheduled track is blocked during their passage **must** reroute; they may not wait for the disruption to end. Replace (7) by $y_{ie}=u_{ie}$ to force this, or by $y_{ie}\ge u_{ie}$ to allow waiting.)*

**(C5) Segment capacity — no two trains share a segment simultaneously.** For each segment $e$ and each pair of trains $i<j$ that both may use $e$:
$$
d_{i,e^-} \;\le\; a_{j,e^+} - \sum_p r_{jp,e}x_{jp,e} + M(3 - \sigma_{ij} - x^{seg}_{ie} - x^{seg}_{je}) \tag{8a}
$$
$$
d_{j,e^-} \;\le\; a_{i,e^+} - \sum_p r_{ip,e}x_{ip,e} + M(2 - \sigma_{ij} + x^{seg}_{ie} + x^{seg}_{je}) \tag{8b}
$$
where $x^{seg}_{ie}=\sum_p x_{ipe}$ and $\sigma_{ij}=1$ means $i$ precedes $j$. These two big-M constraints enforce non-overlapping occupancy in either order.

**(C6) Station headway (same-direction and crossing conflicts at stations):** for trains $i\ne j$ at station $s$:
$$
d_{is} \le a_{js} + M(1-\sigma_{ijs}) \qquad\text{or}\qquad d_{js} \le a_{is} + M\,\sigma_{ijs} \tag{9}
$$
implemented as two complementary big-M inequalities with ordering variable $\sigma_{ijs}$.

**(C7) Overtaking / consistency of ordering variables along the line** (FIFO-like consistency, allowing overtaking only where station tracks permit — assumption: all stations have ≥2 platform tracks, so overtaking is allowed everywhere but must be consistent):
$$
\sigma_{ij,s} \le \sigma_{ij,s+1} + \sigma_{ij,s+1}' \quad\text{(linearized consistency; standard transitivity cuts)} \tag{10}
$$
$$
\sigma_{ij} + \sigma_{ji} = 1,\qquad \sigma_{ij} + \sigma_{jk} - \sigma_{ik} \le 1 \qquad \forall i<j<k \tag{11}
$$

**(C8) Horizon and initial conditions:**
$$
0 \le a_{is} \le d_{is} \le T \qquad \forall i,s \tag{12}
$$
$$
a_{i,0} = a_i^{0},\qquad d_{i,0}=d_i^0 \qquad \forall i \tag{13}
$$

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{is}, d_{is}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0};\quad x_{ipe},\, y_{ie},\, \sigma_{ij}\in\{0,1\} \tag{14}
$$

## 5. Remarks

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear; products such as $r_{ipe}x_{ipe}$ do not appear (the sum over profiles handles the choice), and pair conflicts use standard big-M disjunctions — hence the model is a genuine MILP.
- **Rerouting conflicts:** Constraints (8) apply to *all* pairs on a segment regardless of direction, which automatically coordinates bidirectional trains sharing the opposite track during the disruption window.
- **Equivalence to speed profiles:** By (1), (3), (4), the chosen timetable times are exactly consistent with a dynamically feasible profile, ensuring control-level executability (the coupling between TRP and TSMP).
- **Solution approach (as in the paper):** The model decomposes into (i) a master IP over ordering variables $\sigma$ selecting among train-plan candidates (profile + route combinations per train) and (ii) per-train timing subproblems; an adaptive iterative scheme refines the candidate plan sets near the incumbent solution, with local branching to accelerate convergence. For sufficiently fine profile discretization the IP is equivalent to the MILP above.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations (or block sections) indexed along the line. A disruption partially blocks one track of a segment during a known time window. Affected trains may either wait or **reroute onto the opposite track** (single-track operation in the disrupted segment), subject to bidirectional conflict avoidance. For each train and each inter-station run, a finite set of **candidate speed profiles** (e.g., "fast/energy-intensive", "slow/energy-saving") is pre-generated; selecting a profile fixes the running time and energy consumption.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) The disruption time window [T^s, T^e] and blocked segment are known in advance (deterministic disruption).
- (A2) Candidate speed profiles per train and section are pre-computed by a train-dynamics simulator; each profile is characterized by a running time and energy consumption (discretization assumption).
- (A3) Rolling stock is not re-circulated within the planning horizon (each train runs once); *assumption*.
- (A4) Minimum headways are constant per track section; *assumption*.
- (A5) Cancellation is not allowed (all trains must run); *assumption* — could be relaxed with an additional binary and penalty.
- (A6) Dwell times may be extended but not shortened below a minimum.

## 2. Sets and Indices

- $I$: trains, $i \in I$
- $S$: stations, $s \in S$; ordered along the line
- $A_i \subseteq S$: stations at which train $i$ stops (ordered)
- $K$: track sections between consecutive stations, $k \in K$; each section has two tracks: $t \in \{1,2\}$ (1 = normal track for the train's direction, 2 = opposite track)
- $P_{ik}$: candidate speed profiles of train $i$ on section $k$, $p \in P_{ik}$

## 3. Parameters

- $T^s, T^e$: disruption start and end time
- $K^d \subseteq K$: disrupted sections (one track blocked in $[T^s, T^e]$)
- $r^{p}_{ik}$: running time of train $i$ on section $k$ with profile $p$
- $e^{p}_{ik}$: energy consumption of train $i$ on section $k$ with profile $p$
- $d^{sched}_i, a^{sched}_i$: scheduled departure/arrival times of train $i$ (at origin/destination)
- $\underline{dw}_{is}, \overline{dw}_{is}$: min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $h$: minimum headway (time) between trains on the same track of a section
- $M$: big constant (horizon length)
- $\alpha$: weight of total delay in the objective; $\beta$: weight of energy
- $\tau^{arr}, \tau^{dep}$: safety margins for arrival/departure headways

## 4. Decision Variables

- $a_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{is} \ge 0$: actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $x_{ikt} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses track $t$ of section $k$
- $y_{ikp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ runs profile $p$ on section $k$
- $z_{ik} \ge 0$: entry time of train $i$ into section $k$
- $D_{is} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (defined by constraints)

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize weighted sum of total delay and total energy:

$$\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in A_i} D_{is} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{k \in K}\sum_{p \in P_{ik}} e^{p}_{ik}\, y_{ikp}$$

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable consistency — section entry/exit times.** For each train $i$, section $k$ between stations $s$ and $s'$, and profile $p$:

$$z_{ik} \ge d_{is} \quad \forall i,k \text{ adjacent to } s$$
$$a_{is'} = z_{ik} + \sum_{p \in P_{ik}} r^{p}_{ik}\, y_{ikp} \quad \forall i, k=(s,s')$$

**(C2) Profile selection — uniqueness.**

$$\sum_{p \in P_{ik}} y_{ikp} = 1 \quad \forall i,k$$

**(C3) Rerouting — track choice.** Each train uses exactly one track per section:

$$x_{ik1} + x_{ik2} = 1 \quad \forall i,k$$

Rerouting onto the opposite track is only meaningful in disrupted sections; outside the disruption, track 2 use is forbidden (or allowed with no benefit):

$$x_{ik2} = 0 \quad \forall i, k \notin K^d$$

**(C4) Disruption time window.** A train may traverse a disrupted section on the blocked track (track 1) only outside the disruption window; using the opposite track (track 2) is always possible:

$$z_{ik} \ge T^e - M(1 - x_{ik1}) \quad \forall i, k \in K^d \text{ (direction A)}$$
$$z_{ik} + \sum_p r^p_{ik} y_{ikp} \le T^s + M(1 - x_{ik1}) \quad \forall i, k \in K^d \text{ (direction A)}$$

i.e., if train $i$ uses the blocked track, it must fully clear the section before $T^s$ or enter after $T^e$. *(Analogous constraints apply for trains of the opposite direction with track roles swapped.)*

**(C5) Bidirectional conflict-free headways on shared track.** For each disrupted section $k \in K^d$ and each pair of trains $i, j$ of **opposite directions** (both may use track 2):

$$z_{jk} \ge z_{ik} + \sum_p r^p_{ik} y_{ikp} + h - M(2 - x_{ik2} - x_{jk2}) \quad \forall i<j,\; k \in K^d$$
$$z_{ik} \ge z_{jk} + \sum_p r^p_{jk} y_{jkp} + h - M(2 - x_{ik2} - x_{jk2}) \quad \forall i<j,\; k \in K^d$$

The big-$M$ deactivates the constraint unless both trains occupy the shared track.

**(C6) Same-direction headways.** For trains $i,j$ in the same direction on any section $k$ and track $t$:

$$z_{jk} \ge z_{ik} + \sum_p r^p_{ik} y_{ikp} + h - M(3 - x_{ikt} - x_{jkt} - \sigma_{ij}) \quad \forall i<j,\; k,t$$

where $\sigma_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ is an ordering variable ($\sigma_{ij}=1$ if $i$ precedes $j$), with

$$\sigma_{ij} + \sigma_{ji} = 1 \quad \forall i<j$$

*(Symmetric counterpart constraints enforce the reverse ordering.)*

**(C7) Station capacity / dwell times.**

$$d_{is} \ge a_{is} + \underline{dw}_{is} \quad \forall i,s \in A_i$$
$$d_{is} \le a_{is} + \overline{dw}_{is} \quad \forall i,s \in A_i$$

**(C8) Delay definition.**

$$D_{is} \ge a_{is} - a^{sched}_{is} \quad \forall i,s \in A_i, \qquad D_{is} \ge 0$$

**(C9) Schedule bounds.**

$$d_{i, o(i)} \ge d^{sched}_i \quad \forall i, \qquad a_{i, f(i)} \ge a^{sched}_i \quad \forall i$$

**(C10) Variable domains.**

$$a_{is}, d_{is}, z_{ik}, D_{is} \ge 0; \qquad x_{ikt}, y_{ikp}, \sigma_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$$

## 7. Remarks

- **Linearity:** All constraints are linear; products of binaries are avoided via big-$M$ linearization (C5, C6).
- **Coupling TRP–TSMP:** Constraints (C1)–(C2) link timetable times to chosen speed profiles; the objective (C-energy term) makes the rescheduling and speed-management decisions jointly optimal, so the resulting timetable is guaranteed executable at the control level.
- **Equivalence note:** As stated in the source, with a sufficiently fine discretization of candidate profiles $P_{ik}$, this MILP is equivalent to the exact integrated problem; the decomposition into an IP over train interactions plus per-train plans (each plan = a combination of $y_{ikp}, x_{ikt}$ and implied times) and the adaptive iterative refinement apply directly to this formulation.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP (Equations Only)

## Sets and Parameters
- Trains *i, j* ∈ {1,…,I}; stations *s* = 1,…,S; segments *k* = (s, s+1), s = 1,…,S−1
- Speed profiles *p* ∈ P_{i,k} with running time r_{i,k,p} and energy e_{i,k,p} (pre-discretized — **assumption**)
- Scheduled arrival/departure A⁰_{i,s}, D⁰_{i,s}; minimum dwell D_min_{i,s}; headway h; max delay U_max_i
- Disruption window [T_start, T_end] on blocked segments K^B (one track blocked — **assumption**)
- Weights w^d, w^e, w^r, w^c; big-M; horizon [0, T_max]

## Variables
- a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} ≥ 0: arrival/departure times of train i at station s
- u_{i,s} ≥ 0: delay of train i at station s
- x_{i,k,p} ∈ {0,1}: train i uses profile p on segment k
- y_{i,k} ∈ {0,1}: train i rerouted to opposite track on segment k (only defined for k ∈ K^B)
- z_{i,j,k} ∈ {0,1}: train i precedes train j on segment k (same direction, same actual track)
- b_{i,j,k} ∈ {0,1}: bidirectional ordering on shared rerouted track (opposing pairs, k ∈ K^B)
- g_{i,k} ∈ {0,1}: train i occupies segment k during the disruption window
- c_i ∈ {0,1}: train i is cancelled

## Objective
min  Σ_i Σ_s w^d·u_{i,s} + Σ_i Σ_k Σ_p w^e·e_{i,k,p}·x_{i,k,p} + Σ_i Σ_{k∈K^B} w^r·y_{i,k} + Σ_i w^c·c_i

## Constraints

**(1) Speed profile selection and running time** (∀i, k=(s,s+1)):
- Σ_p x_{i,k,p} = 1 − c_i
- d_{i,s} + Σ_p r_{i,k,p}·x_{i,k,p} = a_{i,s+1} + M·c_i  (equality relaxed by big-M if cancelled)

**(2) Minimum dwell** (∀i, s):  d_{i,s} − a_{i,s} ≥ D_min_{i,s} − M·c_i

**(3) Delay definition and cap** (∀i, s):
- a_{i,s} − A⁰_{i,s} ≤ u_{i,s} + M·c_i
- u_{i,s} ≤ U_max_i

**(4) Same-direction headway on the same actual track** (∀ ordered pairs i,j with same direction, ∀k):
- z_{i,j,k} + z_{j,i,k} = 1 if trains i and j use the same actual track (linear expression of y_{i,k}, y_{j,k}); z_{i,j,k} + z_{j,i,k} ≤ 1 otherwise
- If z_{i,j,k} = 1:  a_{i,s+1} + h ≤ a_{j,s+1} + M(1 − z_{i,j,k}) + M(c_i + c_j) and d_{i,s} + h ≤ d_{j,s} + M(1 − z_{i,j,k}) + M(c_i + c_j); symmetric constraints for z_{j,i,k} = 1

**(5) Bidirectional conflict on shared rerouted track** (∀ opposing pairs i<j, k ∈ K^B), where "both" = y_{i,k} + y_{j,k} − (c_i + c_j):
- If b_{i,j,k} = 1:  d_{i,s} + h − a_{j,s} ≤ M(1 − b_{i,j,k}) + M(2 − both)  (j enters only after i fully clears)
- If b_{i,j,k} = 0:  d_{j,s} + h − a_{i,s} ≤ M·b_{i,j,k} + M(2 − both)  (i enters only after j fully clears)

**(6) Rerouting logic** (∀i, k ∈ K^B):
- y_{i,k} ≤ g_{i,k}  (rerouting only if the train's passage overlaps the disruption window)
- g_{i,k} = 1 iff a_{i,s} ≤ T_end and d_{i,s} ≥ T_start (enforced via big-M indicator constraints, relaxed by M·c_i)

**(7) Disruption window on blocked track** (∀i, k ∈ K^B), with uses_blocked = 1 − y_{i,k} − c_i:
- Either the train fully exits before T_start or enters after T_end:
  d_{i,s} ≤ T_start + M(1 − uses_blocked) + M(1 − g_{i,k}) + M·c_i
  a_{i,s} ≥ T_end − M(1 − uses_blocked) + M(1 − g_{i,k}) − M·c_i

**(8) Horizon bounds** (∀i, s):  0 ≤ a_{i,s} ≤ d_{i,s} ≤ T_max

## Key Assumptions (marked)
1. Speed profiles are pre-generated and discretized, so running time and energy are linear coefficients — this keeps the model MILP.
2. Rerouting is only permitted on blocked segments and only for trains whose passage overlaps the disruption window.
3. Cancellations fully relax a train's timing/resource constraints via big-M terms, with a fixed penalty w^c.
4. Headways are uniform (h) on all segments; bidirectional sharing requires complete segment occupancy (no meets mid-segment).
5. Delay is measured as positive deviation of arrivals from the planned timetable.

# Final MILP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Assumptions

- **A1.** Double-track corridor; each segment has an up/down track. Segment $s_b$ is partially blocked: its scheduled-direction track $k^{blk}$ is unavailable during $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$; the opposite track $k^{alt}$ remains usable (single-track bidirectional operation).
- **A2.** For each train–segment pair, a finite set of discretized feasible speed profiles $P_{f,s}$ is precomputed, each with running time $\tau_{f,s,p}$ and energy $E_{f,s,p}$.
- **A3.** Rerouting is allowed only on the blocked segment $s_b$.
- **A4.** Station platform capacity is non-binding; only segment conflicts are modeled.
- **A5.** Time horizon $[0, T_{max}]$; all times continuous (or integer) within it.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$, $S$ | trains; ordered segments; $s_b$ = blocked segment |
| $K_s$ | tracks of segment $s$; $K_{s_b}=\{k^{blk},k^{alt}\}$, $K_s=\{k^{sch}\}$ otherwise |
| $a^{sch}_{f,s}, d^{sch}_{f,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure of $f$ at endpoints of $s$ |
| $\tau_{f,s,p}, E_{f,s,p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ for $f$ on $s$ |
| $\underline{dw}_{f,s}, \overline{dw}_{f,s}$ | min/max dwell of $f$ at the station before $s$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway on a track |
| $T^{start}, T^{end}$ | disruption window |
| $w_f, \pi_f, \beta$ | delay weight, cancellation penalty, energy weight |
| $M$ | big-M (use $M = T_{max}$, or tighter per-constraint values) |

## 3. Variables

- $a_{f,s}, d_{f,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times at segment endpoints.
- $x_{f,s,p} \in \{0,1\}$: speed profile selection.
- $y_{f,s_b} \in \{0,1\}$: rerouting to $k^{alt}$ on $s_b$.
- $z_f \in \{0,1\}$: cancellation.
- $o_{f,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: occupancy of track $k$ on $s$ by $f$.
- $u_{f,f',s} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering ($f$ before $f'$), defined for both ordered pairs.
- $\Delta_f \ge 0$: terminal lateness of $f$.

## 4. Objective

$$\min\; Z = \sum_{f\in F} w_f \Delta_f \;+\; \beta \sum_{f\in F}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{p\in P_{f,s}} E_{f,s,p}\, x_{f,s,p} \;+\; \sum_{f\in F} \pi_f z_f$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Profile selection** (exactly one profile unless cancelled):
$$\sum_{p\in P_{f,s}} x_{f,s,p} = 1 - z_f \qquad \forall f,\, s$$

**(C2) Running time from selected profile:**
$$a_{f,s+1} \;\ge\; d_{f,s} + \sum_{p\in P_{f,s}} \tau_{f,s,p}\, x_{f,s,p} - M z_f \qquad \forall f,\, s \ne s_{last}$$

**(C3) Dwell bounds:**
$$\underline{dw}_{f,s} \le d_{f,s} - a_{f,s} \le \overline{dw}_{f,s} - M z_f \qquad \forall f,\, s$$
(through-stations: $\underline{dw}=\overline{dw}=0$; the upper bound relaxed by $Mz_f$ when cancelled)

**(C4) No early arrival/departure:**
$$a_{f,s} \ge a^{sch}_{f,s} - M z_f, \qquad d_{f,s} \ge d^{sch}_{f,s} - M z_f \qquad \forall f,\, s$$

**(C5) Lateness (one-sided, early arrival not rewarded):**
$$\Delta_f \ge a_{f,s_{last}} - a^{sch}_{f,s_{last}} \qquad \forall f$$

**(C6) Cancellation removes all resources:**
$$0 \le a_{f,s},\, d_{f,s} \le M z_f \qquad \forall f,\, s$$

**(C7) Rerouting only on blocked segment:**
$$y_{f,s} = 0 \qquad \forall f,\, s \ne s_b$$

**(C8) Track occupancy (linear in $y$, $z$):**
$$o_{f,s_b,k^{blk}} = 1 - y_{f,s_b} - z_f, \qquad o_{f,s_b,k^{alt}} = y_{f,s_b} - z_f \;\;(\text{with } o \ge 0 \text{ enforced by } o \le y,\; o \le 1-z_f,\; o \ge y - z_f)$$
$$o_{f,s,k^{sch}} = 1 - z_f, \quad o_{f,s,k} = 0 \;\;\forall k\ne k^{sch} \qquad \forall f,\, s \ne s_b$$

**(C9) Disruption window** — using the blocked track requires full traversal outside $[T^{start},T^{end}]$:
$$a_{f,s_b+1} \le T^{start} + M\big(1 - o_{f,s_b,k^{blk}} + z_f\big) \qquad \forall f$$
$$d_{f,s_b} \ge T^{end} - M\big(1 - o_{f,s_b,k^{blk}} + z_f\big) \qquad \forall f$$

**(C10) Track-aware headway / no-overlap** (for all pairs $f<f'$, all $s$, all $k\in K_s$):
$$a_{f',s} \ge d_{f,s} + h - M_u(1-u_{f,f',s}) - M(z_f+z_{f'}) - M(1 - o_{f,s,k} - o_{f',s,k})$$
$$a_{f,s} \ge d_{f',s} + h - M_u\,u_{f,f',s} - M(z_f+z_{f'}) - M(1 - o_{f,s,k} - o_{f',s,k})$$
Active only when both trains run **and** share track $k$ — this captures bidirectional conflicts on $k^{alt}$ between a rerouted train and a train scheduled on that track.

**(C11) Consistent ordering and transitivity:**
$$u_{f,f',s} + u_{f',f,s} = 1 \qquad \forall f<f',\, s$$
$$u_{f,f',s} + u_{f',f'',s} - 1 \le u_{f,f'',s} \qquad \forall f<f'<f'',\, s$$

**(C12) Domains:**
$$a_{f,s}, d_{f,s}, \Delta_f \ge 0; \quad x_{f,s,p},\, y_{f,s_b},\, z_f,\, o_{f,s,k},\, u_{f,f',s} \in \{0,1\}$$

## 6. Explanation

- **Retiming** via $a,d$ with propagation (C2)–(C4); **reordering** via $u$ disjunctions (C10)–(C11); **rerouting** via $y$ restricted to $s_b$ (C7)–(C8); **cancellation** via $z$ (C1, C6, big-M deactivations).
- **Speed management** via $x$: slower profiles increase running time (C2) but reduce energy in $Z$ — the timetable–profile coupling is exact and linear.
- **Disruption** (C9) forces blocked-track trains to clear before $T^{start}$ or enter after $T^{end}$; otherwise they must reroute ($y=1$) or be cancelled.
- **Big-M guidance:** $M = T_{max}$ globally; tighter values per constraint (e.g., $M_a \ge U_f - T^{start}$, $M_d \ge T^{end} - L_f$) strengthen the LP relaxation.

All expressions are linear; the model is a complete, self-contained MILP solvable by standard branch-and-bound, and matches the structure required for decomposition into a train-plan selection IP with adaptive plan refinement.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

**Assumptions** (marked where not given in the input): double-track line with stations s₀…sₙ and segments (a,b); disruption blocks one direction of one segment during window [T₁,T₂]; a discrete set of precomputed speed profiles per segment (running time, energy); cancellation allowed; minimum headway h; dwell bounds [dᵐⁱⁿ, dᵐᵃˣ]; big-M relaxation for cancelled trains.

## Sets and Parameters
- T: trains, with direction dir(t), weight wₜ, cancellation penalty pₜ
- S: stations; E: segments (a,b); K_b: speed profiles of segment b with running time rᵏ_b and energy eᵏ_b
- Rerouted profile on blocked segment: running time r^R_b, energy e^R_b

(weighted total delay + cancellation penalties + energy cost)

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations (or block sections) indexed by $i \in I = \{1,\dots,n\}$. Each segment $i$ (between stations $i$ and $i+1$) has two tracks: the normal track per direction and the opposite track usable for **local rerouting** during a disruption. A set of trains $T$ operates according to a scheduled timetable. A partial blockage affects a set of segments $D \subset I$ on one side (say, the down direction) during time window $[t^{start}, t^{end}]$.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Trains run in both directions; each train $t$ has a fixed scheduled route (sequence of stations) and cannot be cancelled (cancellation could be added with a binary variable; we exclude it for clarity).
- (A2) Rerouting to the opposite track is only possible in disrupted segments $D$, only during the disruption window, and only one train may occupy a segment at a time (single-track operation during blockage).
- (A3) Each segment $i$ offers a finite set of pre-enumerated **speed profiles** $P_i$ for each train type, each with running time $r_{tip}$ and energy consumption $e_{tip}$ (linearized from trapezoidal/eco-driving profiles). This is the standard linearization of the speed-management coupling.
- (A4) Headway times (arrival–arrival, departure–departure, arrival–departure) are uniform constants per segment.
- (A5) Disruption start time and duration are known deterministically at the moment rescheduling begins.
- (A6) Dwell times have minimum and maximum values; running times may be stretched only via the discrete profile choice.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T, T^{up}, T^{down}$ | trains; per direction |
| $I$ | segments; $D \subseteq I$ disrupted segments |
| $P_i$ | speed profiles on segment $i$; $r_{tip}, e_{tip}$ running time / energy of train $t$, profile $p$ |
| $a_t, d_t$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $t$ at its terminal |
| $L^{arr}_t, U^{arr}_t$ | arrival time window at station $i$ for train $t$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway (time) |
| $dw^{min}_t, dw^{max}_t$ | min/max dwell of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $M$ | big constant |
| $w$ | weight trading delay vs. energy |

## 3. Decision Variables

- $x_{ti} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$ (departure from station 1 = arrival at station 1).
- $y_{ti} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: departure time of train $t$ from station $i$.
- $z_{tip} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses profile $p$ on segment $i$.
- $u_{ti} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $i$.
- $\sigma^{arr}_{tsi}, \sigma^{dep}_{tsi} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing variables — 1 if train $t$ passes station $i$ (arrives/departs) before train $s$.
- $\delta_{tsi} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $t,s$ (opposite directions) both occupy segment $i$ with $t$ rerouted, sequenced $t$ before $s$ on the shared track.

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay and energy consumption:

$$
\min \; w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{i \in I}\big[(x_{ti} - L^{arr}_{ti})^+ \big]}_{\text{total arrival delay}} \;+\; w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{p\in P_i} e_{tip}\, z_{tip}}_{\text{total energy}}
$$

Linearized with auxiliary variables $\Delta_{ti} \ge 0$:

$$
\min \; w_1 \sum_{t,i} \Delta_{ti} + w_2 \sum_{t,i,p} e_{tip} z_{tip}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable windows:**
$$
L^{arr}_{ti} \le x_{ti} \le U^{arr}_{ti} \qquad \forall t, i
$$

**(C2) Dwell time:**
$$
dw^{min}_{ti} \le y_{ti} - x_{ti} \le dw^{max}_{ti} \qquad \forall t, i
$$

**(C3) Running time via speed-profile selection (TRP–TSMP coupling):**
$$
x_{t,i+1} = y_{ti} + \sum_{p \in P_i} r_{tip}\, z_{tip} \qquad \forall t, i
$$
$$
\sum_{p \in P_i} z_{tip} = 1 \qquad \forall t, i
$$

**(C4) Rerouting only in disrupted segments and during the window:**
$$
u_{ti} = 0 \qquad \forall t,\; i \notin D
$$
$$
y_{ti} \ge t^{start} \cdot u_{ti}, \qquad x_{t,i+1} \le t^{end} + M(1 - u_{ti}) \qquad \forall t,\, i \in D
$$
(i.e., a rerouted train must traverse segment $i$ entirely within the disruption window).

**(C5) Headway on the normal track (same direction):** for trains $t,s$ in the same direction on segment $i$:
$$
x_{s,i+1} - x_{t,i+1} \ge h - M(1 - \sigma^{arr}_{tsi}) - M(u_{ti} + u_{si}) \qquad \forall t<s,\, i
$$
$$
x_{t,i+1} - x_{s,i+1} \ge h - M(\sigma^{arr}_{tsi}) - M(u_{ti}+u_{si}) \qquad \forall t<s,\, i
$$
Analogous pairs for departures $y_{ti}$ with $\sigma^{dep}_{tsi}$.

**(C6) Single-track operation on shared (rerouted) track — bidirectional conflict resolution:** for opposite-direction trains $t \in T^{up}$, $s \in T^{down}$ on segment $i \in D$:
$$
x_{s,i+1} - x_{t,i+1} \ge h - M(3 - u_{ti} - u_{si} - \delta_{tsi}) \qquad \forall t \in T^{up}, s \in T^{down}, i \in D
$$
$$
x_{t,i+1} - x_{s,i+1} \ge h - M(2 - u_{ti} - u_{si} + \delta_{tsi}) \qquad \forall t \in T^{up}, s \in T^{down}, i \in D
$$
These enforce: if both trains use the shared track, one must completely clear the segment before the other enters (headway $h$ between the follower's entry and leader's entry, with running times ensuring clearance).

**(C7) Station capacity (optional, one train per platform at a time):** analogous pairwise sequencing constraints on $x_{ti}$ at each station with headway $h^{station}$.

**(C8) Delay linearization:**
$$
\Delta_{ti} \ge x_{ti} - L^{arr}_{ti}, \qquad \Delta_{ti} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,i
$$

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{ti}, y_{ti} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\quad z_{tip}, u_{ti}, \sigma^{arr}_{tsi}, \sigma^{dep}_{tsi}, \delta_{tsi} \in \{0,1\},\quad \Delta_{ti} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Coupling:** Constraint (C3) is the core TRP–TSMP link: the timetable's running times are not free parameters but are selected from physically executable speed profiles, each carrying its own energy cost — capturing the trade-off between accelerating (earlier arrival, more energy) and coasting/decelerating (later arrival, less energy).
- **Rerouting:** Constraints (C4)–(C6) implement local rerouting on the opposite track during the blockage and guarantee conflict-free bidirectional sharing of that track.
- **Equivalence note (as in the paper):** If each segment's continuous speed profile is discretized into a sufficiently fine set of interval plans $P_i$, the MILP above is equivalent to the exact integrated problem; the decomposition into a train-interaction IP plus per-train plan selection follows by fixing $(x,y,z)$ per train as candidate plans and keeping only the sequencing variables in the IP.

This model is a complete MILP: linear objective, linear constraints, mixed integer variables — solvable directly by branch-and-bound for moderate instances, or by the adaptive plan-refinement decomposition for large-scale corridors.

# MILP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains $i$ |
| $S$ | ordered set of segments (stations and blocks) on the double-track line |
| $K_i$ | set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ per segment |
| $D=[t^d_1, t^d_2]$ | disruption time window on segment $s^*$ (one track blocked) |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | weights for delay, energy, cancellations |
| $h$ | minimum headway (min) |
| $r_{i,s,k}$, $e_{i,s,k}$ | running time / energy of train $i$ on segment $s$ with profile $k$ |
| $\underline{d}_{i,s}, \bar{d}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time at station $s$ |
| $a^{sch}_{i,s}, d^{sch}_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $M$ | big-M constant; $H$ planning horizon |

## 2. Decision Variables

- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: actual arrival/departure times (**retiming**)
- $\delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: arrival delay
- $x_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (**reordering**)
- $y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ rerouted to opposite track on $s$ (**rerouting**)
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled
- $u_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ (**speed management**)
- $o_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing of opposite-direction trains on the shared track

## 3. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, \delta_{i,\text{term}} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{i,s,k}\, u_{i,s,k} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in T} C_i z_i
$$

## 4. Constraints

**(C1) Schedule consistency and delay definition**
$$a_{i,s} \ge a^{sch}_{i,s}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^{sch}_{i,s}, \qquad \delta_{i,s} \ge 0$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency with selected profile**
$$d_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K_i} r_{i,s,k}\, u_{i,s,k} \le a_{i,s+1} + M z_i, \qquad \sum_{k \in K_i} u_{i,s,k} = 1 - z_i$$

**(C3) Dwell time bounds**
$$\underline{d}_{i,s}(1-z_i) \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \bar{d}_{i,s}(1-z_i)$$

**(C4) Headway on same track (big-M disjunctions)**
$$d_{i,s} + h \le a_{j,s} + M(1 - x_{ij,s}) + M(y_{i,s} + y_{j,s}) + M z_j$$
$$d_{j,s} + h \le a_{i,s} + M\, x_{ij,s} + M(y_{i,s} + y_{j,s}) + M z_i$$

**(C5) Rerouting only within disruption window and only on affected segment**
$$y_{i,s} = 0 \;\; \forall s \ne s^*; \qquad a_{i,s^*} \ge t^d_1 - M(1-y_{i,s^*}), \quad d_{i,s^*} \le t^d_2 + M(1-y_{i,s^*})$$

**(C6) Bidirectional conflict on shared single track during disruption**
$$d_{i,s^*} + h \le a_{j,s^*} + M(3 - y_{i,s^*} - y_{j,s^*} - o_{ij})$$
$$d_{j,s^*} + h \le a_{i,s^*} + M(2 - y_{i,s^*} - y_{j,s^*} - o_{ij})$$

**(C7) Blocked track during disruption** — trains not rerouted cannot occupy $s^*$ during $[t^d_1, t^d_2]$:
$$a_{i,s^*} \ge t^d_2 - M(y_{i,s^*} + z_i), \qquad d_{i,s^*} \le t^d_1 + M(y_{i,s^*} + z_i)$$

**(C8) Cancellation propagation**
$$a_{i,s} \le H z_i \quad \forall i, s$$

**(C9) Variable domains**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \delta_{i,s} \ge 0; \quad x_{ij,s}, y_{i,s}, z_i, u_{i,s,k}, o_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$$

## 5. Key Modeling Notes

- **Retiming** via continuous $a,d$; **reordering** via pairwise sequencing binaries $x_{ij,s}$ with big-M disjunctions (C4).
- **Rerouting** binaries $y_{i,s}$ allow affected trains to use the surviving track during the disruption window only (C5), with bidirectional conflict prevention on the shared track (C6).
- **Speed management**: exactly one discrete profile per train–segment (C2) links running time and energy — a piecewise-linear approximation of the nonlinear speed–energy tradeoff.
- **Disruption handling**: (C7) forces trains to wait, reroute, or be cancelled; cancellations carry penalties in the objective.
- The objective balances punctuality ($\alpha$), energy efficiency ($\beta$), and service continuity ($\gamma$), capturing the integrated TRSMP.

# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i$ |
| $S$ | set of stations, indexed $s$ |
| $L$ | set of segments (blocks between consecutive stations), indexed $l$; segment $l$ connects stations $s_l$ and $s_{l+1}$ |
| $P_i(l)$ | set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $l$ |
| $T^{div}$ | set of trains eligible to reroute (route passes disrupted segment $l^*$) |
| $K$ | tracks per segment, $K=\{1,2\}$ (index $k$) |

**Disruption:** segment $l^*$ is partially blocked during window $[\tau^{start}, \tau^{end}]$; reduced capacity on the affected track during this window.

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{tr}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, trailing-through |
| $d^{min}_i(s), d^{max}_i(s)$ | min / max dwell of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\rho^{run}_{i,l,p}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $l$ with profile $p$ |
| $e_{i,l,p}$ | energy of train $i$ on segment $l$ with profile $p$ |
| $a^{sched}_i(s), b^{sched}_i(s)$ | scheduled arrival / departure |
| $w_i$ | delay weight (priority) of train $i$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights of delay and energy in the objective |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $C_s$ | station capacity |
| $\Delta^{max}$ | maximum allowable delay |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{i,s}, b_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | actual arrival / departure of train $i$ at $s$ |
| $x_{i,l,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $l$ |
| $y_{i,l}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to track 2 on segment $l$ |
| $z_{ij,l}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $l$ |
| $\delta_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_+$ | delay of train $i$ at station $s$ |

## 4. Objective

$$\min \; \alpha \sum_{i\in T} w_i \sum_{s\in S} \delta_{i,s} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i,l,p} e_{i,l,p}\, x_{i,l,p}$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Dwell:**
$$d^{min}_i(s) \le b_{i,s}-a_{i,s} \le d^{max}_i(s) \quad \forall i,s$$

**(C2) Delay:**
$$\delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s}-a^{sched}_i(s),\quad \delta_{i,s}\ge 0,\quad \delta_{i,s}\le \Delta^{max} \quad \forall i,s$$

**(C3) Profile–timetable link:**
$$a_{i,s_{l+1}}-b_{i,s_l} \ge \sum_{p}\rho^{run}_{i,l,p}x_{i,l,p} \quad \forall i,l$$

**(C4) One profile per train–segment:**
$$\sum_{p\in P_i(l)}x_{i,l,p}=1 \quad \forall i,l$$

**(C5) Time windows:** $t^{min}_{i,s}\le a_{i,s},b_{i,s}\le t^{max}_{i,s}$.

**(C6) Headway sequencing (big-M disjunctions; same-track full headway, cross-track reduced headway $\bar h$):**
$$a_{j,s_{l+1}}-a_{i,s_{l+1}} \ge h^{arr}-M(1-z_{ij,l})-M(y_{i,l}+y_{j,l}-2)$$
$$a_{i,s_{l+1}}-a_{j,s_{l+1}} \ge h^{arr}-M\,z_{ij,l}-M(y_{i,l}+y_{j,l}-2)$$
(analogously for $b_{i,s_l}$ with $h^{dep}$, and through headways $h^{tr}$; different tracks use $\bar h$).

**(C7) Order consistency:** $z_{ij}+z_{ji}=1$; transitivity $z_{ij}+z_{jk}-z_{ik}\le 1$.

**(C8) Conflict-free occupancy on segment $l$ (with $g^{\pm}_{ij,l}\ge \pm(y_{i,l}-y_{j,l})$ linearizing $|y_i-y_j|$):**
$$b_{j,s_l} \le a_{i,s_{l+1}}+M\big(z_{ij,l}+g^+_{ij,l}+g^-_{ij,l}\big),\qquad b_{i,s_l} \le a_{j,s_{l+1}}+M\big(1-z_{ij,l}+g^+_{ij,l}+g^-_{ij,l}\big)$$

**(C9) Partial blockage capacity on $l^*$** — at most one train on the affected (default) track intersects the disruption window, via occupancy binaries $\sigma_i$ with big-M activation:
$$\sum_i \sigma_i \le 1,\qquad \sigma_i \ge 1-\tfrac{a_{i,s_{l^*+1}}-\tau^{end}}{M},\quad \sigma_i \ge 1-\tfrac{\tau^{start}-b_{i,s_{l^*}}}{M} \ \text{(for } y_{i,l^*}=0\text{)}$$

**(C10) Rerouting eligibility:** $y_{i,l}=0$ for $i\notin T^{div}$ or $l\ne l^*$; diverted trains must occupy $l^*$ inside the window:
$$b_{i,s_{l^*}}\ge \tau^{start}-M(1-y_{i,l^*}),\qquad a_{i,s_{l^*+1}}\le \tau^{end}+M(1-y_{i,l^*})$$

**(C11) Bidirectional headway on the shared diverted track:**
$$a_{j,s_{l^*+1}}-b_{i,s_{l^*}} \ge h^{tr}-M(3-y_{i,l^*}-y_{j,l^*}-z_{ij,l^*})$$
$$b_{i,s_{l^*}}-a_{j,s_{l^*+1}} \ge h^{tr}-M(2-y_{i,l^*}-y_{j,l^*}+z_{ij,l^*}) \quad \forall i,j \text{ opposite directions}$$

**(C12) Station capacity:** time-indexed occupancy $o_{i,s,t}$ with
$$\sum_i o_{i,s,t}\le C_s,\quad o_{i,s,t}\ge 1-\tfrac{a_{i,s}-t}{M},\quad o_{i,s,t}\ge 1-\tfrac{t-b_{i,s}}{M}$$

**(C13) Domains:** $a,b,\delta\ge 0$; $x,y,z,\sigma,o\in\{0,1\}$.

## 6. Rationale

- **Retiming** via $a,b$ with dwell (C1), delay (C2), time windows (C5).
- **Reordering** via $z$ with big-M disjunctions (C6, C8) and transitivity (C7).
- **Rerouting** via $y$, restricted to affected trains inside the disruption window (C10), with blockage capacity (C9) and bidirectional headways on the borrowed track (C11).

Text:
# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP (Equations Only)

## Sets and Parameters
- Trains *i, j ∈ I*; stations *s ∈ S*; segments *s ∈ SEG* (segment *s* connects stations *s* and *s+1*); speed profiles *p ∈ P*.
- *Aᵢₛ, Dᵢₛ*: scheduled arrival/departure times; *tᵢₛₚ*: running time of profile *p*; *eᵢₛₚ*: energy of profile *p*.
- *T₀, T₁*: disruption window; *s_B*: blocked segment; *h*: min same-direction headway; *h_on*: min headway on shared (opposite) track; *M*: big-M; *w₁, w₂, w₃*: weights.

## Variables
- *aᵢₛ, dᵢₛ*: actual arrival/departure times (continuous, ≥ 0, ≤ horizon).
- *rᵢₛ*: running time on segment *s* (continuous).
- *δᵢₛ ≥ 0*: delay at station *s*.
- *yᵢₛ ∈ {0,1}*: 1 if train *i* is rerouted to the opposite track on segment *s*.
- *xᵢⱼₛ ∈ {0,1}*: 1 if train *i* precedes train *j* on segment *s* (same direction).
- *zᵢⱼₛ ∈ {0,1}*: head-on ordering on the shared track of the blocked segment.
- *vᵢₛₚ ∈ {0,1}*: 1 if train *i* uses speed profile *p* on segment *s*.
- *cᵢ ∈ {0,1}*: 1 if train *i* is cancelled.
- *b₁ᵢ, b₂ᵢ ∈ {0,1}*: auxiliary binaries for the disruption-window disjunction.

## Objective
Minimize weighted total delay + energy + cancellation penalty:

min  *w₁ Σᵢ Σₛ δᵢₛ + w₂ Σᵢ Σₛ Σₚ eᵢₛₚ · vᵢₛₚ + w₃ Σᵢ cᵢ*

## Constraints

**(a) Timetable linkage**
- *dᵢₛ + rᵢₛ = aᵢ,ₛ₊₁*  ∀ i, s ∈ SEG
- *rᵢₛ = Σₚ tᵢₛₚ · vᵢₛₚ*  ∀ i, s
- *dᵢₛ − aᵢₛ ≥ dwell_min · (1 − cᵢ)*  ∀ i, s (intermediate stations)

**(b) Profile selection**
- *Σₚ vᵢₛₚ = 1 − cᵢ*  ∀ i, s (exactly one profile, none if cancelled)

**(i) Running time bounds**
- *r_min_frac · tᵢₛ₁ · (1 − cᵢ) ≤ rᵢₛ ≤ r_max_frac · tᵢₛ₁ · (1 − cᵢ)*  ∀ i, s

**(j) Delay definition**
- *δᵢₛ ≥ aᵢₛ − Aᵢₛ − M·cᵢ*,  *δᵢₛ ≥ 0*  ∀ i, s

**(c) Same-direction headways (big-M disjunctions)**
- *aⱼ,ₛ₊₁ ≥ aᵢ,ₛ₊₁ + h − M(1 − xᵢⱼₛ) − M·cᵢ − M·cⱼ*  ∀ i < j, s
- *dⱼₛ ≥ dᵢₛ + h − M(1 − xᵢⱼₛ) − M·cᵢ − M·cⱼ*  ∀ i < j, s
- *xᵢⱼₛ + xⱼᵢₛ ≥ 1 − cᵢ − cⱼ*  ∀ i < j, s (complete ordering unless cancelled)

**(e) Rerouting only on the blocked segment**
- *yᵢₛ = 0*  ∀ i, s ≠ s_B

**(f) Disruption time window (enter before T₀, after T₁, or reroute)**
- *aᵢ,ₛ_B₊₁ ≤ T₀ + M(b₁ᵢ + yᵢ,ₛ_B + cᵢ)*  ∀ i
- *dᵢ,ₛ_B ≥ T₁ − M(b₂ᵢ + yᵢ,ₛ_B + cᵢ)*  ∀ i
- *b₁ᵢ + b₂ᵢ + yᵢ,ₛ_B ≥ 1 − cᵢ*  ∀ i

**(d) Head-on conflict avoidance on the shared opposite track (s = s_B)**
- *aⱼ,ₛ_B₊₁ ≥ dᵢ,ₛ_B + h_on − M(1 − zᵢⱼₛ_B) − M(1 − yᵢ,ₛ_B) − M·yⱼ,ₛ_B − M·cᵢ − M·cⱼ*  ∀ i, j
- *aᵢ,ₛ_B₊₁ ≥ dⱼ,ₛ_B + h_on − M·zᵢⱼₛ_B − M(1 − yᵢ,ₛ_B) − M·yⱼ,ₛ_B − M·cᵢ − M·cⱼ*  ∀ i, j
- *zᵢⱼₛ_B + zⱼᵢₛ_B ≥ yᵢ,ₛ_B + (1 − yⱼ,ₛ_B) − cᵢ − cⱼ − 1*  ∀ i, j (ordering required when a rerouted train meets a normal-direction train)

**(g) Planning horizon**
- *aᵢₛ ≤ horizon*  ∀ i, s

**(h) Cancellation frees resources**
- *aᵢₛ ≤ M(1 − cᵢ)*  ∀ i, s

## Assumptions (marked as such)
- Single corridor, double track, one blocked segment with one track unavailable during [T₀, T₁]; rerouting allowed only there.
- Speed profiles are discretized into a finite candidate set per train–segment (time/energy pairs), making the dynamics linear.
- Big-M disjunctions model all ordering and time-window decisions; delays are linearized via δ ≥ a − A_sched.
- Cancellation removes a train's resource consumption and delay penalty entirely.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

**Assumptions** (marked where inferred): a double-track high-speed line with stations S = {S₁,…,Sₙ} and segments k between consecutive stations; trains T each with fixed direction (+1 up / −1 down); a disruption blocks one direction of one segment during window [t₀, t₁]; each train/segment has a finite set P of discrete speed profiles p with fixed running time rₜₖₚ and energy eₜₖₚ; dwell bounds [dᵐⁱⁿ, dᵐᵃˣ]; minimum headway h; big-M; weights w_d, w_e, w_c.

## Variables
- aₜₛ, dₜₛ ≥ 0 — arrival/departure (retiming) of train t at station s (continuous)
- oᵢⱼₖ ∈ {0,1} — ordering: train i traverses segment k before train j (reordering)
- ρₜₖ ∈ {0,1} — train t reroutes to the opposite track on segment k (only allowed for trains of the blocked direction on the disrupted segment)
- cₜ ∈ {0,1} — train t is cancelled
- yₜₖₚ ∈ {0,1} — train t uses speed profile p on segment k
- Dₜ ≥ 0 — delay of train t at its destination

## Objective
Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellations:

min Σₜ w_d·Dₜ + Σₜ Σₖ Σₚ w_e·eₜₖₚ·yₜₖₚ + Σₜ w_c·cₜ

## Constraints

**1. Timetable consistency (dwell):** for each t and intermediate station s:
- dₜₛ ≥ aₜₛ + dᵐⁱⁿ(1−cₜ)
- dₜₛ ≤ aₜₛ + dᵐᵃˣ(1−cₜ) + M·cₜ

**2. Running time from selected speed profile:** for each t, segment k on its route, with next station s′:
- aₜ,ₛ′ ≥ dₜₛ + Σₚ rₜₖₚ·yₜₖₚ − M·cₜ
- aₜ,ₛ′ ≤ dₜₛ + Σₚ rₜₖₚ·yₜₖₚ + M(1 − Σₚ yₜₖₚ) + M·cₜ

**3. Profile exclusivity:** Σₚ yₜₖₚ = 1 − cₜ for every t, k.

**4. Disruption time window:** for trains t of the blocked direction on the disrupted segment (entry time dₜₛ, nominal running time r⁰):
- dₜₛ ≥ t₁ − M(ρₜₖ + cₜ)  (enter after window ends), or
- dₜₛ + r⁰ ≤ t₀ + M(ρₜₖ + cₜ)  (clear segment before window starts), or
- ρₜₖ = 1 (reroute onto the opposite track, subject to constraint 6).

**5. Delay definition** (at destination station s*ᵗ with scheduled arrival πₜ):
- Dₜ ≥ aₜ,ₛ*ᵗ − πₜ, Dₜ ≥ 0; Dₜ forced to 0 if cₜ = 1.

**6. Conflict-free headways:**
- *Same direction* (i, j on segment k): with oᵢⱼₖ = 1 meaning i first:
 dᵢₛᵢ + h ≤ dⱼₛⱼ + M(1 − oᵢⱼₖ) + M(cᵢ + cⱼ), and symmetrically with oᵢⱼₖ.
- *Opposite directions (bidirectional conflict when rerouting):* occupancy intervals [dₜₛ, aₜ,ₛ′] must not overlap with headway h whenever ρᵢₖ or ρⱼₖ is active:
 aⱼ,ₛ′ⱼ + h ≤ dᵢₛᵢ + M(1 − oᵢⱼₖ) + M(1 − ρᵢₖ − ρⱼₖ + ρᵢₖρⱼₖ) + M(cᵢ + cⱼ), and symmetrically with oᵢⱼₖ. (Without rerouting, opposite-direction trains use separate tracks and are conflict-free.)

**7. Rerouting feasibility:** ρₜₖ = 0 unless t runs in the blocked direction on the disrupted segment.

**8. Domains:** aₜₛ, dₜₛ, Dₜ ≥ 0; oᵢⱼₖ, ρₜₖ, cₜ, yₜₖₚ ∈ {0,1}.

This model simultaneously optimizes train times (retiming), orders (reordering), routes (rerouting within the disruption window), service cancellations, and speed profile selection, yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable whose running times are exactly matched to executable speed profiles, minimizing delay, energy, and cancellation cost.

Below is the final, corrected model (I fixed two logical slips in the last draft: the bidirectional clearance relaxation direction in C7, and the ordering-variable definition, which should be one symmetric binary per unordered pair).

---

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP) — MILP

## 1. Sets
- $I$ — trains; $\mathcal{P}_j$ — unordered pairs $\{i,k\}$, $i<k$, both traversing segment $j$; split into $\mathcal{D}_j$ (same direction) and $\mathcal{O}_j$ (opposite directions, $\sigma_i \ne \sigma_k$)
- $J$ — segments; $B_d \subseteq J$ — segments partially blocked during $[T_0, T_1]$
- $S_i$ — ordered segments of train $i$'s path; $F$ — platforms
- $P_{i,j}$ — discretized speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $j$

## 2. Parameters
- $r_{i,j,p}$, $e_{i,j,p}$ — running time and energy of profile $p$
- $h$ — minimum headway (same track); $\tau$ — clearance time for bidirectional single-track operation
- $T^{\min}_{i,j}, T^{\max}_{i,j}$ — time-window bounds; $\Delta^{arr}_i$ — planned final arrival; $\rho^{\max}_{i,j}$ — max stretching
- $w_i, \theta_{i,j}, \alpha, \gamma, \beta$ — weights (delay, stretching, energy, rerouting, cancellation); $H$ — horizon; $M \ge H + \max r + h + \tau$

## 3. Variables
- Continuous: $T^{in}_{i,j}, T^{out}_{i,j} \ge 0$ (entry/exit times); $\rho_{i,j} \ge 0$ (stretching); $d_i, u_i \ge 0$ (final lateness/earliness)
- Binary: $x_{i,k,j}$ (symmetric ordering, $1 \Leftrightarrow i$ enters before $k$); $s_{i,k,j}$ ($1 \Leftrightarrow$ same track); $z_{i,j}$ (rerouting, $j \in B_d$ only); $q_{i,j}$ ($1 \Leftrightarrow$ traverse after $T_1$); $c_i$ (cancellation); $y_{i,j,p}$ (profile selection)
- Derived: $\delta_{i,j} = 1 - z_{i,j}$ for $j \in B_d$ (default-track indicator), $\delta_{i,j} = 1$ otherwise.

## 4. Objective
$$\min \sum_i w_i d_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i}\sum_{j \in S_i}\sum_{p} e_{i,j,p}\, y_{i,j,p} \;+\; \sum_{i,j}\theta_{i,j}\,\rho_{i,j} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i}\sum_{j \in B_d} z_{i,j} \;+\; \beta \sum_i c_i$$

Earliness $u_i$ appears only in constraints and is never rewarded, so only lateness is penalized.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Time windows:**
$$T^{\min}_{i,j} - M c_i \le T^{in}_{i,j} \le T^{\max}_{i,j} + M c_i \qquad \forall i, j \in S_i$$

**(C2) Route continuity:**
$$T^{in}_{i,j'} \ge T^{out}_{i,j} \qquad \forall i,\ j \to j' \text{ consecutive in } S_i$$

**(C3) Profile selection and running time (stretching only upward):**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{i,j}} y_{i,j,p} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, j$$
$$\sum_p r_{i,j,p} y_{i,j,p} \;\le\; T^{out}_{i,j} - T^{in}_{i,j} \;\le\; \sum_p r_{i,j,p} y_{i,j,p} + \rho_{i,j}, \qquad 0 \le \rho_{i,j} \le \rho^{\max}_{i,j}$$

**(C4) Same-track indicator ($s = 1 \Leftrightarrow$ same track), for $\{i,k\} \in \mathcal{P}_j$, $j \in B_d$:**
$$s_{i,k,j} \ge \delta_{i,j} + \delta_{k,j} - 1,\quad s_{i,k,j} \le \delta_{i,j},\quad s_{i,k,j} \le \delta_{k,j},\quad s_{i,k,j} \ge 0$$
($s_{i,k,j} = 0$ fixed for $j \notin B_d$, since $\delta \equiv 1$ gives $s=1$ — instead fix $s_{i,k,j}=1$ for $j \notin B_d$.)

**(C5) Ordering consistency:** one binary per unordered pair; if either train is cancelled, ordering is free:
$$x_{i,k,j} \le 1 - c_i, \qquad x_{i,k,j} \le 1 - c_k$$

**(C6) Headways on the same track (same direction, $\{i,k\} \in \mathcal{D}_j$):**
$$T^{in}_{k,j} \ge T^{in}_{i,j} + h - M(1 - x_{i,k,j}) - M(1 - s_{i,k,j}) - M c_i - M c_k$$
$$T^{in}_{i,j} \ge T^{in}_{k,j} + h - M\,x_{i,k,j} - M(1 - s_{i,k,j}) - M c_i - M c_k$$
(analogously for $T^{out}$).

**(C7) Bidirectional clearance on disrupted segments ($\{i,k\} \in \mathcal{O}_j$, $j \in B_d$) — active only on the same track ($s=1$):**
$$T^{in}_{k,j} \ge T^{out}_{i,j} + \tau - M(1 - x_{i,k,j}) - M(1 - s_{i,k,j}) - M c_i - M c_k$$
$$T^{in}_{i,j} \ge T^{out}_{k,j} + \tau - M\,x_{i,k,j} - M(1 - s_{i,k,j}) - M c_i - M c_k$$

**(C8) Disruption time-window logic (non-rerouted trains must avoid $[T_0,T_1]$):**
$$T^{out}_{i,j} \le T_0 + M q_{i,j} + M z_{i,j} + M c_i$$
$$T^{in}_{i,j} \ge T_1 - M(1 - q_{i,j}) + M z_{i,j} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,\ j \in S_i \cap B_d$$

**(C9) FIFO (no overtaking inside a block):**
$$T^{out}_{k,j} \ge T^{out}_{i,j} - M(1 - x_{i,k,j}) - M(1 - s_{i,k,j}) - M c_i - M c_k$$
$$T^{out}_{i,j} \ge T^{out}_{k,j} - M\,x_{i,k,j} - M(1 - s_{i,k,j}) - M c_i - M c_k \qquad \forall \{i,k\} \in \mathcal{D}_j$$

**(C10) Platform occupancy ($m_f = 1$):** for $i<k$ assigned to platform $f$, with $u_{i,k,f} \in \{0,1\}$:
$$T^{dep}_{k,f} \ge T^{arr}_{i,f} + h^f - M(1 - u_{i,k,f}) - M c_i - M c_k$$
$$T^{dep}_{i,f} \ge T^{arr}_{k,f} + h^f - M\,u_{i,k,f} - M c_i - M c_k$$
(for $m_f > 1$, use the time-indexed variant $\sum_{i \in \Pi_f} o_{i,f,t} \le m_f$).

**(C11) Final delay decomposition (one-sided):**
$$T^{out}_{i,\,last} = \Delta^{arr}_i + d_i - u_i, \qquad d_i, u_i \ge 0$$

**(C12) Domains:**
$$T^{in}, T^{out}, \rho, d, u \ge 0;\qquad x, s, z, q, c, y \in \{0,1\}; \qquad 0 \le T^{in}, T^{out} \le H$$

## 6. Decision dimensions
- **Retiming** — continuous $T^{in}, T^{out}$ (C1–C2); only lateness penalized via (C11).
- **Reordering** — symmetric binaries $x$ with headways (C6) and FIFO (C9).
- **Rerouting** — $z$ sends a train onto the opposite track of $j \in B_d$, exempting it from the blocked window (C8), at cost $\gamma$ and subject to bidirectional clearance $\tau$ when sharing the track (C7).
- **Cancellation** — $c_i$ deactivates train $i$'s constraints via Big-M at cost $\beta$.
- **Speed management** — $y_{i,j,p}$ selects a profile, coupling running time (C3) with energy in the objective; penalized stretching $\rho$ allows bounded slow-downs.

All constraints are linear (Big-M conditional logic), so the model is a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/cut; its size is dominated by the ordering variables $O(\sum_j |\mathcal{P}_j|)$ and profile variables $O(\sum_{i,j} |P_{i,j}|)$.

# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP model for real-time railway rescheduling with ETCS Level 2 (fixed-block, TTD).

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **(A1)** The network is a set of *routes* (paths through the infrastructure). Each route $r$ is a sequence of TTD sections; some routes pass through switch areas, others do not.
- **(A2)** Each train $t$ has a set of feasible routes $R_t$ from its origin to destination; reordering is captured by route choice and sequencing on shared resources.
- **(A3)** Each train $t$ has a set of **speed profile options** $P_t$ (e.g., coasting vs. full service braking). Each profile $p$ induces a maximum speed $v_{tp}$ and, for each TTD section $s$, a **speed-dependent braking distance** $b_{tp}(v)$ — hence a speed-dependent **brake indication point (IP)** and approach time before the end of authority (EoA).
- **(A4)** The blocking time of a TTD section under DTG is train- and speed-dependent: it includes the approach (braking) time from the IP to the EoA, computed from the selected profile and entry speed.
- **(A5)** A train occupies a section for the interval between the passage times at its boundaries, extended by the DTG approach time at the EoA section.
- **(A6)** Delays are measured against the original timetable at scheduled events (passages/stops).
- **(A7)** Dwell times may be stretched within given bounds; minimum headways are implied by mutual exclusion of blocking-time intervals.
- **(A8)** Linearisation: speed-profile choice is discrete (binary), so all speed-dependent quantities are precomputed per (train, profile, section) — keeping the model linear.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | trains; $S$ TTD sections; $R$ routes; $R_t \subseteq R$ routes of train $t$ |
| $P_t$ | speed profiles of train $t$ |
| $S_r$ | ordered TTD sections of route $r$ |
| $\sigma^r_{ts}$ | scheduled (unconstrained) entry time of train $t$ into section $s$ via route $r$ |
| $\beta_{trsp}$ | blocking (occupancy + DTG approach) duration of section $s$ for train $t$, route $r$, profile $p$ |
| $d^{min}_{trsp}, d^{max}_{trsp}$ | min/max dwell on station section $s$ |
| $w_t$ | delay weight of train $t$ |
| $M$ | big-M |
| $H$ | planning horizon |
| $E_t$ | set of scheduled events (passages/stops) of train $t$; $a_{te}$ scheduled time |

## 3. Variables

- $x_{tr} \in \{0,1\}$: train $t$ uses route $r$.
- $y_{tp} \in \{0,1\}$: train $t$ uses speed profile $p$.
- $z_{tts'} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variables — $z_{t_1 t_2 s} = 1$ iff train $t_1$ traverses section $s$ before $t_2$.
- $e_{ts} \ge 0$: actual entry time of train $t$ into section $s$.
- $q_{ts} \ge 0$: actual exit time of train $t$ from section $s$.
- $D_{te} \ge 0$: delay of train $t$ at event $e$.

## 4. Objective

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{e \in E_t} w_t \, D_{te}$$

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Route choice** — exactly one route per train:
$$\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{tr} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(2) Speed profile choice** — exactly one profile per train:
$$\sum_{p \in P_t} y_{tp} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(3) Section sequencing along a route** — entry times follow route order:
$$e_{t,s_{i+1}} \ge q_{t s_i} - M(1 - x_{tr}) \qquad \forall t, r \in R_t,\; s_i, s_{i+1} \in S_r$$

**(4) Section occupancy (blocking time incl. DTG approach):**
$$q_{ts} \ge e_{ts} + \sum_{r \in R_t:\, s \in S_r} \sum_{p \in P_t} \beta_{trsp}\, x_{tr} y_{tp} - M\Big(1 - \sum_{r \in R_t:\, s \in S_r} x_{tr}\Big) \qquad \forall t, s$$

**(5) Dwell time bounds** (station sections $s \in St_t$):
$$\sum_{r,p} \big(d^{min}_{trsp} x_{tr} y_{tp}\big) \le q_{ts} - e_{ts} \le \sum_{r,p} \big(d^{max}_{trsp} x_{tr} y_{tp}\big) \qquad \forall t,\, s \in St_t$$

**(6) Mutual exclusion on each section (conflict resolution)** — for every pair $(t_1, t_2)$, $t_1 \neq t_2$, and every section $s$ used by both:
$$q_{t_1 s} \le e_{t_2 s} + M(1 - z_{t_1 t_2 s}) + M\Big(2 - \textstyle\sum_{r \in R_{t_1}: s \in S_r} x_{t_1 r} - \sum_{r \in R_{t_2}: s \in S_r} x_{t_2 r}\Big)$$
$$q_{t_2 s} \le e_{t_1 s} + M\, z_{t_1 t_2 s} + M\Big(2 - \textstyle\sum_{r \in R_{t_1}: s \in S_r} x_{t_1 r} - \sum_{r \in R_{t_2}: s \in S_r} x_{t_2 r}\Big)$$

**(7) Switch-area sequencing** — for switch sections $\Sigma \subset S$, additionally enforce order consistency across consecutive switch sections (no crossing within the switch area):
$$z_{t_1 t_2 s} = z_{t_1 t_2 s'} \qquad \forall t_1 \neq t_2,\; s, s' \in \Sigma \text{ on a common route pair}$$

**(8) Delay definition:**
$$D_{te} \ge e_{t, s(e)} - a_{te} \qquad \forall t, e \in E_t$$
where $s(e)$ is the section whose entry corresponds to event $e$.

**(9) Initial conditions (given primary delays):**
$$e_{t, s_0(t)} = a_{t}^{obs} \qquad \forall t \text{ (observed entry time of delayed trains)}$$

**(10) Horizon:** $a_{te} \le e_{ts} \le H$ for all relevant $t,s$.

**(11) Variable domains:** $x, y, z \in \{0,1\}$; $e, q, D \ge 0$.

## 6. Remarks on DTG-specific features

- The **speed-dependent separation** enters through $\beta_{trsp}$ in Constraint (4): the blocking time of the EoA section includes the approach time $\tau_{brake}(v_{tp}) = b_{tp}/\bar{v}_{brake}$ from the speed-dependent brake indication point, so a follower cannot enter the preceding section until the leader's braking envelope is clear.
- **Speed profile options** (Constraints 2, 4, 5) let the optimiser trade run time (e.g., coasting reduces speed and thus braking distance) against delay propagation — a feature absent in fixed-block CDR models.
- The model reduces to the original RECIFE-MILP when each train has one profile and $\beta$ is the conventional fixed blocking time.

**Solution method:** branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut (e.g., CPLEX), with big-Ms tightened per instance.
