# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP-style model. All assumptions not stated in the input are marked **(A)**.

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **(A1)** The network is a directed graph of track resources: TDS/block sections (open line), station tracks, and switches. Switches are modelled as distinct resources with locking semantics.
- **(A2)** Each train has a predefined set of *routes* through the network (macroscopic itineraries); local rerouting is limited to route choice, as in RECIFE-MILP.
- **(A3)** For each (train, route) pair, a finite set of *speed profile options* is precomputed offline (microscopic simulation). Each option specifies, for every resource on the route, a **blocking time** that accounts for the speed-dependent braking distance, i.e., the approach/braking time before the EoA under continuous braking-curve supervision, plus running, reaction, and clearing times.
- **(A4)** Trains are not re-routed dynamically inside a route; overtaking/reordering is allowed on shared resources.
- **(A5)** Entry times into the network area are controllable within a bounded time window; the reference timetable gives scheduled entry times.
- **(A6)** Delays are measured at the exit of the modelled area.
- **(A7)** A train occupies a resource for exactly the blocking time of its chosen speed profile option (deterministic, precomputed).

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $R_t$ | set of feasible routes for train $t$ |
| $P_{t,r}$ | set of speed profile options for train $t$ on route $r$ |
| $S$ | set of resources (TDS sections, station tracks); $S^{sw} \subset S$ switches |
| $S_{t,r,p}$ | resources used by train $t$ on route $r$ with profile $p$ |
| $b_{t,r,p,s}$ | blocking time of train $t$ on resource $s$ under option $(r,p)$ |
| $a_{t,r,s}$ | entry time of train $t$ into resource $s$ on route $r$ (relative to area entry) |
| $e_t^{sched}$ | scheduled entry time of train $t$ |
| $e_t^{min}, e_t^{max}$ | bounds on rescheduled entry time **(A5)** |
| $x_t^{sched}$ | scheduled exit time of train $t$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $\tau_{tt'}$ | minimum headway offset between entries of $t$ and $t'$ if $t'$ follows $t$ on the same first resource **(A2, optional)** |

## 3. Variables

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_{t,r,p} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if train } t \text{ uses route } r \text{ with speed profile option } p\\
e_t &\ge 0 && \text{rescheduled entry time of train } t \text{ into the area}\\
d_t &\ge 0 && \text{final delay of train } t\\
\delta_{t}^{in} &\ge 0 && \text{entry delay of train } t\\
o_{t,t',s} &\in \{0,1\} && \text{1 if } t \text{ enters resource } s \text{ before } t' \text{ (for } t\neq t' \text{ sharing } s\text{)}
\end{aligned}
$$

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total final delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} d_t
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route and speed profile choice** — each train selects exactly one route and one speed profile option:

$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} \sum_{p \in P_{t,r}} y_{t,r,p} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

**(C2) Entry time bounds:**

$$
e_t^{min} \le e_t \le e_t^{max} \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{2}
$$

**(C3) Entry delay:**

$$
\delta_t^{in} \ge e_t - e_t^{sched} \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{3}
$$

**(C4) Final delay** — exit time is entry time plus route running time (last resource), via the chosen option:

$$
d_t \ge e_t + \sum_{r \in R_t}\sum_{p \in P_{t,r}} a_{t,r,s_t^{out}}\, y_{t,r,p} - x_t^{sched} \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{4}
$$

where $s_t^{out}$ is the last resource of any route of train $t$ **(A6: identical exit resource for all routes of a train)**.

**(C5) Resource occupancy windows.** Train $t$ occupies resource $s$ over interval $[e_t + a_{t,r,s},\; e_t + a_{t,r,s} + b_{t,r,p,s}]$ if $(r,p)$ is chosen. For any two trains $t, t'$ that can both use resource $s$, no overlap:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\big(e_{t'} + a_{t',r',s} + b_{t',r',p',s}\big) - \big(e_t + a_{t,r,s}\big) \le M\,(3 - y_{t,r,p} - y_{t',r',p'} - o_{t,t',s}) \\
&\qquad \forall t<t',\; \forall r\in R_t, p\in P_{t,r}, r'\in R_{t'}, p'\in P_{t',r'} \text{ with } s \in S_{t,r,p} \cap S_{t',r',p'} \tag{5a}
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\big(e_t + a_{t,r,s} + b_{t,r,p,s}\big) - \big(e_{t'} + a_{t',r',s}\big) \le M\,(2 + o_{t,t',s} - y_{t,r,p} - y_{t',r',p'}) \\
&\qquad \forall t<t',\; \text{(same pairs as (5a))} \tag{5b}
\end{aligned}
$$

If both trains choose options using $s$ ($y_{t,r,p}=y_{t',r',p'}=1$), then either (5a) with $o_{t,t',s}=1$ or (5b) with $o_{t,t',s}=0$ holds — i.e., one train fully clears $s$ (including its speed-dependent braking/approach time) before the other enters. **This is where DTG enters:** $b_{t,r,p,s}$ depends on the speed profile, hence on the braking distance to the EoA.

**(C6) Consistent ordering along routes.** If two trains share several resources, their order must be consistent (no crossing) **(A4)**:

$$
o_{t,t',s} = o_{t,t',s'} \qquad \forall t<t',\; \forall s,s' \in \bigcup_{r,p} S_{t,r,p} \cap \bigcup_{r',p'} S_{t',r',p'} \tag{6}
$$

**(C7) Switch locking.** A switch is locked from the first approach (start of blocking, which includes the braking approach) until the train clears it; no other train may use the same switch concurrently. This is enforced by (5) applied to $s \in S^{sw}$; additionally, since a switch serves converging routes, trains on routes that *cross* at switch $s$ must also respect (5)–(6) **(A1)**. Optionally, a minimum switching/settling time $\ell_s$ is added:

$$
\big(e_{t'} + a_{t',r',s}\big) - \big(e_t + a_{t,r,s} + b_{t,r,p,s}\big) \ge \ell_s \cdot \big(y_{t,r,p} + y_{t',r',p'} - 1\big) \quad \forall s \in S^{sw},\; o_{t,t',s}=1 \text{ active} \tag{7}
$$

**(C8) Variable domain:**

$$
y_{t,r,p} \in \{0,1\},\quad o_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\},\quad e_t, d_t, \delta_t^{in} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Speed-dependent separation (DTG core):** unlike fixed-block models where blocking times are fixed per block, here $b_{t,r,p,s}$ is precomputed per speed profile option and includes the absolute braking distance from the brake indication point to the EoA. Selecting a faster profile yields a longer approach/braking component of the blocking time; the MILP trades off speed (lower delay) vs. separation (fewer conflicts).
- **Linearity:** all constraints are linear; nonlinearity from speed dynamics is avoided by enumerating speed profile options **(A3)**.
- The model is a big-$M$ disjunctive MILP, solvable by branch-and-bound; warm starts from the original timetable are possible.

Text:
Below is the final, complete MILP for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockage.

---

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $S=\{0,\dots,n\}$ | stations; segment $s$ connects stations $s$ and $s+1$ |
| $I=I^{up}\cup I^{dn}$ | trains, up/down directions |
| $s^*\in S$ | disrupted segment |
| $\mathcal{T}=[T_1,T_2]$ | disruption time window |
| $P_{is}$ | admissible speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $s$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $A_{is}, D_{is}$ | planned arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $r_{isp}, e_{isp}$ | running time and energy of profile $p$ on segment $s$ |
| $dw^{min}_{is}, dw^{max}_{is}$ | dwell-time bounds |
| $h_s,\ h^a_s$ | departure/arrival headways (same track) |
| $h^{bi}$ | meeting headway for opposing trains on $s^*$ |
| $w_i,\ W_i$ | delay weight, cancellation penalty |
| $\underline D_{i0},\overline D_{i0}$ | departure window at origin |
| $T^{hor}$ | planning horizon |
| $M$ | big-M, valid choice $M=T^{hor}+\max r_{isp}+h^{bi}$ |

## 3. Variables

**Continuous:** $a_{is}, d_{is}\ge 0$ (actual arrival/departure); $t^a_{is}, t^d_{is}\ge 0$ (linearized delays).

**Binary:** $c_i$ (cancellation); $x_{is}$ (1 = own track on segment $s$; fixed to 1 for $s\ne s^*$); $u_{isp}$ (profile selection); $y_{ijs}\in\{0,1\}$ (ordering of $i<j$ on segment $s$); $\delta_{ijs}\in\{0,1\}$ (1 if $i,j$ use different tracks on $s$); $z_{is}\in\{0,1\}$ (1 if train $i$ occupies segment $s$ within the disruption window); $o_{ij}$ (bidirectional ordering on $s^*$); $g_{ij}$ (enforcement indicator for the bidirectional constraint).

## 4. Objective

$$\min\ Z=\sum_{i\in I} w_i\sum_{s\in S}\big(t^a_{is}+t^d_{is}\big)\;+\;\sum_{i\in I} W_i c_i\;+\;\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s}\sum_{p\in P_{is}} e_{isp}\,u_{isp}$$

with delay linearization
$$t^a_{is}\ge a_{is}-A_{is},\qquad t^d_{is}\ge d_{is}-D_{is},\qquad t^a_{is},t^d_{is}\ge 0 .$$
(Since delay costs are positive, $t=\max(0,\cdot)$ at optimum.)

## 5. Constraints

**C1 — Timetable consistency** (running time from chosen profile):
$$a_{i,s+1}=d_{is}+\sum_{p\in P_{is}} r_{isp}\,u_{isp}+M c_i\qquad \forall i,\ s=0,\dots,n-1$$

**C2 — Exactly one profile unless cancelled:**
$$\sum_{p\in P_{is}}u_{isp}=1-c_i\qquad\forall i,\ s$$

**C3 — Dwell times:**
$$dw^{min}_{is}(1-c_i)\ \le\ d_{is}-a_{is}\ \le\ dw^{max}_{is}(1-c_i)+M c_i\qquad\forall i,\ s$$

**C4 — Rerouting feasibility.** $x_{is}=1$ for all $s\ne s^*$. On $s^*$, $z_{is}=1$ iff occupancy $[d_{is},a_{i,s+1}]$ intersects $[T_1,T_2]$:
$$d_{is}\ge T_2-M(1-z_{is}),\qquad a_{i,s+1}\le T_1+M z_{is}\qquad s=s^*$$
Trains outside the window cannot reroute (their own track is free):
$$x_{is}\ \ge\ 1-z_{is}\qquad s=s^*$$

**C5 — Same-track headways** (exact linearization via $\delta$). For all $i<j$, $s$:
$$\delta_{ijs}\ge x_{is}-x_{js},\qquad \delta_{ijs}\ge x_{js}-x_{is}$$
$$d_{js}\ \ge\ d_{is}+h_s-M(2-y_{ijs}+\delta_{ijs}+c_i+c_j)$$
$$d_{is}\ \ge\ d_{js}+h_s-M(1+y_{ijs}+\delta_{ijs}+c_i+c_j)$$
$$a_{j,s+1}\ \ge\ a_{i,s+1}+h^a_s-M(2-y_{ijs}+\delta_{ijs}+c_i+c_j)$$
$$a_{i,s+1}\ \ge\ a_{j,s+1}+h^a_s-M(1+y_{ijs}+\delta_{ijs}+c_i+c_j)$$
If $y_{ijs}=1$ the first of each pair is active; if $y_{ijs}=0$ the second is. When $\delta_{ijs}=1$ (different tracks on $s^*$) or either train is cancelled, both are vacuous.

**C6 — Bidirectional meeting on the single-tracked disrupted segment.** For all $i\in I^{up}, j\in I^{dn}$, enforce only when both share a track and both traverse the window:
$$g_{ij}\ \ge\ 1-\delta_{ijs^*}-z_{i,s^*}-z_{j,s^*}-c_i-c_j$$
$$a_{j,s^*}\ \ge\ a_{i,s^*+1}+h^{bi}-M(1-o_{ij}+1-g_{ij})$$
$$a_{i,s^*}\ \ge\ a_{j,s^*+1}+h^{bi}-M(o_{ij}+1-g_{ij})$$
$g_{ij}=1$ forces exactly one of the two (via $o_{ij}$): the following opposing train may enter $s^*$ only after the preceding one has fully cleared it.

**C7 — Cancellation semantics.** All timing constraints (C1, C3, C5, C6, C10) carry $c_i$ big-M terms, so cancelled trains are fully deactivated; C2 removes their path/profile usage. Box bounds:
$$0\le a_{is},\,d_{is}\le T^{hor}+M c_i\qquad\forall i,\ s$$

**C8 — Departure window:**
$$\underline D_{i0}(1-c_i)\ \le\ d_{i0}\ \le\ \overline D_{i0}(1-c_i)+M c_i\qquad\forall i$$

**C9 — Profile feasibility.** Ensured in preprocessing: $P_{is}=\{p:\ r^{min}_{is}\le r_{isp}\le r^{max}_{is}\}$; energy data $e_{isp}$ satisfies monotonicity (longer running time ⇒ lower energy).

**C10 — Platform capacity.** For each station $s$, binary $\pi_{ijs}$ (=1 if dwells of $i$ and $j$ at $s$ overlap), for all $i<j$:
$$a_{js}\ge d_{is}-M(1-\pi_{ijs})-M(c_i+c_j),\qquad a_{is}\ge d_{js}-M\pi_{ijs}-M(c_i+c_j)$$
$$\sum_{j\ne i}\pi_{ijs}\ \le\ C_s\qquad\forall i\quad(\text{pairwise counting relaxation of at most } C_s \text{ simultaneous dwells})$$

**C11 — Binary declarations:**
$$c_i,\ x_{is},\ u_{isp},\ y_{ijs},\ \delta_{ijs},\ z_{is},\ o_{ij},\ g_{ij},\ \pi_{ijs}\in\{0,1\}$$

## 6. Assumptions

1. Running times depend only on the chosen discrete speed profile; profiles are precomputed, satisfy speed limits, and energy decreases with running time.
2. Rerouting is possible only on $s^*$, and only for trains whose occupancy overlaps the disruption window.
3. Headways are constant per segment/station; C10 gives a valid pairwise platform-capacity relaxation.
4. Cancellation is a full-train decision; cancelled trains incur $W_i$, consume no capacity, and their times are driven to 0 by the positive objective weights.
5. Big-M $=T^{hor}+\max r_{isp}+h^{bi}$ is valid since all times lie in $[0,T^{hor}+M]$.
6. Delay is measured as lateness only (no earliness penalty); weights $w_i, W_i$ are exogenous.

This model simultaneously decides retiming ($a,d$), reordering ($y,o$), rerouting ($x$), cancellation ($c$), and speed-profile selection ($u$), yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable with executable speed profiles, and minimizes total delay, cancellation cost, and energy consumption.

# MILP: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

This model integrates (A) a rolling stock **composition model** (in the spirit of Fioole et al., 2006) and (B) an **infrastructure feasibility model** (in the spirit of Van Aken et al., 2017), coupled through **combinatorial Benders cuts**.

---

## 1. Assumptions (marked where information was missing)

- **A1.** The timetable is fixed; only rolling stock assignments change. Passenger trains may be delayed by at most Δ = 5 minutes (assumption) to create shunting windows; delays are absorbed by timetable buffers.
- **A2.** A set of train unit types exists with fixed capacities and lengths; composition changes (adding/coupling units) are allowed only at stations.
- **A3.** Shunting movements occur only at the disrupted-relevant stations S (e.g., Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal).
- **A4.** Infrastructure is modeled at track-section level: each track section can host at most one movement (train or shunting) at a time (exclusive occupancy).
- **A5.** All shunting movements require an available shunting driver (capacity limit per time window, assumption).
- **A6.** Cancellations of passenger trips are allowed at a high penalty.
- **A7.** Disruption: a set of trips/tracks is unavailable during [T_d^start, T_d^end].

---

## 2. Sets and parameters

**Rolling stock part**

- $T$: set of scheduled passenger trips (timetabled, with fixed departure/arrival times and stations).
- $K$: set of train unit types; $c_k$: seats of type $k$; $l_k$: length (m); $L_s$: max platform length at station $s$.
- $N_k^0$: available units of type $k$.
- $A_t$: required seats on trip $t$ (peak load estimate).
- $o_t, d_t$: origin/destination station of trip $t$; $\tau_t$: duration.
- $w_{tt'} = 1$ if trip $t'$ can directly succeed trip $t$ with the same unit (compatible stations/times).
- $M$: set of potential shunting movements $m$ at stations in $S$, each with origin track, destination track, earliest start time $e_m$, duration $p_m$.
- $\alpha^{cap}, \alpha^{bal}, \alpha^{dev}, \alpha^{canc}, \alpha^{shunt}$: objective weights (assumption: tuned weights).

**Infrastructure part**

- $R$: track sections at stations in $S$; $r(m)$: sections used by shunting movement $m$.
- $P$: passenger train events (arrivals/departures at $S$) with scheduled times $\pi_e$.
- $u_{ee'}$: minimal headway between events $e, e'$ on shared sections.
- $D$: shunting drivers available per time window.

---

## 3. Variables

**Rolling stock**

- $x_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $k$ on trip $t$.
- $y_{tt',k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: units of type $k$ continuing from trip $t$ to trip $t'$.
- $z_{mk} \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $m$ is performed with a unit of type $k$.
- $h_{s,k}^{start}, h_{s,k}^{end} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: units of type $k$ starting/ending the day at station $s$.
- $\delta_t \in \{0,1\}$: trip $t$ is cancelled.

**Infrastructure**

- $\sigma_m \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $m$ is executed (equals $\sum_k z_{mk}$).
- $a_m \ge 0$: start-time shift (delay in minutes) of shunting movement $m$.
- $d_e \in \{0,1,\dots,\Delta\}$: delay (minutes) of passenger event $e$.
- $q_{mm'} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering: $m$ before $m'$ on conflicting infrastructure.
- $b_{me} \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $m$ is scheduled **before** event $e$.

---

## 4. Objective function

$$
\min \; \alpha^{cap}\sum_{t\in T}\delta_t A_t
+ \alpha^{dev}\Big(\sum_{e\in P} d_e + \sum_{m\in M} a_m\Big)
+ \alpha^{shunt}\sum_{m\in M}\sum_{k\in K} z_{mk}
+ \alpha^{bal}\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{k\in K} \big|h^{start}_{s,k}-h^{end}_{s,k}\big|
+ \alpha^{cap}\sum_{t\in T}\Big(c^{seat}\big(A_t-\sum_k c_k x_{t,k}\big)^+ + c^{len}\big(\sum_k l_k x_{t,k}-L_{d_t}\big)^+\Big)
$$

Linearized by introducing $u_t \ge 0$ (seat shortage) and $v_t \ge 0$ (length excess):

$$
\min \; \alpha^{canc}\sum_t \delta_t A_t + \alpha^{dev}\big(\sum_e d_e + \sum_m a_m\big) + \alpha^{shunt}\sum_{m,k} z_{mk} + \alpha^{bal}\sum_{s,k} g_{s,k} + c^{seat}\sum_t u_t + c^{len}\sum_t v_t
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Rolling stock (composition model)

**(C1) Seat coverage:**
$$\sum_{k\in K} c_k\, x_{t,k} + \delta_t A_t \ge A_t \qquad \forall t\in T$$

**(C2) Composition feasibility / length:**
$$\sum_{k\in K} l_k\, x_{t,k} \le L_{d_t} + v_t \qquad \forall t\in T$$
$$u_t \ge A_t - \sum_k c_k x_{t,k} \qquad \forall t\in T$$

**(C3) Flow conservation per type and trip:**
$$x_{t,k} = \sum_{t': w_{tt'}=1} y_{tt',k} + \sum_{m \in M_{out}(t)} z_{mk} \qquad \forall t, k$$
$$x_{t',k} = \sum_{t: w_{tt'}=1} y_{tt',k} + \sum_{m \in M_{in}(t')} z_{mk} \qquad \forall t', k$$

where $M_{out}(t)$ / $M_{in}(t)$ are shunting movements leaving/entering the station right after/before trip $t$.

**(C4) Fleet size:**
$$\sum_{s} h^{start}_{s,k} \le N_k^0 \qquad \forall k$$
$$h^{start}_{s,k} + \sum_{t: o_t = s} \sum_{k} x_{t,k}\big|_{\text{first trip}} = \text{(inflow balance)} \qquad \text{(standard flow initialization)}$$

**(C5) Balance (stick-to-plan / night repositioning):**
$$g_{s,k} \ge h^{start}_{s,k} - h^{end}_{s,k}, \quad g_{s,k} \ge h^{end}_{s,k} - h^{start}_{s,k} \qquad \forall s,k$$

**(C6) Shunting movement selection consistency:**
$$\sigma_m = \sum_{k\in K} z_{mk} \le 1 \qquad \forall m\in M$$

### 5.2 Infrastructure model

**(I1) Timing of shunting movements** with start time $s_m = e_m + a_m$:
$$a_m \le \bar{A}_m (1 - \sigma_m) \qquad \forall m$$

**(I2) No overlap between conflicting shunting movements** (they use a common track section): either $m$ finishes before $m'$ starts, or vice versa:
$$s_m + p_m \le s_{m'} + \bar{T}(1 - q_{mm'}) \qquad \forall (m,m') \in C$$
$$s_{m'} + p_{m'} \le s_m + \bar{T}\, q_{mm'} \qquad \forall (m,m') \in C$$

**(I3) No overlap with delayed passenger events** on shared sections:
$$s_m + p_m \le \pi_e + d_e + \bar{T}(1 - b_{me}) \qquad \forall (m,e) \in C'$$
$$\pi_e + d_e + h_{ee'} \le s_m + \bar{T}\, b_{me} \qquad \forall (m,e) \in C'$$

**(I4) Delay bounds:**
$$0 \le d_e \le \Delta \qquad \forall e \in P$$

**(I5) Shunting driver capacity:** for each time window $W$:
$$\sum_{m: [s_m, s_m+p_m] \cap W \neq \emptyset} \sigma_m \le D_W$$
(linearized via big-M time-indexed binaries $\phi_{m,\theta} \in \{0,1\}$: $\sum_\theta \phi_{m\theta} = \sigma_m$, $\sum_{m: \theta \in [s_m, s_m+p_m)} \phi_{m\theta} \le D_W$.)

### 5.3 Combinatorial Benders cuts (link between models)

Let the master (rolling stock) propose a set $\hat{M} = \{m : \hat\sigma_m = 1\}$. If the infrastructure subproblem is infeasible for $\hat{M}$, it returns a minimal infeasible subset $I \subseteq \hat{M}$. Add the **no-good cut** to the master:

$$\sum_{m \in I} \sigma_m \le |I| - 1 \qquad \text{(infeasibility cut)}$$

If the subproblem is feasible but yields required delays $\hat d_e, \hat a_m$, add an **optimality cut**:

$$\alpha^{dev}\Big(\sum_{e} d_e + \sum_m a_m\Big) \ge \alpha^{dev}\Big(\sum_e \hat d_e + \sum_m \hat a_m\Big) - \bar{B}\Big(|\hat{M}| - \sum_{m\in \hat M}\sigma_m\Big)$$

The algorithm iterates: solve master → check infrastructure → add cuts → repeat until no violations.

---

## 6. Model summary

- **Variables:** integer ($x, y, h$), binary ($z, \delta, \sigma, q, b, \phi$), continuous nonnegative ($a, d, u, v, g$).
- **Objective:** weighted sum of cancellations, seat shortages, length violations, deviations/delays, number of shunting movements, and day-balance asymmetry.
- **Constraints:** composition flow (C1–C6), infrastructure non-overlap and resource constraints (I1–I5), and iteratively generated Benders cuts.

This formulation completely describes the integrated rolling stock rescheduling problem with infrastructure feasibility, matching the described exact Combinatorial Benders framework; the iterative heuristic is obtained by fixing $\sigma_m$ sequentially (one shunting movement at a time) instead of solving the infrastructure model for all movements simultaneously.

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## Sets and Parameters

- **T** trains; **S** stations (|S| stations, ordered); **E** segments (each segment e connects stations `s(e)` and `s'(e)`); **K** admissible speed profiles (e.g., k = 1,…,4)
- `schedArr(i,j)`, `schedDep(i,j)`: scheduled arrival/departure of train i at station j
- `run(i,e,k)`: running time of train i on segment e under profile k
- `en(i,e,k)`: energy consumption of train i on segment e under profile k
- `w(i)`: passenger weight of train i; `cC(i)`: cancellation penalty; `cD`: delay cost per time unit
- `h`: minimum headway on a segment; `dw`: minimum dwell time
- Blocked segment(s) B and disruption window [τ₁, τ₂]
- **M**: sufficiently large constant

**Assumptions (marked where missing in the input):** double-track corridor with one direction per track; a single disruption blocks one track of segment(s) e ∈ B during [τ₁, τ₂]; a discrete, finite set of precomputed dynamically feasible speed profiles per train–segment is given (time–energy trade-off: faster profiles consume more energy); delays are weighted by on-board passengers.

## Variables

**Continuous:**
- `a(i,j) ≥ 0` — actual arrival time of train i at station j
- `d(i,j) ≥ 0` — actual departure time of train i at station j
- `δ(i,j) ≥ 0` — delay of train i at station j

**Binary:**
- `x(i,e,k) ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train i runs profile k on segment e
- `r(i,e) ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train i is rerouted to the opposite track on segment e
- `y(i,i',e) ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train i traverses segment e before train i′ (ordering), for i < i′
- `z(i) ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train i is cancelled
- `c(i,i',j) ∈ {0,1}` — station platform ordering binary (i before i′ at station j)

## Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay + cancellation cost + energy:

**min** Σᵢ Σⱼ cD·w(i)·δ(i,j) + Σᵢ cC(i)·z(i) + Σᵢ Σₑ∈E Σ_k en(i,e,k)·x(i,e,k)

## Constraints

**1. Delay definition:**
- δ(i,j) ≥ a(i,j) − schedArr(i,j) − M·z(i)  ∀i,j

**2. Timetable time windows:**
- d(i,j) ≥ schedDep(i,j)  ∀i,j (no early departure)
- a(i,j) ≤ schedArr(i,j) + Δ_max + M·z(i)  ∀i,j (maximum admissible delay Δ_max; cancelled trains unrestricted)

**3. Dwell time:**
- d(i,j) ≥ a(i,j) + dw − M·z(i)  ∀i, j intermediate

**4. Running-time consistency with selected speed profile:**
- a(i,s′(e)) − d(i,s(e)) = Σ_k run(i,e,k)·x(i,e,k) − M·z(i)  ∀i,e∈E
 (actual segment running time must exactly match the chosen profile's running time — this couples timetable and speed management)

**5. Exactly one profile per train–segment:**
- Σ_k x(i,e,k) = 1 − z(i)  ∀i,e

**6. Route continuity / flow conservation:**
- d(i,s(e+1)) ≥ a(i,s′(e)) − M·z(i)  ∀i, consecutive segments e, e+1

**7. Rerouting logic:**
- r(i,e) = 0 for e ∉ B (rerouting only on blocked segments)
- r(i,e) ≤ 1 − z(i)  ∀e ∈ B
- If train i traverses e ∈ B within [τ₁, τ₂] then r(i,e) = 1 (forced reroute to opposite track): r(i,e) ≥ g(i,e) − z(i), where g(i,e) is a binary indicator that train i's passage time overlaps the disruption window (modeled via standard big-M indicator constraints on a(i,s′(e)) vs τ₁, τ₂)

**8. Conflict-free ordering on each segment (same track, pairwise big-M disjunction):** for all i < i′, e:
- a(i′,s′(e)) − a(i,s′(e)) ≥ h − M·( y(i,i′,e) + z(i) + z(i′) )
- a(i,s′(e)) − a(i′,s′(e)) ≥ h − M·( 1 − y(i,i′,e) + z(i) + z(i′) )

**9. Bidirectional conflict on the shared (rerouted) track:** for all i < i′ with opposite scheduled directions and e ∈ B, the disjunction additionally requires that if both trains use the same physical track (i.e., rerouted train meets a train on its original track), one must fully exit before the other enters:
- d(i′,s(e)) − a(i,s′(e)) ≥ 0 − M·( 3 − r(i,e) − r(i′,e) + σ(i,i′) + y(i,i′,e) )
- d(i,s(e)) − a(i′,s′(e)) ≥ 0 − M·( 3 − r(i,e) − r(i′,e) + σ(i,i′) + (1 − y(i,i′,e)) )

where σ(i,i′) = 1 if i and i′ have the same scheduled direction (constraint relaxed in that case, since constraint 8 applies).

**10. Station/platform capacity:** for all i < i′, j:
- d(i′,j) − a(i,j) ≥ −M·( 1 − c(i,i′,j) + z(i) + z(i′) )
- d(i,j) − a(i′,j) ≥ −M·( c(i,i′,j) + z(i) + z(i′) )

**11. Speed-profile feasibility:**
- x(i,e,k) = 0 for inadmissible (i,e,k) combinations (dynamics/rolling-stock restrictions)

**12. Variable domains:** a, d, δ ≥ 0; x, r, y, z, c binary; departure from origin within operating horizon.

## Notes

- Constraint 4 is the key coupling: it links the continuous timetable variables to the discrete speed-profile choice, so the rescheduled timetable is guaranteed executable at train-control level.
- Constraint 9 ensures conflict-free bidirectional operation when trains divert to the opposite track within the disruption window.
- Cancellation (z) relaxes all constraints of a train via big-M and charges cC(i) in the objective.
- The model is linear: energy enters through the binary profile-selection variables; all timing interactions are big-M disjunctions.

# Final MILP: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## Assumptions
- Discretized time horizon [0, T]; double-track corridor with stations 1..S; one segment e* = (σ, σ+1) partially blocked during [T₀, T₁], leaving one open track.
- Train dynamics are precomputed into a finite menu of speed profiles per train-segment (each with min/max running time and energy), keeping the model linear.
- One platform track per direction at each station; right-shift-only rescheduling (trains never run earlier than scheduled); hard deadlines at destination (a lateness-penalty variant is noted).

## Sets
Trains i ∈ I; stations s ∈ S; segments e = (s, s+1) ∈ E; disrupted segment e*; profiles p ∈ P_{i,e}; station routes d ∈ D_i.

## Parameters
τ^{min/max}_{i,e,p} (running time bounds per profile), E_{i,e,p} (energy), dwell^{min}_{i,s}, headways h_seg, h_arr, h_dep, h_cross, margins γ^{in}, γ^{out}, reference times r_{i,s}, deadline D_i^{max}, weights w^c, w^d, w^r (normalized w^c ≫ w^d ≫ w^r), u_{i,e*} (parameter: 1 if train i normally uses the open track), big-M = T.

## Variables
- Continuous: arrival a_{i,s}, departure d_{i,s}, entry/exit times t^{in}_{i,e}, t^{out}_{i,e}, right-shift deviation Δ_i ≥ 0.
- Binary: cancellation c_i; rerouting y_i; profile x_{i,e,p}; station route q_{i,d}; ordering binaries z_{ik,e} (segments), z*_{ik} (open track of e*), β_{ik,s} (station A–A/D–D), g_{ik,s} (platform crossing); occupancy o^i_{e*}.

## Objective
min Σ_i ( w^c_i c_i + w^d_i Δ_i ) + β Σ_{i,e,p} E_{i,e,p} x_{i,e,p}
(cancellation + weighted delay + energy, with w^c ≫ w^d ≫ β so energy is minimized within the delay budget).

## Constraints
- **(C1) Selection:** Σ_p x_{i,e,p} = 1 − c_i; Σ_d q_{i,d} = 1 − c_i.
- **(C3) Propagation with profile time windows:**
 a_{i,s+1} − d_{i,s} ≥ τ^{min}_{i,e,p} − M(1 − x_{i,e,p}) − M c_i
 a_{i,s+1} − d_{i,s} ≤ τ^{max}_{i,e,p} + M(1 − x_{i,e,p}) + M c_i  ∀ e=(s,s+1), p
 Dwell: d_{i,s} − a_{i,s} ≥ dwell^{min}_{i,s} − M c_i.
- **(C4) Right-shift-only:** a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} ≥ r_{i,s} − M c_i; Δ_i ≥ a_{i,dest} − r_{i,dest} − M c_i.
- **(C5) Occupancy times:** t^{in}_{i,e} = d_{i,s} − γ^{in} + M c_i; t^{out}_{i,e} = a_{i,s+1} + γ^{out} − M c_i.
- **(C6) Same-direction segment headway (e ≠ e\*):** for same-direction pairs, ordering binary z_{ik,e}:
 t^{in}_{k,e} ≥ t^{in}_{i,e} + h_seg − M(1 − z_{ik,e}) − M(c_i + c_k)
 t^{in}_{i,e} ≥ t^{in}_{k,e} + h_seg − M z_{ik,e} − M(c_i + c_k).
- **(C7) Single-track no-overlap on e\*** (replaces C6 there): occupancy indicators o^i_{e*} = y_i for trains normally on the closed track, o^i_{e*} = 1 − c_i for trains normally on the open track. For all pairs:
 t^{in}_{k,e*} ≥ t^{out}_{i,e*} − M(2 − o^i_{e*} − o^k_{e*}) − M(1 − z*_{ik})
 t^{in}_{i,e*} ≥ t^{out}_{k,e*} − M(2 − o^i_{e*} − o^k_{e*}) − M z*_{ik}.
- **(C6-disruption) Blocked-track availability:** if a train uses the blocked track (o on blocked track = 1), it must clear e* before T₀ − γ^{out} or enter after T₁ + γ^{in}; otherwise it must reroute (y_i = 1), enforced by big-M disjunction:
 t^{out}_{i,e*} ≤ T₀ − γ^{out} + M(1 − v_i) + M c_i
 t^{in}_{i,e*} ≥ T₁ + γ^{in} − M(1 − v_i) + M c_i
 where v_i indicates use of the blocked track (v_i = 1 − y_i for normally-closed-track trains, v_i ≡ 1 otherwise, with the disjunction forcing timing outside the window).
- **(C9) Station conflicts:** arrival–arrival and departure–departure headways (h_arr, h_dep) for same-direction callers only, via β_{ik,s}; arrival–departure crossing (h_cross) only for opposite-direction pairs sharing a platform track, via g_{ik,s}; all relaxed by M(c_i + c_k).
- **(C10) Route consistency:** Σ_{d ∈ D_i^{compat(e\*)}} q_{i,d} ≥ y_i − c_i.
- **(C11) Deadline:** a_{i,s_dest} ≤ D_i^{max} + M c_i (alternative: replace with lateness variable L_i ≥ a_{i,dest} − D_i^{max} penalized by w^L_i).
- **(C12) Domains:** times ≥ 0 and ≤ T; c, y, x, q, z, z*, β, g ∈ {0,1}.

This MILP jointly decides retiming (a, d), reordering (ordering binaries), rerouting (y, q), cancellation (c), and speed profile selection (x), yielding a conflict-free timetable whose running times are exactly realizable by the chosen profiles, with the delay–energy tradeoff handled endogenously through the profile menu.

The revised model addressed the occupancy and track-sharing issues correctly. Two remaining fixes I incorporated directly into the final version below: (1) the objective must use nonnegative delay variables (raw deviations could be negative for early trains, distorting the objective); (2) the energy term from the first draft was dropped and is restored, since energy-efficient profile selection is a core part of the TRSMP.

# Final MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices
- $I$: trains; $S_i$: ordered stations on train $i$'s route; $J$: segments (segment $j$ between stations $s, s{+}1$), each with an up and a down physical track.
- $K_{i,j}$: precomputed speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $j$ (running time $\tau_{i,j,k}$, energy $e_{i,j,k}$).
- $P_j$: conflicting train pairs $(i,h)$, $i<h$, both traversing $j$.
- $D \subseteq I \times J$: (train, segment) pairs whose original track is blocked during $[t_0, t_1]$.

## 2. Parameters
$\tau_{i,j,k}, e_{i,j,k}$ (profile data); $dw_{i,s}$ (dwell); $H$ (headway); $t_0,t_1$ (disruption window); $T^{arr}_{i,s}, T^{dep}_{i,s}$ (scheduled times); $w_i$ (delay weight); $\lambda$ (energy weight); $\Pi$ (cancellation penalty); $\delta^{max}$ (max delay); $M$ (big-M, e.g. $M = t_1 + \delta^{max} + \max_k \tau_{i,j,k} + H$).

## 3. Variables
- Continuous: $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0$ (arrival/departure); $\Delta^{arr}_{i,s}, \Delta^{dep}_{i,s} \ge 0$ (delays).
- Binary: $y_{i,j,k}$ (profile selection); $c_i$ (cancellation); $r_{i,j}$ (rerouting to opposite track); $b_{i,j}$ (enters blocked segment before $t_0$); $z_{i,h,j}$ (ordering: $i$ first); $g_{i,h,j}$ (pair shares a physical track).

Derived: $e_{i,j} = d_{i,s}$ (entry), $x_{i,j} = a_{i,s+1}$ (exit/release).

## 4. Objective
$$\min \sum_{i} w_i \Big[\sum_{s} \big(\Delta^{arr}_{i,s} + \Delta^{dep}_{i,s}\big) + \Pi\, c_i\Big] \;+\; \lambda \sum_{i}\sum_{j}\sum_{k} e_{i,j,k}\, y_{i,j,k}$$

Delay linearization:
$$\Delta^{arr}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s}, \quad \Delta^{dep}_{i,s} \ge d_{i,s} - T^{dep}_{i,s}, \quad \Delta^{arr}_{i,s}, \Delta^{dep}_{i,s} \ge 0$$

## 5. Constraints

**(5.1) Propagation** (running time from selected profile; relaxed only for cancellation):
$$a_{i,s+1} \ge d_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} \tau_{i,j,k}\, y_{i,j,k} - M c_i \qquad \forall i,\; \forall j \in S_i$$

**(5.2) Dwell time:**
$$d_{i,s+1} \ge a_{i,s+1} + dw_{i,s+1} - M c_i \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(5.3) Time bounds (no early departure; max delay):**
$$T^{dep}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} \le T^{dep}_{i,s} + \delta^{max} + M c_i, \qquad T^{arr}_{i,s} \le a_{i,s} \le T^{arr}_{i,s} + \delta^{max} + M c_i$$

**(5.4) Cancellation suppresses all movements:**
$$d_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i), \quad a_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i) \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(5.5) Exactly one profile per (running) train–segment:**
$$\sum_{k \in K_{i,j}} y_{i,j,k} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, j$$

**(5.6) Rerouting only on disrupted segments:**
$$r_{i,j} = 0 \quad \forall (i,j) \notin D$$

**(5.7) Disruption window:** for $(i,j) \in D$, a train on its blocked track must enter before $t_0$ or after $t_1$; rerouting relaxes both:
$$e_{i,j} \le t_0 + M b_{i,j} + M r_{i,j}$$
$$e_{i,j} \ge t_1 - M(1 - b_{i,j}) - M r_{i,j}$$

**(5.8) Shared-track indicator** (opposite directions: each train's original track is the other's reroute track, so any rerouting creates sharing):
$$g_{i,h,j} \ge r_{i,j} + r_{h,j} - 1, \quad g_{i,h,j} \ge r_{i,j}, \quad g_{i,h,j} \ge r_{h,j}, \quad g_{i,h,j} \le r_{i,j} + r_{h,j}$$

**(5.9) Occupancy-based headway disjunction** (exit-to-entry separation, guaranteeing no overlap despite differing running times):

*Same direction (always share original track):*
$$x_{i,j} + H \le e_{h,j} + M(1 - z_{i,h,j}) + M c_i + M c_h$$
$$x_{h,j} + H \le e_{i,j} + M z_{i,h,j} + M c_i + M c_h$$

*Opposite directions (share only if $g_{i,h,j}=1$):*
$$x_{i,j} + H \le e_{h,j} + M(1 - z_{i,h,j}) + M(1 - g_{i,h,j}) + M c_i + M c_h$$
$$x_{h,j} + H \le e_{i,j} + M z_{i,h,j} + M(1 - g_{i,h,j}) + M c_i + M c_h$$

**(5.10) Domains:** $a, d, \Delta \ge 0$; $y, c, r, b, z, g \in \{0,1\}$.

## 6. Assumptions
1. Fixed station sequence per train; only track choice within a segment is flexible (local rerouting).
2. One track of a disrupted segment is blocked; the opposite track remains available.
3. Speed profiles are precomputed and discrete; no continuous speed optimization.
4. Pairwise occupancy separation (exit + headway before entry) guarantees conflict-free segment usage.
5. No early departures; delays penalized linearly; cancellation is a whole-train decision with penalty $\Pi$.
6. Trains rerouted onto a shared track traverse the segment within the disruption window (symmetric window logic applies to the shared track if it too is blocked at other times).

This is a fully linear MILP (continuous: $a, d, \Delta$; binary: $y, c, r, b, z, g$) that simultaneously optimizes train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles under a partial segment blockage, and is the natural basis for the decomposition into a train-plan selection IP described in the paper's solution framework.

Text:
**Selected model: Model 1** — it is the most complete and internally consistent formulation: it covers all four levers (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation), correctly couples running times to discrete speed profiles with a clean linear interpolation, and handles the bidirectional conflict on the shared opposite track during the disruption window.

# Integrated MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Physical setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ and inter-station segments $B = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$. Each segment $b$ has two directed tracks: the *normal* track (down trains use track $D_b$, up trains track $U_b$) and the *opposite* track available for counter-flow rerouting.

**Disruption.** A partial segment blockage affects the normal track of segments $B^{dis} \subseteq B$ on one direction during time window $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$. Trains scheduled to traverse these segments during the window may either wait (retiming/reordering) or be rerouted onto the opposite track (single-track operation), subject to conflict-free bidirectional use.

**Key assumptions (explicit):**
- (A1) Time is handled via big-$M$ continuous variables; all headways are fixed minimum separation times.
- (A2) Each inter-station run has a finite set of *discrete speed profiles* $P_{i,b}$ for train $i$ on segment $b$, each with known duration $\tau_{i,b,p}$ and energy $e_{i,b,p}$; intermediate profiles are captured by **linear interpolation** between adjacent profiles.
- (A3) Train order within a segment on a track cannot change (no overtaking on the same track between stations); overtaking is possible at stations via reordering.
- (A4) A train may be rerouted to the opposite track **only** if its entry time into the affected segment lies within the disruption window.
- (A5) Rolling stock is bounded: each train must have a feasible turnaround at its terminal.
- (A6) Cancellation is a binary decision with a fixed penalty; a cancelled train occupies no infrastructure.
- (A7) Station capacity is expressed as a maximum number of simultaneously occupied platform tracks.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains, $i \in I$; $I^{dis} \subseteq I$: trains potentially affected |
| $S$, $B$ | stations, segments ($b$ connects stations $b$ and $b+1$) |
| $K_b = \{D_b, U_b\}$ | tracks on segment $b$ (directional) |
| $P_{i,b}$ | candidate speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $b$ |
| $B^{dis}$ | blocked segments (normal track blocked in window) |
| $T$ | planning horizon $[0, T^{max}]$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a^{sch}_{i,s}, d^{sch}_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{run}$ | minimum headways: arrival–arrival, departure–departure, run-in/run-out (same track) |
| $\underline{dw}_{i,s}, \overline{dw}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\tau_{i,b,p}, e_{i,b,p}$ | duration and energy of profile $p$ of train $i$ on segment $b$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights: delay cost per minute, energy cost per kWh |
| $\gamma_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $C_s$ | station capacity (number of platforms) at station $s$ |
| $T^{start}, T^{end}$ | disruption window |
| $M$ | big-$M$ constant |
| $t^{turn}_i$ | minimum turnaround time at terminal of train $i$ |

## 4. Variables

**Timetable:**
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival / departure times (continuous, minutes).
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**.

**Routing:**
- $r_{i,b} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **rerouted to the opposite track** on segment $b$ (only defined for $b \in B^{dis}$, $i \in I^{dis}$).

**Speed profiles:**
- $x_{i,b,p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if profile $p$ selected for train $i$ on segment $b$.
- $\lambda_{i,b} \in [0,1]$: interpolation weight between adjacent profile pairs.

**Ordering (same-track sequencing):**
- $\delta_{i,j,b,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on track $k$ of segment $b$.

**Occupancy (station capacity):**
- $o_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ occupies station $s$ during (discretized) time slice $t$; $\Delta_t$ slice length.

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z =
\sum_{i \in I} w_i \Big[ (a_{i,S_{end}} - a^{sch}_{i,S_{end}}) + \sum_{s \in S} L_{i,s} \Big]
+ \beta \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{b \in B} \Big( \sum_{p \in P_{i,b}} e_{i,b,p} x_{i,b,p} + \Delta e_{i,b}\, \lambda_{i,b} \Big)
+ \sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i y_i
$$

Delay linearization: introduce $L_{i,s} \ge 0$ with

$$
L_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^{sch}_{i,s}, \qquad L_{i,s} \ge 0 \quad \forall i, s
$$

(only terminal or passenger-relevant stations may be included in the delay sum, per operator policy).

## 6. Timetable Feasibility Constraints

**(C1) Cancellation decouples the train:**

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-y_i) \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C2) Dwell time bounds:**

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge \underline{dw}_{i,s}(1-y_i), \qquad
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \overline{dw}_{i,s}(1-y_i) + M y_i \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C3) Consistency along the route** (arrival at next station = departure from previous + running time):

$$
a_{i,b+1} = d_{i,b} + \Big(\sum_{p \in P_{i,b}} \tau_{i,b,p} x_{i,b,p} + \Delta\tau_{i,b}\lambda_{i,b}\Big)(1-y_i) \quad \forall i,\, b \in B
$$

**(C4) Headways on the same track of segment $b$**, for each ordered pair $(i,j)$ on the same track $k$, linearized with ordering variable $\delta_{i,j,b,k}$:

$$
d_{j,b} \ge a_{i,b+1} + h^{run} - M(1-\delta_{i,j,b,k}) - M(y_i + y_j)
$$
$$
d_{i,b} \ge a_{j,b+1} + h^{run} - M\delta_{i,j,b,k} - M(y_i + y_j)
$$

Analogous constraints with $h^{arr}$ on arrivals into the following station and $h^{dep}$ on departures from the preceding station.

**(C5) Track consistency:** for $b \in B^{dis}$, train $i$ uses the normal track iff $r_{i,b}=0$ and the opposite track iff $r_{i,b}=1$; ordering variables $\delta_{i,j,b,k}$ are activated only when both trains are on $k$ (enforced via big-$M$ products).

**(C6) Station capacity:**

$$
\sum_{i \in I} o_{i,s,t} \le C_s \quad \forall s, t
$$

with occupancy linking via standard big-$M$:

$$
a_{i,s} \le t\Delta_t + M(1-o_{i,s,t}), \qquad d_{i,s} \ge (t-1)\Delta_t - M(1-o_{i,s,t})
$$

**(C7) Horizon bounds:** $0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le T^{max}$.

## 7. Speed Profile Coupling and Linear Interpolation

**(C8) Running time = selected profile duration.** Discrete choice part:

$$
\sum_{p \in P_{i,b}} x_{i,b,p} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i, b
$$

**Linear interpolation** between adjacent profiles (indexed $p = 1,\dots,m$ in increasing duration order):

$$
\tau^{eff}_{i,b} = \sum_{p} \tau_{i,b,p} x_{i,b,p} + \sum_{p=1}^{m-1} \lambda_{i,b,p}\big(\tau_{i,b,p+1} - \tau_{i,b,p}\big)
$$
$$
e^{eff}_{i,b} = \sum_{p} e_{i,b,p} x_{i,b,p} + \sum_{p=1}^{m-1} \lambda_{i,b,p}\big(e_{i,b,p+1} - e_{i,b,p}\big)
$$

with activation only between the chosen profile and its neighbors (big-$M$):

$$
\lambda_{i,b,p} \le x_{i,b,p} + x_{i,b,p+1} \quad \forall p = 1,\dots,m-1
$$

The effective duration $\tau^{eff}_{i,b}$ and energy $e^{eff}_{i,b}$ enter (C3) and the objective, respectively. (If pure discrete profiles suffice, set all $\lambda = 0$.)

## 8. Disruption, Rerouting, and Bidirectional Operation

**(C9) Rerouting allowed only during the disruption window:**

$$
d_{i,b} \ge T^{start} - M(1 - r_{i,b}), \qquad
d_{i,b} \le T^{end} + M(1 - r_{i,b}) \quad \forall i \in I^{dis},\, b \in B^{dis}
$$

**(C10) Blocked normal track:** trains *not* rerouted must not enter $b$ during the window — with binary $z_{i,b}$ ("runs before window"):

$$

**(C13) Turnaround at terminal:** for feasible turnaround pairs $(i,j) \in A^{turn}$:

$$
d_{j,1} \ge a_{i,S_{end}} + t^{turn}_{ij} - M(y_i + y_j) \quad \forall (i,j) \in A^{turn}
$$

I generated three candidate MILP formulations and selected the best one below (Model 3), which is the most complete and internally consistent: it cleanly integrates retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and discrete speed-profile selection, with correct big-M deactivation logic and a clear delay–energy trade-off.

# MILP Formulation: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions

- A double-track railway line divided into segments; each segment can host at most one train per direction at a time (block section occupancy).
- A disruption partially blocks segment set $\mathcal{B}$ during time window $[T^{dis}_1, T^{dis}_2]$; affected trains may be **rerouted** to the opposite track on blocked segments during the window (single-track operation).
- Each train–segment pair has a discrete set of precomputed feasible speed profiles, each with fixed running time and energy consumption.
- Delays are measured against the original timetable; trains may be retimed, reordered, rerouted, or cancelled.
- All times are integer (minutes), giving a linear model.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{I}$ | set of trains, $i \in \mathcal{I}$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | set of segments, $s \in \mathcal{S}$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_{is}$ | set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $\mathcal{T}$ | set of discrete time instants in the planning horizon |
| $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | blocked segments during disruption |
| $o(i)$ | direction of train $i$ (1 = up, 0 = down) |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $a^{orig}_{is}, d^{orig}_{is}$ | original arrival/departure time of train $i$ at segment $s$ |
| $\tau^{min}_{is}$ | minimum dwell/turnaround time of train $i$ at boundary of segment $s$ |
| $r_{isp}$ | running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $e_{isp}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway (min) between trains on a segment |
| $H_{ij}$ | 1 if trains $i,j$ are scheduled on the same segment sequence (potential conflict pair) |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ |
| $c_i$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $\alpha$ | energy cost coefficient (€/kWh or weighted) |
| $U^{dis}_s$ | capacity of segment $s$ during disruption (1 if single-track usable) |

## 4. Variables

**Timetable variables**
- $a_{is}, d_{is} \in \mathbb{Z}_+$: actual arrival/departure times.
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**.
- $\delta_{is} \ge 0$: arrival delay of train $i$ at segment $s$.

**Ordering / rerouting**
- $x_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on their shared segment.
- $z_{is} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses the **opposite track** on segment $s$ (rerouting; only defined for $s \in \mathcal{B}$).

**Speed-profile selection**
- $u_{isp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $s$.

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} w_i\, \delta_{is}}_{\text{total weighted delay}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} c_i\, y_i}_{\text{cancellation penalties}}
+ \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}}\sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}}\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{is}} e_{isp}\, u_{isp}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
\tag{1}
$$

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Speed-profile uniqueness.** Exactly one profile per train–segment (unless cancelled):
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{is}} u_{isp} = 1 - y_i \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{I},\ \forall s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{2}
$$

**(C2) Timetable dynamics (running + dwell).** Departure from segment $s$ equals arrival plus running time plus minimum dwell:
$$
d_{is} = a_{is} + \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{is}} r_{isp}\, u_{isp} + \tau^{min}_{is}(1-y_i) \quad \forall i,\ s
\tag{3}
$$

**(C3) Delay definition.**
$$
\delta_{is} \ge a_{is} - a^{orig}_{is} - M y_i \quad \forall i,\ s
\tag{4}
$$

**(C4) Disruption window on blocked segments.** A train occupying a blocked segment with its own track must not be inside the window; rerouted trains bypass this:
$$
a_{is} \ge T^{dis}_2 - M\big(y_i + z_{is}\big), \qquad
d_{is} \le T^{dis}_1 + M\big(y_i + z_{is}\big)
\quad \forall i,\ \forall s \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{5}
$$

**(C5) Rerouting availability.** Rerouting only allowed on blocked segments:
$$
z_{is} = 0 \quad \forall i,\ \forall s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{B}
\tag{5a}
$$

**(C6) Same-direction headway (conflict freedom).** For trains $i,j$ sharing segment $s$ in the same direction, separated in time by headway $h$:
$$
a_{js} \ge d_{is} + h - M(1 - x_{ij}) - M y_i - M y_j \quad \forall i<j,\ H_{ij}=1
\tag{6}
$$
$$
a_{is} \ge d_{js} + h - M\, x_{ij} - M y_i - M y_j \quad \forall i<j,\ H_{ij}=1
\tag{7}
$$

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict on rerouted segments.** If train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on $s$, it conflicts with trains $j$ of the opposite direction using their normal track; they must be sequenced:
$$
a_{js} \ge d_{is} + h - M(1 - x_{ij}) - M y_i - M y_j - M(1 - z_{is}) \quad \forall i,\ j: o(j) \ne o(i),\ s \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{8}
$$
$$
a_{is} \ge d_{js} + h - M\, x_{ij} - M y_i - M y_j - M(1 - z_{is}) \quad \forall i,\ j: o(j) \ne o(i),\ s \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{9}
$$

**(C8) Single-track capacity during disruption.** At most one train (any direction) may occupy a blocked segment at a time via rerouting; combined with (6)–(9) this ensures mutual exclusion:
$$
\sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \big(\sigma_{is} + z_{is}\big) \le U^{dis}_s \quad \forall s \in \mathcal{B},\ \forall t \in [T^{dis}_1, T^{dis}_2]
\tag{10}
$$
where $\sigma_{is} \in \{0,1\}$ is an auxiliary occupancy indicator defined by:
$$
\sigma_{is} \ge 1 - \frac{a_{is} - t}{M} - y_i, \qquad
\sigma_{is} \ge 1 - \frac{t - d_{is}}{M} - y_i \quad \forall i, s \in \mathcal{B},\ t \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{10a–10b}
$$

**(C9) Cancellation propagation.** A cancelled train occupies no resources (handled via $y_i$ terms above) and its times are free:
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \le M(1 - y_i) \quad \forall i,\ s
\tag{11}
$$

**(C10) Horizon bounds.**
$$
0 \le a_{is}, d_{is} \le T^{max} \quad \forall i,\ s
\tag{12}
$$

**(C11) Variable domains.**
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \in \mathbb{Z}_+,\quad \delta_{is} \ge 0,\quad y_i, x_{ij}, z_{is}, u_{isp}, \sigma_{is} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{13}
$$

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Timetable variables** ($a, d$) allow retiming; **order binaries** $x_{ij}$ allow reordering by selecting which disjunctive branch of the big-M headway constraints (6)–(9) is active.
- **Rerouting binaries** $z_{is}$ relax constraint (5) so affected trains may pass blocked segments on the opposite track during the disruption; constraints (8)–(9) then impose bidirectional conflict-free sequencing on the shared single track.
- **Cancellation binaries** $y_i$ remove a train entirely, paying penalty $c_i$ and deactivating its profile selection (2), timing (3), and delay (4) via big-M terms.
- **Speed-profile variables** $u_{isp}$ link discrete speed choices to the timetable: the running time in (3) becomes a linear function of the chosen profile, while the objective (1) charges energy $e_{isp}$ — capturing the delay–energy trade-off (faster profiles reduce delay but consume more energy).
- **Big-M constraints** (6)–(9) are disjunctive pairwise ordering constraints guaranteeing headway and conflict-free segment occupancy, including the mixed-direction case arising from rerouting.
- The objective balances three weighted criteria: passenger-weighted delay, service cancellation, and total traction energy.

All constraints are linear and the model contains both continuous and binary variables, hence it is a valid MILP for the TRSMP under partial segment blockage.

# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

The model describes a macroscopic railway network where trains must be rescheduled, rerouted, and reordered after primary delays occur, minimizing total secondary delay.

**Assumptions (marked where not given in the text):**
- **(A1)** Macroscopic infrastructure model: signals and block sections below station/track-group level are aggregated (as in Pellegrini et al., 2014).
- **(A2)** A finite set of feasible alternative routes exists for each train through each station.
- **(A3)** Minimum running and headway times per route are known constants.
- **(A4)** Trains cannot be canceled; all scheduled trains must run.
- **(A5)** Safety-relevant overlaps (margins behind stop signals) are treated as additional occupancy time of resources (per Lindenmaier et al., 2022); they are included in route-specific occupancy times.
- **(A6)** Delay propagation is modeled through resource occupancy conflicts (linear, as in the extended model of Section 3.3 of the paper).
- **(A7)** A finite rolling horizon (disturbance horizon) is considered; times are integer minutes (or seconds).

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $t$ |
| $S$ | set of infrastructure resources (track groups / routes' resources), index $s$ |
| $R_t \subseteq R$ | set of feasible alternative routes for train $t$; $R = \bigcup_t R_t$, index $r$ |
| $O_r$ | set of resources occupied by route $r$ |
| $K$ | set of scheduled events (arrival/departure/passing) of trains, index $k$; event $k$ belongs to train $t(k)$ |
| $P$ | set of ordered pairs of trains $(t_1,t_2)$ that may conflict, index $(t_1,t_2)$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d^{sched}_k$ | scheduled time of event $k$ |
| $d^{prim}_k$ | primary delay of event $k$ (input disturbance) |
| $w^{min}_{k}$ | minimum time between event $k$ and its successor on the same train |
| $h^{min}_{r_1 r_2 s}$ | minimum headway between routes $r_1, r_2$ on resource $s$ (includes safety overlap per A5) |
| $M$ | big-M constant (horizon length) |
| $H$ | disturbance horizon length |

## 4. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_t$ |
| $y_{t_1 t_2} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t_1$ passes resource before train $t_2$ (ordering) |
| $a_k \ge 0$ | continuous | actual (scheduled + primary + secondary) time of event $k$ |
| $\delta_k \ge 0$ | continuous | total (secondary) delay of event $k$ |
| $z_{t_1 t_2} \ge 0$ | continuous | pair-wise wait: time train $t_1$ waits for train $t_2$ |

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total delay:

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{k \in K} \delta_k$$

Optionally weighted: $\min \sum_k w_k \delta_k$ with priority weights $w_k$.

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Delay definition** (delay = actual − scheduled − primary):

$$\delta_k \ge a_k - d^{sched}_k - d^{prim}_k \qquad \forall k \in K$$

**(C2) Schedule consistency along each train** (minimum running/holding times):

$$a_{k+1} - a_k \ge w^{min}_k \qquad \forall k \in K \text{ with successor } k+1 \text{ on same train}$$

**(C3) Route selection — exactly one route per train:**

$$\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{t,r} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(C4) Pair-wise conflict definition** (sub-optimal model, no delay propagation): if $t_1$ precedes $t_2$ on a shared resource, $t_1$'s event must be sufficiently earlier:

$$a_{k_1} + \sum_{r_1 \in R_{t_1}} h^{min}_{r_1 r_2 s}\, x_{t_1 r_1} \le a_{k_2} + M(1 - y_{t_1 t_2}) \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P,\ \forall s \in O_{r_1} \cap O_{r_2}$$

and symmetrically:

$$a_{k_2} + \sum_{r_2 \in R_{t_2}} h^{min}_{r_2 r_1 s}\, x_{t_2 r_2} \le a_{k_1} + M\, y_{t_1 t_2} \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P$$

Together these force exactly one ordering per conflicting pair.

**(C5) Pair-wise wait variables** (linking delays to "who is waited for"):

$$z_{t_1 t_2} \ge \delta_{k_1} - \delta_{k_2} - M(1 - y_{t_1 t_2}) \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P$$

**(C6) Delay propagation (extended, globally optimal model):** waiting for another train propagates delay:

$$\delta_{k_1} \ge z_{t_1 t_2} + \delta_{k_2} - M(1 - y_{t_1 t_2}) \qquad \forall (t_1,t_2) \in P$$

*(Note: including C6 makes the model the global-optimum formulation of Section 3.3; omitting it yields the fast sub-optimal model of Section 3.1.)*

**(C7) Horizon bounds:**

$$a_k \le d^{sched}_k + d^{prim}_k + H \qquad \forall k \in K$$

**(C8) Variable domains:**

$$x_{t,r} \in \{0,1\},\quad y_{t_1t_2} \in \{0,1\},\quad a_k, \delta_k, z_{t_1t_2} \ge 0$$

## 7. Two-Stage Use of the Model

1. **Stage 1 (rerouting + reordering):** Solve the model with C1–C5, C7–C8 (no propagation, C6 omitted) → fast, sub-optimal route selection $\hat{x}$ and ordering $\hat{y}$.
2. **Stage 2 (rescheduling):** Fix $x = \hat{x}$ (and optionally $y = \hat{y}$), solve the full model including C6 → optimal delays for the given routes; or solve the full model with free $x,y$ for the guaranteed global optimum.

## 8. Complexity Note

The model has $O(|R| + |P|)$ binary variables and $O(|K| + |P|)$ continuous variables, with the big-M constraints (C4, C6) dominating; this decomposition into rerouting/reordering/rescheduling reduces runtime versus the monolithic formulation of Pellegrini et al. (2014), particularly in complex scenarios.

# Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Availability Constraints

A complete MILP description of the two model components (Composition Model and Infrastructure Model) and the Combinatorial Benders framework connecting them.

---

## 1. Problem setting and assumptions

**Given:**
- A timetable of passenger train trips $T = \{1,\dots,|T|\}$, each trip $t$ with scheduled departure/arrival times and stations.
- A set of stations $S$; at the disrupted stations $\bar S \subseteq S$ (here: Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal) shunting is allowed.
- A fleet of train units of types $V$ (e.g., VIRM-4, VIRM-6, ICM-3), with capacity $c_v$ (seats) and count $N_v$.
- A set of shunting movements $M$ that could be performed at stations in $\bar S$ (e.g., "send a unit from platform 5 to the shunting yard and return it later").
- Infrastructure data for stations in $\bar S$: tracks, platform tracks, routes between tracks, minimal headway times, route traversal times.

**Assumptions (marked where not given in the text):**
- **(A1)** All passenger trips must be operated; cancellation is not allowed (the paper allows short delays only).
- **(A2)** Shunting movements may only be delayed or canceled; passenger trains may be delayed by at most $\Delta$ minutes (a few minutes, absorbed by timetable buffers).
- **(A3)** Train units are coupled/decoupled only at stations, and composition changes take negligible time (as in Fioole et al., 2006).
- **(A4)** Shunting drivers are available; only track availability constrains shunting.
- **(A5)** The disruption has a known duration; during it, certain tracks are blocked.

---

## 2. Composition Model (CM)

Based on Fioole et al. (2006). For each trip $t$ arriving at / departing from a station, composition variables describe how many units of each type are in the train, split into an "old" part (continuing) and a "new" part.

### Variables

- $x_{t,v} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $v$ assigned to trip $t$.
- $x^{arr}_{s,t,v}, x^{dep}_{s,t,v} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: units of type $v$ arriving on / departing from trip $t$ at station $s$.
- $x^{res}_{s,t,v} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: units of type $v$ remaining at station $s$ after trip $t$ arrives (not continuing on the same train).
- $x^{cand}_{s,t,v} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: units of type $v$ added to trip $t$ at station $s$ (from stock on the station or from shunting).
- $y_{m} \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $m \in M$ is performed.
- $d_t \in \{0,\dots,\Delta\}$: extra delay (minutes) of trip $t$.
- $b_{s,t,v} \in \{0,1\}$: composition change (couple/decouple of type $v$) at station $s$ on trip $t$.

### Objective

Minimize a weighted sum of operational cost, passenger inconvenience, and deviation from the plan:

$$
\min \; Z_{CM} = 
\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{v \in V} \kappa_v \, x_{t,v}
\;+\; \sum_{t \in T} \pi \, d_t \cdot \text{load}_t
\;+\; \sum_{s,t,v} \beta \, b_{s,t,v}
\;+\; \sum_{m \in M} \gamma_m (1 - y_m)
\;+\; \sum_{t \in T}\sum_{v} \sigma \, |x_{t,v} - \bar x_{t,v}|
$$

where $\kappa_v$ = carriage-kilometer cost, $\text{load}_t$ = expected passengers on $t$, $\bar x_{t,v}$ = units in the original (pre-disruption) plan, $\gamma_m$ = penalty for canceling shunting movement $m$, $\beta,\sigma,\pi$ weights. (Weights are assumed, as exact values are not given.)

### Constraints

1. **Composition balance** at each station $s$ and trip $t$:
$$
x^{arr}_{s,t,v} + x^{res}_{s,t,v} = x^{dep}_{s,t,v} + x^{cand}_{s,t,v} \quad \forall s, t, v
$$

2. **Trip composition consistency:**
$$
x_{t,v} = x^{dep}_{s^{dep}(t),t,v} = x^{arr}_{s^{arr}(t),t,v} \quad \forall t, v
$$

3. **Composition-change indicator:**
$$
x^{res}_{s,t,v} + x^{cand}_{s,t,v} \le \Big(\sum_{v'} x_{t,v'}\Big) b_{s,t,v} \quad \forall s,t,v
$$
(a change of type $v$ forces $b=1$; linearized big-M).

4. **Shunting supplies/absorbs units:** each shunting movement $m$ at station $s$ either delivers $\nu^{in}_{m,v}$ units or removes $\nu^{out}_{m,v}$ units:
$$
x^{cand}_{s(m),t(m),v} \ge \nu^{in}_{m,v} \, y_m, \qquad
x^{res}_{s(m),t(m),v} \ge \nu^{out}_{m,v} \, y_m \quad \forall m, v
$$

5. **Fleet count:** total units of each type in circulation does not exceed available stock:
$$
\sum_{t} x_{t,v} \le N_v \quad \forall v
$$
(more precisely, via a time-space network flow balance per station; the flow formulation is standard and linear).

6. **Capacity / service level:** seat capacity on each trip must cover demand (possibly with a target seat ratio $\rho$):
$$
\sum_{v} c_v x_{t,v} \ge \rho \cdot \text{load}_t \quad \forall t
$$

7. **Delay bounds (A2):**
$$
0 \le d_t \le \Delta \quad \forall t
$$

8. **Composition feasibility:** allowed composition types per line, e.g. $x_{t,v} = 0$ for disallowed $(t,v)$, and ordering constraints within a train (linearizable).

The CM outputs the set of selected shunting movements $\hat M = \{m : y_m = 1\}$ with their (delayed) execution times.

---

## 3. Infrastructure Model (IM)

Based on Van Aken et al. (2017), applied per disrupted station $s \in \bar S$ over the disruption horizon. Every train passage and every candidate shunting movement is an event on a track.

### Variables

- $z_{e,k} \in \{0,1\}$: event $e \in E$ (a train arrival/departure or shunting movement $m \in \hat M$) is assigned to track $k \in K_s$.
- $\tau_e \ge 0$: actual start time of event $e$; $\delta_e \ge 0$ its delay w.r.t. the planned time.
- $o_{e,e'} \in \{0,1\}$: event $e$ precedes $e'$ on the same track.
- $w_m \in \{0,1\}$: shunting movement $m$ is actually executable (equals $y_m$ if feasible, 0 otherwise).

### Constraints

1. **Track assignment:** each event gets exactly one admissible track:
$$
\sum_{k \in K_s(e)} z_{e,k} = 1 \quad \forall e \in E_s
$$

2. **No overlap on a track:** for events $e, e'$ that cannot overlap on track $k$:
$$
\tau_{e'} \ge \tau_e + p_e - \mathcal{M}(1 - o_{e,e'}) - \mathcal{M}(2 - z_{e,k} - z_{e',k})
$$
$$
\tau_{e} \ge \tau_{e'} + p_{e'} - \mathcal{M}\, o_{e,e'} - \mathcal{M}(2 - z_{e,k} - z_{e',k})
$$
with $p_e$ the occupation duration and $\mathcal{M}$ a big constant.

3. **Headway between conflicting routes:** if events $e,e'$ use conflicting routes $r, r'$:
$$
\tau_{e'} \ge \tau_e + h_{r,r'} - \mathcal{M}(1 - o_{e,e'})
$$
(and symmetric), where $h_{r,r'}$ is the minimal headway.

4. **Route-track compatibility:** $z_{e,k} = 0$ if route of $e$ is incompatible with track $k$; blocked tracks (disruption) removed from $K_s$.

5. **Delay bounds:** $\delta_e \le \Delta$ for passenger events; shunting events may be delayed more freely within the horizon.

6. **Execution indicator:**
$$
w_m \le \sum_{k} z_{m,k} \quad \forall m \in \hat M
$$

The IM either certifies feasibility ($w_m = 1\ \forall m \in \hat M$) or returns violated combinations.

---

## 4. Combinatorial Benders framework

The CM proposes $\hat M$; the IM checks it. If infeasible, the IM produces a **combinatorial Benders cut** over the $y$-variables. Let $\Omega$ be the set of infeasible subsets found so far (e.g., a set $C \subseteq M$ of shunting movements that cannot all be executed simultaneously given the track occupancy). Then add to the CM:

$$
\sum_{m \in C} y_m \le |C| - 1 \quad \forall C \in \Omega
$$

More generally, with the IM's dual information, cuts of the form
$$
\sum_{m \in \hat M \setminus C} y_m \ge w(\hat M) - |C| \quad \text{(no-good / cover cuts)}
$$
are added. The algorithm iterates:

1. Solve CM with current cuts → candidate plan and $\hat M$.
2. Solve IM for $\hat M$ (per station).
3. If feasible: **optimal** solution found. If infeasible: extract minimal infeasible subset $C$, add cut $\sum_{m\in C} y_m \le |C|-1$, go to 1.

Since the number of shunting movement subsets is finite, the loop terminates with a proven optimum of the joint problem.

**Iterative heuristic variant:** instead of checking $\hat M$ jointly, movements are fed to the IM **one by one** (in a given order); a movement that cannot be routed is canceled ($y_m := 0$) and the CM is re-solved. This mimics the split between rolling stock dispatchers and infrastructure dispatchers; the paper reports it attains the optimum on all instances because conflicts arise only with passenger trains, not among shunting movements.

---

## 5. Summary of the joint model

$$
\min Z_{CM} \quad \text{s.t. CM constraints (1)–(8), IM constraints as lazy cuts, } \; \sum_{m \in C} y_m \le |C|-1 \;\; \forall C \in \Omega
$$

All variables: $x$-variables integer non-negative, $y, z, o, b, w$ binary, $d, \tau, \delta$ continuous. The model is a valid MILP; the Benders iteration is exact because every infeasible shunting combination is eventually excluded by a cut.

# MILP Model: Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single urban rail transit line with stations $S = \{1,\dots,N\}$ and one direction of operation. The prediction horizon $[0,T]$ is divided into equal-length time intervals $\mathcal{K}=\{1,\dots,K\}$ (assumption: passenger demand is piecewise constant per interval, as in Liu et al., 2023a). A fleet of train units (TUs) is available at a depot; each train service departs from station 1 and is composed of one or more coupled train units (flexible composition). Rolling stock circulation is captured by requiring that the number of TUs in use at any time does not exceed the fleet size, and TUs return to the depot after each service.

**Assumptions (marked where not given in the input):**
- (A1) Single track direction, no overtaking; train order is fixed by departure sequence.
- (A2) Running times between stations are fixed (no speed-level optimization).
- (A3) Passengers board the first arriving train with sufficient residual capacity; leftover passengers wait (no stranded passengers, since capacity can be extended via composition).
- (A4) Composition changes between consecutive services require a minimum turnaround time at the depot.
- (A5) All data are deterministic over the prediction horizon (MPC receding-horizon setting).

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{F}=\{1,\dots,F\}$ | train services (departures) in the horizon |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | time intervals, length $\Delta$ |
| $d_{i,k}$ | passengers arriving at station $i$ during interval $k$ (demand) |
| $r_i$ | running time from station $i$ to $i+1$ |
| $d^{min}, d^{max}$ | minimum/maximum dwell time at a station |
| $h^{min}$ | minimum headway between consecutive departures |
| $c$ | capacity of one train unit |
| $M^{max}$ | max number of coupled TUs per service |
| $R$ | total fleet size (number of TUs) |
| $\tau^{turn}$ | minimum turnaround time at depot |
| $T^{ref}_{f,i}$ | reference (nominal) arrival time of service $f$ at station $i$ |
| $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ | weights: waiting time, deviation, operation cost |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{f,i} \ge 0$: arrival time of service $f$ at station $i$
- $dep_{f,i} \ge 0$: departure time of service $f$ from station $i$
- $w_{i,k} \ge 0$: passengers waiting at station $i$ at the start of interval $k$
- $b_{f,i} \ge 0$: passengers boarding service $f$ at station $i$

**Integer/binary:**
- $y_{f} \in \{1,\dots,M^{max}\}$: number of TUs of service $f$ (composition)
- $x_{f,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if service $f$ stops at station $i$
- $z_{f} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if service $f$ is operated (may be cancelled in off-peak)

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted passenger waiting time, timetable deviation, and operation cost:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i\in S}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{K}} w_{i,k}\,\Delta
+ \beta \sum_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\sum_{i\in S} \left| a_{f,i} - T^{ref}_{f,i} \right|
+ \gamma \sum_{f\in\mathcal{F}} c^{op} y_{f}
$$

Linearized with auxiliary variables $\delta_{f,i}\ge 0$:

$$
\delta_{f,i} \ge a_{f,i}-T^{ref}_{f,i},\qquad \delta_{f,i} \ge T^{ref}_{f,i}-a_{f,i}
$$

so $Z = \alpha\sum w_{i,k}\Delta + \beta\sum\delta_{f,i} + \gamma\sum c^{op}y_f$.

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable dynamics (running and dwell times):**
$$
dep_{f,i} = a_{f,i} + dw_{f,i},\qquad d^{min}x_{f,i}\le dw_{f,i}\le d^{max}x_{f,i}+d^{min}(1-x_{f,i})
$$
$$
a_{f,i+1} = dep_{f,i} + r_i,\qquad \forall f,\; i=1,\dots,N-1
$$

**(C2) Stop pattern:** first and last stations are always served:
$$
x_{f,1}=x_{f,N}=1,\qquad x_{f,i}\le z_f \quad \forall f,i
$$

**(C3) Headway (fixed order, no overtaking):**
$$
dep_{f+1,1} - dep_{f,1} \ge h^{min},\qquad a_{f+1,i}-a_{f,i}\ge h^{min}\quad \forall f,i
$$

**(C4) Waiting-passenger dynamics (piecewise-constant demand):**
$$
w_{i,k+1} = w_{i,k} + d_{i,k}\Delta - \sum_{f:\, dep_{f,i}\in[k\Delta,(k+1)\Delta)} b_{f,i}
$$
Linearized with big-M binaries $\rho_{f,i,k}\in\{0,1\}$ indicating whether service $f$ departs station $i$ in interval $k$:
$$
k\Delta\,\rho_{f,i,k} \le dep_{f,i}\,\rho_{f,i,k} \le (k+1)\Delta\,\rho_{f,i,k} + M(1-\rho_{f,i,k})
$$
$$
\sum_k \rho_{f,i,k} = x_{f,i}
$$

**(C5) Boarding limited by demand and capacity:**
$$
b_{f,i} \le w_{i,k} + d_{i,k}\Delta \quad \text{for } k \text{ with } \rho_{f,i,k}=1 \quad(\text{big-}M\text{ form})
$$
$$
b_{f,i} \le c\, y_f - \sum_{i'\le i} \ell_{f,i'} \quad\text{(residual capacity; with onboard load } \ell_{f,i}=\ell_{f,i-1}-b^{alight}_{f,i}+b_{f,i}\text{)}
$$
Simplified linear onboard-load recursion (assumption: alighting proportional to boarding pattern, or given fixed alighting fractions $\theta_i$):
$$
\ell_{f,i} = \ell_{f,i-1} + b_{f,i} - \theta_i \ell_{f,i-1},\qquad \ell_{f,0}=0,\qquad \ell_{f,i}\le c\,y_f
$$

**(C6) Flexible composition bounds:**
$$
z_f \le y_f \le M^{max} z_f,\qquad y_f\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}
$$

**(C7) Rolling stock circulation (fleet size):** each service occupies $y_f$ TUs from its depot departure to its return after turnaround $\tau^{turn}$:
$$
\sum_{f:\, dep_{f,1}\le t \le dep_{f,1} + (r_{sum}+\tau^{turn})} y_f \le R \qquad \forall t
$$
Linearized with binaries $\sigma_{f,t}$ (service $f$ in circulation at time $t$) and big-M:
$$
dep_{f,1} \le t\,\sigma_{f,t}\le dep_{f,1}+M(1-\sigma_{f,t}),\qquad
t \le (dep_{f,1}+r_{sum}+\tau^{turn})\sigma_{f,t} + M(1-\sigma_{f,t})
$$
$$
\sum_f y_f \sigma_{f,t} \le R \qquad \forall t
$$

**(C8) Turnaround between consecutive uses of TUs** is enforced implicitly by (C7); composition coupling changes require (A4):
$$
dep_{f+1,1} - (a_{f,N}+r_{sum}^{ret}) \ge \tau^{turn}\cdot \mathbb{1}\{y_{f+1}\ne y_f\}
$$
Linearized with binaries $\eta^{\pm}_{f}$: $\eta^+_{f}\ge y_{f+1}-y_f$, $\eta^-_{f}\ge y_f-y_{f+1}$, $\eta^+_{f}+\eta^-_{f}\le 1$, and
$$
dep_{f+1,1} - a_{f,N} - r_{sum}^{ret} + M(\eta^+_{f}+\eta^-_{f}) \ge \tau^{turn}
$$

**(C9) Horizon bounds:**
$$
0 \le a_{f,i},\, dep_{f,i} \le T,\qquad w_{i,k}\ge 0,\; b_{f,i}\ge 0,\; \delta_{f,i}\ge 0
$$

## 6. Model Summary

- **Continuous variables:** $a_{f,i}, dep_{f,i}, dw_{f,i}, w_{i,k}, b_{f,i}, \ell_{f,i}, \delta_{f,i}$
- **Integer variables:** $y_f \in \{0,\dots,M^{max}\}$
- **Binary variables:** $x_{f,i}, z_f, \rho_{f,i,k}, \sigma_{f,t}, \eta^{\pm}_f$

The model is a complete MILP (all nonlinearities — absolute values, interval membership, fleet occupancy — are linearized with auxiliary binaries and big-M constants). In the MPC framework, this MILP is solved at each control step over the receding horizon $[t, t+T_p]$ with measured/predicted demands $d_{i,k}$; the first-step decisions are applied and the horizon rolls forward. In the learning-based extension, the integer variables ($y_f$, $x_{f,i}$, $z_f$) after presolve pruning are predicted by an LSTM network, and the remaining continuous timetable variables are recovered by solving the reduced LP with integers fixed — guaranteeing constraint feasibility while reducing online computation.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

**Assumptions (marked where assumed):** double-track high-speed corridor; a partial blockage closes one track of segment $k^*$ during window $[d^s, d^e]$; trains may reroute onto the opposite track within that window under single-track headways; speed profiles are precomputed discrete energy-optimal driving plans per train–segment (a standard disaggregation); headways are uniform. The planning horizon is $H$.

## 1. Sets and Parameters

**Sets**
- $T$: trains; $S$: ordered stations; $B$: segments $k=(s,s+1)$
- $P_t$: admissible speed profiles for train $t$ on segment $k$, with running time $\tau^{p}_{tk}$ and energy $e^{p}_{tk}$
- $\mathcal{D}=[d^s,d^e]$: disruption window on segment $k^*$; $\mathcal{U}_t$: segments of train $t$'s route

**Parameters**
- $a^{sch}_{ts}, d^{sch}_{ts}$: scheduled arrival/departure times
- $h$: minimum headway (same-track); $h^{opp}$: single-track headway on the blocked segment
- $d^{min}_{ts}$: minimum dwell; $M$: big constant; $w_1, w_2$: delay/energy weights

## 2. Variables

- $a_{ts}, d_{ts} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times (retiming)
- $x_{tk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite track on segment $k$ (rerouting; only for $k=k^*$)
- $y^{same}_{tk\ell}, y^{opp}_{tk\ell} \in \{0,1\}$: precedence variables (train $t$ enters segment $k$ before train $\ell$; same-track / opposite-track usage)
- $z^{p}_{tk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ runs segment $k$ with speed profile $p$
- $\delta_{ts} \ge 0$: delay of train $t$ at station $s$

## 3. Objective

$$
\min\; Z = w_1 \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\delta_{ts} + w_2 \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in\mathcal{U}_t}\sum_{p\in P_t} e^{p}_{tk}\, z^{p}_{tk}
$$

## 4. Constraints

**(C1) Exactly one speed profile per train–segment:**
$$\sum_{p\in P_t} z^{p}_{tk} = 1 \qquad \forall t, k\in\mathcal{U}_t$$

**(C2) Running-time link (timetable ↔ speed profile):**
$$a_{t,s+1} = d_{ts} + \sum_{p\in P_t}\tau^{p}_{tk} z^{p}_{tk} \qquad \forall t,\; k=(s,s+1)\in\mathcal{U}_t$$

**(C3) Dwell times:**
$$d_{ts} \ge a_{ts} + d^{min}_{ts} \qquad \forall t,\; s \text{ intermediate}$$

**(C4) Delay definition:**
$$\delta_{ts} \ge a_{ts} - a^{sch}_{ts}, \qquad \delta_{ts} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t, s$$

**(C5) Same-track headways (reordering):** for each unordered pair $\{t,\ell\}$ on segment $k$, with $y^{same}_{tk\ell} + y^{same}_{\ell kt} = 1$:
$$d_{\ell s_k} - d_{t s_k} \ge \sum_p \tau^p_{tk} z^p_{tk} + h - M\big(3 - y^{same}_{tk\ell} - y^{same}_{\ell kt} - (2 - x_{tk} - x_{\ell k})\big)$$
$$d_{t s_k} - d_{\ell s_k} \ge \sum_p \tau^p_{\ell k} z^p_{\ell k} + h - M\big(3 - y^{same}_{\ell kt} - y^{same}_{tk\ell} - (2 - x_{tk} - x_{\ell k})\big)$$
(the big-M terms deactivate the constraint when the trains use different tracks).

**(C6) Single-track headways on the disrupted segment (bidirectional conflicts):** for each pair $t,\ell$ on $k^*$ with at least one using the opposite track, $y^{opp}_{tk\ell} + y^{opp}_{\ell kt} = 1$:
$$d_{\ell s_{k^*}} \ge d_{t s_{k^*}} + \sum_p \tau^p_{tk^*} z^p_{tk^*} + h^{opp} - M\big(2 - y^{opp}_{tk\ell} - (x_{tk}+x_{\ell k})\big)$$
$$d_{t s_{k^*}} \ge d_{\ell s_{k^*}} + \sum_p \tau^p_{\ell k^*} z^p_{\ell k^*} + h^{opp} - M\big(2 - y^{opp}_{\ell kt} - (x_{tk}+x_{\ell k})\big)$$
This enforces mutual exclusion on the shared track regardless of travel direction.

**(C7) Disruption window:**
- Opposite-track usage must lie within $[d^s,d^e]$:
$$d_{t s_{k^*}} \ge d^s - M(1-x_{tk^*}), \qquad d_{t s_{k^*}} + \sum_p \tau^p_{t k^*} z^p_{t k^*} \le d^e + M(1-x_{tk^*})$$
- Otherwise, trains on the blocked track must wait until the disruption ends (or reroute):
$$d_{t s_{k^*}} \ge d^e - M x_{tk^*}$$

**(C8) Route consistency:**
$$x_{tk} = 0 \qquad \forall t,\; k \ne k^*$$

**(C9) Domains:**
$$x_{tk}, y^{same}_{tk\ell}, y^{opp}_{tk\ell}, z^{p}_{tk} \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_{ts}, d_{ts}, \delta_{ts} \ge 0$$

## 5. Modeling Rationale

- **Retiming** via continuous $a_{ts}, d_{ts}$, penalized through C4.
- **Rerouting**: $x_{tk^*}=1$ permits using the opposite track strictly inside the disruption window (C7), with single-track headways $h^{opp}$ via C6.
- **Reordering**: pairwise precedence binaries with big-M disjunctions guarantee exactly one order per train pair per segment (C5–C6).
- **Speed management**: binary $z^p$ selects one precomputed profile per segment (C1); its running time drives the timetable (C2) and its energy enters the objective — the key *linking* between timetable and control level.
- The objective balances total delay ($w_1$) against traction energy ($w_2$): trains may decelerate into energy-efficient profiles when slack exists, or accelerate to recover delay.

The model is a linear MILP (binaries + continuous times with big-M linearization) solvable with standard branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut, and is amenable to the decomposition into train-plan selection problems (one plan per train = a tuple of profile choices and route choice) described in the paper's solution framework.
