Here is the final, consolidated model — it merges the corrected disruption-window logic and rerouting constraints from the revision with the speed-profile selection, energy objective, and cancellation options from the first formulation.

# Integrated MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and indices

- $I$: trains; $d_i \in \{+,-\}$ planned direction of train $i$.
- $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$: stations; segment $s$ connects stations $s$ and $s+1$, $s=1,\dots,n-1$.
- $P_{i,s}$: pre-enumerated speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $s$.
- $s^\ast$: disrupted segment (one track blocked); disruption window $[T_0,T_1]$.

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\bar a_{i,s},\bar d_{i,s}$ | planned arrival/departure times |
| $r_{i,s,p}, E_{i,s,p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $\Delta_{i,s}$ | extra running time when rerouted to the opposite track |
| $d^{\min}_{i,s}, d^{\max}_{i,s}$ | dwell bounds |
| $h^{run}_{i,j,s}, h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{tr}$ | segment, arrival, departure, transit headways |
| $w_i, C_i$ | delay weight, cancellation penalty |
| $M$ | big-M $=T_{horizon}$ |

**Assumptions.** (A1) Only one track of $s^\ast$ is blocked during $[T_0,T_1]$; the opposite track is usable bidirectionally at reduced speed. (A2) Delay, energy and cancellation costs are commensurable. (A3) Speed profiles are pre-enumerated with fixed $(r,E)$ — this keeps the model linear. (A4) Every station has one platform per direction, so arrival headways guarantee platform separation. (A5) All trains may be cancelled; $C_i$ is large. (A6) No rolling-stock/crew constraints.

## 3. Variables

- $t^{arr}_{i,s}, t^{dep}_{i,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times.
- $u_{i,s} \ge 0$: lateness at station $s$.
- $x_{i,s,p}\in\{0,1\}$: speed-profile selection.
- $y_{i,s}\in\{0,1\}$: $=1$ iff train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $s$.
- $z_i\in\{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled.
- $\alpha_i,\beta_i\in\{0,1\}$: on the normal track of $s^\ast$, train $i$ passes entirely before $T_0$ / entirely after $T_1$.
- $p_i,q_i\in\{0,1\}$, $z^{ov}_i\in\{0,1\}$: overlap detection of train $i$'s passage with $[T_0,T_1]$.
- $o^{arr}_{i,j,s}, o^{dep}_{i,j,s}\in\{0,1\}$: station orderings; $o^{seg}_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}$: ordering on $s^\ast$; $\gamma_{i,j}\in\{0,1\}$: conflict indicator for opposite-direction pairs on the normal track.

## 4. Objective

$$\min\; \underbrace{\sum_{i}\sum_{s} w_i u_{i,s}}_{\text{weighted delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i}\sum_{s}\sum_{p} E_{i,s,p}\,x_{i,s,p}}_{\text{energy}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i} C_i z_i}_{\text{cancellations}}$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Profile selection** (exactly one if running, none if cancelled):
$$\sum_{p\in P_{i,s}} x_{i,s,p} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i,\; s=1,\dots,n-1$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency with chosen profile:**
$$t^{arr}_{i,s+1} = t^{dep}_{i,s} + \sum_{p} r_{i,s,p}x_{i,s,p} + \Delta_{i,s}\,y_{i,s} + \sigma_{i,s},\qquad \sigma_{i,s}\le M z_i \qquad \forall i,\;s$$

**(C3) Dwell times:**
$$d^{\min}_{i,s} - M z_i \le t^{dep}_{i,s}-t^{arr}_{i,s} \le d^{\max}_{i,s} + M z_i \qquad \forall i,\;s$$

**(C4) Lateness:** $u_{i,s}\ge t^{arr}_{i,s}-\bar a_{i,s}$, $u_{i,s}\ge 0$, and $u_{i,s}\le M(1-z_i)$ (cancelled trains incur no delay cost).

**(C5) Release / horizon:** $t^{dep}_{i,1}\ge \bar d_{i,1}-Mz_i$; all times in $[0,T_{horizon}]$.

**(C6) Rerouting only on the disrupted segment:**
$$y_{i,s}=0 \quad \forall i,\; s\neq s^\ast$$

**(C7) Window avoidance on the normal track** ($e_{i}=t^{dep}_{i,s^\ast}$, $q_{i}=t^{arr}_{i,s^\ast+1}$):
$$\alpha_i+\beta_i+y_{i,s^\ast}\ge 1-z_i,\qquad \alpha_i+\beta_i\le 1,\qquad \alpha_i+\beta_i\le 1-y_{i,s^\ast}$$
$$q_{i}\le T_0+M(1-\alpha_i)+M y_{i,s^\ast},\qquad e_{i}\ge T_1-M(1-\beta_i)-M y_{i,s^\ast}$$

**(C8) Overlap detection** (entry before $T_1$ and exit after $T_0$):
$$t^{arr}_{i,s^\ast+1}\ge T_1-M(1-p_i),\qquad t^{dep}_{i,s^\ast}\le T_0+M(1-q_i),\qquad z^{ov}_i\ge p_i+q_i-1$$
$$\alpha_i+\beta_i\ge z^{ov}_i-y_{i,s^\ast}\qquad\text{(consistency with C7)}$$

**(C9) Same-direction running headways on segment $s$** (active only if both trains use the same track), for $i<j$ with $d_i=d_j$:
$$t^{arr}_{j,s+1}\ge t^{arr}_{i,s+1}+h^{run}_{i,j,s}-M\big(1-o^{seg}_{i,j}-2+2y_{i,s}\big)-Mz_i-Mz_j$$
$$t^{arr}_{i,s+1}\ge t^{arr}_{j,s+1}+h^{run}_{j,i,s}-M\big(o^{seg}_{i,j}-2+2y_{i,s}\big)-Mz_i-Mz_j$$
(the $y$-terms deactivate the constraint when the trains are on different tracks).

**(C10) Station arrival/departure headways** (for $i<j$ at each station $s$):
$$t^{arr}_{j,s}\ge t^{arr}_{i,s}+h^{arr}-M(1-o^{arr}_{i,j,s})-Mz_i-Mz_j,\qquad t^{arr}_{i,s}\ge t^{arr}_{j,s}+h^{arr}-M\,o^{arr}_{i,j,s}-Mz_i-Mz_j$$
$$t^{dep}_{j,s}\ge t^{dep}_{i,s}+h^{dep}-M(1-o^{dep}_{i,j,s})-Mz_i-Mz_j,\qquad t^{dep}_{i,s}\ge t^{dep}_{j,s}+h^{dep}-M\,o^{dep}_{i,j,s}-Mz_i-Mz_j$$
with consistency $o^{arr}_{i,j,s}=o^{dep}_{i,j,s}$, and transit headway (A4):
$$t^{arr}_{j,s}\ge t^{dep}_{i,s}+h^{tr}-M(1-o^{arr}_{i,j,s})-Mz_i-Mz_j \qquad \forall i\neq j,\; 1\le s<n$$

**(C11) Serialization on the alternative track of $s^\ast$** (all rerouted trains share one track):
$$t^{arr}_{j,s^\ast+1}\ge t^{dep}_{i,s^\ast}+h^{run}_{i,j,s^\ast}-M(1-o^{seg}_{i,j})-M(2-y_{i,s^\ast}-y_{j,s^\ast})-Mz_i-Mz_j$$
$$t^{arr}_{i,s^\ast+1}\ge t^{dep}_{j,s^\ast}+h^{run}_{j,i,s^\ast}-M\,o^{seg}_{i,j}-M(2-y_{i,s^\ast}-y_{j,s^\ast})-Mz_i-Mz_j$$

**(C12) Conditional conflict serialization for opposite-direction pairs on the normal track.** $\gamma_{i,j}=1$ unless the pair is exempt (one rerouted, or one passes before and the other after the window):
$$\gamma_{i,j}\ge 1-y_{i,s^\ast}-y_{j,s^\ast}-\beta_i-\beta_j,\qquad \gamma_{i,j}\ge 1-y_{i,s^\ast}-y_{j,s^\ast}-\alpha_i-\alpha_j \qquad \forall i<j,\; d_i\neq d_j$$
$$t^{arr}_{j,s^\ast+1}\ge t^{dep}_{i,s^\ast}+h^{run}_{i,j,s^\ast}-M(1-o^{seg}_{i,j})-M(y_{i,s^\ast}+y_{j,s^\ast})-M(1-\gamma_{i,j})$$
$$t^{arr}_{i,s^\ast+1}\ge t^{dep}_{j,s^\ast}+h^{run}_{j,i,s^\ast}-M\,o^{seg}_{i,j}-M(y_{i,s^\ast}+y_{j,s^\ast})-M(1-\gamma_{i,j})$$

**(C13) Domains:** $t^{arr},t^{dep},u,\sigma\ge 0$; $x,y,z,\alpha,\beta,p,q,z^{ov},o^{arr},o^{dep},o^{seg},\gamma\in\{0,1\}$.

## 5. Remarks

Text:
# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the described framework (Pellegrini et al. 2014-style model, extended with pair-wise delay interpretation and route selection), the following complete MILP is proposed.

## 1. Assumptions

- **A1 (Macroscopic infrastructure):** The network is a set of blocks/resources; signals and track gradients are neglected.
- **A2 (Routes):** Each train $t \in T$ has a set of feasible routes $R_t$ through the network; each route $r$ occupies an ordered set of resources $B(r)$.
- **A3 (Scheduled times):** Each train has a nominal scheduled entrance time $e_t$ and exit time $x_t$ from the area under study.
- **A4 (Primary delay):** Trains may enter with primary delay $\delta_t \ge 0$.
- **A5 (Fixed speed profile):** Running times per resource are fixed constants; only waiting/held time is decision-dependent.
- **A6 (FIFO not imposed):** Ordering is a decision variable (FIFO is only a heuristic baseline).
- **A7 (Horizon):** All decisions must be within a finite time horizon $H$.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $R$ | set of all routes; $R_t \subseteq R$ routes feasible for train $t$ |
| $B$ | set of block resources; $B(r) \subseteq B$ resources of route $r$ |
| $O_{rr'}$ | $\in \{0,1\}$: routes $r, r'$ have a resource in common |
| $p_{tr}$ | running time of train $t$ on route $r$ |
| $\sigma_{tr}$ | scheduled entrance time of train $t$ if route $r$ is used |
| $\delta_t$ | primary delay of train $t$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant (e.g., $M = H$) |
| $w_{\min}$ | minimum headway time between consecutive trains on the same resource |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $y_{tr}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_t$ |
| $x_{tt'}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ passes before train $t'$ (ordering), for $t \ne t'$ |
| $a_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | actual entrance time of train $t$ |
| $d_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | actual exit time of train $t$ |
| $s_{tt'}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | pair-wise delay: time train $t$ waits because of train $t'$ |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total (secondary) delay at the exit:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} \left( d_t - x_t \right)
$$

Equivalently, since $d_t = a_t + \sum_{r} p_{tr} y_{tr}$, one may minimize $\sum_t a_t$ (constant running times).

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route choice — exactly one route per train:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} y_{tr} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Entrance time with primary delay:**
$$
a_t \ge e_t + \delta_t \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C3) Exit time definition:**
$$
d_t \ge a_t + \sum_{r \in R_t} p_{tr}\, y_{tr} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C4) Pair-wise delay definition (train $t$ waits for $t'$ only if ordered after and routes conflict):**
$$
s_{tt'} \ge a_{t'} + \sum_{r \in R_{t'}} p_{t'r} y_{t'r} + w_{\min} - a_t - M(1 - x_{t't}) - M\left(2 - \sum_{r \in R_t}\sum_{r' \in R_{t'}} O_{rr'}\, y_{tr} y_{t'r}\right)
$$

*Linearization note:* replace the bilinear term $y_{tr} y_{t'r}$ by auxiliary variables $z_{tt'rr'} \in \{0,1\}$ with:
$$
z_{tt'rr'} \ge y_{tr} + y_{t'r} - 1, \quad z_{tt'rr'} \le y_{tr}, \quad z_{tt'rr'} \le y_{t'r}
$$
for all $t \ne t'$, $r \in R_t$, $r' \in R_{t'}$, $O_{rr'} = 1$.

**(C5) Delay propagation into entrance time:**
$$
a_t \ge \sum_{t' \in T \setminus \{t\}} s_{tt'} \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C6) Antisymmetry of ordering:**
$$
x_{tt'} + x_{t't} = 1 \qquad \forall t, t' \in T,\; t < t'
$$

**(C7) Headway / conflict-freedom on shared resources** (if $t'$ precedes $t$ and routes conflict, $t$ enters at least running time + headway after $t'$):
$$
a_t \ge a_{t'} + \sum_{r \in R_{t'}} p_{t'r} y_{t'r} + w_{\min} - M(1 - x_{t't}) - M\sum_{r,r'} \left(1 - z_{tt'rr'}\right)
$$
$$
a_{t'} \ge a_t + \sum_{r \in R_t} p_{tr} y_{tr} + w_{\min} - M(1 - x_{tt'}) - M\sum_{r,r'} \left(1 - z_{tt'rr'}\right)
$$
for all $t < t'$ with $\exists\, r \in R_t, r' \in R_{t'} : O_{rr'} = 1$.

**(C8) Time horizon:**
$$
d_t \le H \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C9) Non-negativity / bounds:**
$$
a_t, d_t, s_{tt'} \ge 0; \qquad y_{tr}, x_{tt'}, z_{tt'rr'} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Sub-optimal variant (Stage 1 of the paper):** Drop constraint (C5) — delay propagation is neglected; $s_{tt'}$ then only captures pair-wise waiting. This yields the fast, low-complex model for rerouting and reordering.
- **Global-optimum variant (Stage 2):** With (C5) included, the pair-wise delay variables fully reproduce the standard delay-propagation formulation of Pellegrini et al. (2014), guaranteeing the global optimum of the rtRTMP.
- **Extension (Lindenmaier et al. 2022):** Safety-relevant overlaps behind stop signals can be added by enlarging the conflict set $O_{rr'}$ (i.e., declaring overlap resources as shared), leaving the model structure unchanged.
- **Complexity:** The dominant combinatorial part is route selection ($\sum_t |R_t|$ binaries) and ordering ($|T|(|T|-1)/2$ binaries); fixing $y_{tr}$ and $x_{tt'}$ from Stage 1 reduces the Stage-2 MILP to a linear program in $a_t, d_t, s_{tt'}$.

# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE‑MILP model. All assumptions are explicitly marked **(A#)**.

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **(A1)** The network is a directed graph of *microscopic* track elements (TDS sections and switches). Trains follow fixed global routes through the network; only local rerouting around stations/switches is allowed via a finite set of route options per train.
- **(A2)** Each train has a set of feasible **speed profile options** per route (e.g., coasting vs. full service braking), each characterized by a deterministic space–time trajectory.
- **(A3)** Under DTG (ETCS L2 with TTD), the **end of authority (EoA)** is at the end of a TDS, but the **brake indication point (IP)** lies anywhere on the track and depends on the train and its entry speed. Hence the **blocking time** of a TDS for train *f* depends on the chosen speed profile option and on the position of the preceding train, i.e., separation is speed‑dependent.
- **(A4)** A train occupies a TDS from the moment its IP‑to‑EoA approach (braking) curve enters the TDS until its tail clears it; this interval is the blocking time.
- **(A5)** Delays are measured against the original timetable at scheduled events (departure/arrival times).
- **(A6)** Rolling‑stock composition, dwell times (within given bounds) and driver behaviour are deterministic; delays originate from an initial perturbation.
- **(A7)** All data (running times per speed profile, blocking times per (train, profile, speed‑state) combination) are precomputed from microscopic simulation and are thus constants of the model — this preserves linearity.

---

## 2. Sets and indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | trains, indexed $f$ |
| $S$ | TDS sections, indexed $s$ |
| $S^{sw} \subseteq S$ | switch sections |
| $R_f$ | admissible local routes (route options) for train $f$ |
| $P_f$ | admissible speed profile options for train $f$ |
| $E_f$ | scheduled events of train $f$ (with ideal times $t^0_e$) |
| $K$ | discretised time horizon $\{0,\dots,T\}$, index $k$ |

---

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{f r s}$ | 1 if route $r\in R_f$ of train $f$ uses section $s$, else 0 |
| $\rho^{arr}_{f r p},\ \rho^{dep}_{f r p}$ | arrival / departure time of train $f$ on route $r$, profile $p$ (unconstrained run) |
| $B_{f p s}(v)$ | **speed‑dependent blocking time** of section $s$ for train $f$ with profile $p$ when entering at speed class $v$ — precomputed per speed class $v\in V$ **(A3, A7)** |
| $\sigma_{f p s}$ | speed class of train $f$, profile $p$ at the approach to section $s$ (deterministic given $p$) |
| $h_{min}$ | minimum headway / interlocking setup time |
| $d^{max}_e$ | maximum allowable delay at event $e$ |
| $M$ | big‑M constant |
| $\underline{\delta}_f,\ \bar{\delta}_f$ | earliest departure / latest arrival window bounds |

---

## 4. Variables

**Binary**

- $x_{f r p}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses route $r$ and speed profile $p$.
- $y_{f s k}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ **starts occupying** section $s$ during time interval $k$.
- $z_{f g s}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ passes section $s$ **before** train $g$ (ordering variable).

**Continuous**

- $t_f \ge 0$: entry time of train $f$ into the network (retiming variable).
- $d_e \ge 0$: delay of event $e$.

---

## 5. Objective function

Minimise total (weighted) delay:

$$
\min \; Z=\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{e\in E_f} w_e\, d_e
$$

with weights $w_e$ (e.g., $w_e = 1$, or higher for passenger arrivals). **(A5)**

---

## 6. Constraints

### 6.1 Route and speed profile choice

$$
\sum_{r\in R_f}\sum_{p\in P_f} x_{f r p} = 1 \qquad \forall f\in F \tag{1}
$$

### 6.2 Retiming and delay definition

$$
t_f \ge \underline{\delta}_f,\qquad t_f \le \bar{\delta}_f \qquad \forall f\in F \tag{2}
$$

$$
d_e \ge \big(\rho^{arr/dep}_{f r p} + t_f\big) - t^0_e - M(1-x_{f r p}) \qquad \forall e\in E_f,\ r,p \tag{3}
$$

$$
d_e \le d^{max}_e \qquad \forall e \tag{4}
$$

### 6.3 Occupation of sections (blocking time with speed‑dependent braking)

If train $f$ with route/profile $(r,p)$ enters section $s$ at time $t_f + \rho^{in}_{f r s}$, it occupies $s$ for the blocking time $B_{f p s}(\sigma_{f p s})$:

$$
y_{f s k} \ge x_{f r p} - \sum_{k' < k} y_{f s k'} - M\big(2 - x_{f r p} - \mathbb{1}[k = \kappa(f,r,s)]\big)
$$

expressed linearly as: the first occupation interval of $s$ by $f$ is fixed by its chosen route/profile and entry time:

$$
\sum_{k} y_{f s k} \;=\; \sum_{r,p} \ell_{f r s}\, x_{f r p}
\qquad \forall f, s \tag{5}
$$

where $\ell_{f r s}=1$ if route $r$ uses $s$ (i.e., $\ell_{f r s}=a_{f r s}$), and the occupation interval index is linked to entry time by

$$
\sum_{k\ge \kappa(f,r,s)} y_{f s k} \ge x_{f r p},\qquad
\sum_{k< \kappa(f,r,s)} y_{f s k} \le 1 - x_{f r p}
\qquad \forall f,r,p,s \tag{6}
$$

with $\kappa(f,r,s)=\lceil t_f + \rho^{in}_{f r s}\rceil$ linearised via standard time‑indexing of $t_f$ (entry time discretised on $K$).

**Blocking duration (speed‑dependent):** the number of consecutive occupied intervals equals the blocking time in intervals:

$$
\sum_{k} y_{f s k}\,\Delta \;\ge\; \sum_{r,p} a_{f r s}\, B_{f p s}(\sigma_{f p s})\, x_{f r p} \qquad \forall f,s \tag{7}
$$

and occupation must be contiguous (enforced by the time‑indexed structure: once started, $y$ stays 1 until the blocking time elapses — standard contiguous‑occupancy formulation).

### 6.4 Conflict‑free section usage (no double occupancy)

$$
\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{k'\in[k-B^{max}+1,\,k]} y_{f s k'} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall s,\ k \tag{8}
$$

i.e., at most one train may occupy (or have its DTG braking approach inside) section $s$ at any time — the DTG separation condition **(A3, A4)**.

### 6.5 Ordering and precedence on shared sections

For every pair of trains $f,g$ sharing section $s$ on their chosen routes:

$$
z_{f g s} + z_{g f s} \;\ge\; x_{f r p} + x_{g q u} - 1 \qquad \forall r,p,q,u:\ a_{f r s}=a_{g q u}=1 \tag{9}
$$

$$
z_{f g s} + z_{g f s} \;\le\; 1 \qquad \forall f<g,\ s \tag{10}
$$

Sequencing consistency with occupation times:

$$
\sum_k k\,\Delta\, y_{g s k} \;\ge\; \sum_k k\,\Delta\, y_{f s k} + \sum_{r,p} a_{f r s} B_{f p s}(\sigma_{f p s}) x_{f r p} + h_{min} - M(1 - z_{f g s}) \tag{11}
$$

$$
\sum_k k\,\Delta\, y_{f s k} \;\ge\; \sum_k k\,\Delta\, y_{g s k} + \sum_{q,u} a_{g q s} B_{g u s}(\sigma_{g u s}) x_{g q u} + h_{min} - M(1 - z_{g f s}) \tag{12}
$$

### 6.6 Switch constraints

Switch sections $s\in S^{sw}$ additionally require exclusive route locking (no conflicting switch positions simultaneously):

$$
\sum_{f}\sum_{r,p:\, a_{f r s}=a_{f r s'}=1} x_{f r p} \le 1 \quad \text{for each pair of conflicting switch positions } (s,s') \tag{13}
$$

and switching/setting time between successive trains:

$$
\sum_k k\,\Delta\, y_{g s k} \ge \sum_k k\,\Delta\, y_{f s k} + \tau^{sw} - M(1-z_{f g s}) \qquad \forall s\in S^{sw} \tag{14}
$$

with switch setting time $\tau^{sw} \ge h_{min}$.

### 6.7 Variable domains

$$
x_{f r p},\, y_{f s k},\, z_{f g s}\in\{0,1\};\qquad t_f,\ d_e \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Model summary

- **Decision:** route + speed profile per train (1), entry times (2), train ordering on shared sections (9)–(10).
- **DTG‑specific:** blocking times (7) depend on train, speed profile and entry speed class, so brake indication points and separation distances are speed‑dependent (A3); conflicts are excluded at the level of TDS occupancy including braking approach (8).
- **Objective:** minimum total weighted delay (5).

The model is a time‑indexed big‑M MILP; it reduces to the original RECIFE‑MILP when all blocking times $B_{f p s}$ are set to the fixed conventional values and $|P_f|=1$ for all $f$.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

Below are the equations of the model (interpretation of the generated code; no code returned).

## Sets and Parameters
- Trains *i, j ∈ I* with directions (up/down); stations *s, t ∈ S*; segments *(s,t)* between consecutive stations.
- Disrupted segment *D* with disruption window [T0, T1]; one track blocked, opposite track usable (rerouting).
- Speed profile options *k ∈ K(i,s,t)* per train per segment, each with precomputed running time **r(i,k,s)** and energy **e(i,k,s)** (assumption: profiles pre-enumerated from train dynamics).
- Scheduled arrivals **A_sched(i,s)**; dwell bounds [dwell_min, dwell_max]; headways h_dep, h_arr, switch-over margin h_sw; station capacities C_s; weights w1, w2, w3; cancellation penalty p_i; horizon T; big-M.

## Variables
- **a(i,s), d(i,s)** ∈ [0,T]: arrival / departure times of train i at station s (continuous).
- **u(i,s)** ≥ 0: delay of train i at station s.
- **x(i,s,t,k)** ∈ {0,1}: train i uses speed profile k on segment (s,t).
- **y(i,j,s)** ∈ {0,1}: ordering — train i departs station s before train j.
- **g(i,s)** ∈ {0,1}: train i is rerouted to the opposite track on segment (s, s+1).
- **c(i)** ∈ {0,1}: train i is cancelled.
- **occ(i,s,τ)** ∈ {0,1}: train i dwells at station s at time point τ (time-indexed grid).

## Objective
Minimize

  **min Σ_{i,s} w1·u(i,s) + Σ_i w2·p_i·c(i) + Σ_{i,(s,t),k} w3·e(i,k,s)·x(i,s,t,k)**

(total delay + cancellation penalties + total energy consumption).

## Constraints

**(1) Dwell bounds** (relaxed if cancelled, big-M·c_i):
- d(i,s) ≥ a(i,s) + dwell_min(i,s) − M·c(i)
- d(i,s) ≤ a(i,s) + dwell_max(i,s) + M·c(i)

**(2) Running-time consistency** (speed profile ↔ timetable coupling, big-M relaxed by cancellation):
- a(i,t) = d(i,s) + Σ_k r(i,k,s)·x(i,s,t,k)  (written as paired inequalities ± M·c_i)

**(3) Profile selection:** Σ_k x(i,s,t,k) = 1 − c(i)  for every train and segment.

**(4) Disruption window / forced rerouting:** if train i occupies disrupted segment D during [T0, T1] (i.e., a(i,s_D) ≤ T1 and d(i,t_D) ≥ T0), then g(i,s_D) = 1:
- a(i,s_D) ≤ T1 + M·(1 − g(i,s_D))
- d(i,t_D) ≥ T0 − M·(1 − g(i,s_D))

**(5) Single-track non-overlap on disrupted segment** (for all pairs i<j, active only when both rerouted):
- y(i,j,s) + y(j,i,s) = 1
- a(j,s_D) ≥ d(i,t_D) + h_sw − M·(1−y(i,j,s)) − M·(1−g(i,s)) − M·(1−g(j,s))
- a(i,s_D) ≥ d(j,t_D) + h_sw − M·(1−y(j,i,s)) − M·(1−g(i,s)) − M·(1−g(j,s))

**(6) Headways on normal segments** (same direction, not rerouted; via ordering variables):
- d(j,s) ≥ d(i,s) + h_dep − M·(1−y(i,j,s)) − M·g(i,s) − M·g(j,s), and symmetric
- a(j,t) ≥ a(i,t) + h_arr − M·(1−y(i,j,s)) − M·g(i,s) − M·g(j,s), and symmetric

**(7) Station capacity** (time-indexed occupancy linking, relaxed by cancellation):
- d(i,s) ≥ τ + 0.5 − M·(1−occ(i,s,τ)) − M·c(i)
- a(i,s) ≤ τ − 0.5 + M·(1−occ(i,s,τ)) + M·c(i)
- Σ_i occ(i,s,τ) ≤ C_s  for all stations s, time points τ

**(8) Delay definition:** u(i,s) ≥ a(i,s) − A_sched(i,s); u(i,s) ≥ 0.

**(9) Cancellation:** if c(i)=1, all timings fixed to schedule:
- a(i,s), d(i,s) = A_sched(i,s) ± M·(1−c(i)) (paired big-M inequalities)

**(10) Rerouting feasibility:** g(i,s) ≤ 1 − c(i); plus switch-over margins at stations adjacent to D between rerouted trains and opposite-direction trains:
- d(j,s_D) ≥ d(i,s_D) + h_sw − M·(1−y(i,j,s_D)) − M·(1−g(i,s_D)), and symmetric
- a(j,t_D) ≥ a(i,t_D) + h_sw − M·(1−y(i,j,s_D)) − M·(1−g(i,s_D)), and symmetric

**(11) Horizon bounds:** 0 ≤ a(i,s), d(i,s) ≤ T.

## Key Assumptions (explicit)
1. Speed profiles are pre-enumerated; each is linearly characterized by (running time, energy) — the timetable–speed-profile coupling is captured by constraint (2).
2. Only one segment is partially blocked; rerouting means using the opposite track during the window.
3. Cancellation carries a fixed penalty; cancelled trains occupy no capacity.
4. Conflicts are modeled via pairwise ordering variables (big-M disjunctions) and time-indexed station occupancy.
5. Single weighted-sum objective over delay, cancellations, and energy.

All constraints are linear (big-M transformations), yielding a valid MILP for the TRSMP.

# TRSMP — MILP Formulation (Equations Only)

## Sets and Parameters
- Trains $i, j \in \{1,\dots,N\}$; stations $s \in \{1,\dots,S\}$; segments $k \in \{1,\dots,S-1\}$ (segment $k$ connects stations $k$ and $k+1$); speed profiles $p \in P_{ik}$.
- $r_{ikp}$: running time of profile $p$ for train $i$ on segment $k$; $e_{ikp}$: its energy consumption.
- $D$: disrupted segments; $[T_0, T_1]$: disruption time window (one track blocked).
- $dw^{\min}_{is}$: minimum dwell; $h$: headway; $H$: planning horizon; $M$: big-M.
- $a^{plan}_{is}, d^{plan}_{is}$: planned arrival/departure times.

## Decision Variables
- $a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $x_{ikp} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $k$.
- $y_{ik} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ rerouted to opposite track on segment $k$.
- $o_{ijk} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $k$.
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled.
- $w_{ik} \ge 0$: waiting/dwell-extension slack.
- $\delta^a_{is}, \delta^d_{is} \ge 0$: arrival/departure delay vs plan.
- Auxiliary binaries: $u_{ijk}$ (same-track indicator), $v^1_{ik}, v^2_{ik}$ (disruption-overlap indicator), $b_{ijs}$ (station occupancy overlap).

## Objective (lexicographic weights $M_1 \gg M_2 \gg M_3$)

$$\min \; M_1 \sum_i \sum_s \left(\delta^a_{is} + \delta^d_{is}\right) \;+\; M_2 \sum_i c_i \;+\; M_3 \sum_i \sum_k \sum_{p \in P_{ik}} e_{ikp}\, x_{ikp}$$

## Constraints

**(1) Running time with chosen speed profile** (for each train $i$, segment $k$ on its route, with $s_{from} \to s_{to}$ per direction):
$$d_{i,s_{from}} + w_{ik} + \sum_{p} r_{ikp}\, x_{ikp} \;\le\; a_{i,s_{to}} + M c_i$$

**(2) Speed-profile uniqueness:**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{ik}} x_{ikp} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, k$$

**(3) Minimum dwell time:**
$$a_{is} + dw^{\min}_{is} \le d_{is} + M c_i \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(4)+(7) Headway on shared track** (trains share a track iff $y_{ik} = y_{jk}$, linearized by $u_{ijk} \ge y_{ik} - y_{jk}$, $u_{ijk} \ge y_{jk} - y_{ik}$):
$$a_{jk} \ge d_{ik} + h - M(1 - o_{ijk}) - M u_{ijk} - M(c_i + c_j)$$
$$a_{ik} \ge d_{jk} + h - M\, o_{ijk} - M u_{ijk} - M(c_i + c_j) \qquad \forall i < j,\, k$$

**(5) Rerouting only on disrupted segments:**
$$y_{ik} = 0 \qquad \forall i,\, k \notin D$$

**(6) Disruption blockage** (occupancy overlapping $[T_0,T_1]$ forces rerouting; $v^1=1$ if $d_{ik} \le T_0$, $v^2=1$ if $a_{ik} \ge T_1$):
$$d_{ik} \le T_0 + M v^1_{ik}, \qquad a_{ik} \ge T_1 - M v^2_{ik}$$
$$y_{ik} \ge 1 - v^1_{ik} - v^2_{ik} \qquad \forall i,\, k \in D$$

**(8) Station platform capacity** (at most $P_s$ trains dwelling simultaneously; pairwise overlap binaries $b_{ijs}$ with $b_{ijs} \ge \frac{d_{is}-a_{is}}{M} + \frac{d_{js}-a_{js}}{M} - 1$):
$$\sum_{(i,j) \subset Q} b_{ijs} \le \binom{|Q|}{2} - P_s \qquad \forall s,\ \forall Q \subseteq N,\ |Q| = P_s + 1$$

**(9) Time horizon:**
$$0 \le a_{is} \le H, \qquad 0 \le d_{is} \le H \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(10) Cancellation propagation:**
$$y_{ik} \le 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i, k$$

**(11) Delay definitions:**
$$\delta^a_{is} \ge a_{is} - a^{plan}_{is} - M c_i, \qquad \delta^d_{is} \ge d_{is} - d^{plan}_{is} - M c_i \qquad \forall i, s$$

## Assumptions (marked where information was missing)
- Double-track corridor; disruption blocks one track on segments $D$ during $[T_0,T_1]$; rerouting to the opposite track is allowed only within this window.
- Speed profiles are pre-enumerated per (train, segment) with fixed running time and energy (piecewise-constant discretization keeps the model linear).
- Lexicographic objective (delay ≫ cancellations ≫ energy) realized via large weights.
- Big-M constants derived from horizon $H$; headway $h$ and platform counts $P_s$ are uniform parameters.
- The model simultaneously decides retiming ($a,d$), reordering ($o$), rerouting ($y$), cancellation ($c$), and speed-profile selection ($x$), yielding a conflict-free timetable with executable speed profiles.

# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor consists of stations $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ connected by segments $E = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$. Each segment $e$ has two tracks: the normal track (direction-dependent) and the opposite track. A partial blockage disables the normal track of segment $e^*$ during the disruption time window $[T^{start}, T^{end}]$. Affected trains may **reroute** to the opposite track (single-track, bidirectional operation) during the window.

**Assumptions (marked where invented):**
- (A1) Trains run on a fixed set of scheduled stops; overtaking only at stations.
- (A2) Each train–segment pair has a finite set of pre-enumerated speed profiles (train plans), each with fixed running time and energy consumption (piecewise-linear approximation of train dynamics, as in the decomposition framework of the paper).
- (A3) Disruption start time is known; end time is deterministic (or a set of scenarios).
- (A4) Cancellation is allowed with a penalty (optional binary variable).
- (A5) Headway times are constant and known.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains; $T^{up}, T^{down}$: direction subsets |
| $E$ | segments; $e^*$ disrupted segment |
| $K_{i,e}$ | speed profiles (plans) for train $i$ on segment $e$; each $k$ has running time $r_{ike}$ and energy $\epsilon_{ike}$ |
| $h^{arr}, h^{dep}, h^{sec}$ | arrival, departure, and section headways |
| $d_i$ | scheduled departure from origin; scheduled times $a^{sch}_{is}, d^{sch}_{is}$ |
| $w_{1}, w_{2}, w_{3}$ | weights: total delay, energy, cancellation |
| $M$ | big constant |
| $[\underline{L}_{e}, \bar{U}_{e}]$ | disruption window on segment $e$ ($= e^*$) |

## 3. Decision Variables

- $a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $x_{ike} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $e$.
- $y_{ie} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ traverses segment $e$ on the **opposite track** (rerouting).
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ is cancelled.
- $\sigma_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable on segment $e$ (train $i$ before $j$), defined for pairs sharing a track resource.
- $\delta_{is} \ge 0$: arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \sum_{i \in T} \sum_{s \in S} \delta_{is} \;+\; w_2 \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{e \in E}\sum_{k \in K_{i,e}} \epsilon_{ike}\, x_{ike} \;+\; w_3 \sum_{i \in T} z_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Timetable consistency (running times from selected speed profile):**
$$
a_{i,s+1} \;\ge\; d_{is} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,e}} r_{ike}\, x_{ike} \qquad \forall i,\; e=(s,s+1)
$$

**(2) Exactly one speed profile per train–segment (if not cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{k \in K_{i,e}} x_{ike} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, e
$$

**(3) Dwell time and scheduled stops:**
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{is} + \tau^{min}_{is} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(4) Delay definition:**
$$
\delta_{is} \ge a_{is} - a^{sch}_{is}, \qquad \delta_{is} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(5) Rerouting feasibility — opposite track only usable within disruption window:**
$$
a_{i,s+1} \le \underline{L}_{e} \;+\; M(1 - y_{ie}), \qquad
d_{is} \ge \bar{U}_{e} \;-\; M(1 - y_{ie}) \qquad \forall i,\; e = e^*
$$
(i.e., if train $i$ reroutes, it must fully traverse segment $e^*$ inside the window $[\underline{L}_{e^*}, \bar{U}_{e^*}]$; trains outside the window use the normal track: $y_{ie}=0$.)

**(6) Rerouting only on the disrupted segment:**
$$
y_{ie} = 0 \qquad \forall i,\; e \neq e^*
$$

**(7) Bidirectional conflict-free operation on a shared track (segment $e^*$ during disruption):** for trains $i,j$ that may share a track resource on segment $e$ (same chosen track, opposite directions):
$$
a_{j,s+1} \ge d_{is} + h^{sec} - M(3 - \sigma_{ij} - y_{ie} - y_{je})
$$
$$
a_{i,s+1} \ge d_{js} + h^{sec} - M(2 - \sigma_{ij} - y_{ie} - y_{je} + \sigma_{ij}\cdot 1) \;\equiv\; a_{i,s+1} \ge d_{js} + h^{sec} - M(3 + \sigma_{ij} - y_{ie} - y_{je} - 2\sigma_{ij})
$$
Equivalently, with the standard big-M disjunction: if both trains use the opposite track ($y_{ie}=y_{je}=1$), then either $j$ enters after $i$ leaves ($\sigma_{ij}=1$) or vice versa ($\sigma_{ij}=0$).

**(8) Same-direction headway on the same track:** for trains $i,j$ in the same direction using the same track on segment $e$:
$$
d_{js} \ge d_{is} + h^{dep} - M(2 - \sigma_{ij} - u_{ije}), \qquad
d_{is} \ge d_{js} + h^{dep} - M(1 + \sigma_{ij} - u_{ije})
$$
where $u_{ije} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates $i,j$ share the same track on $e$:
$$
u_{ije} \ge y_{ie} + y_{je} - 1, \qquad u_{ije} \le y_{ie}, \quad u_{ije} \le y_{je}
$$

**(9) Station arrival headway (overtaking/conflict at stations):**
$$
a_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{arr} - M(2 - \sigma^{s}_{ij} - o_{ijs}), \qquad
a_{is} \ge a_{js} + h^{arr} - M(1 + \sigma^{s}_{ij} - o_{ijs})
$$
with ordering variables $\sigma^{s}_{ij}$ and same-track indicators $o_{ijs}$ at station $s$.

**(10) Cancellation propagation:** if train $i$ is cancelled, its times are free:
$$
a_{is}, d_{is} \le M z_i, \qquad \delta_{is} \le M z_i \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(11) Time horizon:**
$$
0 \le a_{is}, d_{is} \le H \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(12) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{ike}, y_{ie}, z_i, \sigma_{ij}, \sigma^{s}_{ij}, u_{ije} \in \{0,1\}; \quad a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Remarks

- Constraints (1)–(2) couple the timetable with the speed-profile (train plan) selection, ensuring the rescheduled timetable is executable at the control level — this is the TRP–TSMP integration.
- Constraints (5)–(9) model local rerouting to the opposite track during the disruption window and guarantee conflict-free bidirectional sharing of the single available track.
- Following the paper's decomposition idea, fixing the plan-selection variables $x_{ike}$ yields a pure train-plan IP over interactions, while each train's plan set can be refined adaptively (interval plans) — the MILP above with sufficiently fine plan enumeration is equivalent to that IP.

Text:
# MILP Model: Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Scheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

We consider a single urban rail transit line with stations indexed in one direction (extension to bidirectional is straightforward by duplicating variables per direction). Trains depart from the first station, stop at a subset of stations, and return via rolling stock circulation. Passenger demand is time-varying and approximated as **piecewise constant** over time intervals.

**Assumptions (explicitly marked where reasonable assumptions were needed):**

- **(A1)** The line is a single corridor; overtaking is not possible (train order is fixed). *(Standard for urban rail.)*
- **(A2)** Passenger demand is deterministic and known over the prediction horizon, piecewise constant per time interval. *(As in Liu et al., 2023a.)*
- **(A3)** Passengers board the first arriving train with sufficient residual capacity; otherwise they wait (no left-behind beyond capacity constraint — waiting passengers carry over).
- **(A4)** Train composition is chosen from a set of train unit configurations; a train of composition $c$ has capacity $Cap_c$ and energy/operation cost $\gamma_c$.
- **(A5)** Running times between stations are fixed; dwell times are decision variables within bounds.
- **(A6)** Skipped stops are allowed (stop-skipping), with skipped passengers waiting for later trains.
- **(A7)** Rolling stock: each train run must be assigned a successor run (circulation) with minimum turnaround time; fleet size is limited.
- **(A8)** MPC setting: the model is solved over a receding prediction horizon; below we state the single-horizon problem.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I = \{1,\dots,n\}$ | stations |
| $F = \{1,\dots,m\}$ | train runs (services) in the horizon |
| $C$ | set of train compositions (e.g., $\{1,2,3\}$ train units) |
| $K = \{1,\dots,H\}$ | time intervals of length $\Delta$ |
| $\mathcal{A} = \{(f,i): f \in F, i \in I\}$ | arcs (train, station) |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $r_i$ | running time from station $i$ to $i+1$ |
| $\underline d_i, \bar d_i$ | min/max dwell time at station $i$ |
| $h^{\min}$ | minimum headway between consecutive trains (same station) |
| $T^{turn}_{\min}$ | minimum turnaround time at terminal |
| $Cap_c$ | passenger capacity of composition $c$ |
| $\gamma_c$ | operation cost per run with composition $c$ |
| $D_{i,k}$ | demand at station $i$ destined in direction of travel, interval $k$ (pax) |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $N^{max}$ | maximum number of train units in the fleet |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | weights: waiting time, travel/deviation, operation cost |
| $t^{ref}_{f,i}$ | reference (nominal) arrival time of train $f$ at station $i$ |

## 4. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{f,i} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $f$ at station $i$
- $d_{f,i} \ge 0$: departure time of train $f$ from station $i$
- $q_{f,i} \ge 0$: passengers left waiting at station $i$ after departure of train $f$
- $b_{f,i} \ge 0$: passengers boarding train $f$ at station $i$
- $y_{f,i} \ge 0$: passengers on board train $f$ on section $(i, i+1)$

**Binary/Integer:**
- $x_{f,i} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ stops at station $i$
- $z_{f,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses composition $c$
- $u_{f,g} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if run $g$ is the immediate successor of run $f$ in the rolling stock circulation

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize weighted sum of passenger waiting time, timetable deviation, and operation cost:

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 \underbrace{\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{i\in I} q_{f,i}\,\Delta}_{\text{total waiting}}
+ w_2 \underbrace{\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{i\in I} \left(a_{f,i} - t^{ref}_{f,i}\right)}_{\text{deviation from nominal timetable}}
+ w_3 \underbrace{\sum_{f\in F}\sum_{c\in C} \gamma_c\, z_{f,c}}_{\text{operation cost}}
$$

*(Waiting time is approximated linearly by leftover passengers per interval, as in Liu et al. (2023a); a more refined version weights $q_{f,i}$ by the elapsed time since demand arrival — marked as a linearization assumption.)*

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable dynamics — running and dwell times:**
$$
d_{f,i} = a_{f,i} + \underline d_i\, x_{f,i} + s_{f,i}, \qquad 0 \le s_{f,i} \le (\bar d_i - \underline d_i)\, x_{f,i}, \quad \forall f, i < n
$$
$$
a_{f,i+1} = d_{f,i} + r_i, \qquad \forall f,\; i < n
$$

**(C2) Headway (fixed train order, A1):**
$$
a_{f+1,i} - a_{f,i} \ge h^{\min}, \qquad \forall f < m,\; i \in I
$$

**(C3) Stop consistency:** if a train does not stop, no boarding occurs:
$$
b_{f,i} \le M\, x_{f,i}, \qquad \forall f, i
$$

**(C4) Composition selection (exactly one composition per run):**
$$
\sum_{c \in C} z_{f,c} = 1, \qquad \forall f \in F
$$

**(C5) Capacity constraint (on-board load limited by chosen composition):**
$$
y_{f,i} \le \sum_{c\in C} Cap_c\, z_{f,c}, \qquad \forall f,\; i < n
$$

**(C6) Passenger flow balance — station (demand + carry-over = boarded + left behind):**
$$
D_{i,k(f,i)} + q_{f-1,i} = b_{f,i} + q_{f,i}, \qquad \forall f,\; i
$$
where $k(f,i)$ is the interval containing departure time $d_{f,i}$ (linearized via standard time-indexing or indicator constraints; see remark below). With $q_{0,i} = 0$.

**(C7) Passenger flow balance — on-board load per section:**
$$
y_{f,1} = b_{f,1}, \qquad
y_{f,i} = y_{f,i-1} - \beta_{f,i-1} + b_{f,i}, \qquad \forall f,\; 1 < i < n
$$
where $\beta_{f,i} \ge 0$ is the number of alighting passengers at station $i$, with $\beta_{f,i} \le y_{f,i-1}$ and $\beta_{f,i} \le \rho_i\, y_{f,i-1}$ (a fixed alighting fraction $\rho_i$ — *(A9, assumed)*; alternatively alighting demand $A_{i,k}$ replaces $\beta$ linearly).

**(C8) Rolling stock circulation — each run has exactly one successor and one predecessor:**
$$
\sum_{g \in F} u_{f,g} = 1, \qquad \forall f \in F
$$
$$
\sum_{f \in F} u_{f,g} = 1, \qquad \forall g \in F
$$

**(C9) Turnaround time and composition consistency of successor:**
$$
d_{g,1} \ge a_{f,n} + T^{turn}_{\min} - M(1 - u_{f,g}), \qquad \forall f, g
$$
$$
z_{g,c} - z_{f,c} \le 1 - u_{f,g} \;\text{ and }\; z_{f,c} - z_{g,c} \le 1 - u_{f,g}, \qquad \forall f,g,c
$$
*(A10, assumed: train units are coupled/decoupled only at the depot, so composition is inherited between coupled runs; if composition may change at the terminal, replace by $z_{g,c} \le \sum_{c': c' \le c} z_{f,c'}$ to allow only unit additions.)*

**(C11) Fleet size limit:** the circulation must form at most $N^{max}$ cycles. Using a standard single-commodity flow formulation on the successor graph with flow variable $\phi_{f,g} \ge 0$:
$$
\phi_{f,g} \le M\, u_{f,g}, \quad \sum_g \phi_{f,g} - \sum_g \phi_{g,f} \ge 1 - M(1-u_{f,0}), \quad \sum_{f,g}\phi_{f,g} \le N^{max}
$$
where $u_{f,0}$ links runs to a depot dummy node *(A11: standard MTZ or flow-based subtour/fleet formulation; any equivalent formulation may be substituted)*.

**(C12) Terminal departure within horizon:**
$$
a_{f,1} \ge 0, \qquad a_{f,n} \le T^{horizon}, \qquad \forall f
$$

**(C13) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{f,i}, d_{f,i}, q_{f,i}, b_{f,i}, y_{f,i}, \beta_{f,i}, s_{f,i} \ge 0; \quad x_{f,i}, z_{f,c}, u_{f,g} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 7. Remark on Demand–Time Coupling

The term $D_{i,k(f,i)}$ in (C6) couples continuous times with interval indices. Two standard linearizations:

1. **Time-indexed:** introduce binary $\delta_{f,i,k} = 1$ if $d_{f,i}$ falls in interval $k$, with $\sum_k \delta_{f,i,k}=1$ and $d_{f,i} \in [\sum_k (k-1)\Delta\,\delta_{f,i,k},\, \sum_k k\Delta\,\delta_{f,i,k}]$; then (C6) becomes $b_{f,i} + q_{f,i} = q_{f-1,i} + \sum_k D_{i,k}\delta_{f,i,k}$.
2. **MPC piecewise-constant approximation:** fix $\delta$ from the previous MPC iteration's timetable (as done in Liu et al., 2023a), keeping the online problem linear.

## 8. MPC / Learning-Based Usage (Context)

In the proposed framework, at each MPC step this MILP is solved over a receding horizon. The integer variables ($x_{f,i}$, $z_{f,c}$, $u_{f,g}$) are obtained by the LSTM network after presolve pruning; with integers fixed, constraints (C1)–(C13) reduce to a **linear program (LP)** in $(a, d, q, b, y, \beta, s)$, which is solved to guarantee feasibility and optimality of the continuous timetable. Only the first control actions are applied, and the horizon rolls forward.

# Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling MILP
### with Time-Varying Demand, Flexible Train Composition, and Rolling Stock Circulation

This model extends the MILP-based MPC formulation of Liu et al. (2023a) with flexible train composition and rolling stock circulation, as described in the introduction. It is the MILP solved at each MPC step (with integer variables fixed, it reduces to an LP).

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L$ | Set of lines in the network, index $\ell$ |
| $S_\ell$ | Ordered set of stations on line $\ell$, index $s$ (down direction: $s=1,\dots,|\ell|$; up direction reversed) |
| $T_\ell$ | Set of train services on line $\ell$ within the prediction horizon, index $t$ |
| $K$ | Set of time intervals of length $\Delta t$ partitioning the horizon, index $k$ |
| $C$ | Set of train composition types (number of coupled train units), e.g. $C=\{1,2,3,4\}$, index $c$ |
| $U_\ell$ | Set of train units (rolling stock) available on line $\ell$, index $u$ |
| $\mathcal{T}(u)$ | Set of feasible trips of unit $u$ (successive services it can cover) |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $d^{arr}_{\ell,t,s}, d^{dep}_{\ell,t,s}$ | Nominal arrival/departure times of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $r_{\ell,s}$ | Minimum running time from $s$ to $s+1$ on line $\ell$ |
| $w_{\ell,s}$ | Minimum dwell time at station $s$ |
| $h^{\min}_{\ell}, h^{\max}_{\ell}$ | Minimum/maximum headway between successive trains |
| $q_{\ell,s,k}$ | Passenger demand arriving at station $s$ of line $\ell$ during interval $k$ (piecewise constant) |
| $\alpha_{\ell,s}$ | Fraction of passengers at $s$ destined beyond the next station (boarding share) |
| $Cap$ | Passenger capacity of one train unit |
| $M$ | Large positive constant |
| $\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3$ | Weights for waiting time, travel time deviation, and operation cost |
| $e_u$ | Operating cost per trip of train unit $u$ |
| $\tau^{turn}$ | Minimum turnaround time at terminal stations |
| $H$ | Prediction horizon length; $N_p$ number of MPC steps |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{\ell,t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: actual arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$
- $d_{\ell,t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: actual departure time
- $B_{\ell,t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: number of passengers boarding train $t$ at station $s$
- $W_{\ell,t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: passengers left waiting at station $s$ after train $t$ departs
- $P_{\ell,t,s} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: in-vehicle load of train $t$ on section $(s, s+1)$

**Binary/Integer:**
- $x_{\ell,t,c} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ on line $\ell$ runs with composition $c$
- $y_{u,\ell,t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train unit $u$ is assigned to service $t$ on line $\ell$
- $z_{u,\ell,t,t'} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if unit $u$ covers service $t'$ immediately after service $t$ (rolling stock circulation)

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; J = \beta_1 \underbrace{\sum_{\ell}\sum_{t}\sum_{s} W_{\ell,t,s}}_{\text{total waiting passengers}}
+ \beta_2 \underbrace{\sum_{\ell}\sum_{t}\sum_{s}\left[(a_{\ell,t,s}-d^{arr}_{\ell,t,s})^+ + (d_{\ell,t,s}-d^{dep}_{\ell,t,s})^+\right]}_{\text{timetable deviation}}
+ \beta_3 \underbrace{\sum_{\ell}\sum_{t}\sum_{c} e_c\, x_{\ell,t,c}}_{\text{operation cost}}
$$

Deviation is linearized with auxiliary variables $\delta^a_{\ell,t,s}, \delta^d_{\ell,t,s} \ge 0$:
$$
\delta^a_{\ell,t,s} \ge a_{\ell,t,s}-d^{arr}_{\ell,t,s},\quad \delta^d_{\ell,t,s} \ge d_{\ell,t,s}-d^{dep}_{\ell,t,s}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**Timetable dynamics (running and dwell times):**
$$
d_{\ell,t,s} \ge a_{\ell,t,s} + w_{\ell,s} \qquad \forall \ell,t,s \tag{1}
$$
$$
a_{\ell,t,s+1} \ge d_{\ell,t,s} + r_{\ell,s} \qquad \forall \ell,t,s \tag{2}
$$

**Headway (line capacity):**
$$
d_{\ell,t+1,s} - d_{\ell,t,s} \ge h^{\min}_{\ell}, \qquad
d_{\ell,t+1,s} - d_{\ell,t,s} \le h^{\max}_{\ell} \qquad \forall \ell,t,s \tag{3}
$$

**Turnaround / circulation compatibility:**
$$
d_{\ell,t',1} \ge d_{\ell,t,|\ell|} + \tau^{turn} - M(1 - z_{u,\ell,t,t'}) \qquad \forall u,\ell,t,t'\in\mathcal{T}(u) \tag{4}
$$

**Flexible composition — exactly one composition per train:**
$$
\sum_{c\in C} x_{\ell,t,c} = 1 \qquad \forall \ell,t \tag{5}
$$
$$
\sum_{u\in U_\ell} y_{u,\ell,t} = \sum_{c\in C} c\, x_{\ell,t,c} \qquad \forall \ell,t \tag{6}
$$

**Rolling stock circulation — each unit used at most once, circulation consistency:**
$$
\sum_{\ell,t} y_{u,\ell,t} \le 1 \qquad \forall u \tag{7}
$$
$$
\sum_{t'\in\mathcal{T}(u)} z_{u,\ell,t,t'} \le y_{u,\ell,t} \qquad \forall u,\ell,t \tag{8}
$$
$$
\sum_{t:\,t'\in\mathcal{T}(u)} z_{u,\ell,t,t'} \le y_{u,\ell,t'} \qquad \forall u,\ell,t' \tag{9}
$$

**Passenger flow dynamics (piecewise-constant demand):**

Demand arriving during interval $k$ can board trains departing in that interval or later:
$$
\sum_{t:\, d_{\ell,t,s}\in[k\Delta t,(k+1)\Delta t)} B_{\ell,t,s} + W_{\ell,t,s}^{k} = q_{\ell,s,k} + W_{\ell,t^{-},s}^{k-1} \qquad \forall \ell,s,k \tag{10}
$$
where $W^k_{\ell,t,s}$ is the residual waiting stock after train $t$ (assumption: linearized boarding, see §7), and $t^{-}$ is the previous train serving $s$.

**Boarding limited by capacity of the chosen composition:**
$$
B_{\ell,t,s} \le \sum_{c\in C} c\cdot Cap \cdot x_{\ell,t,c} - P_{\ell,t,s-1} + M(1-\sigma_{\ell,t,s}) \qquad \forall \ell,t,s \tag{11}
$$
with load propagation:
$$
P_{\ell,t,s} = P_{\ell,t,s-1} + B_{\ell,t,s} - \alpha_{\ell,s} P_{\ell,t,s-1} \qquad \forall \ell,t,s \tag{12}
$$
($\sigma_{\ell,t,s}\in\{0,1\}$ indicates a stop; skipped stations have $B_{\ell,t,s}=0$.)

**Bounds:**
$$
0 \le a_{\ell,t,s}, d_{\ell,t,s} \le H,\qquad 0 \le P_{\ell,t,s} \le \sum_c c\,Cap\, x_{\ell,t,c} \tag{13}
$$

## 6. MPC Formulation

At each MPC step $i$:
1. Measure current train positions and waiting passengers; update demand forecasts $\hat q_{\ell,s,k}$ over horizon $N_p$.
2. Solve MILP (1)–(13) over the receding horizon.
3. Apply only the first control actions (departures in the first interval); shift horizon and repeat.

## 7. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** Demand $q_{\ell,s,k}$ is piecewise constant per interval $\Delta t$ (as in Liu et al., 2023a).
- **(A2)** Boarding is linearized: passengers board FIFO; leftover passengers roll to the next train via constraint (10).
- **(A3)** All train units are homogeneous with capacity $Cap$; composition $c$ uses $c$ coupled units.
- **(A4)** Skipped stops are pre-decided (stop-skipping variables $\sigma$ fixed by presolve), keeping the model linear.
- **(A5)** Learning-based MPC: an LSTM predicts the integer variables $\{x, y, z\}$; with these fixed, (1)–(13) reduce to an LP solved online — this is the optimization-driven learning framework of the paper.

**Complexity:** $O(|L||T||S|)$ continuous and $O(|L||T|(|C|+|U_\ell|))$ binary variables, reduced by the four presolve techniques before LSTM prediction.

I generated three candidate MILP formulations and selected the best one below (Model 3), which most cleanly and completely captures retiming, reordering, rerouting with bidirectional conflict handling, discrete speed-profile selection, and cancellation.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions

- A double-track corridor divided into segments; each track of a segment can be occupied by at most one train at a time (block-section occupancy).
- A disruption blocks one track (partial segment blockage) of segment set $\mathcal{B}$ during time window $[T^{dis}_s, T^{dis}_e]$.
- Trains may be rerouted to the opposite track of a segment during the disruption window (single-track operation).
- Each train–segment has a finite set of speed profiles, each giving a (running time, energy) pair.
- Cancellation of trains is allowed at a cost.
- All times are discretized or treated as continuous; ordering decisions are modeled with binary variables.
- Rolling-stock turnaround constraints are included as optional constraints.

## 2. Sets and Indices

- $\mathcal{I}$: set of trains, indexed $i$.
- $\mathcal{S}$: ordered set of segments along the corridor, indexed $s$.
- $\mathcal{K}_s = \{1,2\}$: tracks of segment $s$ (1 = normal track, 2 = opposite track).
- $\mathcal{P}_{is}$: set of speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $s$, indexed $p$.
- $\mathcal{B} \subseteq \mathcal{S}$: blocked segments.

## 3. Parameters

- $d^{sch}_{is}, a^{sch}_{is}$: scheduled departure/arrival of train $i$ at segment $s$ boundaries.
- $\underline{w}_{is}, \bar{w}_{is}$: min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station at end of segment $s$.
- $t^{run}_{isp}$: running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ with profile $p$.
- $e_{isp}$: energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ with profile $p$.
- $h$: minimum headway (same direction); $h^{op}$: minimum headway for opposite-direction meetings on single-track operation.
- $T^{dis}_s, T^{dis}_e$: disruption start/end times.
- $M$: big constant.
- $c^{can}_i$: cancellation cost of train $i$.
- $\alpha, \beta$: weights for delay and energy ($\beta$ scaled so delay is primary, e.g., $\alpha \gg \beta \cdot \max e$).
- $T^{max}$: maximum allowed delay.
- $\tau^{turn}$: minimum turnaround time at terminal stations.

## 4. Variables

- $a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure times of train $i$ at segment $s$.
- $y_{isk} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses track $k$ of segment $s$.
- $x_{isp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $p$ on segment $s$.
- $\delta_{is} \ge 0$: delay of train $i$ at segment $s$ (departure delay).
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled.
- $o_{ijs} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ traverse segment $s$ in **opposite** directions (both present due to rerouting).
- $b_{ijs} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (same direction).
- $u_{ijs} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ enters segment $s$ before train $j$ (used for opposite-direction sequencing).

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \delta_{is} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{is}} e_{isp}\, x_{isp} \;+\; \sum_{i \in \mathcal{I}} c^{can}_i z_i
$$

Delay is primary via $\alpha \gg \beta$; energy is the secondary weighted term; cancellation costs penalize dropping trains.

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile selection (exactly one profile, or none if cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_{is}} x_{isp} \le 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C2) Track assignment (exactly one track, or none if cancelled):**
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_s} y_{isk} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C3) Disruption window forbids blocked track:**
$$
d_{is} \le T^{dis}_s + M(1 - y_{is1}) \qquad \forall i,\, s \in \mathcal{B}
$$
$$
a_{is} \ge T^{dis}_e - M(1 - y_{is1}) \qquad \forall i,\, s \in \mathcal{B}
$$
A train may use the blocked track only if it fully clears the segment before the disruption starts or enters after it ends; otherwise it must use track 2 ($y_{is2}=1$).

**(C4) Running time consistency with chosen profile:**
$$
a_{is} \ge d_{i,s-1} + \sum_{p} t^{run}_{isp} x_{isp} - M z_i \qquad \forall i,\, s \ge 2
$$
(with $d_{i,1}$ the origin departure). Equivalently, $a_{is} - d_{i,s-1} \ge \sum_p t^{run}_{isp} x_{isp}$.

**(C5) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
d_{is} - a_{is} \ge \underline{w}_{is} - M z_i, \qquad d_{is} - a_{is} \le \bar{w}_{is} + M z_i \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C6) Delay definition:**
$$
\delta_{is} \ge d_{is} - d^{sch}_{is} - M z_i, \qquad \delta_{is} \ge 0 \qquad \forall i, s
$$
$$
\delta_{is} \le T^{max} \qquad \forall i, s
$$

**(C7) Same-direction conflict-free headway on each track.** For each pair $i<j$ with the same direction on segment $s$ and track $k$:
$$
d_{js} \ge a_{is} + h - M(3 - b_{ijs} - y_{isk} - y_{jsk})
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{js} + h - M(2 - b_{ijs} - y_{isk} - y_{jsk})
$$
If both trains occupy the same track, exactly one ordering holds and the follower departs at least $h$ after the leader's arrival (exit–entry headway ensuring block-section exclusivity).

**(C8) Opposite-direction (single-track) conflict-free meeting.** For each pair $i,j$ with opposite directions on segment $s$ where rerouting may cause sharing:
$$
d_{js} \ge a_{is} + h^{op} - M(3 - u_{ijs} - o_{ijs} - y_{is2}) \qquad \text{(i enters before j)}
$$
$$
d_{is} \ge a_{js} + h^{op} - M(2 - u_{ijs} - o_{ijs} - y_{is2}) \qquad \text{(j enters before i)}
$$
where the opposite-direction indicator is enforced by:
$$
o_{ijs} \ge y_{is2} + y_{js1} - 1, \quad o_{ijs} \ge y_{is1} + y_{js2} - 1 \qquad \forall i<j,\, s
$$
This guarantees two opposing trains never occupy the single available track simultaneously during the disruption.

**(C9) Cancellation propagation:** if $z_i = 1$, all times are free (relaxed via $M z_i$ above) and no resources are consumed (C1, C2).

**(C10) Rolling-stock turnaround (optional).** For train $i$ whose next service is train $i'$ at terminal station $s^{end}$:
$$
d_{i', s^{start}} \ge a_{i, s^{end}} + \tau^{turn} - M(z_i + z_{i'})
$$

**(C11) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is} \ge 0; \quad y_{isk}, x_{isp}, z_i, o_{ijs}, b_{ijs}, u_{ijs} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Retiming:** continuous variables $a_{is}, d_{is}$ reschedule all trains subject to running (C4) and dwell (C5) times.
- **Reordering:** binaries $b_{ijs}, u_{ijs}$ let the optimizer choose new train sequences, with big-$M$ disjunctive headway constraints (C7, C8) ensuring conflict-free occupancy.
- **Rerouting:** binaries $y_{isk}$ assign trains to tracks; C3 forces use of the opposite track during the disruption window, and C8 handles bidirectional sharing conflicts.
- **Speed management:** binaries $x_{isp}$ select discrete profiles; C4 links the chosen running time to the timetable, and the energy term in $Z$ trades speed (time) against energy.
- **Cancellation:** $z_i$ relaxes all train-specific constraints at cost $c^{can}_i$, providing feasibility guarantees under severe disruption.
- **Linearity:** all constraints are linear; big-$M$ terms activate/deactivate disjunctions, giving a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut.

# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Assumptions
- Double-track high-speed corridor with stations S = {1,…,n+1} and segments b ∈ B between consecutive stations; trains f ∈ F with scheduled direction dir(f) ∈ {up, down}.
- Disruption: a set D of (segment, track) pairs is blocked during time window [T_start, T_end]; affected trains may reroute to the opposite track (y = 1) only during this window.
- Each train f has a set of discrete speed profiles P_{f,b} on segment b, with running time r_{f,b,p} and energy e_{f,b,p}.
- Time is discretized over horizon [0, H]; big-M = H.
- Trains may not arrive earlier than scheduled; cancellation of a whole service is allowed at penalty K_f.

## Variables
- x_{f,b,p} ∈ {0,1}: train f uses speed profile p on segment b
- A_{f,s}, D_{f,s} ∈ ℤ⁺: actual arrival / departure time of train f at station s
- A⁺_{f,s}, D⁺_{f,s} ≥ 0: positive-part delays w.r.t. schedule
- y_{f,b} ∈ {0,1}: train f is rerouted to the opposite track on segment b
- u_f ∈ {0,1}: train f is cancelled
- ord_{f,g,b} ∈ {0,1}: f precedes g on segment b
- o_{f,b,tr,t} ∈ {0,1}: train f occupies segment b on track tr at time t

## Objective
Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellation penalties:

min Σ_f Σ_s [ α_f · A⁺_{f,s} + β_f · D⁺_{f,s} ] + γ · Σ_{f,b} Σ_p e_{f,b,p} · x_{f,b,p} + Σ_f K_f · u_f

## Constraints

**1. Timetable consistency (running time from chosen profile):**
A_{f,s₂} = D_{f,s₁} + Σ_p r_{f,b,p} · x_{f,b,p} + Δ_b · y_{f,b},  ∀f, b = (s₁,s₂)

**2. Profile uniqueness:** Σ_p x_{f,b,p} = 1 − u_f,  ∀f, b

**3. Dwell time bounds:**
dw_min_{f,s} · (1 − u_f) ≤ D_{f,s} − A_{f,s} ≤ dw_max_{f,s} + M·u_f,  ∀f, s

**4. Positive-part delays:** A⁺_{f,s} ≥ A_{f,s} − A^sched_{f,s},  D⁺_{f,s} ≥ D_{f,s} − D^sched_{f,s},  A⁺, D⁺ ≥ 0

**5. No earliness:** A_{f,s} ≥ A^sched_{f,s} − M·u_f,  ∀f, s

**6. Cancellation:** A_{f,s} + D_{f,s} ≤ 2M·u_f,  ∀f, s (if u_f = 1, all times are zero)

**7. Rerouting only on blocked segments:** y_{f,b} = 0 if (b, opp_track(f)) ∉ D

**8. Rerouting only within disruption window (for (b, opp_track(f)) ∈ D):**
- D_{f,s₁} ≥ T_start · y_{f,b} − M(1 − y_{f,b})
- A_{f,s₂} ≤ T_end + M(1 − y_{f,b})

**9. Conflict-free sequencing with minimum headway h_b (big-M):**
- If ord_{f,g,b} = 1 (f before g): A_{g,s₁} ≥ D_{f,s₂} + h_b − M(3 − ord_{f,g,b} − (1−u_f) − (1−u_g))
- If ord_{f,g,b} = 0 (g before f): A_{f,s₁} ≥ D_{g,s₂} + h_b − M(2 + ord_{f,g,b} − (1−u_f) − (1−u_g))

**10. Track capacity (unidirectional occupancy):** Σ_f o_{f,b,tr,t} ≤ 1,  ∀b, tr ∈ {up, down}, t

**11. Occupancy linking (both directions, big-M):** o_{f,b,tr,t} = 1 iff A_{f,s₁} ≤ t ≤ D_{f,s₂} and train f uses track tr on segment b (scheduled track iff y_{f,b} = 0, opposite track iff y_{f,b} = 1); enforced via:
- o_{f,b,tr,t} ≥ 1 − [A_{f,s₁} > t] − [D_{f,s₂} < t] − u_f − (track-mismatch indicator)
- t · o_{f,b,tr,t} ≤ D_{f,s₂} and A_{f,s₁} − H·o_{f,b,tr,t} ≤ t

**12. Time windows:** T_lo_f ≤ A_{f,s}, D_{f,s} ≤ T_hi_f,  ∀f, s

All constraints are linear; the model jointly determines retiming (A, D), reordering (ord), rerouting (y), cancellation (u), and speed-profile selection (x), yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable with executable, energy-efficient speed profiles.

Text:
# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

Consider a bidirectional double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $S = \{1,\dots,n_S\}$ connected by segments $L=\{1,\dots,n_L\}$, where segment $l$ links stations $l$ and $l+1$. A train set $T=\{1,\dots,n_T\}$ operates according to a scheduled timetable. During a disruption time window $[\underline{t}_D,\ \bar{t}_D]$, one track of a set of blocked segments $L^D \subseteq L$ is unavailable, so trains may either wait or **locally reroute** on the opposite track (single-track operation through the disrupted area).

**Assumptions (stated explicitly):**
- (A1) Each train runs on a fixed station sequence; only track choice (original vs. opposite track) within $L^D$ is a decision (local rerouting).
- (A2) For each segment $l$ and train $t$, a finite set of pre-computed speed profiles $P_{tl} = \{1,\dots,|P_{tl}|\}$ exists, each characterized by running time $\rho_{tlp}$, energy consumption $e_{tlp}$, arrival speed $v^{arr}_{tlp}$, and departure speed $v^{dep}_{tlp}$. Profiles are pre-generated by optimal train control (pseudo-spectral/maximum-acceleration methods) — this is what keeps the model linear.
- (A3) Safety is enforced by departure/arrival headways between consecutive trains using the same track resource.
- (A4) Train cancellations are not modeled (trains must run); delays are weighted by train priority $w_t$.
- (A5) Time horizon $[0,H]$ is discretized in the plan generation but the MILP itself uses continuous times.

## 2. Sets, Parameters, and Variables

**Sets/parameters:**
- $a_{ts}$ / $d_{ts}$: scheduled arrival / departure of train $t$ at station $s$.
- $\underline{dw}_{ts}, \overline{dw}_{ts}$: min/max dwell time of $t$ at $s$.
- $\underline{h}^{arr}_l, \underline{h}^{dep}_l, \underline{h}^{mix}_l$: minimum arrival, departure, and mixed headways on track of segment $l$.
- $M$: sufficiently large constant (e.g., $M = H + \sum \overline{dw}$).

**Variables:**
- $x_{ts} \in \mathbb{R}_+$: actual arrival time of $t$ at $s$; $y_{ts}\in\mathbb{R}_+$: actual departure time.
- $\delta_{ts}\in\mathbb{R}_+$: arrival delay of $t$ at $s$.
- $z_{tl} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses the *original* track of segment $l$; 0 if it reroutes (only relevant if $l\in L^D$).
- $p_{tl} \in \{0,1\}^{|P_{tl}|}$: speed-profile selection; $p_{tlq}=1$ iff profile $q$ chosen.
- $r_{t\bar{t}l}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ departs segment $l$ before train $\bar{t}$ (ordering variable), for $t<\bar{t}$.
- $u_{t\bar{t}l}\in\{0,1\}$: 1 if $t$ and $\bar{t}$ traverse $l$ in *opposite* directions.

## 3. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total passenger delay and total energy consumption:

$$
\min\; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S} w_t\, \delta_{ts}}_{\text{total delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\beta \sum_{t\in T}\sum_{l\in L}\sum_{q\in P_{tl}} e_{tlq}\, p_{tlq}}_{\text{total energy}} \tag{1}
$$

where $\beta > 0$ converts energy units into time-equivalent cost (**assumption A6**: linear scalarization of the two objectives).

## 4. Constraints

### 4.1 Timetabling (retiming)

**Delay definition** (final station delay counted; delay propagation through dwells):

$$
\delta_{ts} \ge x_{ts} - a_{ts}, \qquad \forall t\in T,\ \forall s\in S \tag{2}
$$

**Dwell time bounds:**

$$
\underline{dw}_{ts} \le x_{t,s} - y_{t,s-1} \le \overline{dw}_{ts}, \qquad \forall t\in T,\ s=2,\dots,n_S \tag{3}
$$

**Running time from selected speed profile:**

$$
x_{t,s} - y_{t,s-1} \; \text{is replaced by} \quad x_{ts} \ge y_{t,s-1} + \sum_{q\in P_{t,s-1}} \rho_{t,s-1,q}\, p_{t,s-1,q},\quad \forall t,\ s\ge 2 \tag{4}
$$

(For a train that does not stop at $s$, the dwell lower bound in (3) is set to 0.)

**Profile uniqueness:**

$$
\sum_{q\in P_{tl}} p_{tlq} = 1, \qquad \forall t\in T,\ \forall l\in L \tag{5}
$$

**Horizon bounds:**

$$
0 \le x_{ts} \le y_{ts} \le H, \qquad \forall t,\ s \tag{6}
$$

### 4.2 Disruption and rerouting

Track choice is forced onto the opposite track when the original track is blocked:

$$
z_{tl} = 0 \qquad \forall t\in T,\ \forall l\in L^D \text{ such that } [y_{t,l-1},\, x_{t,l}] \subseteq [\underline{t}_D,\bar{t}_D] \tag{7a}
$$

Since containment is data-dependent once times are fixed, this is implemented linearly via big-M: let $b_{tl}\in\{0,1\}$ indicate that train $t$ traverses $l$ within the disruption window:

$$
y_{t,l-1} \ge \underline{t}_D - M(1-b_{tl}), \qquad
x_{tl} \le \bar{t}_D + M(1-b_{tl}), \tag{7b}
$$
$$
y_{t,l-1} \le \underline{t}_D - \epsilon + M\, b_{tl}, \qquad
x_{tl} \ge \bar{t}_D + \epsilon - M(1-b_{tl}) + M\,b_{tl}\ \text{(relaxed alternative branch)}, \tag{7c}
$$
$$
z_{tl} \le 1 - b_{tl}\cdot \mathbb{1}\{l \in L^D,\ \text{original track blocked}\} \tag{7d}
$$

**Simplification (assumption A7, common in the literature):** the disruption is declared at time 0 of the recovery horizon, so every train entering $l\in L^D$ before $\bar{t}_D$ must decide its route; (7) reduces to:
$$
z_{tl} \ge 1 \text{ if } y_{t,l-1} \ge \bar{t}_D, \qquad \text{i.e.,}\quad y_{t,l-1} \le \bar{t}_D + M\, z_{tl} \quad \forall t,\ \forall l\in L^D \tag{7'}
$$
i.e., trains departing after $\bar{t}_D$ ($z_{tl}=1$) use the original track freely; trains departing before must choose $z_{tl}\in\{0,1\}$ (rerouting permitted). If $z_{tl}=0$ (rerouted), the extended running time and extra energy of profiles on the opposite track apply through $P_{tl}$: rerouted profiles have $\tilde{\rho}_{tlq}, \tilde{e}_{tlq}$, linked by:

$$
\sum_q \rho_{tlq}p_{tlq} \le \rho^{0}_{tl} + M(1-z_{tl}), \qquad
\sum_q \rho_{tlq}p_{tlq} \ge \tilde{\rho}^{0}_{tl} - M(1-z_{tl}) \tag{8}
$$

with $\rho^0_{tl}$ ($\tilde{\rho}^0_{tl}$) the minimum running time on the original (opposite) track. *(Alternative cleaner formulation: define profile sets $P_{tl} = P^O_{tl}\cup P^R_{tl}$ with $p_{tlq}$ over the union and constraints $\sum_{q\in P^O}p_{tlq}\le z_{tl}$, $\sum_{q\in P^R}p_{tlq}\le 1-z_{tl}$. We adopt this:)*

$$
\sum_{q\in P^O_{tl}} p_{tlq} \le z_{tl}, \qquad \sum_{q\in P^R_{tl}} p_{tlq} \le 1 - z_{tl}, \qquad \forall t,\ \forall l\in L^D \tag{8'}
$$

### 4.3 Headway and ordering constraints (conflict-free operation)

For each segment $l$ and pair of trains $t<\bar{t}$, if they use the **same track** and the **same direction**, enforce departure headway:

**Case 1 — $t$ precedes $\bar{t}$ on the same track:**
$$
y_{\bar{t},l-1} \ge y_{t,l-1} + \underline{h}^{dep}_l - M(3 - r_{t\bar{t}l} - z_{tl} - z_{\bar{t}l}) - M\,u_{t\bar{t}l}, \tag{9a}
$$

**Case 2 — $\bar{t}$ precedes $t$ (ordering reversed):**
$$
y_{t,l-1} \ge y_{\bar{t},l-1} + \underline{h}^{dep}_l - M(2 - r_{t\bar{t}l} - z_{tl}\cdot z_{\bar{t}l}\text{-term}) - M\,u_{t\bar{t}l}, \tag{9b}
$$

Linearized equivalently (with $o_{t\bar{t}l} = $ same-track-same-direction indicator, linearized via $o_{t\bar{t}l} \ge z_{tl}+z_{\bar{t}l}-1 - u_{t\bar{t}l}$, $o_{t\bar{t}l}\le z_{tl}$, $o_{t\bar{t}l}\le z_{\bar{t}l}$, $o\le 1-u$):

$$
y_{\bar{t},l-1} - y_{t,l-1} \ge \underline{h}^{dep}_l - M(1 - o_{t\bar{t}l}) - M(1 - r_{t\bar{t}l}), \tag{9c}
$$
$$
y_{t,l-1} - y_{\bar{t},l-1} \ge \underline{h}^{dep}_l - M(1 - o_{t\bar{t}l}) - M\, r_{t\bar{t}l}. \tag{9d}
$$

**Arrival headway** (analogously, at the arrival endpoint of segment $l$):
$$
x_{\bar{t}l} - x_{tl} \ge \underline{h}^{arr}_l - M(1-o_{t\bar{t}l}) - M(1-r_{t\bar{t}l}), \tag{10a}
$$
$$
x_{tl} - x_{\bar{t}l} \ge \underline{h}^{arr}_l - M(1-o_{t\bar{t}l}) - M\,r_{t\bar{t}l}. \tag{10b}
$$

**Mixed (bidirectional) headway on rerouted / opposite track:** when trains traverse $l$ in opposite directions sharing one available track ($u_{t\bar{t}l}=1$, at least one rerouted), a train may not enter until the opposing train has cleared:

$$
y_{\bar{t},l-1} \ge x_{tl} + \underline{h}^{mix}_l - M(1 - u_{t\bar{t}l}) - M(1 - r_{t\bar{t}l}), \tag{11a}
$$
$$
y_{t,l-1} \ge x_{\bar{t}l} + \underline{h}^{mix}_l - M(1 - u_{t\bar{t}l}) - M\, r_{t\bar{t}l}. \tag{11b}
$$

**Opposite-direction indicator definition (linearized):** let $g_{tl}\in\{0,1\}$ denote the direction of $t$ on $l$ (fixed data $g^0_{tl}$, rerouting does not change direction — **assumption A8**). Then $u_{t\bar{t}l}=1$ iff $g_{tl}\neq g_{\bar{t}l}$; since directions are fixed, $u_{t\bar{t}l}$ is a constant parameter $u^0_{t\bar{t}l}$. Consequently (11) applies with constant $u^0$.

### 4.4 Variable domains

$$
x_{ts},\ y_{ts},\ \delta_{ts} \in \mathbb{R}_+;\quad
p_{tlq},\ z_{tl},\ r_{t\bar{t}l},\ o_{t\bar{t}l} \in \{0,1\}. \tag{12}
$$

## 5. Summary of the Model

$$
\textbf{MILP-TRSMP:}\quad \min\ (1)\quad \text{s.t. } (2)-(6),\ (7'),\ (8'),\ (9c)-(9d),\ (10a)-(10b),\ (11a)-(11b),\ (12).
$$

**Model properties.**
- The model simultaneously decides: (i) retiming ($x,y$), (ii) reordering ($r$), (iii) local rerouting ($z$), and (iv) speed-profile selection ($p$) — i.e., a fully integrated TRSMP.
- Linearity is preserved because nonlinear train dynamics are embedded in the discrete profile choice (A2): running time and energy are linear in $p$.
- The model is equivalent to the exact integrated problem if the profile library $P_{tl}$ is sufficiently fine (fine-grained discretization of running times / energy levels), which is the basis of the decomposition approach sketched in Section 5 of the referenced work: the MILP decomposes into an IP over train interactions (ordering/routing variables) plus single-train plan-selection subproblems, solvable by adaptive iterative plan refinement with local branching.

**Parameters to instantiate per instance:** timetable $(a,d)$, headway standards, disruption window $(\underline{t}_D,\bar{t}_D)$ and blocked segments $L^D$, per-train profile libraries $(\rho_{tlq}, e_{tlq})$ for both tracks, weights $w_t$, and cost coefficient $\beta$.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## Assumptions
1. A double-track bidirectional corridor with stations s = 1,…,S and segments i = 1,…,S−1; each segment has a normal track N_i and an opposite (reversible) track R_i.
2. During a known disruption window [t0, t1], the normal track of blocked segments B is unavailable; trains may traverse i ∈ B in the window only by rerouting onto R_i (single-track bidirectional operation).
3. Speed profiles are pre-generated and finite: each (train, segment) has a set P_{f,i} of profiles p with running time τ and energy e. Profiles may be valid on the normal track, the reroute track, or both.
4. Trains may be cancelled only if f ∈ F₀; cancellation removes a train from the network via big-M relaxations.
5. Headway Δ is uniform on segments; dwell bounds u^low/u^high apply at intermediate stations; energy of dwelling is neglected; big-M = T (planning horizon).

## Sets
- F trains; I_f ordered segments of train f; B blocked segments, B^N ⊆ B those whose normal track is blocked in direction d_f.
- P_{f,i}: admissible profiles; P^N_{f,i}, P^R_{f,i} ⊆ P_{f,i}: profiles valid on normal / reroute track.

## Parameters
- T, t0, t1, Δ; scheduled times s^dep_{f,s}, s^arr_{f,s}; release time r_f; dwell bounds u^low_{f,s}, u^high_{f,s}; max terminal delay Δ^max_f.
- τ^{p,N}_{f,i}, τ^{p,R}_{f,i}: running times of profile p on the two tracks; e_{f,i,p}: energy of profile p.
- Weights: w^D (delay), w^E (energy), w^C (cancellation), w^R (rerouting).

## Variables
- x^arr_{f,s}, x^dep_{f,s} ≥ 0: actual arrival/departure times.
- y_{f,i,p} ∈ {0,1}: profile selection.
- w_{f,i,p} ∈ {0,1}: auxiliary (linearizes y·z for route-dependent running time).
- z_{f,i} ∈ {0,1}: rerouting on segment i; c_f ∈ {0,1}: cancellation (f ∈ F₀ only).
- σ_{f,i} ∈ {0,1}: disruption-window side switch.
- δ_{fg,i}, h_{fg,i} ∈ {0,1}: precedence and same-track indicators for segment headways.

## Objective
min Z = w^D Σ_f (x^arr_{f,S} − s^arr_{f,S})
      + w^E Σ_f Σ_i Σ_p e_{f,i,p} y_{f,i,p}
      + w^C Σ_f c_f
      + w^R Σ_f Σ_{i∈B} z_{f,i}

## Constraints

**(1) Running time, route-dependent, with cancellation relaxation.** With auxiliary binaries w_{f,i,p} ≤ y_{f,i,p}, w_{f,i,p} ≤ z_{f,i}, w_{f,i,p} ≥ y_{f,i,p} + z_{f,i} − 1:

x^arr_{f,i+1} − x^dep_{f,i} ≥ Σ_p τ^{p,N}_{f,i} y_{f,i,p} − Σ_p τ^{p,N}_{f,i} w_{f,i,p} + Σ_p τ^{p,R}_{f,i} w_{f,i,p} − M c_f
x^arr_{f,i+1} − x^dep_{f,i} ≤ Σ_p τ^{p,N}_{f,i} y_{f,i,p} − Σ_p τ^{p,N}_{f,i} w_{f,i,p} + Σ_p τ^{p,R}_{f,i} w_{f,i,p} + M c_f  ∀f, i

**(2) Dwell bounds (intermediate stations), cancelled trains relaxed:**
x^dep_{f,s} − x^arr_{f,s} ≥ u^low_{f,s} − M c_f
x^dep_{f,s} − x^arr_{f,s} ≤ u^high_{f,s} + M c_f  ∀f, s = 2,…,S−1

**(3) Disruption window — normal track (no partial overlap):** for f, i ∈ B^N with z_{f,i}=0, occupancy [x^dep_{f,i}, x^arr_{f,i+1}] must lie entirely before t0 or entirely after t1:
x^arr_{f,i+1} ≤ t0 + M(σ_{f,i} + z_{f,i})
x^dep_{f,i} ≥ t1 − M(1 − σ_{f,i}) − M z_{f,i}

**(4) Rerouted trains occupy the opposite track entirely within [t0, t1]:**
x^dep_{f,i} ≥ t0 − M(1 − z_{f,i})
x^arr_{f,i+1} ≤ t1 + M(1 − z_{f,i})  ∀f, i ∈ B
(Also z_{f,i} = 0 for i ∉ B and for trains whose normal-direction track remains open.)

**(5) Profile selection and route–profile compatibility:**
Σ_p y_{f,i,p} = 1 − c_f  ∀f, i
y_{f,i,p} ≤ 1 − z_{f,i}  ∀p ∈ P^N_{f,i} \ P^R_{f,i}
y_{f,i,p} ≤ z_{f,i}      ∀p ∈ P^R_{f,i} \ P^N_{f,i}

**(6) Segment headway / precedence.** For each segment i and pair f ≠ g: h_{fg,i} ≥ z_{f,i} − z_{g,i}, h_{fg,i} ≥ z_{g,i} − z_{f,i} (h = 1 iff routing differs). With δ_{fg,i} = 1 meaning f precedes g:

x^dep_{g,i} − x^dep_{f,i} ≥ Δ − M(1 − δ_{fg,i}) − M h_{fg,i}
x^dep_{f,i} − x^dep_{g,i} ≥ Δ − M δ_{fg,i} − M h_{fg,i}

Activation logic: if z_{f,i} ≠ z_{g,i}, h = 1 relaxes both (different tracks, no conflict); if z_{f,i} = z_{g,i}, exactly one ordering constraint is binding via δ. Add analogous arrival-side headway constraints with δ shared. For blocked segments i ∈ B, apply the same pairwise ordering to **all** trains using the shared rerouted track (including opposite-direction rerouted trains), which resolves head-on conflicts by sequencing.

**(7) Origin departure, release, and terminal arrival:**
x^dep_{f,1} ≥ s^dep_{f,1};  x^dep_{f,1} ≥ r_f;  x^arr_{f,S} ≤ s^arr_{f,S} + Δ^max_f + M c_f

**(8) Timing consistency:** x^arr_{f,i+1} ≥ x^dep_{f,i} ∀f, i; all x ≥ 0.

**(9) Domains:** y, w, z, c, σ, δ, h ∈ {0,1}; x^arr, x^dep ≥ 0.

All constraints are linear; the objective balances total delay, traction energy (driving the eco-speed-profile choice), cancellation penalties, and rerouting costs, while constraints (1)–(6) couple timetable feasibility, speed-profile executability, and conflict-free bidirectional operation through the disrupted area.

# TRSMP — MILP Formulation (Equations Only)

**Sets:** trains *i, j ∈ T*; stations *s ∈ S*; segments *s ∈ E* (segment *s* connects stations *s* and *s+1*); speed profiles *p ∈ P_s*; route options *d ∈ {0 (own track), 1 (opposite track)}*.

**Parameters:** scheduled times *A⁰ᵢₛ, D⁰ᵢₛ*; min dwell *dwₛ*; headways *h_dep, h_arr*; disruption window *[t₀, t₁]* on segment *e* blocking direction *dir\**; running time *rt[s][p]* and energy *E[s][p]* of each profile; bounds *rt_min, rt_max*; delay weights *wᵢ*; energy coefficient *α*; cancellation penalty *πᵢ*; horizon/big-M *H*.

## Variables
- *A[i,s], D[i,s] ∈ [0, H]* — actual arrival / departure times (continuous)
- *y[i,s,p] ∈ {0,1}* — speed-profile selection
- *x[i,s,d] ∈ {0,1}* — route (track) selection
- *z[i,j,s] ∈ {0,1}* — order: 1 if train *i* enters segment *s* before *j* (pairs *i<j*)
- *b[i] ∈ {0,1}* — 1 if train *i* passes disrupted segment before *t₀*
- *c[i] ∈ {0,1}* — cancellation indicator
- *delay[i] ≥ 0* — final delay at terminal station

## Objective
Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellation cost:

$$\min \sum_{i} w_i \, delay_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i}\sum_{s}\sum_{p} E[s][p]\, y_{i,s,p} \;+\; \sum_{i} \pi_i c_i$$

## Constraints

**(0) Route choice** — exactly one track per train-segment:
$$\sum_{d} x_{i,s,d} = 1 \quad \forall i, s$$

**(1) Dwell linkage:**
$$D_{i,s} \ge A_{i,s} + dw_s - M c_i, \qquad D_{i,s} \le A_{i,s} + dw_s + M c_i \quad \forall i, s$$

**(2) Running-time consistency** (for each segment *s* traversed by *i*, with arrival station *s⁺*):
$$\sum_{p} y_{i,s,p} = 1$$
$$A_{i,s^+} = D_{i,s} + \sum_{p} rt[s][p]\, y_{i,s,p} \quad (\pm\, M c_i)$$
$$rt_{\min}[s] \le \sum_p rt[s][p]\, y_{i,s,p} \le rt_{\max}[s] \quad (\pm\, M c_i)$$

**(3)–(4) Headway / conflict-free operation** — for every pair *(i, j)* and segment *s*, per track option *d* (constraints active only when both trains use track *d*, via big-M on *x* and *z*):
- if *z[i,j,s] = 1* (i first):
$$D_{j,s} \ge D_{i,s} + h_{dep}, \qquad A_{j,s^+} \ge A_{i,s^+} + h_{arr}$$
- if *z[i,j,s] = 0* (j first): symmetric inequalities with roles swapped.

Big-M form (as coded):
$$D_{j,s} - D_{i,s} - h_{dep} \ge -M(3 - x_{i,s,d} - x_{j,s,d} - z_{i,j,s})$$
$$A_{j,s^+} - A_{i,s^+} - h_{arr} \ge -M(3 - x_{i,s,d} - x_{j,s,d} - z_{i,j,s})$$
and the mirrored pair with *(2 − x_{i,s,d} − x_{j,s,d} + z_{i,j,s})*. This covers both same-direction conflicts and bidirectional conflicts on a shared (opposite) track.

**(5) Disruption window** — for trains *i* of the blocked direction on disrupted segment *e*:
$$D_{i,e} \le t_0 + M(1 - b_i) + M c_i$$
$$A_{i,e^+} \ge t_1 - M b_i - M c_i$$
$$b_i \ge 1 - x_{i,e,0} - c_i$$
i.e., a train on the blocked (normal) track must fully traverse before *t₀* or after *t₁*; rerouting to the opposite track (*x=1*) bypasses the disjunction.

**(6) Delay definition and cancellation:**
$$delay_i \ge A_{i,\text{term}(i)} - A^0_{i,\text{term}(i)} - M c_i, \qquad delay_i \ge 0$$
If *cᵢ = 1*, all timing constraints of train *i* are relaxed (via *±Mcᵢ*) and cost is *πᵢ* instead of delay/energy.

**(7) Horizon and origin readiness:**
$$0 \le A_{i,s}, D_{i,s} \le H \quad \forall i, s; \qquad D_{i,s_0} \ge A^0_{i,s_0}$$

**Assumptions (marked):** single corridor with one track per direction; discrete speed-profile set per segment with precomputed (rt, E) pairs; constant minimum dwell; disruption blocks one direction's track on one segment during *[t₀, t₁]*; opposite-track use permitted during the window with conflicts handled by headway constraints; big-M = horizon *H*; segment occupancy capacity is implied by the headway constraints.
