# MILP for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

Below is a complete MILP formulation inspired by the described problem. Since no numerical data is given, all sets/parameters are symbolic; missing information is filled with explicit assumptions (marked **[A]**).

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **[A1]** A double-track high-speed corridor with ordered stations (blocks) between consecutive stations. Each block has two tracks: the scheduled track and the opposite track.
- **[A2]** A disruption partially blocks **one track** of one or more consecutive blocks during a known time window \([T^{start}, T^{end}]\). Trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track, which then carries **bidirectional** traffic.
- **[A3]** For each train and each block, a finite set of **discrete speed profiles** is available (e.g., generated offline by optimal control / pseudospectral methods), each characterized by its running time and energy consumption. This discretization is what keeps the model linear **[A3, standard in the literature]**.
- **[A4]** Train order on each track segment is a decision (reordering allowed); headway times enforce conflict-freeness.
- **[A5]** Cancellation is permitted at a known penalty cost.
- **[A6]** Rolling stock constraints (turnarounds) are ignored; each train runs its full route or is cancelled.

---

## 2. Sets and indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(T\) | set of trains, \(i \in T\) |
| \(S\) | ordered set of stations, \(s \in S\) |
| \(B = \{1,\dots,|S|-1\}\) | set of blocks (between consecutive stations), \(b \in B\); block \(b\) connects stations \(s(b)\) and \(s(b)+1\) |
| \(K_i\) | set of speed profiles of train \(i\) (per block, indexed \(k\)) |
| \(\mathcal{D}\) | set of disrupted blocks |
| \(R \in \{\mathrm{sch}, \mathrm{opp}\}\) | track choice: scheduled track or opposite track |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| \(a^{sched}_{is}, d^{sched}_{is}\) | scheduled arrival/departure of train \(i\) at station \(s\) |
| \(\tau^{run}_{ikb}\) | running time of train \(i\) in block \(b\) with speed profile \(k\) |
| \(e_{ikb}\) | energy consumption of train \(i\) in block \(b\) with profile \(k\) |
| \(\underline{\tau}^{dwell}_{is}, \overline{\tau}^{dwell}_{is}\) | min/max dwell time of train \(i\) at station \(s\) |
| \(h_{\mathrm{same}}, h_{\mathrm{opp}}\) | headway for same-direction / opposite-direction trains on a track (s) |
| \(\Delta^{max}_{is}\) | maximum allowed arrival delay |
| \(\alpha_i\) | delay weight of train \(i\) (e.g., priority / passengers) |
| \(\beta\) | energy cost coefficient (¥/kWh) |
| \(\gamma_i\) | cancellation penalty of train \(i\) |
| \(M\) | big-M constant (large time value) |
| \([T^{start}, T^{end}]\) | disruption time window |

## 4. Decision variables

| Symbol | Meaning | Domain |
|---|---|---|
| \(a_{is}, d_{is}\) | actual arrival / departure time of train \(i\) at station \(s\) | continuous \(\ge 0\) |
| \(x_{ikb} \in \{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(i\) uses speed profile \(k\) in block \(b\) | binary |
| \(y_{ibr} \in \{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(i\) traverses block \(b\) on track \(r \in \{\mathrm{sch},\mathrm{opp}\}\) | binary |
| \(z_i \in \{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(i\) is **cancelled** | binary |
| \(\delta_{is} \ge 0\) | arrival delay of train \(i\) at station \(s\) | continuous |
| \(\sigma_{i\ell b r} \in \{0,1\}\) | 1 if train \(i\) precedes train \(\ell\) on block \(b\), track \(r\) (ordering variable) | binary |

## 5. Objective function

Minimize weighted total delay plus energy cost plus cancellation penalties:

\[
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \alpha_i \, \delta_{is} \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{b \in B}\sum_{k \in K_i} e_{ikb}\, x_{ikb} \;+\; \sum_{i \in T} \gamma_i z_i
\]

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile selection — exactly one profile per train and block (if not cancelled):**
\[
\sum_{k \in K_i} x_{ikb} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; \forall b \in B
\]

**(C2) Track routing — each non-cancelled train uses exactly one track per block:**
\[
y_{ib,\mathrm{sch}} + y_{ib,\mathrm{opp}} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; \forall b \in B
\]

**(C3) Blockage — scheduled track unusable in disrupted blocks during the window.** A train may use the scheduled track of a disrupted block only if it fully passes before the start or after the end of the disruption:
\[
d_{i,s(b)} \le T^{start} + M(1 - y_{ib,\mathrm{sch}}) \qquad \forall i,\; b \in \mathcal{D}
\]
\[
a_{i,s(b)+1} \ge T^{end} - M(1 - y_{ib,\mathrm{sch}}) \qquad \forall i,\; b \in \mathcal{D}
\]

**(C4) Timetable–speed-profile coupling (running time):** the running time in a block equals that of the chosen profile:
\[
a_{i,s(b)+1} - d_{i,s(b)} = \sum_{k \in K_i} \tau^{run}_{ikb}\, x_{ikb} \qquad \forall i,\; b \in B
\]
*(This constraint aligns timetable times with executable speed profiles — the core of the integration.)*

**(C5) Dwell times:**
\[
d_{is} - a_{is} \ge \underline{\tau}^{dwell}_{is}(1 - z_i) \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S \setminus \{\text{terminals}\}
\]
\[
d_{is} - a_{is} \le \overline{\tau}^{dwell}_{is} + M z_i \qquad \forall i,\; s \in S \setminus \{\text{terminals}\}
\]

**(C6) Delay definition and bounds:**
\[
\delta_{is} \ge a_{is} - a^{sched}_{is} \qquad \forall i,\; s
\]
\[
\delta_{is} \le \Delta^{max}_{is} + M z_i \qquad \forall i,\; s
\]

**(C7) Headway — same direction on a track.** For all train pairs \(i \neq \ell\), blocks \(b\), tracks \(r\), with ordering variable \(\sigma_{i\ell br}\) (1 if \(i\) precedes \(\ell\)):
\[
d_{\ell,s(b)} - d_{i,s(b)} \ge h_{\mathrm{same}} - M(3 - y_{ibr} - y_{\ell br} - \sigma_{i\ell br}) \qquad \forall i<\ell,\, b,\, r
\]
\[
d_{i,s(b)} - d_{\ell,s(b)} \ge h_{\mathrm{same}} - M(2 - y_{ibr} - y_{\ell br} + \sigma_{i\ell br}) \qquad \forall i<\ell,\, b,\, r
\]

**(C8) Headway — opposite directions on the shared opposite track (bidirectional conflicts).** For trains \(i\) (downstream direction) and \(\ell\) (upstream direction) both using the opposite track of block \(b\), their occupancy intervals must not overlap; if \(i\) exits before \(\ell\) enters (\(\sigma_{i\ell b,\mathrm{opp}}=1\)):
\[
a_{\ell,s(b)} - a_{i,s(b)+1} \ge h_{\mathrm{opp}} - M(3 - y_{ib,\mathrm{opp}} - y_{\ell b,\mathrm{opp}} - \sigma_{i\ell b,\mathrm{opp}})
\]
and symmetrically for the reverse ordering:
\[
a_{i,s(b)} - a_{\ell,s(b)+1} \ge h_{\mathrm{opp}} - M(2 - y_{ib,\mathrm{opp}} - y_{\ell b,\mathrm{opp}} + \sigma_{i\ell b,\mathrm{opp}})
\]

**(C9) Consistency of ordering variables (anti-symmetry):**
\[
\sigma_{i\ell br} + \sigma_{\ell i br} = y_{ibr}\, y_{\ell br} \quad \text{(linearized as } \sigma_{i\ell br} + \sigma_{\ell i br} \ge y_{ibr} + y_{\ell br} - 1\text{)}
\]
\[
\sigma_{i\ell br} \le y_{ibr}, \quad \sigma_{i\ell br} \le y_{\ell br} \qquad \forall i<\ell,\, b,\, r
\]

**(C10) Cancellation propagation:** a cancelled train occupies no track and has no profile (already enforced by C1–C2); additionally its times are free:
\[
a_{is}, d_{is} \le M z_i + M(1-z_i) \;\text{— relaxed via } a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0,\; \delta_{is} \le M z_i
\]

**(C11) Variable domains:**
\[
a_{is}, d_{is}, \delta_{is} \ge 0; \quad x_{ikb}, y_{ibr}, z_i, \sigma_{i\ell br} \in \{0,1\}
\]

---

## 7. Remarks

- **Conflict-freeness** is guaranteed by (C7)–(C8); the bidirectional conflicts arising from rerouting onto the opposite track are handled by (C8).
- **Integration of TRP and TSMP** is achieved by (C4), which forces the timetable to be consistent with an executable discrete speed profile, whose energy is priced in the objective.
- The model is a valid MILP; per the paper's contribution, it can be decomposed into a train-interaction IP plus single-train plan subproblems (each plan = a combination of profile, route and times), solved by the adaptive iterative refinement algorithm — the MILP above serves as the exact reference model.

Text:
# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under DTG (ETCS L2) Signalling

An extension of RECIFE-MILP (Pellegrini et al., 2015) with speed-profile options and train- and speed-dependent blocking times.

---

## 1. Assumptions (marked where not given)

- **(A1)** Trains run on a fixed microscopic infrastructure of resources; each resource is either a **TDS/block section** or a **switch**. Switches require fully exclusive occupancy.
- **(A2)** Each train $f$ has a finite set of feasible **speed profile options** per resource (e.g., coasting, partial braking, service braking), precomputed offline. *(Assumption: profile set and times are given as data.)*
- **(A3)** Under DTG, the **blocking time** $b_{f,r,p}$ of train $f$ on resource $r$ with profile $p$ is speed- and train-dependent: it includes the approach distance to the brake indication point (absolute braking distance to the EoA), reaction time, and clearing time. *(Assumption: precomputed as data, linearized via profile selection.)*
- **(A4)** Rescheduling decisions: retiming, reordering, route choice, speed profile choice. No rolling-stock changes.
- **(A5)** Delays are measured at network exit; weights $w_f$ may differ per train.
- **(A6)** Big-$M$ linearization; all times in integer seconds.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | set of trains |
| $R$ | set of track resources (TDS sections and switches) |
| $P_f$ | speed profile options of train $f$ |
| $Y_{f,r}$ | feasible routes (paths) of train $f$ through resource $r$ |
| $A_f,\ D_f$ | planned entry / exit time of train $f$ |
| $\tau_{f,r,p}$ | running time of $f$ on $r$ with profile $p$ |
| $b_{f,r,p}$ | DTG blocking time of $f$ on $r$ with profile $p$ (speed-dependent) |
| $S\subseteq R$ | subset of switch resources |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $w_f$ | delay weight of train $f$ |

## 3. Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{f,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $f$ uses speed profile $p$ |
| $y_{f,\rho}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $f$ uses route $\rho \in Y_{f,r}$ |
| $t^{in}_{f,r},\ t^{out}_{f,r}$ | $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ | entry / exit time of $f$ on $r$ |
| $\bar b_{f,r},\ \bar\tau_{f,r}$ | $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ | realized blocking time / running time (linearized) |
| $\delta_{f,g,r}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if $f$ passes $r$ before $g$ ($f<g$ fixed ordering of indices) |
| $d_f$ | $\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ | exit delay of train $f$ |

## 4. Objective

$$\min \quad Z = \sum_{f \in F} w_f \, d_f$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed profile choice — exactly one profile per train:**
$$\sum_{p \in P_f} x_{f,p} = 1 \qquad \forall f \in F$$

**(C2) Route choice — exactly one route per train–resource pair:**
$$\sum_{\rho \in Y_{f,r}} y_{f,\rho} = 1 \qquad \forall f \in F,\ \forall r \in R$$

**(C3) Linearized realized running and blocking times (DTG enhancement):**
$$\bar\tau_{f,r} = \sum_{p \in P_f} \tau_{f,r,p}\, x_{f,p}, \qquad \bar b_{f,r} = \sum_{p \in P_f} b_{f,r,p}\, x_{f,p} \qquad \forall f \in F,\ \forall r \in R$$

**(C4) Timing consistency within a resource:**
$$t^{out}_{f,r} = t^{in}_{f,r} + \bar\tau_{f,r} \qquad \forall f \in F,\ \forall r \in R$$

**(C5) Entry not before scheduled time:**
$$t^{in}_{f,r} \ge A_f \qquad \forall f \in F,\ \forall r \in R \text{ first on } f\text{'s route}$$

**(C6) Path continuity (linearized on chosen route):**
$$t^{in}_{f,r'} \ge t^{out}_{f,r} - M\,(1 - y_{f,\rho}) \qquad \forall f,\ \forall \rho \in Y_{f,r},\ \forall (r \to r') \in \rho$$

**(C7) DTG blocking-time conflict freedom (core separation constraint).**
The occupancy window of $f$ on $r$ is $[t^{in}_{f,r} - \bar b_{f,r},\ t^{out}_{f,r} + \bar b_{f,r}]$; windows must not overlap:
$$t^{in}_{f,r} - \bar b_{f,r} \ \ge\ t^{out}_{g,r} + \bar b_{g,r} - M\,(1 - \delta_{f,g,r}) \qquad \forall f<g,\ \forall r \in R$$
$$t^{in}_{g,r} - \bar b_{g,r} \ \ge\ t^{out}_{f,r} + \bar b_{f,r} - M\,\delta_{f,g,r} \qquad \forall f<g,\ \forall r \in R$$

**(C8) Switch exclusivity (stricter than TDS):** on switch resources, no overlap of even the pure occupancy intervals (blocking windows already enforced by C7; additionally routes through the same switch are mutually exclusive via C7 on the switch resource itself):
$$t^{in}_{f,r} \ge t^{out}_{g,r} - M(1-\delta_{f,g,r}), \qquad t^{in}_{g,r} \ge t^{out}_{f,r} - M\,\delta_{f,g,r} \qquad \forall f<g,\ \forall r \in S$$

**(C9) Delay definition:**
$$d_f \ge t^{out}_{f,r} - D_f, \qquad d_f \ge 0 \qquad \forall f \in F,\ r = \text{last resource of } f$$

## 6. Model summary

The model is a MILP with binary variables $x_{f,p}, y_{f,\rho}, \delta_{f,g,r}$, integer time variables, and linear constraints C1–C9. The **DTG-specific enhancement** lies in (C3)+(C7): the separation between trains is enforced via blocking-time windows whose length depends on the selected speed profile (through the speed-dependent braking distance to the brake indication point), rather than on fixed multi-block separations as in conventional fixed-block RECIFE-MILP. Switches (C8) are distinguished from plain TDS sections as required by interlocking logic under ETCS L2.

Text:
# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

## Sets and Parameters

- **T**: trains; **S**: stations; **L**: segments (between consecutive stations)
- **K_{tl}**: admissible speed profiles for train *t* on segment *l*, each with running time τ_{tlk} and energy e_{tlk}
- **H**: minimum headway time
- **w_t**: delay weight; **c_t**: cancellation penalty; **α**: energy cost coefficient
- **a^{min/max}_{ts}, d^{min/max}_{ts}**: arrival/departure time-window bounds; **a^{sch}_{ts}**: scheduled arrival
- **δ^{min}_{ts}**: minimum dwell time
- **[T₁^{dis}, T₂^{dis}]**: disruption time window on blocked segment l* (track 1)
- **R_{tl} ∈ {0,1}**: rerouting feasibility of train *t* on segment *l*
- **M**: big-M constant

## Variables

- **a_{ts}, d_{ts} ≥ 0**: actual arrival/departure times (continuous)
- **β_{ts} ≥ 0**: arrival delay at station *s*
- **x_{tt'l} ∈ {0,1}**: 1 if train *t* precedes train *t'* on segment *l* (same track)
- **y_{tl} ∈ {0,1}**: 1 if train *t* is rerouted to the opposite track on segment *l*
- **z_{tlk} ∈ {0,1}**: 1 if train *t* uses speed profile *k* on segment *l*
- **u_t ∈ {0,1}**: 1 if train *t* is cancelled
- **E_t ≥ 0**: energy consumption of train *t*

## Objective

$$\min \; \sum_{t \in T} w_t \sum_{s \in S} \beta_{ts} \;+\; \alpha \sum_{t \in T} E_t \;+\; \sum_{t \in T} c_t u_t$$

(total weighted delay + total energy consumption + cancellation penalties)

## Constraints

**(1) Time windows and delays**
$$a^{min}_{ts}(1-u_t) \le a_{ts} \le a^{max}_{ts}, \qquad d^{min}_{ts}(1-u_t) \le d_{ts} \le d^{max}_{ts}$$
$$\beta_{ts} \ge a_{ts} - a^{sch}_{ts}, \qquad \beta_{ts} \ge 0$$

**(2) Minimum dwell time**
$$d_{ts} - a_{ts} \ge \delta^{min}_{ts}(1-u_t)$$

**(3) Running-time consistency with the selected speed profile** (segment *l* runs from station s₁(l) to s₂(l)):
$$a_{t,s_2(l)} - d_{t,s_1(l)} = \sum_{k \in K_{tl}} \tau_{tlk}\, z_{tlk} \quad \forall t, l$$
$$\sum_{k \in K_{tl}} z_{tlk} = 1 - u_t \quad \forall t, l$$

**(4) Energy consistency**
$$E_t = \sum_{l} \sum_{k \in K_{tl}} e_{tlk}\, z_{tlk} \quad \forall t$$

**(5) Rerouting feasibility**
$$y_{tl} \le R_{tl} \quad \forall t, l$$

**(6) Headway / conflict-free ordering** — for each pair t < t′ on segment *l* on the same track (y_{tl} = y_{t′l}), one of two orderings must hold with minimum headway *H*:

Entry headway:
$$a_{t',s_1(l)} - d_{t,s_1(l)} \ge H - M(1 - x_{tt'l}) - M(y_{tl} + y_{t'l}) - M(u_t + u_{t'})$$
$$a_{t,s_1(l)} - d_{t',s_1(l)} \ge H - M\,x_{tt'l} - M(2 - y_{tl} - y_{t'l}) - M(u_t + u_{t'})$$

Exit headway:
$$a_{t',s_2(l)} - a_{t,s_2(l)} \ge H - M(1 - x_{tt'l}) - M(y_{tl} + y_{t'l}) - M(u_t + u_{t'})$$
$$a_{t,s_2(l)} - a_{t',s_2(l)} \ge H - M\,x_{tt'l} - M(2 - y_{tl} - y_{t'l}) - M(u_t + u_{t'})$$

The big-M terms deactivate the constraints when trains use different tracks (rerouted) or are cancelled, so bidirectional trains sharing the opposite track during the disruption are still coordinated by the same ordering logic.

**(7) Disruption time-window constraint** — no train may occupy the blocked track (track 1 of segment l*) during [T₁^{dis}, T₂^{dis}]. A train occupies track 1 iff y_{tl*} = 0; it must either pass entirely before the window, entirely after, or reroute:
$$a_{t,s_2(l^*)} \le T^{dis}_1 + M(y_{tl^*} + u_t)$$
$$d_{t,s_1(l^*)} \ge T^{dis}_2 - M(y_{tl^*} + u_t)$$

**(8) Cancellation consistency**
$$z_{tlk} \le 1 - u_t, \qquad y_{tl} \le 1 - u_t \quad \forall t, l, k$$

## Key Assumptions (stated where input was implicit)

1. **Speed profiles are discretized**: each train–segment combination has a finite set of pre-computed profiles (τ, e), linearizing the nonlinear train dynamics — this is what keeps the model MILP and links timetable times to control-level feasibility.
2. **Single blocked segment and track**: the disruption blocks one track of segment l* during a single time window; rerouting diverts trains to the opposite track, which then serves bidirectional traffic under the same headway constraints.
3. **Fixed train paths/routes** except for the binary rerouting decision on affected segments (no general re-routing via alternative corridors).
4. **Cancellations** are allowed as a last resort and remove the train from all resource constraints.
5. **Big-M values** should be tightened per instance (e.g., set to the planning horizon length) for tractability; the model can be discretized to integer time slots for a pure-IP reformulation (the basis of the plan-selection decomposition described in the paper).

The model simultaneously decides train times (retiming), orders (reordering), routes (rerouting), service cancellations, and speed profiles, yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable with executable, energy-efficient driving strategies.

Below is the complete MILP formulation of the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under a partial segment blockage, in equation form.

## Sets and Parameters

- **K**: trains, each with fixed direction dir_k ∈ {0,1} (down/up), origin departure time d⁰_k, planned destination arrival A_k, weight w_k, cancellation penalty C_k
- **I = {1,…,n−1}**: segments between stations 1,…,n; segment i connects stations i, i+1
- **I_dis ⊂ I**: disrupted segment(s), blocked on one side during window [t0, t1]
- **P_{ki}**: candidate speed plans for train k on segment i, plan p with running time r_{kip} and energy e_{kip}
- **τ_{ki}**: minimum dwell of train k at station i; **h**: same-direction headway; **h_opp**: opposite-direction headway on shared single track; **M**: big-M constant
- Assumptions (marked): overtaking only at stations; times discretized/integer; speed profiles pre-enumerated as linear interval plans (running time, energy) per segment; trains on the disrupted segment may divert to the opposite track during [t0, t1].

## Decision Variables

- x_{kip} ∈ {0,1}: train k uses speed plan p on segment i
- a_{ki}, d_{ki} ∈ ℤ⁺: arrival / departure time of train k at station i
- y_{ki,dir} ∈ {0,1}: train k occupies track of direction dir on segment i
- c_k ∈ {0,1}: train k is cancelled
- o_{kk'i} ∈ {0,1} (k < k′, same direction): ordering — 1 if k enters before k′ on segment i
- z_{kk'i} ∈ {0,1} (k < k′, opposite directions): antecedence on shared single track — 1 if k passes before k′
- δ_k ≥ 0: final delay of train k

## Objective

Minimize total weighted delay + cancellation cost + energy:

$$\min \sum_{k \in K} w_k \delta_k + \sum_{k \in K} C_k c_k + \alpha \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{p \in P_{ki}} e_{kip}\, x_{kip}$$

## Constraints

**(1) Plan selection** — exactly one speed profile per (train, segment) unless cancelled:
$$\sum_{p \in P_{ki}} x_{kip} = 1 - c_k \quad \forall k, i$$

**(2) Running-time linkage** (timetable aligned with chosen speed profile):
$$a_{k,i+1} \geq d_{ki} + \sum_{p \in P_{ki}} r_{kip}\, x_{kip} \quad \forall k, i$$

**(3) Origin departure:**
$$d_{k1} \geq d^0_k \quad \forall k$$

**(4) Minimum dwell:**
$$d_{ki} \geq a_{ki} + \tau_{ki} \quad \forall k, i < n$$

**(5) Delay definition (linear, early arrivals not penalized):**
$$\delta_k \geq a_{kn} - A_k, \quad \delta_k \geq 0 \quad \forall k$$

**(6) Track assignment** — own-direction track on normal segments; on the disrupted segment exactly one of the two tracks:
$$y_{ki,dir_k} = 1 - c_k \quad \forall k,\ i \neq I_{dis}$$
$$y_{ki,dir_k} + y_{ki,1-dir_k} \geq 1 - c_k \quad \forall k,\ i = I_{dis}$$

**(11) Rerouting restricted to the disruption window** (opposite track only if entering during [t0, t1]):
$$d_{ki} \geq t_0 - M(1 - y_{ki,1-dir_k}) \quad \forall k,\ i = I_{dis}$$
$$d_{ki} \leq t_1 + M(1 - y_{ki,1-dir_k}) \quad \forall k,\ i = I_{dis}$$

**(7) Same-direction headway (disjunctive ordering):**
$$a_{k'i,i+1} \geq d_{ki} + h - M(1 - o_{kk'i}) - M(c_k + c_{k'}) \quad \forall k<k',\ i,\ dir_k = dir_{k'}$$
$$a_{k,i+1} \geq d_{k'i} + h - M\,o_{kk'i} - M(c_k + c_{k'}) \quad \forall k<k',\ i,\ dir_k = dir_{k'}$$

**(9) No overtaking between stations** (ordering consistent on consecutive segments):
$$o_{kk',i+1} \leq o_{kk',i} + M(c_k + c_{k'}) \quad \forall k<k',\ i,\ i+1 \in I$$

**(8) Opposite-direction single-track headway on the disrupted segment** (active only when both trains use the shared track):
$$d_{k'i} \geq a_{k,i+1} + h_{opp} - M(1 - z_{kk'i}) - M(c_k + c_{k'}) - M\big(2 - y_{ki,1-dir_k} - y_{k'i,1-dir_{k'}}\big)$$
$$d_{ki} \geq a_{k',i+1} + h_{opp} - M\,z_{kk'i} - M(c_k + c_{k'}) - M\big(2 - y_{ki,1-dir_k} - y_{k'i,1-dir_{k'}}\big)$$
for all opposite-direction pairs k < k′, i = I_dis.

**(10) Cancellation consistency** (cancelled trains pinned to scheduled times):
$$a_{kn} \leq A_k + M(1 - c_k) \quad \forall k$$
$$d_{ki} \leq a_{ki} + \tau_{ki} + M\,c_k \quad \forall k,\ i$$

All constraints are linear (big-M disjunctions); the model simultaneously determines retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellations, and speed-profile selection, yielding a conflict-free rescheduled timetable with executable speed profiles.

Text:
**Selected model: Model 1** — it is the most complete and self-consistent formulation: it explicitly handles bidirectional crossing conflicts on the shared track (C8), the disruption window on the blocked track (C10), same-direction headways on both the normal and single track (C6, C9), and cleanly deactivates all constraints for cancelled trains.

---

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | set of trains, index $t$ |
| $\mathcal{T}^{up}, \mathcal{T}^{down}$ | trains traveling in up / down direction ($\mathcal{T}=\mathcal{T}^{up}\cup\mathcal{T}^{down}$) |
| $\mathcal{S}=\{1,\dots,n\}$ | stations along the corridor, index $i$ |
| $\mathcal{L}=\{1,\dots,n-1\}$ | segments between consecutive stations, index $l$ (segment $l$ connects stations $l$ and $l+1$) |
| $\mathcal{P}_l$ | discrete set of speed profiles feasible on segment $l$, index $p$ |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | trains affected by the disruption area (those allowed to reroute) |

*Assumptions:* a double-track high-speed corridor with one disrupted segment $l^*$ whose original track is blocked during the window; each train has a precomputed set of feasible speed profiles per segment with fixed running time and energy; minimum dwell and headway parameters are given.

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $d^{arr}_{t,i}$, $d^{dep}_{t,i}$ | scheduled arrival / departure time of train $t$ at station $i$ |
| $w_{t}$ / $c_{t}$ | delay weight / cancellation penalty of train $t$ |
| $r_{l}^{p}$, $e_{l}^{p}$ | running time and energy on segment $l$ under profile $p$ |
| $dt_{i}$ | minimum dwell time at station $i$ |
| $h^{arr},h^{dep},h^{seg}$ | minimum headways: arrivals, departures, segment occupancy |
| $H$ | safety headway on the single (opposite) track used bidirectionally |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $[\tau^{b}_{1},\tau^{b}_{2}]$ | disruption time window |
| $l^*$ | blocked segment (one of its two tracks out of service during the window) |
| $T^{max}$ | maximum allowed delay |
| $\alpha$ | monetary conversion factor for energy |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:** $arr_{t,i}, dep_{t,i}, \Delta_{t,i}\ge 0$ — actual arrival/departure times and arrival delay of train $t$ at station $i$.

**Binary:**
- $y^{p}_{t,l}$: 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $l$
- $x_{t,l^*}$: 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite (single, bidirectional) track on $l^*$ (only for $t\in\mathcal{K}$)
- $o_{uv,l}$: 1 if same-direction train $u$ precedes $v$ on segment $l$
- $b_{uv}$: 1 if up-train $u$ occupies the single track before down-train $v$
- $\gamma_{t}$: 1 if train $t$ is **cancelled**

## 4. Objective Function

$$\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}} w_t\,\Delta_{t,i}}_{\text{weighted delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}} c_t\,\gamma_t}_{\text{cancellation penalties}} \;+\; \underbrace{\alpha\sum_{t\in\mathcal{T}}\sum_{l\in\mathcal{L}}\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_l} e_l^p\, y^p_{t,l}}_{\text{energy consumption}}$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable consistency (dynamics).** $\forall t,l$:
$$arr_{t,l+1} = dep_{t,l} + \sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_l} r_l^p\, y^p_{t,l} + M\,\gamma_t$$

**(C2) Dwell times.** $\forall t,i$: $dep_{t,i} \ge arr_{t,i} + dt_i$ (relaxed by $+M\gamma_t$ when cancelled).

**(C3) Speed profile uniqueness.** $\forall t,l$: $\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_l} y^p_{t,l} = 1-\gamma_t$

**(C4) Delay definition / no early departure.** $\forall t,i$:
$$arr_{t,i} \le d^{arr}_{t,i} + \Delta_{t,i},\qquad \Delta_{t,i}\le T^{max},\qquad dep_{t,i}\ge d^{dep}_{t,i}\ (\text{relaxed if } \gamma_t=1)$$

**(C5) Cancellation forbids activity.** $\forall t,i$: $arr_{t,i},\,dep_{t,i}\le M(1-\gamma_t)$

**(C6) Same-direction segment ordering and headways.** $\forall$ same-direction pairs $u,v$ on $l$:
$$arr_{v,l+1} \ge arr_{u,l+1} + h^{seg} - M(1-o_{uv,l}),\qquad arr_{u,l+1} \ge arr_{v,l+1} + h^{seg} - M\,o_{uv,l}$$
(analogous pairs for departures with $h^{dep}$ and arrivals with $h^{arr}$).

**(C7) Track-choice consistency.** $x_{t,l^*}\le 1-\gamma_t$ for $t\in\mathcal{K}$; $x_{t,l^*}=0$ for $t\notin\mathcal{K}$.

**(C8) Single-track crossing conflicts (bidirectional).** For $u\in\mathcal{T}^{up}\cap\mathcal{K}$, $v\in\mathcal{T}^{down}\cap\mathcal{K}$, with $occ^{start}_t=dep_{t,l^*}$, $occ^{end}_t=arr_{t,l^*+1}$:
$$occ_{u}^{end} \le occ_{v}^{start} - H + M(1-b_{uv}) + M(1-x_{u,l^*}) + M(1-x_{v,l^*})$$
$$occ_{v}^{end} \le occ_{u}^{start} - H + M\,b_{uv} + M(1-x_{u,l^*}) + M(1-x_{v,l^*})$$

**(C9) Same-direction headway on the single track.** For same-direction pairs both with $x=1$: non-overlap constraints as in C8 with headway $H$ (single track admits one train at a time).

**(C10) Disruption window restrictions.** With binaries $\beta^{s}_t,\beta^{e}_t$ (occupancy entirely before/after the window), for trains on the blocked track ($x_{t,l^*}=0$):
$$dep_{t,l^*}\ge \tau^b_2 - M\beta^s_t - M x_{t,l^*},\qquad arr_{t,l^*+1}\le \tau^b_1 + M\beta^e_t + M x_{t,l^*},\qquad \beta^s_t+\beta^e_t \ge 1$$

**(C11) Domains.** $arr,dep,\Delta\ge 0$; $y^p_{t,l}, x_{t,l^*}, o_{uv,l}, b_{uv}, \gamma_t\in\{0,1\}$.

## 6. Explanation

- **Retiming:** $arr,dep$ give the new conflict-free timetable; C4 ties delay minimization to schedule deviation.
- **Reordering:** $o_{uv,l}$ with paired big-M inequalities lets the sequence change on every segment.
- **Rerouting:** $x_{t,l^*}$ lets affected trains bypass the blocked track via the opposite track.
- **Crossing-conflict resolution:** $b_{uv}$ decides which of two opposing trains traverses the single track first (non-overlapping occupancy intervals, enforced only when both reroute).
- **Speed management:** C3 selects exactly one precomputed profile per train/segment; C1 injects its running time into the dynamics, and the objective charges its energy — creating the delay–energy trade-off.
- **Cancellations:** $\gamma_t$ removes a train entirely (C1–C5) at penalty $c_t$.
- **Capacity & safety:** C6, C8, C9 enforce headways in all operating modes; C10 models time-dependent track unavailability, which is precisely the rerouting incentive.

All constraints are linear; the model is a standard MILP solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut.

Text:
**Selected model: Model 1** — it is the most complete and clean formulation: it covers retiming, reordering, rerouting (with correct exemption logic via linearized track-sharing), cancellation, discrete speed-profile selection linked to both running time and energy, and a clear three-term objective. Below is the final model.

---

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Assumptions (marked where not given in the input)
1. Double-track high-speed line divided into ordered segments; partial blockage disables **one track** of segment $s^*$ during window $[t^{start}, t^{end}]$, so single-track (bidirectional) operation applies there.
2. Speed profiles are **precomputed** per train–segment (e.g., via optimal train control / pseudospectral methods), each with running time $\tau_{i,s}^k$ and energy $e_{i,s}^k$ — this keeps the model linear.
3. Cancellations are allowed at a large penalty $C^{canc}$ to guarantee feasibility.
4. Times are integer minutes; headways are constant.

## Sets and Parameters
- $T$: trains; $T^{up}, T^{down}$: direction groups
- $S = \{1,\dots,|S|\}$: ordered segments; $s^*$: blocked segment
- $K_{i,s}$: speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $s$ (running time $\tau_{i,s}^k$, energy $e_{i,s}^k$)
- $h$: min. headway; $h^{arr}, h^{dep}$: arrival/departure headways at stations
- $a_{i,s}^0, d_{i,s}^0$: original scheduled times; $\ell_{i,s}$: min. dwell time
- $\delta_i$: delay weight (priority); $\alpha$: energy weight; $C^{canc}$: cancellation penalty
- $\Delta^{max}$: max allowed delay; $M$: big-M

## Decision Variables
- $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: actual arrival/departure times (**retiming**)
- $y_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled**
- $\sigma_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ (**reordering**)
- $r_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on $s$ (only $s = s^*$)
- $x_{i,s}^k \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $s$ (**speed management**)
- $\Delta_{i,s} \ge 0$: arrival delay of train $i$ at station $s$

## Objective
$$\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} \delta_i \, \Delta_{i,s} \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} e_{i,s}^{k}\, x_{i,s}^{k} \;+\; \sum_{i \in T} \delta_i \, C^{canc}\, y_i$$

Weighted total delay + energy cost + cancellation penalty.

## Constraints

**(1) Speed profile uniqueness and running-time consistency (TRP–TSMP coupling):**
$$\sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} x_{i,s}^{k} = 1 - y_i \qquad \forall i, s$$
$$d_{i,s} + \sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} \tau_{i,s}^{k}\, x_{i,s}^{k} \le a_{i,s+1} \qquad \forall i,\ s = 1,\dots,|S|-1$$

**(2) Minimum dwell time:**
$$a_{i,s} + \ell_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(3) Delay definition and cap:**
$$\Delta_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a_{i,s}^{0}, \qquad \Delta_{i,s} \ge 0, \qquad \Delta_{i,s} \le \Delta^{max}(1 - y_i) \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(4) Cancellation logic (times freed if cancelled):**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1 - y_i) \qquad \forall i, s$$

**(5) Rerouting only on the blocked segment, only within the disruption window:**
$$r_{i,s} = 0 \quad \forall i,\ s \ne s^{*}; \qquad r_{i,s} \le 1 - y_i \quad \forall i, s$$
$$a_{i,s^{*}} \ge t^{start}\, r_{i,s}, \qquad a_{i,s^{*}} \le t^{end} + M(1 - r_{i,s}) \qquad \forall i$$

**(6) Same-direction headway per physical track** (with $b_{i,s} = r_{i,s}$ the physical-track indicator; linearize $u_{ij,s} \ge |b_{i,s} - b_{j,s}|$ via $u_{ij,s} \ge b_{i,s}-b_{j,s}$, $u_{ij,s} \ge b_{j,s}-b_{i,s}$):
$$a_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h - M(1 - \sigma_{ij}) - M\,u_{ij,s} \qquad \forall i < j \text{ (same direction)}$$
$$a_{i,s} \ge d_{j,s} + h - M\,\sigma_{ij} - M\,u_{ij,s} \qquad \forall i < j \text{ (same direction)}$$
(Trains on different physical tracks — one rerouted, one not — are exempt via $u_{ij,s}$.)

**(7) Bidirectional conflict on $s^*$ during disruption (single-track operation):** for $i \in T^{up}$, $j \in T^{down}$ occupying $s^*$:
$$a_{j,s^{*}} \ge d_{i,s^{*}} + h - M(1 - \sigma_{ij}), \qquad a_{i,s^{*}} \ge d_{j,s^{*}} + h - M\,\sigma_{ij}$$

**(8) Station arrival/departure headways:**
$$a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h^{arr} - M(1-\sigma_{ij}), \qquad d_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{dep} - M(1-\sigma_{ij}) \quad \forall i<j,\ s$$
(and symmetric versions with $\sigma_{ij}$).

**(9) Rerouting capacity limit:**
$$\sum_{i \in T} r_{i,s^{*}} \le R^{max}$$

**(10) Domains:**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \Delta_{i,s} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}; \quad x_{i,s}^{k}, y_i, \sigma_{ij}, r_{i,s}, u_{ij,s} \in \{0,1\}$$

## Key modeling features
- **Retiming** via $a, d$; **reordering** via pairwise $\sigma_{ij}$ (precedence is a decision, not fixed); **rerouting** via $r_{i,s}$ restricted to the disruption window on $s^*$; **cancellation** via $y_i$ with penalty.
- **Integration of TRP and TSMP**: constraint (1b) ties the chosen speed profile's running time directly to the timetable, so slower energy-saving profiles free capacity while faster profiles reduce delay — the delay–energy trade-off is resolved by the weighted objective.
- **Conflict-free operation**: (6)–(8) enforce headways; the crucial novelty is that rerouted trains are exempt from same-track checks on their original track (via $u_{ij,s}$) but must be conflict-checked against opposite-direction trains sharing the surviving track (7).
- All constraints are linear (absolute values linearized), yielding a valid MILP solvable by branch-and-bound; the model is the basis for the decomposition into a train-plan selection IP with adaptive plan refinement.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the described paper, we formulate a MILP that decomposes the rtRTMP into **rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling**, using **pair-wise delay variables** (each train's delay is expressed by which other train it waits for), with an optional extension capturing **delay propagation** to guarantee global optimality.

---

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly marked)

- **(A1)** The infrastructure is modeled macroscopically: trains traverse a sequence of block sections; signal details are neglected.
- **(A2)** Each train has a set of feasible routes through the network; each route occupies a known set of resources with fixed running times.
- **(A3)** Primary delays are known at the time of optimization (deterministic, rolling-horizon dispatching).
- **(A4)** Trains cannot overtake except where routes allow it (reordering is modeled via ordering binaries).
- **(A5)** Safety is enforced by minimum headway times on shared resources.
- **(A6)** Delay propagation (cascading waits at subsequent blocks) is optional: omitted in the fast sub-optimal model, included in the global-optimum model via constraint (C10).
- **(A7)** All times are integer (minutes or seconds), enabling linearization.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $i, j$ |
| $R_i$ | set of feasible routes for train $i$, index $r$ |
| $B$ | set of block sections (resources), index $b$ |
| $P_i$ | ordered sequence of blocks on train $i$'s route, index $p$ (position) |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_i^{prim}$ | primary delay of train $i$ |
| $t_{ir}^{run}(p)$ | running time of train $i$ on route $r$, block position $p$ |
| $h_{ij}^{b}$ | minimum headway between trains $i,j$ on block $b$ |
| $a_i^{sched}, s_i^{sched}$ | scheduled arrival / departure (exit) times |
| $M$ | big-M constant (horizon length) |
| $w_i$ | delay weight of train $i$ (e.g., priority) |
| $\tau_i^{min}$ | minimum dwell/halt time of train $i$ at stations |

## 4. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{ir} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $i$ uses route $r$ |
| $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | ordering: 1 if train $i$ passes block $b$ before $j$ (per conflicting block; indexed $y_{ij}^{b}$) |
| $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | pair-wise wait: 1 if train $i$ is delayed because it waits for train $j$ |
| $W_{ij} \ge 0$ | continuous | waiting time of train $i$ caused by train $j$ |
| $D_i \ge 0$ | continuous | total (secondary) delay of train $i$ |
| $t_i^{in} \ge 0$ | continuous | entrance time of train $i$ into the network |
| $t_i^{out} \ge 0$ | continuous | exit time of train $i$ |

---

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total (weighted) delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} w_i \, D_i
$$

---

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Route choice — exactly one route per train:**

$$
\sum_{r \in R_i} x_{ir} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C2) Delay definition — pair-wise decomposition:**

$$
D_i = \sum_{j \in T, j \neq i} W_{ij} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C3) Linking pair-wise wait to wait indicator:**

$$
W_{ij} \le M \, z_{ij} \qquad \forall i \neq j
$$

**(C4) Running time consistency (route-dependent exit time):**

$$
t_i^{out} = t_i^{in} + \sum_{r \in R_i} x_{ir} \sum_{p} t_{ir}^{run}(p) + D_i \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C5) Schedule feasibility at exit:**

$$
t_i^{out} \ge s_i^{sched} + d_i^{prim} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(C6) Headway / conflict resolution on shared blocks.** For each pair $i \neq j$ and each block $b$ used by both (route-dependent activation via $\delta_{ir}^{b} \in \{0,1\}$, with $\delta_{ir}^{b} \le x_{ir}$):

$$
t_j^{in} + \sum_{p \le p_b} t_{jr}^{run}(p) + h_{ij}^{b} \le t_i^{in} + \sum_{p \le p_b} t_{ir}^{run}(p) + M(1 - y_{ji}^{b}) + M(2 - \delta_{ir}^{b} - \delta_{jr}^{b})
$$

$$
t_i^{in} + \sum_{p \le p_b} t_{ir}^{run}(p) + h_{ij}^{b} \le t_j^{in} + \sum_{p \le p_b} t_{jr}^{run}(p) + M y_{ji}^{b} + M(2 - \delta_{ir}^{b} - \delta_{jr}^{b})
$$

i.e., if both trains occupy $b$, ordering variable $y$ enforces a strict sequence with headway.

**(C7) Pair-wise wait consistency with ordering:** if train $i$ yields to $j$ on a conflicting block, $i$ waits for $j$:

$$
z_{ij} \ge y_{ji}^{b} + \delta_{ir}^{b} + \delta_{jr}^{b} - 2 \qquad \forall i \neq j,\; \forall b
$$

**(C8) Waiting time lower bound (delay caused by the blocking train):**

$$
W_{ij} \ge \big(t_j^{in} + \sum_p t_{jr}^{run}(p) + h_{ij}^{b}\big) - \big(t_i^{in} + \sum_p t_{ir}^{run}(p)\big) - M(1 - z_{ij}) \qquad \forall i \neq j
$$

**(C9) Minimum dwell times** at scheduled stops (linear in route choice, analogous to C4).

**(C10) *Optional — delay propagation (global-optimum extension):*** the wait induced on train $i$ propagates to all trains that subsequently wait for $i$:

$$
W_{ki} \ge W_{ij} - M(2 - z_{ki} - z_{ij}) \qquad \forall k, i, j \; (k \neq i \neq j)
$$

This closes the chain $k \to i \to j$, ensuring cascading delays are counted — the condition under which the fast model (C1–C9 only) is sub-optimal.

**(C11) Variable bounds:** $0 \le W_{ij} \le M$, $0 \le D_i \le M$, $t_i^{in}, t_i^{out} \in [0, M]$.

---

## 7. Two-Stage Decomposition (as in the paper)

- **Stage 1 (sub-optimal, fast):** solve the model with constraints (C1)–(C9) only, i.e., rerouting + reordering with pair-wise delays, no propagation. Fix $x_{ir}$ (and optionally $y_{ij}^{b}$).
- **Stage 2 (rescheduling):** with routes (and possibly ordering) fixed, solve the full model including (C10) to obtain exact delays and final timing.
- If the optimality condition holds (no cyclic/cascading wait structure in the Stage-1 solution), Stage 1 already yields the global optimum of the full rtRTMP.

---

## 8. Model Summary

- **Type:** MILP (big-M formulation)
- **Binary variables:** route selection $x_{ir}$, ordering $y_{ij}^{b}$, pair-wise wait $z_{ij}$
- **Continuous variables:** $W_{ij}, D_i, t_i^{in}, t_i^{out}$
- **Objective:** minimize weighted sum of total delays
- **Key feature:** pair-wise delay reformulation reduces integer symmetry versus standard delay variables (cf. Pellegrini et al., 2014), lowering computational cost; optional propagation constraint (C10) restores global optimality.

Below is the complete MILP formulation (equations only), derived from the generated model.

## Sets and Parameters
- I: trains; S: stations 0…S−1; F: segments (segment f connects station f and f+1)
- P: speed profiles per (train, segment), with running time τ[i,f,p] and energy E[i,f,p]
- Scheduled times: ā[i,s], d̄[i,s]; minimum dwell time D[i,s]; minimum headway h
- Disrupted segments F^D with blocked track, disruption window [T_start, T_end]
- Weights: w_s (station delay), w_E (energy), P_r (rerouting penalty), P_c (cancellation penalty); big-M; horizon T

## Variables
- a[i,s], d[i,s] ≥ 0 ∈ [0, T]: actual arrival/departure times
- z[i,f,p] ∈ {0,1}: speed profile p selected for train i on segment f
- r[i,f] ∈ {0,1}: train i rerouted to opposite track on segment f
- w[i,f] ∈ {0,1}: train i occupies segment f during the disruption window
- c[i] ∈ {0,1}: train i cancelled
- u[i,j,f] ∈ {0,1}: train i precedes train j on segment f

## Objective
Minimize total weighted delay + energy + rerouting + cancellation cost:

min Σ_i Σ_s w_s·(a[i,s] − ā[i,s]) + Σ_i Σ_f Σ_p w_E·E[i,f,p]·z[i,f,p] + Σ_i Σ_f P_r·r[i,f] + Σ_i P_c·c[i]

(Delay is nonnegative since constraints force a[i,s] ≥ ā[i,s] for non-cancelled trains.)

## Constraints

**(1) Dwell time** (relaxed if cancelled):
d[i,s] ≥ a[i,s] + D[i,s] − M·c[i]  ∀i,s

**(2) Minimum arrival (delay ≥ 0)**:
a[i,s] ≥ ā[i,s] − M·c[i]  ∀i,s

**(3) Running time from selected profile** (arrival at next station = departure + chosen τ):
a[i,f+1] = d[i,f] + Σ_p τ[i,f,p]·z[i,f,p] + M·c[i]  ∀i,f

**(4) Exactly one speed profile if not cancelled**:
Σ_p z[i,f,p] = 1 − c[i]  ∀i,f

**(5) Rerouting feasibility**:
w[i,f] ≤ r[i,f]  ∀i,f
r[i,f] = 0  ∀i, f ∉ F^D
w[i,f] ≤ 1 − c[i]  ∀i,f

**(6) Disruption window** (entry on blocked track only before T_start or after T_end, unless rerouted):
d[i,f] ≤ T_start + M·(w[i,f] + c[i])  ∀i, f ∈ F^D
d[i,f] ≥ T_end − M·(1 − w[i,f]) − M·c[i]  ∀i, f ∈ F^D

**(7) Headway / conflict-free operation** (pairwise disjunction, same direction or shared track):
a[j,f+1] ≥ d[i,f] + h − M·(1 − u[i,j,f]) − M·c[i] − M·c[j]  ∀i≠j,f
a[i,f+1] ≥ d[j,f] + h − M·u[i,j,f] − M·c[i] − M·c[j]  ∀i≠j,f

**(8) Bidirectional conflicts on rerouted track** (opposite-direction pairs constrained only when both rerouted onto the shared track):
a[j,f+1] ≥ d[i,f] + h − M·(1 − u[i,j,f]) − M·(1 − r[i,f]) − M·(1 − r[j,f]) − M·c[i] − M·c[j]  ∀ opposite-direction i,j, f
a[i,f+1] ≥ d[j,f] + h − M·u[i,j,f] − M·(1 − r[i,f]) − M·(1 − r[j,f]) − M·c[i] − M·c[j]  ∀ opposite-direction i,j, f

**(9) Order consistency across consecutive segments** (no order swap without passing loops):
u[i,j,f] − u[i,j,f+1] ≤ 2 − c[i] − c[j]  ∀i≠j, f
u[i,j,f+1] − u[i,j,f] ≤ 2 − c[i] − c[j]  ∀i≠j, f

**(10) Antisymmetry of ordering**:
u[i,j,f] + u[j,i,f] = 1  ∀i<j, f
u[i,j,f] + u[j,i,f] ≤ 2 − (c[i] + c[j])  ∀i<j, f (relaxed if a train is cancelled)

**(11) Horizon bounds**: 0 ≤ a[i,s], d[i,s] ≤ T ∀i,s (variable domains).

## Assumptions (made where input was unspecified)
- Double-track corridor; disruption blocks one track of a subset of segments during a fixed time window; rerouting to the opposite track is allowed only on disrupted segments.
- Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set per (train, segment) with fixed running time and energy — this keeps the model linear (standard assumption for integrating TSMP into a MILP).
- Cancellation fully relaxes timing, profile, and ordering constraints via big-M terms.
- Minimum headway h is uniform across segments and directions; train order may not change between consecutive segments (no overtaking except at stations).

Text:
# MILP Model: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor consists of stations $S = \{1,\dots,n\}$ connected by segments $L = \{1,\dots,n-1\}$. Each segment $l$ has two tracks: track $u \in \{1,2\}$, where track 1 is the scheduled (up/down) direction track and track 2 the opposite track. A partial blockage affects segment $l^*$: one track of $l^*$ is unavailable during disruption window $[T_d, T_r]$. Trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track of $l^*$ during the window, subject to bidirectional conflict avoidance.

**Sets and parameters**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $K$ | set of trains, $k \in K$ |
| $S_k \subseteq S$ | ordered stations served by train $k$ |
| $L_k \subseteq L$ | segments traversed by train $k$ |
| $a_{k,i}, d_{k,i}$ | scheduled arrival / departure of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $\underline{r}_{kl}, \bar{r}_{kl}$ | min / max running time of train $k$ on segment $l$ |
| $\underline{w}_{ki}$ | minimum dwell time of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $h$ | headway time between trains on the same track (assumed uniform) |
| $E_{kl}^{p}$ | energy consumption of train $k$ on segment $l$ using discrete speed profile $p \in P_{kl}$ (precomputed from the train dynamics; **assumption**: profiles are discretized a priori, each with running time $r_{kl}^{p}$, $r_{kl}^{p}\in[\underline{r}_{kl},\bar{r}_{kl}]$) |
| $c^{can}$ | penalty cost of cancelling a train service |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $T^{max}$ | planning horizon end |

**Assumptions (explicit):**
1. Speed profiles are pre-generated per (train, segment) by solving the single-train TSMP; the MILP selects among them (linearizes the nonlinear dynamics).
2. A train occupies a track exclusively; headway $h$ applies between consecutive entries/exit times.
3. Cancellation is allowed only before the train's first departure.
4. Disruption window $[T_d, T_r]$ on segment $l^*$ is known and fixed.
5. Energy cost is linear in profile selection; delay cost is linear in arrival deviations.

## 2. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{k,i},\, d_{k,i}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | actual arrival / departure time |
| $x_{kl}^{p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $k$ uses profile $p$ on segment $l$ |
| $y_{kl}^{u}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $k$ traverses segment $l$ on track $u$ |
| $z_k$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $k$ is cancelled |
| $o_{kl}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | ordering variable: 1 if train $k$ passes segment $l$ before train $k'$ (for $k<k'$) |
| $D_{k,i}^{+}, D_{k,i}^{-}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | positive / negative arrival delay at station $i$ |

## 3. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay, energy consumption, and cancellation cost:

$$
\min \; Z = \underbrace{\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{i\in S_k} \alpha_{k,i}\left(D_{k,i}^{+}+D_{k,i}^{-}\right)}_{\text{passenger delay}}
+ \underbrace{\beta \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{l\in L_k}\sum_{p\in P_{kl}} E_{kl}^{p}\, x_{kl}^{p}}_{\text{energy consumption}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{k\in K} c^{can} z_k}_{\text{cancellations}}
$$

with weights $\alpha_{k,i}$ (delay weight, e.g., passengers on board) and $\beta$ (energy-to-time conversion factor).

## 4. Constraints

**(C1) Delay definition (arrival deviation from schedule):**
$$
a_{k,i} - a^{sched}_{k,i} = D_{k,i}^{+} - D_{k,i}^{-} \qquad \forall k\in K,\; i\in S_k
$$

**(C2) Running time via selected speed profile:**
$$
d_{k,i} + \sum_{p\in P_{kl}} r_{kl}^{p}\, x_{kl}^{p} = a_{k,i'} \qquad \forall k\in K,\; l=(i,i')\in L_k
$$

**(C3) Profile uniqueness:**
$$
\sum_{p\in P_{kl}} x_{kl}^{p} = 1 - z_k \qquad \forall k\in K,\; l\in L_k
$$

**(C4) Dwell time:**
$$
d_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i} + \underline{w}_{ki} \qquad \forall k\in K,\; i\in S_k \setminus\{\text{terminus}\}
$$

**(C5) Track assignment (rerouting on blocked segment):**
$$
\sum_{u\in\{1,2\}} y_{kl}^{u} = 1 - z_k \qquad \forall k\in K,\; l\in L_k
$$

**(C6) Rerouting restricted to disruption window and blocked segment:** Trains may use the opposite track ($u=2$) only on the blocked segment $l^*$ and only if the segment entry time $t^{in}_{kl}$ (entry = departure at upstream station $i$, exit = arrival at downstream station $i'$) lies within the window; otherwise the blocked track is unusable:

$$
t^{in}_{kl^*} \le T_d \;\Rightarrow\; y_{kl^*}^{2}=0 \quad\text{and}\quad t^{in}_{kl^*} \ge T_r \;\Rightarrow\; y_{kl^*}^{2}=0
$$

Linearized (with entry time variable $t^{in}_{kl} = d_{k,i}$ for $l=(i,i')$):
$$
y_{kl^*}^{2} \le \frac{t^{in}_{kl^*} - T_d}{M} + \frac{T_r - t^{in}_{kl^*}}{M} + \dots
$$
implemented via standard indicator/big-M binaries $\delta^{early}_{k}, \delta^{late}_{k}$:
$$
t^{in}_{kl^*} \le T_d + M(1-\delta^{early}_{k}), \qquad
t^{in}_{kl^*} \ge T_r - M(1-\delta^{late}_{k}), \qquad
y_{kl^*}^{2} \le \delta^{early}_{k} + \delta^{late}_{k}
$$

**(C7) Bidirectional conflict-free operation on each track of each segment.** For all trains $k<k'$ both using track $u$ of segment $l$ (i.e., $y_{kl}^{u}=y_{k'l}^{u}=1$), either $k$ exits before $k'$ enters plus headway, or vice versa:

$$
a_{k,i'} + h \le d_{k',i} + M\,(3 - y_{kl}^{u} - y_{k'l}^{u} - o_{kk',l}) \qquad \forall k<k',\, l,\, u
$$
$$
a_{k',i'} + h \le d_{k,i} + M\,(2 - y_{kl}^{u} - y_{k'l}^{u} + o_{kk',l}) \qquad \forall k<k',\, l,\, u
$$

If both trains use different tracks, both constraints are relaxed by the big-M terms.

**(C8) Cancellation consistency:** if train $k$ is cancelled, all its times are free/irrelevant; otherwise times within horizon:
$$
a_{k,i},\, d_{k,i} \le T^{max} + M z_k \qquad \forall k,\, i
$$
$$
d_{k,i} \ge a_{k,i} - M z_k \qquad \forall k,\, i
$$

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{k,i}, d_{k,i}, D_{k,i}^{+}, D_{k,i}^{-} \ge 0; \quad x_{kl}^{p}, y_{kl}^{u}, z_k, o_{kk',l}, \delta \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 5. Remarks

- **Coupling of TRP and TSMP:** Constraint (C2) ties timetable times directly to the selected speed profile, so the rescheduled timetable is executable at the train-control level by construction, and (C3)–(C5) link profile choice, routing, and cancellation.
- **Rerouting:** (C6) permits use of the opposite track only on the blocked segment within the window; (C7) then guarantees conflict-free bidirectional sharing of that track.
- **Equivalence note:** With a sufficiently fine discretization of profile set $P_{kl}$ (fine interval plans), this MILP is equivalent to the fully integrated nonlinear TRSMP, since the single-train speed profile Pareto frontier (running time vs. energy) is approximated arbitrarily well.
- **Solution approach:** The model can be decomposed into an IP over train interactions (ordering and routing variables $o$, $y$, $z$) and per-train plan selection ($x$, times), solved by an adaptive iterative plan-refinement algorithm with local branching, as the plan sets $P_{kl}$ grow combinatorially.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

Below is the complete linear model (equations only), based on the generated formulation. Assumptions are marked where information was missing.

## Sets and Parameters
- **I**: trains; each with direction d(i) ∈ {up, down}, priority weight w_i, cancellation penalty C_i, scheduled times schedArr_{i,s}, schedDep_{i,s}
- **S**: stations; **A**: segments (s, s+1); disrupted segment a* with blocked track during window [T_start, T_end]
- **P_{i,a}**: discrete speed profiles p with running time r_{i,a,p} and energy e_{i,a,p} (precomputed from train dynamics — *assumption: linearization via discrete profiles*)
- H: planning horizon; M = H (big-M); D_min: minimum dwell; h_min: minimum headway; Δ: occupancy interval length; λ: energy weight

## Variables
- t^arr_{i,s}, t^dep_{i,s} ≥ 0: actual arrival/departure times (0 ≤ t ≤ H)
- y_{i,a,p} ∈ {0,1}: speed profile selection
- z_{i,a} ∈ {0,1}: rerouting to opposite track on segment a
- c_i ∈ {0,1}: cancellation of train i
- o_{i,j,s} ∈ {0,1}: ordering (i before j at station/segment s)
- u_{i,a,k} ∈ {0,1}: occupancy of opposite track of a during interval k

## Objective
Minimize total weighted delay + energy + cancellation cost:

min Σ_i w_i · Σ_s [(t^arr_{i,s} − schedArr_{i,s}) + (t^dep_{i,s} − schedDep_{i,s})] + λ · Σ_{i,a,p} e_{i,a,p} · y_{i,a,p} + Σ_i C_i · c_i

## Constraints

**(1) Running-time consistency** (for consecutive stations s, s+1 with segment a):
t^arr_{i,s+1} = t^dep_{i,s} + Σ_p r_{i,a,p} · y_{i,a,p}

**(2) Exactly one profile unless cancelled:**
Σ_p y_{i,a,p} = 1 − c_i  ∀ i, a

**(3) Minimum dwell time:**
t^dep_{i,s} ≥ t^arr_{i,s} + D_min  ∀ i, s (not terminal)

**(4) Rerouting restricted to disrupted segment:**
z_{i,a} = 0  ∀ a ≠ a*

**(5) Rerouting only within disruption window** (big-M, s_in = entry station of a*):
t^dep_{i,s_in} ≥ T_start − M(1 − z_{i,a*})
t^dep_{i,s_in} ≤ T_end + M(1 − z_{i,a*})

**(6) Non-rerouted trains avoid blocked track during window** (enter before T_start or after T_end):
t^dep_{i,s_in} ≤ T_start + M(z_{i,a*} + c_i)
t^dep_{i,s_in} ≥ T_end − M(1 − z_{i,a*}) − M·c_i

**(7) Conflict freedom on same track (same direction, pairwise ordering with headway):**
t^arr_{i,s_in} + h_min − M(1 − o_{i,j,a}) ≤ t^arr_{j,s_in}
t^arr_{j,s_in} + h_min − M·o_{i,j,a} ≤ t^arr_{i,s_in}

**(8) Single-track bidirectional capacity on rerouted track** (interval occupancy):
Σ_i u_{i,a,k} ≤ 1  ∀ a, k
with linking constraints u_{i,a*,k} ≥ 1 − (t^dep_{i,s_in} − kΔ)/Δ − (1 − z_{i,a*}) and u_{i,a*,k} ≤ 1 − (kΔ − t^arr_{i,s_out})/H + c_i

**(9) Cancellation zeroes all times:**
t^arr_{i,s} ≤ M(1 − c_i),  t^dep_{i,s} ≤ M(1 − c_i)  ∀ i, s

**(10) Earliest departure / horizon:**
t^dep_{i,s₀} ≥ schedDep_{i,s₀} − M·c_i (origin); 0 ≤ t ≤ H (bounds)

**(11) Ordering consistency (no overtaking between stations):**
o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} = 1  ∀ i < j, s
o_{i,j,s} ≤ o_{i,j,s'} + (1 − c_i)  for consecutive stations s, s' on train i's route

## Key Assumptions (marked)
- Speed profiles are precomputed discrete alternatives (running time, energy) from train dynamics — this linearizes the nonlinear train-motion coupling.
- Rerouting is only possible on the disrupted segment a*, using the opposite track, only within [T_start, T_end].
- The rerouted track is single-track bidirectional: at most one train occupies it per time interval.
- No overtaking between consecutive stations (ordering consistency), unless station tracks allow it (simplification).
- Big-M = horizon length H; delays measured as deviations from scheduled times; energy weighted by λ.

Text:
Below is the final MILP model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under a partial segment blockage.

# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management MILP

## 1. Sets

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $K$ | set of trains, index $k,l$ |
| $S$ | ordered corridor segments, index $s$ (segment $s$ connects stations $s$ and $s+1$) |
| $P^k_s$ | feasible speed profiles of train $k$ on segment $s$, index $p$ |
| $D \subseteq S$ | disrupted segments (normal track blocked during $[t_0,t_1]$) |
| $K^+, K^-$ | trains in the two directions, $K = K^+ \cup K^-$ |
| $KL$ | unordered train pairs $\{k,l\}$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a^k_s, d^k_s$ | scheduled arrival/departure of train $k$ at stations $s$, $s+1$ |
| $r^k_{s,p}$, $e_{k,s,p}$ | running time and energy of profile $p$ of train $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $dw^k_s$ | minimum dwell time at station $s+1$ |
| $h^{kl}_s$ | minimum headway between trains $k,l$ on segment $s$ |
| $[t_0,t_1]$ | disruption time window |
| $\bar z^{kl}_s$ | planned order (1 if $k$ precedes $l$) |
| $c_{del}, c_{en}, c_{can}, c_{dev}$ | weights: delay, energy, cancellation, order deviation |
| $\Delta^k_{\max}$ | maximum allowed delay of train $k$ |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant (≥ planning horizon) |

## 3. Variables

- $A^k_s, D^k_s \ge 0$: actual arrival/departure of train $k$ at stations $s$, $s+1$. Derived shorthand used consistently: $E^k_s := D^k_s$ (segment entry), $X^k_s := A^k_{s+1}$ (segment exit).
- $x^k_{s,p} \in \{0,1\}$: profile selection
- $c^k \in \{0,1\}$: cancellation
- $y^k_s \in \{0,1\}$, $s\in D$: rerouting to the opposite track; $u^k_s = 1 - y^k_s$ (track-usage indicator)
- $\beta0^k_s, \beta1^k_s, b0^k_s, b1^k_s \in \{0,1\}$: disruption-window position binaries
- $z^{kl}_s \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if $k$ precedes $l$ on segment $s$; $w^{kl}_s \in \{0,1\}$: bidirectional meet selector
- $g^{kl}_s \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if $k,l$ use different physical tracks (relaxes conflicts)
- $o^{kl}_s \ge 0$: order deviation; $\delta^k \ge 0$: terminal delay of train $k$

## 4. Objective

$$\min \; c_{del}\sum_{k}\delta^k \;+\; c_{en}\sum_{k}\sum_{s}\sum_{p} e_{k,s,p}\, x^k_{s,p} \;+\; c_{can}\sum_{k} c^k \;+\; c_{dev}\sum_{(k,l)}\sum_{s} o^{kl}_s$$

## 5. Constraints

**Timetable & speed-profile coupling**

(C1) Exactly one profile, deactivated if cancelled:
$$\sum_{p\in P^k_s} x^k_{s,p} = 1 - c^k \qquad \forall k, s$$

(C2) Running-time linking (two-sided big-M relaxation for cancellations):
$$A^k_{s+1} \ge D^k_s + \sum_p r^k_{s,p} x^k_{s,p} - M c^k, \qquad A^k_{s+1} \le D^k_s + \sum_p r^k_{s,p} x^k_{s,p} + M c^k$$

(C3) Minimum dwell, relaxed if cancelled:
$$D^k_{s+1} \ge A^k_{s+1} + dw^k_s - M c^k$$

**Delay & initial condition**

(C4) $A^k_1 \ge a^k_1 - M c^k$, $\quad A^k_1 \le a^k_1 + \Delta^k_{\max} + M c^k$ (origin departure anchored to schedule, bounded delay)

(C5) Delay definition, neutralized for cancelled trains:
$$\delta^k \ge A^k_{S} - a^k_{S} - M c^k, \qquad \delta^k \ge 0$$

**Rerouting & disruption window ($s\in D$)**

(C6) $u^k_s = 1 - y^k_s$

(C7) Blocked-track exclusion — a non-rerouted, non-cancelled train's occupancy $[D^k_s, A^k_{s+1}]$ must lie entirely before $t_0$ or entirely after $t_1$:
$$D^k_s \le t_0 + M(1-\beta0^k_s), \qquad A^k_{s+1} \ge t_1 - M(1-\beta1^k_s), \qquad \beta0^k_s + \beta1^k_s \ge 1 - y^k_s - c^k$$

(C8) Rerouting eligibility — rerouting allowed only if occupancy intersects $[t_0,t_1]$:
$$A^k_{s+1} \le t_0 + M(1-b0^k_s), \qquad D^k_s \ge t_1 - M(1-b1^k_s), \qquad b0^k_s + b1^k_s \le 1$$
$$y^k_s \le 1 - b0^k_s + c^k, \qquad y^k_s \le 1 - b1^k_s + c^k$$

**Headways (same direction) — disjunctive big-M, entry and exit separation**

For same-direction pairs, with $M g^{kl}_s$ relaxing when trains use different physical tracks and $M(c^k+c^l)$ for cancellations:

(C9) Entry separation:
$$A^l_s \ge A^k_s + h^{kl}_s - M(1-z^{kl}_s) - M g^{kl}_s - M(c^k+c^l)$$
$$A^k_s \ge A^l_s + h^{kl}_s - M z^{kl}_s - M g^{kl}_s - M(c^k+c^l)$$

(C10) Exit separation:
$$A^l_{s+1} \ge A^k_{s+1} + h^{kl}_s - M(1-z^{kl}_s) - M g^{kl}_s - M(c^k+c^l)$$
$$A^k_{s+1} \ge A^l_{s+1} + h^{kl}_s - M z^{kl}_s - M g^{kl}_s - M(c^k+c^l)$$

**Bidirectional conflicts (opposite directions, same physical track)**

(C7a–b) If $u^k_s = u^l_s$ ($g^{kl}_s=0$), one train may enter only after the other has cleared:
$$A^k_s \ge A^l_{s+1} - M\big(w^{kl}_s + g^{kl}_s + c^k + c^l\big)$$
$$A^l_s \ge A^k_{s+1} - M\big(1 - w^{kl}_s + g^{kl}_s + c^k + c^l\big)$$

(C7c) Track-coincidence linearization $g^{kl}_s \ge |u^k_s - u^l_s|$:
$$g^{kl}_s \ge u^k_s - u^l_s, \qquad g^{kl}_s \ge u^l_s - u^k_s \qquad \forall k\in K^+, l\in K^-, s\in D$$

**Order variables**

(C11) Symmetry: $z^{kl}_s + z^{lk}_s = 1$

(C12) Order consistency across consecutive segments (no mid-corridor order reversal; relaxed for cancellations):
$$z^{kl}_{s+1} \ge z^{kl}_s - c^k - c^l$$

(C13) Order-deviation linearization:
$$o^{kl}_s \ge z^{kl}_s - \bar z^{kl}_s, \qquad o^{kl}_s \ge \bar z^{kl}_s - z^{kl}_s$$

(C14) Domains: $A^k_s, D^k_s, \delta^k, o^{kl}_s \ge 0$; all remaining variables binary.

## 6. Assumptions

1. Speed profiles are precomputed from train dynamics with fixed running time and energy (ensures linearity).
2. Each disrupted segment has a normal track and an opposite track; rerouted trains use the opposite track and are exempt from the blocked-track exclusion.
3. Occupancy of a segment is the interval $[D^k_s, A^k_{s+1}]$; one train occupies a track at a time; overtaking only at stations.
4. Cancelled trains are released from all timing/resource constraints via $Mc^k$ terms and penalized by $c_{can}c^k$; their delay $\delta^k$ is forced to zero.
5. $M$ exceeds any feasible time difference; headways are uniform per pair-segment.
6. The disruption window $[t_0,t_1]$ is known and fixed.

The model is a valid MILP: continuous timing variables ($A, D, \delta, o$), binary assignment/ordering/rerouting/cancellation variables ($x, c, y, z, w, g, \beta, b$), and a linear objective jointly minimizing delay, energy, cancellations and order deviation — capturing retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation and speed-profile selection simultaneously.

Text:
# MILP Model: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Feasibility

We present a combined model consisting of (A) a **rolling stock composition model** (based on Fioole et al., 2006) and (B) an **infrastructure feasibility model** (based on Van Aken et al., 2017), connected via **combinatorial Benders cuts**.

---

## A. Rolling Stock Composition Model

### Sets and indices
- $S$: stations; $T$: train trips in the (timetabled) timetable, indexed $t$; ordered by time.
- $K$: train unit types, indexed $k$ (e.g., VIRM-4, ICM-3), with:
  - $c_k$: number of carriages of type $k$
  - $CAP_k$: number of seats of type $k$
  - $IN_k, OUT_k$: units of type $k$ available at start/end of the day
- $A$: shunting activities (park/unpark at a station), indexed $a$.

### Decision variables
- $x_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $k$ in the composition of trip $t$.
- $y_{t} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is **cancelled**, 0 otherwise.
- $d_t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$ (minutes): additional delay of trip $t$ (bounded, e.g. $0 \le d_t \le D^{max}$, $D^{max}=5$ assumed).
- $z_{t}^{dep}, z_{t}^{arr} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units coupled to / decoupled from trip $t$ at its endpoint station (composition change).
- $s_{i,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $k$ on shunting activity $a$ at station $i$.
- $e_{i,k}^{start}, e_{i,k}^{end} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: units of type $k$ present at station $i$ at start/end of the planning horizon.

### Parameters
- $q_t$: required seat capacity on trip $t$ (estimated from expected demand; **assumption**).
- $M_t \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: maximum composition length (carriages) on trip $t$ (platform/track length limit).
- $\pi_{kt'}$: compatibility: type $k$ can be succeeded by type $k'$ on a turnaround ($=1$ if same carriage count or allowed transition).
- $o_t, d_t^{stat}$: origin and destination station of trip $t$; $\tau_t$: scheduled duration.
- $w^{canc}, w^{delay}, w^{car}, w^{shunt}, w^{dev}$: objective weights (operational cost, passenger cost, capital cost, shunting cost, deviation-from-plan cost).

### Objective function
$$
\min \; \sum_{t \in T} \Big( w^{canc} y_t + w^{delay} d_t + w^{car} \sum_{k \in K} c_k x_{t,k} \Big)
+ w^{shunt} \sum_{a \in A} \sum_{k \in K} s_{a,k}
+ w^{dev} \sum_{t \in T} \sum_{k \in K} |x_{t,k} - \bar{x}_{t,k}|
$$
where $\bar{x}_{t,k}$ is the original (pre-disruption) composition. Linearize $|x_{t,k}-\bar x_{t,k}|$ with auxiliary variables $u_{t,k} \ge x_{t,k}-\bar x_{t,k}$, $u_{t,k} \ge \bar x_{t,k}-x_{t,k}$.

### Constraints

**(1) Seat capacity** (cancelled trips require no capacity):
$$
\sum_{k \in K} CAP_k \, x_{t,k} \;\ge\; q_t (1 - y_t) \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(2) Composition length limit:**
$$
\sum_{k \in K} c_k x_{t,k} \;\le\; M_t (1-y_t) \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(3) Composition change consistency** (units entering minus leaving a trip equal couplings/decouplings):
$$
x_{t,k} - x_{t',k} = z_{t}^{dep} - z_{t}^{arr}, \quad \text{for consecutive trips } t' \text{ following } t \text{ (turnaround)}
$$
More precisely, for each station $i$ and each pair of trips $t$ (arriving at $i$) and $t'$ (departing from $i$, $t'$ succeeds $t$ in the circulation):
$$
x_{t,k} - x_{t',k} \;\le\; z_{t}^{arr} \cdot \mathbb{1}[\text{type change allowed}], \qquad \forall k
$$
implemented in standard form:
$$
\sum_{k} c_k (x_{t,k} - x_{t',k}) \le \sum_k c_k z_t^{arr}, \qquad
\sum_{k} c_k (x_{t',k} - x_{t,k}) \le \sum_k c_k z_{t'}^{dep}
$$

**(4) Flow conservation per station and time point** (units arriving + stored = units departing + stored):
$$
e_{i,k}^{start} + \sum_{t: \, d^{stat}_t = i} x_{t,k} + \sum_{a \in A: \, i(a)=i} s_{a,k}
=
e_{i,k}^{end} + \sum_{t: \, o_t = i} x_{t,k} + \sum_{a \in A: \, i(a)=i} s_{a,k}
\qquad \forall i \in S, \forall k
$$
(with appropriate time-ordering of the sums over trips; standard time-space network formulation).

**(5) Fleet size:**
$$
\sum_{i \in S} e_{i,k}^{start} \;\le\; IN_k, \qquad \sum_{i \in S} e_{i,k}^{end} \;\le\; OUT_k \qquad \forall k \in K
$$

**(6) Delay bounds:**
$$
0 \le d_t \le D^{max}(1 - y_t) \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(7) Shunting feasibility (Benders master cuts):** let $Sh$ be the set of proposed shunting movements, and let $\Omega \subseteq Sh$ be infeasible subsets identified by the infrastructure model. With binary $v_a = 1$ if shunting movement $a$ is performed ($v_a = 1 \Leftrightarrow \sum_k s_{a,k} \ge 1$):
$$
\sum_{a \in \Omega} v_a \;\le\; |\Omega| - 1 \qquad \forall \Omega \in \mathcal{O}
$$
where $\mathcal{O}$ is the set of infeasible shunting combinations found so far.

---

## B. Infrastructure Feasibility Model (subproblem)

Given a proposed rolling stock plan (hence fixed shunting movements $a \in Sh$ with proposed times), check whether a conflict-free path exists on the track network of the considered stations (Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal).

### Sets
- $R$: railway tracks (routes) through a station, indexed $r$.
- $E$: train events (arrivals/departures of passenger trips, shunting movements), indexed $e$.
- $P_r$: ordered set of positions/time slots on route $r$ (time–space graph arcs).

### Variables
- $\sigma_e \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: scheduled time shift (delay) of event $e$.
- $f_{e,r,p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if event $e$ occupies route $r$ at position $p$.
- $g_{e,e',r} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable: 1 if event $e$ uses route $r$ before event $e'$.

### Constraints
**(8) Each event gets exactly one route/position:**
$$
\sum_{r \in R} \sum_{p \in P_r} f_{e,r,p} = 1 \qquad \forall e \in E
$$

**(9) Route occupation (no two events on same track segment at same time):**
$$
f_{e,r,p} + f_{e',r,p} \le 1 \qquad \forall e \ne e', \, \forall r, p
$$

**(10) Disjunctive ordering on shared routes:**
$$
\sigma_{e'} - \sigma_{e} \ge \Delta_{e,r} - M(1 - g_{e,e',r}), \qquad
\sigma_{e} - \sigma_{e'} \ge \Delta_{e',r} - M \, g_{e,e',r}
$$
for events $e,e'$ requiring the same route $r$, where $\Delta_{e,r}$ is the minimum headway/occupation time.

**(11) Delay limits:** $\sigma_e \le D^{max}$ for all events; $\sigma_e = 0$ for fixed (non-delayable) trains.

**(12) Shunting time windows:** each shunting movement $a$ must start within its prescribed window $[L_a, U_a]$:
$$
L_a \le \sigma_a \le U_a
$$

**Output:** If feasible → plan accepted. If infeasible → an infeasible subset $\Omega$ of simultaneously requested shunting movements is identified and cut (7) is added; iterate.

---

## Assumptions (explicitly marked)
1. **Demand**: seat requirements $q_t$ are deterministic estimates of passenger demand.
2. **Delays**: delays are limited to $D^{max} = 5$ minutes and absorbed by timetable buffers (as stated in the paper).
3. **Turnaround compatibility**: only units with compatible carriage counts may succeed each other ($\pi$ matrix given).
4. **Shunting duration** and headways $\Delta_{e,r}$ are deterministic and known.
5. **Infrastructure** is only capacity-constrained at Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal; elsewhere shunting is assumed feasible.
6. The objective weights $w$ reflect the trade-off between cancellations, delays, carriage-kilometres, shunting effort, and deviation from the original plan; deviation is minimized to ease night-time repositioning and preserve familiarity for passengers and crew.

The full problem is solved by the Combinatorial Benders scheme: solve (A), check (B), add cuts (7), repeat until the master solution is infrastructure-feasible (exact) or process shunting movements sequentially (iterative heuristic variant).

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices
- **I** — trains, indexed by $i, j$
- **S** — segments, indexed by $s$; segment $s^*$ is the disrupted one (one track blocked during $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$)
- **R_s** — routes on segment $s$: for $s \neq s^*$: $\{r^{norm}\}$; for $s^*$: $\{r^{norm}, r^{opp}\}$ (opposite track usable as detour)
- **P_i** — feasible speed profiles of train $i$ (each with fixed running time and energy)
- **D** — pairs $(i,j)$ with opposite travel directions; **I²** — unordered pairs $i<j$

## 2. Parameters
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T_{start}, T_{end}$ | disruption time window |
| $\tau_{i,s,p}$, $w_{i,s,p}$ | running time / dwell of profile $p$ of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $E_{i,s,p}$ | energy consumption of profile $p$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway on segments |
| $E_i, L_i, L_i^{late}, A_i^{arr}$ | earliest departure, scheduled departure, latest arrival, scheduled destination arrival |
| $c^{delay}, c^{canc}, c^{reroute}, c^{energy}$ | cost coefficients |
| $\delta_{i,p}$ | rerouting/deviation cost (0 for normal-route profiles) |
| $M$ | big-M, larger than any feasible time difference |
| $\bar{B}$ | max number of trains allowed on the opposite track (optional) |

## 3. Variables
- $u_{i,s}, v_{i,s} \ge 0$: entry/exit time of train $i$ on segment $s$ (headway reference $a_{i,s} := v_{i,s}$)
- $d_i \ge 0$: destination delay of train $i$
- $y_{i,s,r,p} \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ traverses segment $s$ with route $r$ and profile $p$
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled
- $\beta_i \in \{0,1\}$: normal-track traversal of $s^*$ before ($=1$) or after ($=0$) the window
- $b_i, n_i \in \{0,1\}$: train $i$ rerouted to $r^{opp}$ / uses $r^{norm}$ on $s^*$
- $o_{ij,s,r} \in \{0,1\}$: per-route ordering of $i,j$ on segment $s$
- $o^B_{ij}, o^N_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering of opposite-direction pair on the shared track
- $q_{ij,s,r} \in [0,1]$: same-track indicator

## 4. Objective
$$
\min \; c^{delay}\sum_i d_i + c^{canc}\sum_i z_i + c^{reroute}\sum_{i,s,r,p}\delta_{i,p}\, y_{i,s,r,p} + c^{energy}\sum_{i,s,r,p} E_{i,s,p}\, y_{i,s,r,p}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**C1 — Assignment/cancellation:**
$$\sum_{r\in R_s}\sum_{p\in P_i} y_{i,s,r,p} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s$$

**C2 — Timetable–profile coupling and chaining:**
$$v_{i,s} = u_{i,s} + \sum_{r,p}(\tau_{i,s,p}+w_{i,s,p})\, y_{i,s,r,p} \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s$$
$$u_{i,s+1} = v_{i,s} \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s < |S|$$

**C3 — Time windows:**
$$u_{i,1} \ge E_i + M z_i, \quad v_{i,|S|} \le L_i^{late} + M z_i \qquad \forall i$$

**C4 — Delay definition:**
$$d_i \ge v_{i,|S|} - A_i^{arr}, \quad d_i \ge 0 \qquad \forall i$$

**C5 — Rerouting window (opposite track fully inside $[T_{start}, T_{end}]$):**
$$u_{i,s^*} \ge T_{start} - M\Big(1-\sum_p y_{i,s^*,r^{opp},p}\Big) \qquad \forall i$$
$$v_{i,s^*} \le T_{end} + M\Big(1-\sum_p y_{i,s^*,r^{opp},p}\Big) \qquad \forall i$$

**C6 — Blocked track unusable during window (before-or-after disjunction):**
$$v_{i,s^*} \le T_{start} + M(1-\beta_i) + M\Big(1-\sum_p y_{i,s^*,r^{norm},p}\Big) + M z_i \qquad \forall i$$
$$u_{i,s^*} \ge T_{end} - M\beta_i + M\Big(1-\sum_p y_{i,s^*,r^{norm},p}\Big) - M z_i \qquad \forall i$$

**C7 — Same-track headway (per route, relaxed across tracks):**
$$q_{ij,s,r} \ge \sum_p y_{i,s,r,p} + \sum_p y_{j,s,r,p} - 1 \qquad \forall (i,j)\in I^2,\ \forall s,\ \forall r$$
$$a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h - M(1-o_{ij,s,r}) - M(1-q_{ij,s,r}) - M(z_i+z_j) \qquad \forall (i,j),\ s,\ r$$
$$a_{i,s} \ge a_{j,s} + h - M\, o_{ij,s,r} - M(1-q_{ij,s,r}) - M(z_i+z_j) \qquad \forall (i,j),\ s,\ r$$

**C8 — Bidirectional conflict on shared opposite track (only if both rerouted):**
$$b_i \ge \sum_p y_{i,s^*,r^{opp},p} \qquad \forall i$$
$$v_{j,s^*} \le u_{i,s^*} + M(1-o^B_{ij}) + M(2-b_i-b_j) \qquad \forall (i,j)\in D$$
$$v_{i,s^*} \le u_{j,s^*} + M\, o^B_{ij} + M(2-b_i-b_j) \qquad \forall (i,j)\in D$$

**C12 — Analogous mutual exclusion on the normal track of $s^*$:**
$$n_i \ge \sum_p y_{i,s^*,r^{norm},p}, \quad n_i \in \{0,1\}$$
$$v_{j,s^*} \le u_{i,s^*} + M(1-o^N_{ij}) + M(2-n_i-n_j) \qquad \forall (i,j)\in D$$
$$v_{i,s^*} \le u_{j,s^*} + M\, o^N_{ij} + M(2-n_i-n_j) \qquad \forall (i,j)\in D$$

**C13 — Reroute limit (optional):** $\sum_i b_i \le \bar{B}$

**Domains:** $u, v, d \ge 0$; $y, z, \beta, b, n, o_{ij,s,r}, o^B_{ij}, o^N_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$; $0 \le q_{ij,s,r} \le 1$.

## 6. Assumptions
1. Each non-cancelled train traverses each segment exactly once with exactly one (route, profile) combination.
2. Speed profiles are pre-enumerated with fixed running times and energy — this discretization keeps the train-dynamics coupling linear.
3. Station dwell is folded into profile parameters; station track assignment is fixed to the scheduled one (ordering handled analogously to C7 if needed).
4. Cancellation ($z_i=1$) deactivates all timing/routing constraints of the train via big-M terms.
5. Trains on the opposite track must traverse $s^*$ entirely within the disruption window; trains on the blocked normal track must avoid the window entirely.
6. Big-M exceeds any feasible time difference; $q$ may be continuous since it only appears in relaxing big-M terms.

The model is fully linear and simultaneously decides **retiming** ($u, v$), **reordering** ($o$-variables), **rerouting** ($y$ route dimension), **speed profiles** ($y$ profile dimension), and **cancellations** ($z$), minimizing delay, cancellation, rerouting, and energy costs.

Text:
Here is the final MILP model for the integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under partial segment blockage:

---

# MILP for the TRSMP

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Set | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | trains, index $i$ |
| $J$ | track segments (blocks), index $j$ |
| $S$ | stations, index $s$ |
| $P_{i,j}$ | precomputed speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $j$, index $p$ |
| $J_i \subseteq J$ | segments traversed by train $i$ (in order) |
| $S_i \subseteq S$ | stations at which train $i$ stops |
| $\mathcal{M}$ | maintenance (disruption) windows $m=[a_m,b_m]$ on affected segments |

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $r_{i,j,p}$, $e_{i,j,p}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ for train $i$ on segment $j$ |
| $w^{\min}_{i,s}, w^{\max}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{seg}, h^{plat}, h^{opp}$ | headways on segments, platforms, and opposite-direction meets |
| $T^{arr}_i, T^{dep}_i$ | scheduled arrival (destination) / departure (origin) times |
| $\alpha^{arr}_i, \alpha^{dep}_i$ | delay weights |
| $\pi_i$ | cancellation penalty |
| $\gamma$ | energy cost coefficient |
| $\Delta^{\max}_i$ | maximum allowed delay |
| $M$ | big-M (horizon length; pairwise tightened values may replace it) |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $\tau^{in}_{i,j}, \tau^{out}_{i,j}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | entry (= departure from upstream station) / exit (= arrival at downstream station) time on segment $j$ |
| $\tau^{arr}_{i,s}, \tau^{dep}_{i,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | arrival / departure at station $s$ |
| $z_{i,j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the **opposite** (rerouted) track on segment $j$ |
| $x_{i,j,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ runs speed profile $p$ on segment $j$ |
| $c_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\Delta^{arr}_i, \Delta^{dep}_i$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ | arrival / departure delays |
| $y^{seg}_{ik,j}, y^{plat}_{ik}, y^{opp}_{ik,j}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | ordering binaries (1 if $i$ precedes $k$) |
| $u^{before}_{i,m}, u^{after}_{i,m}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | occupancy entirely before / after disruption window $m$ |

## 4. Objective

$$
\min\; Z=\sum_i\Big(\alpha^{arr}_i\Delta^{arr}_i+\alpha^{dep}_i\Delta^{dep}_i+\pi_i c_i\Big)
\;+\;\gamma\sum_i\sum_{j\in J_i}\sum_{p\in P_{i,j}} e_{i,j,p}\,x_{i,j,p}
$$

Weighted delays + cancellation penalties + energy consumption.

## 5. Constraints

**C1 — Profile selection** (exactly one profile unless cancelled):
$$\sum_{p\in P_{i,j}} x_{i,j,p}=1-c_i\qquad\forall i,\ \forall j\in J_i$$

**C2 — Minimum running time** (en-route holding allowed; use $=$ to forbid holding):
$$\tau^{out}_{i,j}\ \ge\ \tau^{in}_{i,j}+\sum_p r_{i,j,p}\,x_{i,j,p}-M c_i\qquad\forall i,\ j\in J_i$$

**C3 — τ-linkage with station times.** Normal track:
$$\tau^{in}_{i,j}=\tau^{dep}_{i,s^{up}(j)},\qquad \tau^{out}_{i,j}=\tau^{arr}_{i,s^{dn}(j)}$$
Opposite track ($z_{i,j}=1$, big-M equality, relaxed by $c_i$):
$$\tau^{in}_{i,j}=\tau^{dep}_{i,s^{dn}(j)},\qquad \tau^{out}_{i,j}=\tau^{arr}_{i,s^{up}(j)}$$

**C4 — Dwell times:**
$$w^{\min}_{i,s}-Mc_i\ \le\ \tau^{dep}_{i,s}-\tau^{arr}_{i,s}\ \le\ w^{\max}_{i,s}+Mc_i\qquad\forall i,\ s\in S_i$$

**C5 — Delays:**
$$\Delta^{arr}_i\ge\tau^{arr}_{i,s^{end}_i}-T^{arr}_i,\qquad \Delta^{dep}_i\ge\tau^{dep}_{i,s^{org}_i}-T^{dep}_i$$
$$\Delta^{arr}_i,\Delta^{dep}_i\ \le\ \Delta^{\max}_i(1-c_i)$$

**C6 — Disruption window avoidance** (before, after, or reroute):
$$u^{before}_{i,m}+u^{after}_{i,m}+z_{i,j}\ \ge\ 1-c_i$$
$$\tau^{out}_{i,j}\ \le\ a_m+M\big(1-u^{before}_{i,m}\big),\qquad \tau^{in}_{i,j}\ \ge\ b_m-M\big(1-u^{after}_{i,m}\big)$$

**C7 — Platform headways** (for trains $i,k$ at the same platform):
$$\tau^{dep}_{k,s}+h^{plat}\le\tau^{arr}_{i,s}+M\big(3-y^{plat}_{ik}-(1-c_i)-(1-c_k)\big)$$
$$\tau^{dep}_{i,s}+h^{plat}\le\tau^{arr}_{k,s}+M\big(2+y^{plat}_{ik}-(1-c_i)-(1-c_k)\big)$$

**C8 — Segment conflicts.** Same direction, same track:
$$\tau^{out}_{k,j}+h^{seg}\le\tau^{in}_{i,j}+M\big(3-y^{seg}_{ik,j}-(1-c_i)-(1-c_k)\big)$$
$$\tau^{out}_{i,j}+h^{seg}\le\tau^{in}_{k,j}+M\big(2+y^{seg}_{ik,j}-(1-c_i)-(1-c_k)\big)$$
Opposite-direction meets on a shared (rerouted) track — analogous with $h^{opp}$ and $y^{opp}_{ik,j}$. These apply to all pairs sharing a track; pairs on different tracks are exempt via the $z$-relaxation terms.

**C9 — Order consistency along the route** (no overtaking within segments; relaxed if cancelled):
$$y^{seg}_{ik,j}\ge y^{seg}_{ik,j'}-c_i-c_k,\qquad y^{seg}_{ik,j'}\ge y^{seg}_{ik,j}-c_i-c_k$$

**C10 — Domains:** all $\tau,\Delta\ge0$; all $x,z,c,y,u\in\{0,1\}$.

## 6. Key Modeling Points

- **Retiming** via continuous $\tau$ variables; **reordering** via big-M disjunctions with ordering binaries; **rerouting** via $z_{i,j}$ (opposite track allowed only on affected segments during the window, enforced by C6); **cancellation** via $c_i$, which relaxes all operational constraints at penalty $\pi_i$.
- **Speed management** is the discrete profile choice $x_{i,j,p}$: slower profiles save energy but lengthen running times, creating delays and conflicts — the objective trades these off linearly.
- **Bidirectional conflicts** on the shared opposite track are handled by C8/C8′, ensuring conflict-free operation of opposite-direction trains during partial blockage.
- The model is fully linear and is the MILP that the paper's decomposition (IP over train interactions + per-train plans) is equivalent to when the profile set is sufficiently fine.
