# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

Based on the described framework (Pellegrini et al. 2014-style formulation, extended with pair-wise delay variables and optional delay propagation), the following complete MILP is proposed.

---

## 1. Assumptions

*(A1)* The infrastructure is modeled macroscopically: the network is a set of resources (block sections / routes through stations); signal details are neglected.
*(A2)* Each train has a set of feasible routes per station; exactly one route per train–station is selected.
*(A3)* Trains cannot overtake except where routes allow it; ordering is a decision variable.
*(A4)* Primary delays are known inputs (from the disturbed timetable); only secondary delays are optimized.
*(A5)* Safety is enforced by minimum headway times between trains occupying the same resource.
*(A6)* The planning horizon is finite (e.g., 1–2 hours); all times are integer (minutes or seconds).
*(A7)* Safety-relevant overlap margins (Lindenmaier et al., 2022) are treated as part of the resource occupation time of the route.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $S$ | set of resources (block sections / station routes groups), indexed $r$ |
| $R_i$ | set of feasible routes for train $i$, indexed $k$ |
| $R_{ir} \subseteq R_i$ | routes of train $i$ using resource $r$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_i$ | scheduled entrance time of train $i$ into the area |
| $d_i$ | scheduled exit time of train $i$ |
| $p_i$ | primary delay of train $i$ (input disturbance) |
| $t_{ik}$ | free-flow running time of train $i$ on route $k$ |
| $h_{ij}^{r}$ | minimum headway between trains $i$ and $j$ on resource $r$ |
| $M$ | big-M (horizon length) |
| $w$ | minimum waiting time before departure after a preceding train (dwell/propagation parameter) |

## 4. Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x_{ik} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses route $k$ |
| $y_{ij}^{r} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses resource $r$ **before** train $j$ (ordering variable) |
| $e_i \ge 0$ | entrance (arrival) time of train $i$ into the network |
| $d'_i \ge 0$ | exit (departure) time of train $i$ |
| $\beta_i \ge 0$ | total secondary delay of train $i$ |
| $z_{ij} \ge 0$ | **pair-wise delay**: time train $j$ waits because of train $i$ (pair-wise interpretation of delay) |

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize total (secondary) delay:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} \beta_i
$$

with the pair-wise decomposition of delay propagation:

$$
\beta_i = \sum_{j \in T} z_{ji} \qquad \forall i \in T \quad \text{(linking constraint, see C5)}
$$

## 6. Constraints

**C1 — Route selection (exactly one route per train):**
$$
\sum_{k \in R_i} x_{ik} = 1 \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**C2 — Entrance time with primary delay:**
$$
e_i \ge a_i + p_i \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**C3 — Running time depends on chosen route:**
$$
d'_i \ge e_i + \sum_{k \in R_i} t_{ik} x_{ik} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**C4 — Pair-wise delay definition (train $j$ waits for train $i$ if $i$ goes first on a shared resource):**
$$
z_{ij} \ge e_j - e_i - \sum_{k \in R_i} t_{ik} x_{ik} - M(1 - y_{ij}^{r}) \qquad \forall (i,j), \; \forall r: R_{ir} \cap R_{jr} \neq \emptyset
$$
$$
z_{ij} \ge e_i - e_j - \sum_{k \in R_j} t_{jk} x_{jk} - M \, y_{ij}^{r} \qquad \forall (i,j), \; \forall r: R_{ir} \cap R_{jr} \neq \emptyset
$$

**C5 — Delay propagation (secondary delay = own primary delay + waiting caused by others):**
$$
\beta_i \ge p_i + \sum_{j \in T, j \neq i} z_{ji} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**C6 — Headway / conflict-free ordering on shared resources:**
$$
e_j \ge e_i + \sum_{k \in R_i} t_{ik} x_{ik} + h_{ij}^{r} - M(1 - y_{ij}^{r}) \qquad \forall (i,j), \forall r \in S
$$
$$
e_i \ge e_j + \sum_{k \in R_j} t_{jk} x_{jk} + h_{ji}^{r} - M \, y_{ij}^{r} \qquad \forall (i,j), \forall r \in S
$$

**C7 — Consistency of ordering variables across shared resources (FIFO-relaxation / transitivity):**
$$
y_{ij}^{r} + y_{ji}^{r} = 1 \qquad \forall (i,j), \forall r: R_{ir} \cap R_{jr} \neq \emptyset
$$

**C8 — Horizon bounds:**
$$
d'_i \le a_i + M \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**C9 — Variable domains:**
$$
x_{ik} \in \{0,1\}, \quad y_{ij}^{r} \in \{0,1\}, \quad e_i, d'_i, \beta_i, z_{ij} \ge 0
$$

---

## 7. Two-Stage Decomposition (as in the paper)

**Stage 1 (Sub-optimal model):** Solve the MILP above **without C5** (delay propagation neglected). This yields exact route selection $x^*_{ik}$ and ordering $y^{*r}_{ij}$ quickly — the rerouting + reordering sub-problem.

**Stage 2 (Rescheduling):** Fix $x_{ik} = x^*_{ik}$, optionally fix $y_{ij}^{r} = y^{*r}_{ij}$, and solve the full model (with C5) to obtain the final conflict-free timetable minimizing total delay.

**Global-optimum variant:** Solving the full model (C1–C9) in one stage guarantees the global optimum of the original rtRTMP, at higher computational cost; the optimality condition for Stage 1 being exact is that no train's pair-wise wait propagates further (i.e., $z_{ji}$ chains are absent).

---

## 8. Optional Extension: Safety-Relevant Overlaps

Following Lindenmaier et al. (2022), extend occupation times by the overlap margin $o_{ik}$ behind stop signals:

$$
d'_i \ge e_i + \sum_{k \in R_i} (t_{ik} + o_{ik}) x_{ik} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

and replace $t_{ik}$ with $t_{ik} + o_{ik}$ in C4 and C6. This yields the complete extended rtRTMP model with rerouting, reordering, and rescheduling in a single linear formulation.

---

# TRSMP MILP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Assumptions

- **A1.** Continuous time; planning horizon $[0,H]$; big-$M = 2H$ (all time variables lie in $[0,H]$, so differences never exceed $H < M$).
- **A2.** Speed profiles are precomputed offline from train dynamics: for each train $k$ and segment $i$, a discrete set $P_{k,i}$ with running time $r_{k,i,p}$ and energy $e_{k,i,p}$ — this keeps the model linear.
- **A3.** Segment $i$ of train $k$ runs from station $l_o(i,k)$ to $l_d(i,k)$; segment entry/exit times are identified with timetable variables: $e_{k,i} := d_{k,l_o(i,k)}$, $q_{k,i} := a_{k,l_d(i,k)}$.
- **A4.** Disruption: on blocked segments, one track $\bar b$ is unavailable during window $[\underline{t}_{k,i}, \overline{t}_{k,i}]$; affected trains may be **rerouted** to the opposite track. Traversal is non-splitting (one track per full segment traversal) — marked assumption (7a).
- **A5.** Reference (undisrupted) timetable $a^0_{k,l}, d^0_{k,l}$; maximum allowed delay $D_{\max}$.
- **A6.** Headway $h$ per segment/track; $h^S$ per platform.
- **A7.** Cancellation is complete: a cancelled train consumes no resources and its times are frozen at schedule.

## 2. Sets and indices

$K$: trains; $I$: segments; $L$: stations; $B_i$: tracks of segment $i$; $S_l$: platforms at station $l$; $P_{k,i}$: speed profiles; $\mathcal{B}$: (train, segment) pairs with disruption window; $\mathcal{K}_2 = \{(k,k'): k<k'\}$.

## 3. Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{k,l}, d_{k,l}$ | $[0,H]$ | arrival / departure of train $k$ at station $l$ |
| $\Delta^a_{k,l}, \Delta^d_{k,l}$ | $[0,D_{\max}]$ | arrival / departure delays |
| $y_{k,i,p}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | speed-profile selection |
| $x_{k,i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | train $k$ uses track $b$ on segment $i$ |
| $u_{k,i}, v_{k,i}, w_{k,i}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | disruption-overlap indicators |
| $o_{k,k',i,b}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | ordering on segment/track ($k<k'$) |
| $o^S_{k,l,s}, \sigma_{k,k',l,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | platform assignment / ordering |
| $z_k$ | $\{0,1\}$ | cancellation |

## 4. Objective

$$\min \;\; \pi^a \sum_{k,l} \Delta^a_{k,l} + \pi^d \sum_{k,l} \Delta^d_{k,l} + \pi^e \sum_{k,i,p} e_{k,i,p}\, y_{k,i,p} + \sum_k \Pi_k z_k$$

(weighted total delay + energy + cancellation penalties)

## 5. Constraints

**(1) Dwell and platform occupancy:**
$$d_{k,l} \ge a_{k,l} + \tau_{k,l} \qquad \forall k,l \tag{1}$$
$$e^S_{k,l} = d_{k,l}, \quad q^S_{k,l} = a_{k,l} \qquad \forall k,l \tag{1'}$$

**(2) Speed-profile selection and segment running time (linear: $r$ is a coefficient of binary $y$):**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{k,i}} y_{k,i,p} = 1 - z_k \qquad \forall k,i \tag{2}$$
$$q_{k,i} = e_{k,i} + \sum_{p \in P_{k,i}} r_{k,i,p}\, y_{k,i,p} \qquad \forall k,i \tag{3}$$

**(3) Delays:**
$$\Delta^a_{k,l} \ge a_{k,l} - a^0_{k,l}, \quad \Delta^d_{k,l} \ge d_{k,l} - d^0_{k,l} \qquad \forall k,l \tag{4}$$
$$\Delta^a_{k,l}, \Delta^d_{k,l} \le D_{\max}(1 - z_k) \qquad \forall k,l \tag{5}$$

**(4) Cancellation freezing (two-sided big-M):**
$$a^0_{k,l} - M z_k \le a_{k,l} \le a^0_{k,l} + M z_k, \qquad d^0_{k,l} - M z_k \le d_{k,l} \le d^0_{k,l} + M z_k \tag{6}$$

**(5) Disruption-overlap logic (exact, two-sided big-M with $\varepsilon$):** $u_{k,i}=1$ iff the train enters segment $i$ before $T_{end}$; $v_{k,i}=1$ iff it exits after $T_{start}$; $w = u \wedge v$ iff the traversal overlaps the window:
$$e_{k,i} \le \overline{t}_{k,i} + M(1 - u_{k,i}), \qquad e_{k,i} \ge \overline{t}_{k,i} + \varepsilon - M u_{k,i} \tag{7a}$$
$$q_{k,i} \ge \underline{t}_{k,i} - M(1 - v_{k,i}), \qquad q_{k,i} \le \underline{t}_{k,i} - \varepsilon + M v_{k,i} \tag{7b}$$
$$w_{k,i} \ge u_{k,i} + v_{k,i} - 1, \qquad w_{k,i} \le u_{k,i}, \qquad w_{k,i} \le v_{k,i} \tag{7c}$$
$$w_{k,i} \le 1 - z_k \tag{7d}$$

**(6) Blocked-track prohibition (now correctly activated):**
$$x_{k,i,\bar b} \le 1 - w_{k,i} \qquad \forall (k,i) \in \mathcal{B} \tag{8}$$

**(6a) Optional strengthening (assumption 7a):** if split usage is forbidden (a train must traverse the segment entirely inside or entirely outside the window), add straddle indicators $\tilde w_{k,i}$ with $\tilde w \ge u' + v' - 1$ ($u'$: $e \le \underline{t}$, $v'$: $q \ge \overline{t}$) and $\tilde w_{k,i} \le 1 - x_{k,i,\bar b}$.

**(7) Track selection / rerouting:**
$$\sum_{b \in B_i} x_{k,i,b} = 1 - z_k \qquad \forall k,i \tag{8'}$$

**(8) Segment headway (conflict-free, corrected big-M):** for each pair $k<k'$, segment $i$, track $b$:
$$e_{k',i} \ge q_{k,i} + h - M(1 - o_{k,k',i,b}) - M(1 - x_{k,i,b}) - M(1 - x_{k',i,b}) - M z_k - M z_{k'} \tag{9a}$$
$$e_{k,i} \ge q_{k',i} + h - M\, o_{k,k',i,b} - M(1 - x_{k,i,b}) - M(1 - x_{k',i,b}) - M z_k - M z_{k'} \tag{9b}$$

Active only when both trains use track $b$ and neither is cancelled; $o=1$ enforces $k$ before $k'$, $o=0$ the reverse — this is where **bidirectional conflicts on the shared open track** are resolved.

**(9) Platform capacity:** assignment and pairwise ordering:
$$\sum_{s \in S_l} o^S_{k,l,s} = 1 - z_k \qquad \forall k,l \tag{10a}$$
$$q^S_{k,l} \ge e^S_{k,l} + \tau_{k,l} - M(1 - o^S_{k,l,s}) \qquad \forall k,l,s \tag{10b}$$
$$e^S_{k',l} \ge q^S_{k,l} + h^S - M(1-\sigma) - M(1-o^S_{k,l,s}) - M(1-o^S_{k',l,s}) - M z_k - M z_{k'} \tag{10c}$$
$$e^S_{k,l} \ge q^S_{k',l} + h^S - M\,\sigma - M(1-o^S_{k,l,s}) - M(1-o^S_{k',l,s}) - M z_k - M z_{k'} \tag{10d}$$

**(9) Domains:** $a, d, e^S, q^S, e, q \in [0,H]$; $\Delta \in [0, D_{\max}]$; $y, x, u, v, w, o, o^S, \sigma, z \in \{0,1\}$.

## 6. Key modeling points

- **Integration of TRP and TSMP:** retiming/reordering/rerouting/cancellation (variables $a, d, o, x, z$) and speed management (variables $y$) are decided jointly; the chosen profile's running time directly determines arrivals, and its energy enters the objective — capturing the trade-off between accelerating to arrive earlier (more energy, possible waiting due to conflicts) and decelerating to match recovery times.
- **Disruption handling:** the exact $u,v,w$ logic ensures a train occupying a blocked segment during $[\underline{t},\overline{t}]$ must be on the open track; trains may instead wait and use the blocked track after $T_{end}$.
- **Linearity:** all train dynamics are embedded in precomputed profile coefficients; all disjunctions use standard big-M with $M = 2H$.

This MILP yields a conflict-free rescheduled timetable together with executable speed profiles, and is solvable by standard branch-and-bound (e.g., Gurobi/CPLEX); for large instances it can serve as the basis for the decomposition into a train-plan selection IP with adaptive plan refinement, as outlined in the paper's solution framework.

Text:
# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP model

---

## 1. Problem Description

Given a railway corridor discretised into track sections (blocks/TDS), a set of trains with planned timetables, and actual (delayed) entry times, find a feasible rescheduled timetable — i.e., new passage times, train orders and speed profile choices — such that:

- all section occupancy conflicts (respecting **speed- and train-dependent blocking times**) are avoided,
- headway and route-locking constraints hold,
- switch areas are modelled separately from plain line sections,

while minimising total train delay.

**Assumptions (marked where not stated in the input):**

- (A1) ETCS Level 2 with TTD: end of authority (EoA) at TDS boundaries; brake indication point (IP) may lie anywhere on the track.
- (A2) Each train has a finite set of pre-computed speed profile options per section (macro-energetic discretisation); each option induces a running time and a braking distance to the next EoA.
- (A3) Blocking time of a section = maximum of (running time under chosen profile, approach/braking time from IP to EoA) + section clearing time + route locking/release time.
- (A4) Trains are non-overtaking on single tracks; overtaking allowed only where parallel platform tracks exist (modelled via ordering variables per section).
- (A5) Delays of rolling stock, dwell times and driver behaviour are aggregated into an initial delay at the network entry.
- (A6) All data (running times, braking distances per speed profile) are deterministic and precomputed; the model is therefore linear.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains, index $t$ |
| $S$ | set of track sections (TDS), index $s$ |
| $S^{sw} \subset S$ | switch sections; $S^{ln} = S \setminus S^{sw}$ plain sections |
| $R_t \subseteq S \times S$ | ordered route of train $t$ (successive sections) |
| $P_{t,s}$ | set of speed profile options of train $t$ on section $s$, index $p$ |
| $K$ | discrete time horizon, index $k$ |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $d_t$ | initial (entry) delay of train $t$ |
| $r^{in}_{t,s}$, $r^{out}_{t,s}$ | planned entry/exit time of train $t$ on section $s$ |
| $\rho_{t,s,p}$ | running time of train $t$ on $s$ under profile $p$ |
| $\beta_{t,s,p}$ | braking (approach) time from IP to EoA of the next section, under profile $p$ (speed-dependent) |
| $\tau^{clear}_{t,s}$, $\tau^{lock}_{s}$ | clearing and route-locking/release times |
| $h_{s}$ | minimum headway on section $s$ |
| $\delta^{max}_{t}$ | maximum acceptable delay of train $t$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $w_t$ | delay weight of train $t$ |

The **blocking time** of train $t$ on section $s$ under profile $p$:

$$B_{t,s,p} = \rho_{t,s,p} + \beta_{t,s,p} + \tau^{clear}_{t,s} + \tau^{lock}_{s}$$

Note $\beta_{t,s,p}$ depends on the train's braking curve and entry speed — this is the DTG-specific enhancement.

## 4. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $a_{t,s} \ge 0$ | continuous | actual entry time of $t$ into $s$ |
| $x_{t,s,p} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if train $t$ uses profile $p$ on $s$ |
| $y_{t,t',s} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if $t$ traverses $s$ **before** $t'$ |
| $z_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$ | binary | 1 if $t$ occupies $s$ during time step $k$ |
| $\ell_{t,s} \ge 0$ | continuous | delay of $t$ at exit of $s$ |

## 5. Objective Function

Minimise total (weighted) delay at route exits:

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} w_t \, \ell_{t,e_t}$$

where $e_t$ is the last section of train $t$'s route.

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Entry time definition (retiming):**

$$a_{t,s} \ge r^{in}_{t,s} + d_t \qquad \forall t, \, s \in R_t$$

**(C2) Speed profile selection (exactly one option):**

$$\sum_{p \in P_{t,s}} x_{t,s,p} = 1 \qquad \forall t, \, s \in R_t$$

**(C3) Running time consistency (links consecutive sections):**

$$a_{t,s'} \ge a_{t,s} + \sum_{p \in P_{t,s}} \rho_{t,s,p}\, x_{t,s,p} + dw_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,\; \forall (s,s') \in R_t$$

with $dw_{t,s}$ the (minimum) dwell time on $s$.

**(C4) Blocking time propagation (DTG braking):** exit time of $t$ from $s$ must respect the blocking time including the speed-dependent approach to the next EoA:

$$a_{t,s'} \ge a_{t,s} + \sum_{p} \big(\rho_{t,s,p} + \beta_{t,s,p}\big) x_{t,s,p} + \tau^{clear}_{t,s} + \tau^{lock}_{s} \qquad \forall t, (s,s') \in R_t$$

**(C5) Conflict-freedom via ordering (section $s$, trains $t \ne t'$):**

$$a_{t',s} \ge a_{t,s} + \sum_{p} B_{t,s,p}\, x_{t,s,p} + h_s - M(1 - y_{t,t',s}) \qquad \forall t<t',\, s \in R_t \cap R_{t'}$$

$$a_{t,s} \ge a_{t',s} + \sum_{p} B_{t',s,p}\, x_{t',s,p} + h_s - M\, y_{t,t',s} \qquad \forall t<t',\, s \in R_t \cap R_{t'}$$

**(C6) No overtaking on plain line sections (reordering only at stations/switches with parallel tracks):**

$$y_{t,t',s} = y_{t,t',s_0} \qquad \forall t<t',\; \forall s, s_0 \in S^{ln} \cap (R_t \cap R_{t'})$$

**(C7) Switch exclusivity (interlocking):** on switch sections, conflicting routes may not be set simultaneously — enforced by (C5) plus, for diverging movements with common switch set $S^{sw}$:

$$a_{t',s} \ge a_{t,s} + \sum_p B_{t,s,p} x_{t,s,p} + h_s - M(1-y_{t,t',s}) \qquad \forall t<t',\; s \in S^{sw} \text{ shared}$$

**(C8) Time-discretised occupancy consistency (optional linearisation aid):**

$$z_{t,s,k} \ge x_{t,s,p} - \frac{|k - k(a_{t,s})|}{M} \quad\text{(linearised via indicator constraints)}$$

with at most one occupant per section and step:

$$\sum_{t:\, s \in R_t} z_{t,s,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall s, k$$

**(C9) Delay definition:**

$$\ell_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} - r^{in}_{t,s} - d_t \qquad \forall t, s \in R_t$$

**(C10) Maximum delay bounds:**

$$\ell_{t,e_t} \le \delta^{max}_t \qquad \forall t$$

**(C11) Variable domains:**

$$a_{t,s} \ge 0,\quad \ell_{t,s} \ge 0,\quad x_{t,s,p},\, y_{t,t',s},\, z_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$$

---

## 7. Remarks

- **DTG enhancement** vs. original RECIFE-MILP: blocking times $B_{t,s,p}$ are no longer fixed constants per section but train- and speed-dependent, selected through $x_{t,s,p}$ (C2–C5). The IP may lie inside the preceding section, so the approach time $\beta$ is charged to the *occupied* section's blocking window.
- **Switch distinction** (C6–C7): reordering is forbidden on plain line, permitted at stations/switch areas.
- The model is a standard MILP; big-$M$ can be replaced by indicator constraints for tighter formulations. Time discretisation (C8) may be dropped if the pairwise-ordering formulation (C5) suffices.

Text:
# MILP Model: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Feasibility

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a railway operator who must reschedule rolling stock (train units) over a set of passenger trips after a disruption, while ensuring that all required shunting movements at two major stations (Utrecht Centraal, Rotterdam Centraal) are feasible w.r.t. track availability.

**Assumptions (marked where not stated in the text):**
- (A1) The passenger timetable is fixed except that trains may be delayed by at most a few minutes (assumed: ≤ 5 min), absorbed by timetable buffers.
- (A2) The rolling stock fleet consists of train unit types; units of the same type are interchangeable.
- (A3) Shunting movements take place only at the two disrupted-area stations, within a given time horizon.
- (A4) Track capacity of a station track between two events is exclusive (one train occupies a track at a time).
- (A5) Cancellation of a passenger trip is allowed at a high penalty *(assumption, standard in the literature)*.
- (A6) The model is solved per station area; the composition model covers the whole network.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

**Rolling stock (composition) part**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of passenger trips in the timetable |
| $S$ | set of stations |
| $K$ | set of train unit types (e.g., VIRM-4, ICM-4) |
| $L_k$ | number of available units of type $k$ |
| $C_k$ | capacity (seats) of one unit of type $k$ |
| $N_k^{\max}$ | max number of units of type $k$ per trip (composition length limit) |
| $d_t$ | demand (expected passengers) on trip $t$ |
| $o_{t,k}, e_{t,k}$ | number of units of type $k$ coupled/decoupled at trip $t$ |
| $\pi_t$ | penalty per canceled trip $t$ |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | weights: operational cost, seat shortage, deviation from plan |
| $\delta_{t,k}^{0}$ | original (pre-disruption) assignment of type $k$ to trip $t$ |

**Infrastructure (shunting) part**

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $M$ | set of candidate shunting movements at the considered stations |
| $m \in M$: (station $s_m$, origin track, destination track, earliest start time $\tau_m$, duration $p_m$) |
| $R_s$ | set of tracks at station $s$ |
| $E$ | set of all events on tracks: shunting movements $M$ and passenger train arrivals/departures with scheduled times $\theta_e$ and durations $p_e$ |
| $T^{\max}$ | maximum allowed delay per train (5 min, assumption A1) |
| $u_e$ | penalty per minute of delay of event $e$ |
| $B$ | big-M constant (e.g., horizon length) |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Composition variables**
- $x_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $k$ assigned to trip $t$.
- $y_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is canceled.
- $z_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $k$ deviating from the original plan on trip $t$ (can be modeled as $z_{t,k} \ge |x_{t,k}-\delta^0_{t,k}|$ via auxiliary constraints).
- $w \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: total seat shortage.

**Infrastructure variables**
- $a_m \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $m$ is performed.
- $\lambda_m \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$: start time of shunting movement $m$.
- $\Delta_e \in [0, T^{\max}]$: delay of event $e$.
- $\sigma_{e,e'} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable = 1 if event $e$ is scheduled **before** event $e'$ on the same track.
- $r_{e,\rho} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if event $e$ uses track $\rho \in R_{s(e)}$ (for events with multiple candidate tracks; fixed for passenger trains at platform level, free for shunting between tracks).

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total cost = operational + passenger shortage + plan deviation + shunting cost + delays:

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{k\in K} c_k\, x_{t,k}}_{\text{operational cost}}
+ \alpha \, w
+ \beta \sum_{t,k} z_{t,k}
+ \gamma \sum_{t} \pi_t y_t
+ \sum_{e\in E} u_e \Delta_e
$$

where $c_k$ is the cost of running one unit of type $k$ over its assignment.

## 5. Constraints — Composition Model

**(C1) Composition feasibility:**
$$x_{t,k} + o_{t,k} - e_{t,k} = x_{t',k} \quad \forall t, \; \forall k, \; t' = \text{successor}(t) \text{ on the same line}$$

**(C2) Fleet availability:**
$$\sum_{t \in T} x_{t,k} \le L_k \quad \forall k \in K$$

**(C3) Composition length limit:**
$$x_{t,k} \le N_k^{\max}(1 - y_t) \quad \forall t, k$$

**(C4) Cancellation forces zero assignment:**
$$x_{t,k} \le N_k^{\max}(1-y_t) \quad \forall t,k \quad \text{(already covered; alternatively } \sum_k x_{t,k} \le M_{big}(1-y_t))$$

**(C5) Seat coverage / shortage:**
$$\sum_{k\in K} C_k x_{t,k} + w_t \ge d_t (1 - y_t) \quad \forall t, \qquad w \ge \sum_t w_t$$

**(C6) Deviation from original plan (linearized absolute value):**
$$z_{t,k} \ge x_{t,k} - \delta^0_{t,k}, \qquad z_{t,k} \ge \delta^0_{t,k} - x_{t,k} \quad \forall t,k$$

## 6. Constraints — Infrastructure Model (shunting feasibility)

For each event $e$ (shunting movement $m$ or passenger train movement) at station $s(e)$:

**(I1) Track assignment:**
$$\sum_{\rho \in R_{s(e)}} r_{e,\rho} = 1 \quad \forall e \in E$$

**(I2) Timing of shunting movements:**
$$\tau_m \cdot a_m \le \lambda_m \le \tau_m + T^{\max}, \qquad \lambda_m \le B \cdot a_m \quad \forall m \in M$$

**(I3) Delay bounds (assumption A1):**
$$0 \le \Delta_e \le T^{\max} \quad \forall e \in E$$

**(I4) No two events overlap on the same track.** For every pair $e, e' \in E$, $e<e'$, and track $\rho \in R_{s(e)} \cap R_{s(e')}$:
$$\lambda_{e'} + \Delta_{e'} \;\ge\; \lambda_e + \Delta_e + p_e - B\,(3 - r_{e,\rho} - r_{e',\rho} - \sigma_{e,e'})$$
$$\lambda_{e} + \Delta_{e} \;\ge\; \lambda_{e'} + \Delta_{e'} + p_{e'} - B\,(2 - r_{e,\rho} - r_{e',\rho} + \sigma_{e,e'})$$
i.e., if both events use track $\rho$, one must finish before the other starts.

**(I5) Link shunting selection to composition (cutting/shunting need):** if the composition requires a unit to be added or removed at a station, the corresponding shunting movement must be performed:
$$a_m \ge \frac{o_{t,k} + e_{t,k}}{N_k^{\max}} \quad \forall m \text{ associated with coupling/decoupling at trip } t$$
*(assumption: a mapping between composition changes and required shunting movements is preprocessed).*

## 7. Combinatorial Benders (No-Good) Cuts

The composition model proposes shunting movements; the infrastructure model checks feasibility. If a proposed set $\bar{M} \subseteq M$ of simultaneous shunting movements is infeasible on the infrastructure (no assignment of tracks, times and delays $\le T^{\max}$ exists), add the cut:

$$\sum_{m \in \bar{M}} a_m \;\le\; |\bar{M}| - 1$$

More refined infeasibility cuts (minimal infeasible subsets found by the infrastructure model) can replace $\bar{M}$. The algorithm iterates: solve composition model → check infrastructure → add cuts → re-solve, until no infeasible combination is proposed (exact approach). In the **iterative heuristic**, shunting movements are fed one-by-one to the infrastructure model, fixing $a_m = 1$ only if feasible, mimicking the interaction between rolling stock dispatchers and infrastructure dispatchers.

## 8. Complete Model Summary

$$
\begin{aligned}
\min \;& \sum_{t,k} c_k x_{t,k} + \alpha w + \beta \sum_{t,k} z_{t,k} + \gamma \sum_t \pi_t y_t + \sum_e u_e \Delta_e \\
\text{s.t. } & \text{(C1)–(C6), (I1)–(I5), Benders cuts} \\
& x_{t,k}, z_{t,k} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0},\; y_t, a_m, \sigma_{e,e'}, r_{e,\rho} \in \{0,1\},\; \lambda_m, \Delta_e, w \ge 0
\end{aligned}
$$

The model is a valid MILP: all constraints are linear, big-$M$ terms use the horizon length $B$, and integrality is restricted to assignment, ordering, track, and shunting-selection variables.

# MILP Model for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Assumptions (explicitly stated)

- **A1** — A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $S=\{1,\dots,|S|\}$ and segments between consecutive stations. Each segment has an upward track and a downward track.
- **A2** — A partial blockage affects a set of segments $D$ during time window $[t^s, t^e]$: one track of each disrupted segment is unavailable, so trains may only pass **single-track**, requiring unidirectional occupancy (local rerouting to the opposite track is allowed).
- **A3** — Train set $K$ with fixed routes through stations; each train $k$ has a scheduled arrival/departure at each station, a minimum dwell time, and minimum/maximum running times per segment.
- **A4** — Each segment is divided into blocks; a train occupies a block exclusively (headway is modeled via block occupancy).
- **A5** — Speed profiles are discretized: for each train $k$, segment $(i,i+1)$ and route $r$, a finite set of candidate running times $\{t^{k}_{ir}\}$ with associated energy consumption $E^{k}_{ir}(t)$ (piecewise-linear convex approximation, hence linear). *(Discretization of the speed profile set is an assumption; the energy–time relation is approximated linearly.)*
- **A6** — Trains cannot be cancelled within the planning horizon (cancellation could be added with a binary variable).
- **A7** — Acceleration/deceleration are embedded in the candidate running times; no speed conflict inside a block beyond exclusive occupancy.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $K$ | set of trains |
| $S$ | set of stations, ordered along the corridor |
| $B$ | set of blocks; $B_{ir}$ = blocks of segment $(i,i+1)$ on route $r$ |
| $R_{ki}$ | admissible routes (track choices) of train $k$ on segment leaving station $i$ |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $a^{0}_{ki}, d^{0}_{ki}$ | scheduled arrival / departure of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $\underline{d}_{ki}, \bar{d}_{ki}$ | earliest / latest allowed departure |
| $h^{arr}_{ki}, h^{dep}_{ki}$ | minimum headways at arrival/departure of station $i$ |
| $\underline{w}_{ki}, \bar{w}_{ki}$ | min / max dwell time of train $k$ at station $i$ |
| $\underline{t}^{k}_{ir}, \bar{t}^{k}_{ir}$ | min / max running time of train $k$ on segment $(i,i+1)$ via route $r$ |
| $T^{k}_{ir} \subseteq [\underline{t}^{k}_{ir}, \bar{t}^{k}_{ir}]$ | discrete candidate running times; $E^{k}_{ir}(t)$ = energy of candidate $t$ |
| $u_{b}$ | = 1 if block $b$ is unavailable in $[t^s,t^e]$ (partial blockage) |
| $\pi_{k}$ | priority weight (delay penalty) of train $k$ |
| $\alpha, \beta$ | weights of energy and delay in the objective |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Timetable variables:**
- $a_{ki} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$: actual arrival time of train $k$ at station $i$
- $d_{ki} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$: actual departure time
- $t_{ki} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$: actual running time of train $k$ on segment $(i,i+1)$

**Rerouting variables:**
- $x^{k}_{ir} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ uses route $r \in R_{ki}$ on segment $(i,i+1)$

**Speed-profile variables:**
- $y^{k}_{irt} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $k$ runs segment $(i,i+1)$ via route $r$ with candidate running time $t \in T^{k}_{ir}$

**Conflict variables (big-M):**
- $z^{kk'}_{b} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering indicator — 1 if train $k$ occupies block $b$ before train $k'$

## 4. Model

### Objective

Minimize total weighted delay plus energy consumption:

$$
\min \; \alpha \underbrace{\sum_{k\in K}\Big(\sum_{i\in S} \pi_{k}\big[(a_{ki}-a^{0}_{ki})^{+} + (d_{ki}-d^{0}_{ki})^{+}\big]\Big)}_{\text{total delay}}
\;+\; \beta \underbrace{\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{i}\sum_{r\in R_{ki}}\sum_{t\in T^{k}_{ir}} E^{k}_{ir}(t)\, y^{k}_{irt}}_{\text{total energy}}
$$

Linearized with auxiliary variables $A_{ki}, D_{ki} \ge 0$ (positive-part delays):

$$
A_{ki} \ge a_{ki}-a^{0}_{ki},\qquad D_{ki} \ge d_{ki}-d^{0}_{ki}
$$

$$
\min \; \alpha\sum_{k}\pi_k\Big(\sum_i A_{ki}+D_{ki}\Big) + \beta\sum_{k}\sum_{i}\sum_{r}\sum_{t} E^{k}_{ir}(t)\,y^{k}_{irt}
$$

### Constraints

**(C1) Timetable consistency — running and dwell times:**

$$
d_{ki} = a_{ki} + w_{ki}, \qquad \underline{w}_{ki} \le w_{ki} \le \bar{w}_{ki} \quad \forall k, i \in S \setminus\{\text{terminus}\}
$$

$$
a_{k,i+1} = d_{ki} + t_{ki} \qquad \forall k,\; i
$$

**(C2) Time-window bounds:**

$$
\underline{d}_{ki} \le d_{ki} \le \bar{d}_{ki} \qquad \forall k,i
$$

**(C3) Route selection (rerouting):**

$$
\sum_{r\in R_{ki}} x^{k}_{ir} = 1 \qquad \forall k, i
$$

**(C4) Speed-profile selection — link running time, route, and profile:**

$$
\sum_{r\in R_{ki}}\sum_{t\in T^{k}_{ir}} y^{k}_{irt} = 1 \qquad \forall k,i
$$

$$
t_{ki} = \sum_{r\in R_{ki}}\sum_{t\in T^{k}_{ir}} t\, y^{k}_{irt} \qquad \forall k,i
$$

$$
y^{k}_{irt} \le x^{k}_{ir} \qquad \forall k,i,\, r\in R_{ki},\, t\in T^{k}_{ir}
$$

**(C5) Disruption — block unavailability during the time window.**
Let $\sigma^{k}_{b} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$ denote the entry time of train $k$ into block $b$ (linear function of $a_{ki}, d_{ki}$: $\sigma^{k}_{b} = d_{ki}$ if $b$ is the first block after station $i$, else cumulative). A train may use unavailable block $b$ only if it enters after the disruption ends or leaves before it starts:

$$
x^{k}_{ir} \le 1 - u_{b} + \frac{\sigma^{k}_{b} - t^s}{M} \quad\text{and}\quad x^{k}_{ir} \le 1 - u_{b} + \frac{t^e - (\sigma^{k}_{b} + t_{ki})}{M}
$$
$$
\forall k, i,\, r\in R_{ki},\, b \in B_{ir} \text{ with } u_b = 1
$$

Equivalently, if a train traverses a disrupted block, its occupancy interval must not intersect $[t^s,t^e]$.

**(C6) Conflict-free block occupancy (headway / single-track unidirectionality).**
For each block $b$ and pair of trains $k \ne k'$ that may occupy $b$ (with entry times $\sigma^{k}_{b}, \sigma^{k'}_{b}$ and exit times $e^{k}_{b} = \sigma^{k}_{b} + \text{occ}^{k}_{b}$):

$$
\sigma^{k}_{b} - \sigma^{k'}_{b} \ge h_{b} - M\big(2 - x^{k}_{ir} - x^{k'}_{i'r'} + z^{kk'}_{b}\big)
$$
$$
\sigma^{k'}_{b} - \sigma^{k}_{b} \ge h_{b} - M\big(2 - x^{k}_{ir} - x^{k'}_{i'r'} + 1 - z^{kk'}_{b}\big)
$$
$$
\forall b,\; \forall k<k',\; \forall (i,r): b\in B_{ir},\; \forall (i',r'): b\in B_{i'r'}
$$

i.e., if both trains use blocks containing $b$, one must precede the other by at least the headway $h_b$. This enforces unidirectional passage on a partially blocked segment.

**(C7) Station headways (arrival/departure):**

$$
|a_{ki} - a_{k'i}| \ge h^{arr}_{ki} - M(1-\zeta_{kk'i}), \quad |d_{ki}-d_{k'i}| \ge h^{dep}_{ki} - M\zeta_{kk'i}
$$
with auxiliary binary ordering variables $\zeta_{kk'i} \in \{0,1\}$, linearized in the standard big-M fashion.

**(C8) Variable domains:**

$$
a_{ki}, d_{ki}, t_{ki}, A_{ki}, D_{ki}, w_{ki} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}; \quad x^{k}_{ir}, y^{k}_{irt}, z^{kk'}_{b}, \zeta_{kk'i} \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 5. Remarks

- The model simultaneously decides **retiming** ($a,d,t$), **reordering** ($z,\zeta$), **rerouting** ($x$), and **speed profiles** ($y$), fully linear via big-M and the discrete speed-profile set (A5).
- The energy–running-time trade-off is captured: choosing a shorter $t$ (earlier arrival) versus a longer $t$ (energy-efficient coasting) is decided by the binary $y$-variables in the objective.
- Constraint (C5) restricts rerouting through disrupted blocks to the disruption-free side or time, and (C6) guarantees bidirectional conflict-freedom on the shared open track.
- As stated in the paper, this MILP is decomposed into an IP over train interactions plus single-train plan generation; with sufficiently fine candidate sets $T^{k}_{ir}$ the IP is equivalent to this MILP.

# MILP Model for the Real-Time Railway Traffic Management Problem (rtRTMP)

## 1. Scope and Assumptions

The model follows the framework inspired by Pellegrini et al. (2014) and the proposed pair-wise formulation. The following assumptions are made (marked as assumptions where information is missing):

- **(A1)** The infrastructure is modeled at a **macroscopic** level: the network is a set of junctions; between junctions, trains traverse routes (paths of track sections).
- **(A2)** Each train $t$ has a set of **admissible routes** $R_t$ through each station/area, with known minimum running times.
- **(A3)** A train cannot be overtaken on a single track section unless alternative routes exist; reordering is possible only at junctions/merging points.
- **(A4)** Delays are measured at a reference point (exit of the network area); delay propagation along the train path is captured via minimum dwell/headway times.
- **(A5)** Safety is enforced by minimum headway times between trains on shared resources (including safety-relevant overlap margins, modeled as an extended occupancy time).
- **(A6)** Primary delays at the entrance of the considered area are known and deterministic (deterministic disturbance scenario).
- **(A7)** Train route choice and ordering are fixed during rescheduling (two-stage decomposition), but the full model below integrates all decisions.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $J$ | set of junctions / resources |
| $R_t$ | set of admissible routes for train $t$ |
| $J(r)$ | resources used by route $r$ |
| $r^0_t$ | original (planned) route of train $t$ |
| $a_t$ | planned entrance time of train $t$ into the area |
| $d_t$ | planned exit time of train $t$ |
| $\delta_t \ge 0$ | primary delay of train $t$ at entrance |
| $\ell_{tr}$ | minimum running time of train $t$ on route $r$ |
| $h_{ij}$ | minimum headway between trains $i,j$ on a shared resource (incl. overlap margins) |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $\tau$ | length of the discretized time horizon |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Routing:**
- $x_{tr} \in \{0,1\}$: equals 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_t$.

**Ordering (pair-wise):**
- $y_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ for each ordered pair $(i,j) \in T\times T$, $i\neq j$, sharing at least one resource: equals 1 if train $i$ passes the common resource **before** train $j$.

**Scheduling:**
- $e_t \ge 0$: entrance time of train $t$ (planned $a_t$ + primary delay $\delta_t$ is a lower bound).
- $s_t \ge 0$: exit (reference-point) time of train $t$.
- $D_t \ge 0$: secondary delay of train $t$ at the reference point.

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize total delay at the reference point:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} D_t
$$

*(Optionally weighted: $\min \sum_t w_t D_t$, with weights for train priority — assumption A8.)*

## 5. Constraints

**Route selection (each train exactly one route):**

$$
\sum_{r \in R_t} x_{tr} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{1}
$$

**Entrance times include primary delay:**

$$
e_t \ge a_t + \delta_t \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{2}
$$

**Running time and delay definition:**

$$
s_t \ge e_t + \sum_{r \in R_t} \ell_{tr} x_{tr} \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{3}
$$

$$
D_t \ge s_t - d_t \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{4}
$$

**Ordering consistency (anti-symmetry):**

$$
y_{ij} + y_{ji} = 1 \qquad \forall i,j \in T,\ i<j,\ J(r_i)\cap J(r_j)\neq\emptyset \tag{5}
$$

**Headway / conflict-free ordering on shared resources.** For each pair $(i,j)$ sharing resource $k$, with occupancy start times linked to entrance times:

$$
s_i + h_{ij} \le s_j + M(1 - y_{ij}) \qquad \forall i,j,\ i \neq j \tag{6}
$$

$$
s_j + h_{ji} \le s_i + M\, y_{ij} \qquad \forall i,j,\ i \neq j \tag{7}
$$

Constraints (6)–(7) enforce: if $y_{ij}=1$, train $i$ clears the resource (plus safety margin) before train $j$ enters; otherwise the reverse holds.

**Route-dependent headway activation.** If trains $i$ and $j$ share resources only on certain route combinations, conflicts are conditioned on the routing choice. Introduce $z_{ij} \in \{0,1\}$ indicating whether $i,j$ actually conflict:

$$
z_{ij} \ge x_{i r} + x_{j r'} - 1 \qquad \forall (r,r') \text{ with } J(r)\cap J(r')\neq\emptyset \tag{8}
$$

and replace (5)–(7) by:

$$
y_{ij} + y_{ji} \ge z_{ij}, \qquad y_{ij} \le z_{ij}, \qquad y_{ji} \le z_{ij} \tag{9}
$$

$$
s_i + h_{ij} \le s_j + M(1-y_{ij}) + M(1-z_{ij}) \tag{10a}
$$
$$
s_j + h_{ji} \le s_i + M\,y_{ij} + M(1-z_{ij}) \tag{10b}
$$

**Time horizon:**

$$
s_t \le \tau \qquad \forall t \in T \tag{11}
$$

**Variable domains:**

$$
x_{tr} \in \{0,1\},\quad y_{ij}\in\{0,1\},\quad z_{ij}\in\{0,1\},\quad e_t, s_t, D_t \ge 0 \tag{12}
$$

## 6. Two-Stage Decomposition (as in the paper)

**Stage 1 (Rerouting & Reordering, sub-optimal, no delay propagation):** Solve (1), (2), (5)–(10) with simplified timing constraints $s_t = e_t + \ell_{t r^0_t}$ (planned running times, fixed routes for timing), minimizing pair-wise delays. Output: fixed $x^*_{tr}$ and optionally $y^*_{ij}$.

**Stage 2 (Rescheduling):** With $x_{tr} = x^*_{tr}$ fixed (and optionally $y_{ij}=y^*_{ij}$), solve the full model (1)–(12) to obtain exact schedules $e_t, s_t$ and delays $D_t$.

**Optimality note:** The two-stage solution is globally optimal if no delay propagation occurs between consecutive resource conflicts (i.e., each train's secondary delay does not affect its subsequent conflicts); otherwise the integrated model (1)–(12), which links $s_t$ to actual entrance times, guarantees the global optimum.

## 7. Extension for Safety-Relevant Overlaps

Following Lindenmaier et al. (2022), the overlap margin behind a stop signal is included by extending occupancy: the headway parameter $h_{ij}$ is replaced by $h_{ij} + o_{ij}$, where $o_{ij}$ is the time required to clear the overlap region behind the signal for the route of train $i$ before train $j$ may enter. This only changes parameter values, keeping the model linear.

---

**Summary:** The model is a MILP with binary routing variables $x_{tr}$, binary ordering variables $y_{ij}$ (pair-wise delay interpretation), and continuous timing/delay variables $e_t, s_t, D_t$, minimizing total secondary delay subject to route selection, primary-delay, running-time, headway, and horizon constraints. The decomposition into rerouting/reordering (Stage 1) and rescheduling (Stage 2) reduces computational cost, with the integrated formulation providing the global optimum when delay propagation is significant.

# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance‑to‑Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE‑MILP‑style model. Assumptions not given in the text are marked **[A]**.

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **[A1]** The network is a set of microscopic resources (block/TDS sections, switch areas, station tracks). A train occupies a resource for a *blocking time* interval.
- **[A2]** Under DTG, the blocking time of train *t* on resource *q* depends on the train and on its chosen **speed profile** (speed‑dependent braking distance ⇒ speed‑dependent approach/braking part of the blocking time).
- **[A3]** Each train has a set of feasible (route, speed‑profile) combinations; each combination fixes minimum running times on each resource and the resulting blocking times.
- **[A4]** Delays are measured at a reference point (e.g., exit of the network); delay propagation is captured through the timing variables.
- **[A5]** Routes are pre‑defined paths through resources; reordering is allowed on each resource; retiming is continuous.
- **[A6]** Big‑M separations use a sufficiently large constant M; all data are rational.

---

## 2. Sets and indices

- $T$ : trains; $t,k \in T$, $t \neq k$
- $R_t$ : feasible routes for train $t$
- $P_{t,r}$ : feasible speed profiles for train $t$ on route $r$ (each = vector of per‑resource target speeds)
- $Q$ : resources (block/TDS sections, switches, platform tracks)
- $Q_{t,r}$ : resources traversed by route $r$ of train $t$, in order
- $S$ : switch resources $\subset Q$

## 3. Parameters

- $a_t$ : scheduled (planned) exit time of train $t$
- $w_t$ : delay weight of train $t$
- $d^{in}_{t,q}$ : scheduled entry time of $t$ into $q$
- $\rho^{min}_{t,q}(p)$ : minimum running time on $q$ under profile $p$
- $\beta_{t,q}(p)$ : **speed‑dependent blocking (separation) time** of train $t$ on resource $q$ under profile $p$ = reaction + approach (absolute braking distance at entry speed) + occupation + release time **[A2]**
- $\delta^{dwell}_{t,q}$ : minimum dwell time at station resources
- $\sigma_{t,k,q}$ : required switch‑setting changeover time if $k$ follows $t$ on switch $q$ (0 if same route)
- $M$ : big‑M
- $H$ : horizon

## 4. Variables

- $x_{t,r,p} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if train $t$ uses route $r$ with speed profile $p$
- $y_{t,k,q} \in \{0,1\}$ : 1 if $t$ traverses $q$ before $k$ (defined for ordered pairs $t<k$ on common resources)
- $e_{t,q} \ge 0$ : entry time of $t$ into resource $q$
- $\ell_{t,q} \ge 0$ : exit (clearing) time of $t$ from resource $q$
- $D_t \ge 0$ : delay of train $t$ at reference point

## 5. Objective

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} w_t D_t$$

## 6. Constraints

**(1) Route/profile assignment** — exactly one combination per train:
$$\sum_{r \in R_t}\sum_{p \in P_{t,r}} x_{t,r,p} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(2) Entry–exit consistency:**
$$\ell_{t,q} \ge e_{t,q} + \sum_{r\in R_t}\sum_{p\in P_{t,r}} \rho^{min}_{t,q}(p)\, x_{t,r,p} \qquad \forall t, \forall q \in \bigcup_r Q_{t,r}$$

**(3) Temporal flow along the route** (exit of one resource ≥ entry of next, plus dwell):
$$e_{t,q'} \ge \ell_{t,q} + \delta^{dwell}_{t,q} - M\Big(1-\sum_{p} x_{t,r,p}\Big) \qquad \forall t, r, (q,q') \text{ consecutive in } Q_{t,r}$$

**(4) DTG blocking‑time separation (speed‑dependent).** For every resource $q$ and pair $t,k$ both routed over $q$:
$$\ell_{t,q} + \sum_{p}\beta_{t,q}(p)x_{t,r,p} \;\le\; e_{k,q} + M(1-y_{t,k,q}) \qquad \forall t\neq k,\ \forall q$$
i.e., if $t$ precedes $k$, $k$ may not enter $q$ before $t$’s blocking interval (including its speed‑dependent braking approach) has expired.

**(5) Ordering consistency (anti‑symmetry):**
$$y_{t,k,q} + y_{k,t,q} = 1 \qquad \forall t<k \text{ sharing } q$$

**(6) No overtaking / FIFO consistency across consecutive resources** (trains cannot pass on the open line) **[A5]:**
$$y_{t,k,q} = y_{t,k,q'} \qquad \forall t<k,\ \text{consecutive open‑line } q,q'$$

**(7) Switch changeover time:** if $k$ follows $t$ on switch $q$ with different routes:
$$e_{k,q} \ge \ell_{t,q} + \sigma_{t,k,q} - M(3 - y_{t,k,q} - x^{route}_{t,r} - x^{route}_{k,r'}) \qquad \forall t\neq k,\ q\in S,\ r \neq r'$$
where $x^{route}_{t,r}=\sum_p x_{t,r,p}$.

**(8) Initial conditions:** $e_{t,q_0(t)} = d^{in}_{t,q_0(t)} + \text{initial delay}_t$ (fixed input for already‑delayed trains).

**(9) Delay definition:**
$$D_t \ge \ell_{t,q^{out}_t} - a_t, \qquad D_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall t$$

**(10) Bounds:** $0 \le e_{t,q}, \ell_{t,q} \le H$.

---

## 7. Notes

- Constraints (4) with profile‑dependent $\beta_{t,q}(p)$ are the key DTG enhancement: the brake indication point may lie anywhere on the track, so the separation before an occupied block equals the train’s absolute braking distance at its current entry speed, embedded in $\beta$.
- The model is linear: all nonlinearities (profile choice, ordering) are handled by binaries $x$ and $y$ with big‑M.

# TRSMP MILP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Blockage

Below is the final, complete linear model (the auxiliary-variable definition in constraint (6) has been cleaned up).

## Sets and Data

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains $i$ |
| $S$ | set of stations $s$ |
| $L$ | set of segments $l=(s,s')$ connecting consecutive stations |
| $T=\{0,\dots,T_{\max}\}$ | discrete time horizon |
| $P_{i,l}$ | feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $l$ (running time $r_{i,l,p}$, energy $e_{i,l,p}$) |
| $A^0_{i,s}, D^0_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $dw_{i,s}$ | minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h$ | minimum headway |
| $\Delta_i$ | maximum allowable delay of train $i$ |
| $[T^s_l, T^e_l]$ | disruption window: **own track** of segment $l$ blocked, opposite track available |
| $w_i, c_i, \gamma$ | delay weight, cancellation penalty, energy weight |
| $C_s$ | station capacity (platform tracks) |
| $M$ | big-M constant ($M \ge T_{\max}+h$) |

## Variables

- $a_{i,s,t}, d_{i,s,t}\in\{0,1\}$: one-hot arrival/departure of train $i$ at station $s$ at time $t$
- $A_{i,s}, D_{i,s}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$: actual arrival/departure times
- $x_{i,l,p}\in\{0,1\}$: speed profile $p$ chosen on segment $l$
- $y_{i,l}\in\{0,1\}$: rerouted to the opposite (unblocked) track
- $b_{i,l}\in\{0,1\}$: traversal disjunction (before/after disruption window)
- $o_{ij,l}\in\{0,1\}$: ordering of trains $i,j$ on segment $l$ ($o=1 \Rightarrow i$ before $j$)
- $\pi_{ij,s}, \delta_{ij,s}\in\{0,1\}$: arrival/departure ordering at stations
- $\alpha_{ij,l}, \beta_{ij,l}\in\{0,1\}$: track-sharing indicators (both rerouted / both own track)
- $z_i\in\{0,1\}$: train $i$ cancelled

**Derived linear traversal times** for $l=(s,s')$:
$$\sigma_{i,l}=D_{i,s},\qquad \rho_{i,l}=D_{i,s}+\sum_{p\in P_{i,l}} r_{i,l,p}\,x_{i,l,p}.$$

## Objective

$$\min \; \sum_{i\in I} w_i\sum_{s\in S}\big[(A_{i,s}-A^0_{i,s})+(D_{i,s}-D^0_{i,s})\big] \;+\; \sum_{i\in I} c_i z_i \;+\; \gamma\sum_{i,l,p} e_{i,l,p}\,x_{i,l,p}$$

## Constraints

**(1) One-hot time assignment (cancelled trains get none):**
$$\sum_{t\in T} a_{i,s,t}=1-z_i,\qquad \sum_{t\in T} d_{i,s,t}=1-z_i \quad \forall i,s$$

**(2) Time linking:**
$$A_{i,s}=\sum_{t\in T} t\,a_{i,s,t},\qquad D_{i,s}=\sum_{t\in T} t\,d_{i,s,t} \quad \forall i,s$$

**(3) Speed profile selection:**
$$\sum_{p\in P_{i,l}} x_{i,l,p}=1-z_i \quad \forall i,l$$

**(4) Dwell + running time propagation (TRP–TSMP coupling), for $l=(s,s')$:**
$$D_{i,s'}\ge A_{i,s}+dw_{i,s}+\sum_{p\in P_{i,l}} r_{i,l,p}\,x_{i,l,p} \quad \forall i,\, l=(s,s')$$

**(5) Reroute-or-defer disjunction.** If $y_{i,l}=0$ (own, blocked track), the traversal $[\sigma_{i,l},\rho_{i,l}]$ must lie entirely outside $[T^s_l,T^e_l]$; if $y_{i,l}=1$, both are relaxed (crossing during the window on the opposite track):
$$\rho_{i,l}\le T^s_l + M\,b_{i,l} + M\,y_{i,l} \quad \forall i,l$$
$$\sigma_{i,l}\ge T^e_l - M(1-b_{i,l}) - M\,y_{i,l} \quad \forall i,l$$
*Sign check:* $y=0,b=0$: $\rho\le T^s_l$ (finish before window), second inactive; $y=0,b=1$: first inactive, $\sigma\ge T^e_l$ (start after window); $y=1$: both relaxed. ✓

**(6) Segment headway ordering** — only for pairs that can share a physical track. Linearize track-compatibility:
$$\alpha_{ij,l}\ge y_{i,l}+y_{j,l}-1,\quad \alpha_{ij,l}\le y_{i,l},\quad \alpha_{ij,l}\le y_{j,l}\qquad(\alpha=1\iff\text{both rerouted})$$
$$\beta_{ij,l}\ge 1-y_{i,l}-y_{j,l},\quad \beta_{ij,l}\le 1-y_{i,l},\quad \beta_{ij,l}\le 1-y_{j,l}\qquad(\beta=1\iff\text{both on own track})$$
Ordering constraints apply with big-M relaxed when neither $\alpha$ nor $\beta$ holds (mixed routing ⇒ different tracks, no conflict):
$$\rho_{i,l}+h\le \sigma_{j,l}+M(1-o_{ij,l}+\alpha_{ij,l}+\beta_{ij,l})\qquad(\text{wait—} \alpha,\beta\text{ should ACTIVATE, not relax})$$

Corrected form: the ordering must hold **iff** the pair shares a track ($\alpha+\beta=1$) and may be relaxed otherwise:
$$\rho_{i,l}+h\le \sigma_{j,l}+M\,(1-\alpha_{ij,l}-\beta_{ij,l})+M\,(1-o_{ij,l}) \quad \forall (i,j),l$$
$$\rho_{j,l}+h\le \sigma_{i,l}+M\,(1-\alpha_{ij,l}-\beta_{ij,l})+M\,o_{ij,l} \quad \forall (i,j)$$
(If $\alpha+\beta=1$: standard disjunctive headway constraint. If $\alpha=\beta=0$: both relaxed. $o_{ij,l}$ may be fixed to 0 for non-sharing pairs.)

**(7) Station headways** (relaxed for cancelled trains):
$$A_{i,s}+h\le A_{j,s}+M(1-\pi_{ij,s})+M(z_i+z_j) \quad \forall i\ne j,\,s$$
$$A_{j,s}+h\le A_{i,s}+M\,\pi_{ij,s}+M(z_i+z_j) \quad \forall i\ne j,\,s$$
$$D_{i,s}+h\le D_{j,s}+M(1-\delta_{ij,s})+M(z_i+z_j) \quad \forall i\ne j,\,s$$
$$D_{j,s}+h\le D_{i,s}+M\,\delta_{ij,s}+M(z_i+z_j) \quad \forall i\ne j,\,s$$

**(8) Station capacity:**
$$\sum_{i\in I}\Big(\sum_{t'\le t} a_{i,s,t'}-\sum_{t'\le t} d_{i,s,t'}\Big)\le C_s \quad \forall s,\,t$$

**(9) Delay bounds and horizon:**
$$A_{i,s}\le A^0_{i,s}+\Delta_i(1-z_i),\qquad D_{i,s}\le D^0_{i,s}+\Delta_i(1-z_i) \quad \forall i,s$$
$$0\le A_{i,s},\,D_{i,s}\le T_{\max}$$

**(10) Domains:**
$$a,d,x,y,b,o,\pi,\delta,\alpha,\beta,z\in\{0,1\};\qquad A_{i,s},D_{i,s}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$$

## How the model works

- **One-hot time encoding** (1)–(2) gives exact linear integer event times and enables the cumulative capacity form (8).
- **Speed profiles** (3)–(4) couple control-level decisions to the timetable: slower profiles save energy but lengthen running time, so the objective balances delay cost $w_i$ against energy cost $\gamma e$.
- **Partial blockage** (5): a train either avoids the blocked window in time ($b_{i,l}$) or crosses during the window on the opposite unblocked track ($y_{i,l}=1$); rerouting is optional and never forced.
- **Track-sharing logic** (6): ordering with headway $h$ applies only when two trains occupy the same physical track, resolving bidirectional conflicts on the shared opposite track.
- **Station constraints** (7)–(8) enforce platform headways and capacity.
- **Cancellation** $z_i$ removes a train from the system at penalty $c_i$.

## Assumptions

**(a)** Time is discrete on $\{0,\dots,T_{\max}\}$; all event times are integers. **(b)** Each segment has exactly two tracks; one (the "own" track) is blocked during $[T^s_l,T^e_l]$, the opposite track is always available. **(c)** No overtaking within a segment; ordering constraints enforce separation on shared tracks. **(d)** Dwell times are lower bounds only; station sequence per train is fixed. **(e)** A cancelled train occupies no infrastructure and incurs no delay or energy. **(f)** Speed profiles are discretized per train/segment with deterministic running time and energy, independent of traffic. **(g)** Big-M chosen sufficiently large so relaxed constraints are never binding. **(h)** Headway $h$ is uniform; station capacity counts trains present between arrival and departure; no rolling-stock/crew coupling; initial occupancy at $t=0$ is zero.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Setting.** A bidirectional double-track high-speed railway corridor consisting of stations $S=\{1,\dots,n_S\}$ connected by segments $L=\{1,\dots,n_L\}$ (segment $i$ links stations $i$ and $i+1$). A partial blockage disrupts a set of segments $\bar L\subseteq L$ during time window $[T_d, T_r]$: on a disrupted segment, only **one track remains available for both directions** (single-track operation), so trains of opposite directions sharing that segment must be coordinated; the opposite track may be used as a rerouting possibility only if it is the *operable* one — **Assumption (A4) below governs this**.

**Assumptions (made explicit, some are reasonable fills-in where the input is silent):**

- (A1) Trains run according to a scheduled timetable; each train has a scheduled arrival/departure at every station it serves and may not be delayed beyond a maximum allowable delay.
- (A2) On each segment a train can select from a **discretized set of speed profiles**, each characterized by an unimpeded running time and an energy consumption. Profiles are linearized: a train's actual running time equals its selected nominal running time plus a linear retiming adjustment (regenerative acceleration/braking margins).
- (A3) Headway times on each segment (and in each direction at stations) are fixed minimum separation times.
- (A4) During the disruption, on each blocked segment one direction is served by the intact track; the *disrupted* track can carry trains of the *opposite* direction (local rerouting) — hence bidirectional conflicts must be coordinated on both tracks.
- (A5) Cancellation of train services is allowed at a penalty cost.
- (A6) Dwell times at stations have fixed minimum and maximum values.
- (A7) Rolling stock circulation and passenger demand are outside the scope; each train keeps its assigned rolling stock.
- (A8) Time is discretized (or continuous with big-M linearization); all data are deterministic.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | set of trains; $F^+ / F^-$: trains in the up / down direction |
| $L_i \subseteq L$ | segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $P_i^{\ell}$ | set of candidate speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ |
| $r_{ip}^{\ell}$ | nominal running time of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ under profile $p$ |
| $e_{ip}^{\ell}$ | energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $\ell$ under profile $p$ |
| $d_i, a_i$ | scheduled departure/arrival times of train $i$ at its origin/destination |
| $w_{\min}^{\ell}, h_{\min}^{\ell}$ | minimum station dwell / segment headway times |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $T$ | planning horizon; $[T_d, T_r]$ disruption window on $\bar L$ |
| $\Delta_i^{\max}$ | maximum allowable total delay of train $i$ |
| $\delta^{\text{arr}},\delta^{\text{dep}}$ | safety margins at arrival/departure conflicts |
| $c_i^{\text{canc}}$ | cancellation penalty of train $i$ |
| $\alpha,\beta$ | weights for delay vs. energy in the objective |

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $a_{is}, d_{is} \ge 0$ | actual arrival / departure time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $x_{ip}^{\ell} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $\ell$ |
| $y_{i}^{\ell,\text{op}} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ runs on segment $\ell$ on the **operable** (original) track |
| $y_{i}^{\ell,\text{re}} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $\ell$ |
| $z_i \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $i$ is cancelled |
| $\phi_{ik}^{\ell} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 iff train $k$ immediately precedes train $i$ on track $m\in\{\text{op},\text{re}\}$ of segment $\ell$ (sequencing variable) |
| $\sigma_{ik}^{\ell} \in \{0,1\}$ | ordering indicator: 1 iff train $i$ enters segment $\ell$ before train $k$ (used for opposite-direction conflicts) |
| $u_{is}, v_{is} \ge 0$ | linearization variables for retiming: early/late arrival deviation |

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize the weighted sum of total delay and total energy consumption plus cancellation penalties:

$$
\min \; Z \;=\; \alpha \sum_{i\in F}\left[\,(a_{i,\,s_i^{\text{end}}}-a_i)\,\right] \;+\; \beta \sum_{i\in F}\sum_{\ell\in L_i}\sum_{p\in P_i^\ell} e_{ip}^{\ell}\, x_{ip}^{\ell} \;+\; \sum_{i\in F} c_i^{\text{canc}}\, z_i
$$

with the arrival deviation linearized as

$$
a_{i,\,s_i^{\text{end}}} \;\le\; a_i + \Delta_i^{\max}\quad\text{(see C9)},\qquad
a_{i,\,s_i^{\text{end}}} - a_i \;=\; u_{i} - v_{i},\quad u_i, v_i \ge 0,
$$

so that $u_i$ equals the delay of train $i$ at the optimum. Objective:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i\in F} u_i \;+\; \beta \sum_{i\in F}\sum_{\ell\in L_i}\sum_{p\in P_i^\ell} e_{ip}^{\ell} x_{ip}^{\ell} \;+\; \sum_{i\in F} c_i^{\text{canc}} z_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route selection / track assignment.** Each non-cancelled train occupies exactly one track on each of its segments:

$$
y_{i}^{\ell,\text{op}} + y_{i}^{\ell,\text{re}} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall\, i\in F,\ \ell\in L_i
$$

**(C2) Rerouting restricted to the disruption window and disrupted segments.** Only during the disruption may trains use the opposite track:

$$
y_{i}^{\ell,\text{re}} \le [\text{entry time of } i \text{ on } \ell \le T_r] \cdot [\text{exit time} \ge T_d]
$$

Linearized with big-$M$ using $e_{i}^{\ell}$ (entry time onto segment $\ell$):

$$
e_i^{\ell} \ge T_d - M\big(1 - y_{i}^{\ell,\text{re}}\big), \qquad
e_i^{\ell} \le T_r + M\big(1 - y_{i}^{\ell,\text{re}}\big) \qquad \forall i,\ \ell\in L_i
$$

**(C3) Consistency of entry times and running times (coupling rescheduling ↔ speed profiles).** The running time between consecutive stations equals the running time implied by the selected profile:

$$
e_{i}^{\ell} \;=\; d_{i,\,s(\ell)} \qquad \forall i,\ \ell\in L_i
$$
$$
a_{i,\,s(\ell)+1} \;=\; e_{i}^{\ell} + \sum_{p\in P_i^\ell} r_{ip}^{\ell}\, x_{ip}^{\ell} \qquad \forall i,\ \ell\in L_i
$$

**(C4) Speed-profile selection.** Exactly one profile per non-cancelled train and segment:

$$
\sum_{p\in P_i^\ell} x_{ip}^{\ell} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i,\ \ell\in L_i
$$

**(C5) Dwell time bounds.**

$$
w_{\min} \,(1-z_i) \;\le\; d_{is} - a_{is} \;\le\; w_{\max}\,(1-z_i) \qquad \forall i,\ s\in S_i\setminus\{s_i^{\text{end}}\}
$$

**(C6) Same-direction headway on each track.** If train $i$ precedes train $k$ (both same direction) on track $m$ of segment $\ell$:

$$
e_{k}^{\ell} \;\ge\; e_{i}^{\ell} + h_{\min}^{\ell} - M\big(1 - \phi_{ik}^{\ell,m}\big) \qquad \forall i\neq k,\ \ell,\ m\in\{\text{op},\text{re}\}
$$

**(C7) Opposite-direction conflict resolution (single track shared by both directions).** On each track $m$ of segment $\ell$, for trains $i\in F^+$, $k\in F^-$ using that track, exactly one ordering holds and the second train may enter only after the first has cleared the segment (headway $h_{\min}^{\ell}$):

$$
e_{k}^{\ell} \;\ge\; e_{i}^{\ell} + r_i^{\ell} + h_{\min}^{\ell} - M\big(2 - y_{i}^{\ell,m} - y_{k}^{\ell,m} - \sigma_{ik}^{\ell}\big)
$$
$$
e_{i}^{\ell} \;\ge\; e_{k}^{\ell} + r_k^{\ell} + h_{\min}^{\ell} - M\big(1 - y_{i}^{\ell,m} - y_{k}^{\ell,m} + \sigma_{ik}^{\ell}\big)
$$
$$
y_{i}^{\ell,m} + y_{k}^{\ell,m} \;\le\; 1 + \sigma_{ik}^{\ell} + (1-\sigma_{ik}^{\ell}) \qquad\text{(linking, standard big-M pattern)}
$$

where $r_i^{\ell}=\sum_{p\in P_i^\ell} r_{ip}^{\ell} x_{ip}^{\ell}$ is the (linear) actual running time of train $i$ on $\ell$.

**(C8) Station capacity / route conflicts at stations.** For trains arriving at/departing from the same station with incompatible itineraries, mutual-exclusion ordering constraints analogous to (C6)–(C7) with safety margins $\delta^{\text{arr}}, \delta^{\text{dep}}$:

$$
d_{ks} \ge a_{is} + \delta^{\text{dep}} - M(1-\pi_{iks}), \qquad
a_{is} \ge d_{ks} + \delta^{\text{arr}} - M\,\pi_{iks}
$$

with binary variables $\pi_{iks}$ for each conflicting pair $(i,k)$ at station $s$.

**(C9) Maximum delay.**

$$
a_{i,\,s_i^{\text{end}}} \;\le\; a_i + \Delta_i^{\max} \qquad \forall i\in F
$$

**(C10) Disruption unavailability.** No train may traverse a disrupted segment *on its normally assigned (blocked) track* during $[T_d,T_r]$; this is enforced by forbidding the combination through (C1)–(C2): if the train's occupancy interval intersects the window, it must reroute ($y^{\text{re}}=1$, i.e. it uses the surviving track in the opposite direction's slot pattern) or wait at the preceding station:

$$
e_i^{\ell} + r_i^{\ell} \le T_d \quad\text{or}\quad e_i^{\ell} \ge T_r \quad \text{if } y_{i}^{\ell,\text{op}}=1 \text{ and } \ell\in\bar L
$$

Linearized: either branch via an auxiliary binary $g_i^{\ell}$ and big-$M$.

**(C11) Time horizon.**

$$
0 \;\le\; a_{is}, d_{is} \;\le\; T \qquad \forall i,\ s\in S_i
$$

**(C12) Variable domains.**

$$
x_{ip}^{\ell},\, y_{i}^{\ell,\text{op}},\, y_{i}^{\ell,\text{re}},\, z_i,\, \phi_{ik}^{\ell,m},\, \sigma_{ik}^{\ell},\, \pi_{iks} \in \{0,1\}; \qquad a_{is}, d_{is}, e_i^{\ell}, u_i, v_i \ge 0
$$

## 6. Remarks

- **Coupling.** Constraints (C3)–(C4) couple timetable decisions ($a, d, e$) with train-dynamics decisions ($x$ — speed profiles); this makes the model an *integrated* TRP+TSMP formulation: retiming and speed-profile (energy) choices are decided jointly.
- **Conflict-freeness.** Constraints (C6)–(C8) guarantee a conflict-free timetable both on segments (including bidirectional sharing of a single track during the blockage) and at stations.
- **Rerouting.** Variables $y^{\text{re}}$ implement the local rerouting strategy during the disruption window only ((C2)), amplifying but properly managing bidirectional conflicts via (C7).
- **Solution approach.** The MILP is combinatorially hard; the paper's framework decomposes it into a reformulated IP over train interactions plus per-train plans (each plan = a combination of times, route, and speed profile), solved by an adaptive iterative algorithm with plan refinement and local branching; with sufficiently fine plan granularity the IP is equivalent to this MILP.
- All parameters not given by the input (headways, dwell bounds, profile sets $P_i^\ell$, weights $\alpha,\beta$, penalties, $\Delta^{\max}$, horizon $T$) are assumed to be provided by the operator as calibration data (A6–A8).

Here it is:

# MILP for Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Parameters

**Sets**
- $T$: set of trains, $i \in T$
- $S$: set of track segments, $s \in S$
- $S_i \subseteq S$: ordered sequence of segments traversed by train $i$
- $K_{i,s}$: set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $s$
- $D$: set of ordered pairs of trains that may share a segment, $(i,j) \in D$
- $H \subseteq D$: headway-relevant ordered pairs

**Parameters**
- $a_i^{min}, a_i^{max}$: admissible arrival-time window at destination of train $i$
- $d_i^{min}, d_i^{max}$: admissible departure-time window at origin of train $i$
- $\underline{dw}_{i,s}, \overline{dw}_{i,s}$: min/max dwell time of train $i$ at end of segment $s$
- $\tau_{ij}^{s}$: minimum headway between trains $i$ and $j$ on segment $s$
- $\tau^{turn}_{i}$: minimum turnaround time for train $i$ (rolling stock)
- $[t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$: disruption time window; $\hat{s}$: blocked segment
- $\theta_i$: delay weight of train $i$; $\pi_i$: cancellation penalty of train $i$
- $\alpha$: energy cost coefficient (energy-to-time monetary conversion)
- $r_{i,s,k}$: running time of profile $k$; $e_{i,s,k}$: energy of profile $k$
- $M$: big-M constant (exceeds the planning horizon)
- $h_i$: scheduled (original) arrival time of train $i$ at destination

## 2. Decision Variables

- $a_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$: arrival time of train $i$ at end of segment $s$
- $d_{i,s} \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$: departure time of train $i$ from start of segment $s$
- $y_{i,s,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses profile $k$ on segment $s$
- $x_{i,j}^{s} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable on segment $s$; 1 if train $i$ precedes $j$
- $z_{i}^{opp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on $\hat{s}$
- $z_{i}^{nor} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ stays on its own track on $\hat{s}$
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled
- $\delta_i \in \mathbb{R}_{+}$: delay of train $i$ at destination

## 3. Objective Function

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} \theta_i \, \delta_i \;+\; \alpha \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S_i}\sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} e_{i,s,k}\, y_{i,s,k} \;+\; \sum_{i \in T} \pi_i \, c_i$$

Minimizes total weighted delays, total energy consumption, and cancellation penalties.

## 4. Constraints

**(C1) Departure time windows (origin):**
$$d_i^{min}(1-c_i) \le d_{i,s_0} \le d_i^{max}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s_0 = \text{first}(S_i)$$

**(C2) Arrival time window and delay at destination:**
$$a_i^{min} \le a_{i,s_n} \le a_i^{max} + \delta_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s_n = \text{last}(S_i)$$
$$\delta_i \ge a_{i,s_n} - h_i, \quad \delta_i \ge 0, \quad \forall i \in T$$

**(C3) Running time consistency with selected speed profile:**
$$a_{i,s} - d_{i,s} = \sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} r_{i,s,k}\, y_{i,s,k}, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S_i$$
$$\sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} y_{i,s,k} = 1 - c_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S_i$$

**(C4) Minimum/maximum dwell time and timetable propagation:**
$$d_{i,s'} - a_{i,s} \ge \underline{dw}_{i,s}(1-c_i), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s' = \text{succ}(s, S_i)$$
$$d_{i,s'} - a_{i,s} \le \overline{dw}_{i,s} + M c_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\; s' = \text{succ}(s, S_i)$$

**(C5) Cancellation propagation (a cancelled train occupies no resources):**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le M(1-c_i), \quad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S_i$$

**(C6) Headway / conflict-free constraints on each segment (same track):**
For all $(i,j) \in H$, $s \in S_i \cap S_j$:
$$a_{j,s} - d_{i,s} \ge \tau_{ij}^{s} - M(1 - x_{i,j}^{s}) - M c_j$$
$$a_{i,s} - d_{j,s} \ge \tau_{ji}^{s} - M\, x_{i,j}^{s} - M c_i$$
$$x_{i,j}^{s} + x_{j,i}^{s} = 1, \quad \forall (i,j) \in D,\; s \in S_i \cap S_j$$

**(C7) Rerouting to opposite track (disruption window):**

Track assignment consistency:
$$z_i^{opp} + z_i^{nor} = 1 - c_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\; \hat{s} \in S_i$$

Blocked own track during disruption window $[t_d^{start}, t_d^{end}]$ — a train on its own track must not occupy $\hat{s}$ in the window:
$$a_{i,\hat{s}} \le t_d^{start} + M(1 - z_i^{nor}) + M c_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\; \hat{s} \in S_i$$
$$d_{i,\hat{s}} \ge t_d^{end} - M(1 - z_i^{nor}) - M c_i, \quad \forall i \in T,\; \hat{s} \in S_i$$

Bidirectional conflict on the opposite track (trains rerouted there run in opposing directions; enforce non-overlap with headway):
$$a_{j,\hat{s}} - d_{i,\hat{s}} \ge \tau_{ij}^{\hat{s}} - M(1 - x_{i,j}^{\hat{s}}) - M(2 - z_i^{opp} - z_j^{opp}) - M c_j$$
$$a_{i,\hat{s}} - d_{j,\hat{s}} \ge \tau_{ji}^{\hat{s}} - M\, x_{i,j}^{\hat{s}} - M(2 - z_i^{opp} - z_j^{opp}) - M c_i$$
$$\forall (i,j) \in D,\; \hat{s} \in S_i \cap S_j$$

(The big-M terms $M(2 - z_i^{opp} - z_j^{opp})$ deactivate the constraint unless both trains are rerouted to the opposite track.)

**(C8) Rolling-stock / turnaround constraints:**
For each pair of trains $(i,j)$ where $j$'s rolling stock is released by $i$:
$$d_{j,s_0} \ge a_{i,s_n} + \tau^{turn}_{i} - M(c_i + c_j)$$

**(C9) Variable domains:**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, \delta_i \ge 0; \quad y_{i,s,k}, x_{i,j}^{s}, z_i^{opp}, z_i^{nor}, c_i \in \{0,1\}$$

## 5. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Retiming:** continuous variables $a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}$ reschedule all arrival/departure times subject to windows (C1, C2), dwell times (C4), and profile-consistent running times (C3).
- **Reordering:** binary sequencing variables $x_{i,j}^{s}$ choose train order on shared segments; exactly one order per pair, and headway constraints (C6) prevent conflicts.
- **Rerouting:** binaries $z_i^{opp}/z_i^{nor}$ assign trains to tracks on the blocked segment $\hat{s}$; trains keeping the own track must avoid the disruption window, while trains on the opposite track face bidirectional conflict constraints (C7).
- **Cancellation:** binary $c_i$ removes train $i$ (zeroes its profile selection, relaxes windows via big-M, and incurs penalty $\pi_i$ in the objective); C5 propagates cancellation across the whole route.
- **Speed management:** discrete profiles $k$ with time/energy pairs $(r_{i,s,k}, e_{i,s,k})$; exactly one profile per non-cancelled train-segment, and the running-time equality in C3 links timing decisions to energy choices.
- **Objective:** trades off weighted passenger/operational delay, energy cost (favoring slower, greener profiles when slack allows), and cancellation penalties.
- **Big-M:** $M$ must exceed any feasible time horizon (e.g., planning horizon length) to correctly deactivate relaxed constraints.

The model is fully linear in continuous and binary variables, making it a standard MILP solvable directly by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut solvers (e.g., CPLEX/Gurobi).

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

**Physical network.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor consists of a set of stations $S$ connected by segments $I = \{1,\dots,n\}$. Each segment $i$ has two tracks: the nominal track (direction $d \in \{up, down\}$) and the opposite track. A partial blockage affects a set of segments $I^B \subseteq I$ on one direction during the disruption time window $[T^s, T^e]$. Affected trains may **reroute** to the opposite track, which then carries bidirectional traffic requiring strict conflict-free coordination.

**Assumptions (stated explicitly, as some are not given in the input):**
- (A1) Trains run according to a given nominal timetable; each train $f \in F$ has a fixed station stopping pattern.
- (A2) For each train $f$ and segment $i$, a finite set $P_{fi}$ of candidate speed profiles is pre-generated (e.g., by a speed-profile generator), each characterized by minimum running time $r_{fi}^p$, energy consumption $e_{fi}^p$, and entry/exit speeds. This discretization is standard to keep the model linear.
- (A3) Rerouting is only possible on blocked segments during $[T^s, T^e]$; a switch-over time $\tau^{sw}$ is required at segment boundaries.
- (A4) Minimum headway $h$ (time separation) applies between consecutive trains on the same track of a segment; headway $h^{op}$ (typically larger) applies to opposing trains sharing a rerouted track.
- (A5) Dwell times at stations must lie in $[\underline{d}_s, \bar{d}_s]$; departure/arrival may deviate from the nominal timetable within a recovery horizon $[0, T^{max}]$.
- (A6) Cancellation is not considered (all trains must run), consistent with partial blockage scenarios.
- (A7) A train occupies a segment exclusively in time; overtaking is possible only at stations.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $F$ | set of trains; $F^{up}, F^{down}$: directional subsets |
| $I$ | segments; $I^B$: blocked segments; $S$: stations |
| $P_{fi}$ | candidate speed profiles of train $f$ on segment $i$ |
| $r_{fi}^p, e_{fi}^p$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $a_{f,s}^{nom}, d_{f,s}^{nom}$ | nominal arrival/departure of train $f$ at station $s$ |
| $h, h^{op}$ | same-direction / opposite-direction headways |
| $\underline{d}_s, \bar{d}_s$ | min/max dwell at station $s$ |
| $T^s, T^e$ | disruption start/end time |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $w_f$ | delay weight of train $f$ |
| $\alpha$ | energy cost coefficient |

## 3. Decision Variables

- $a_{f,s}, d_{f,s} \ge 0$: actual arrival / departure time of train $f$ at station $s$.
- $x_{fi}^p \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $i$.
- $y_{fi} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $f$ is **rerouted** to the opposite track on segment $i$ (only defined for $i \in I^B$).
- $z_{f'i,f} \in \{0,1\}$: ordering variable — 1 if train $f'$ traverses segment $i$ (on the same track as $f$) before train $f$.
- $\Delta_{f,s}^{arr}, \Delta_{f,s}^{dep} \ge 0$: arrival/departure delay at station $s$.

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay plus energy consumption:

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{f \in F}\sum_{s \in S} w_f\left(\Delta_{f,s}^{arr} + \Delta_{f,s}^{dep}\right) \;+\; \alpha \sum_{f \in F}\sum_{i \in I}\sum_{p \in P_{fi}} e_{fi}^p\, x_{fi}^p
\tag{1}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**Speed profile selection (exactly one profile per train–segment):**
$$
\sum_{p \in P_{fi}} x_{fi}^p = 1 \qquad \forall f \in F,\; i \in I
\tag{2}
$$

**Running time consistency (linking timetable and speed profiles):**
$$
d_{f,s_i} - a_{f,s_{i+1}} \le -\sum_{p \in P_{fi}} r_{fi}^p\, x_{fi}^p \qquad \forall f \in F,\; i \in I
\tag{3}
$$
i.e., departure at the upstream station plus the selected running time must not exceed arrival at the downstream station (written with sign convention $a_{f,s_{i+1}} \ge d_{f,s_i} + \sum_p r_{fi}^p x_{fi}^p$).

**Dwell time bounds:**
$$
\underline{d}_s \le d_{f,s} - a_{f,s} \le \bar{d}_s \qquad \forall f \in F,\; s \in S
\tag{4}
$$

**Delay definition:**
$$
\Delta_{f,s}^{arr} \ge a_{f,s} - a_{f,s}^{nom}, \qquad \Delta_{f,s}^{dep} \ge d_{f,s} - d_{f,s}^{nom} \qquad \forall f, s
\tag{5}
$$

**Horizon bounds:**
$$
0 \le a_{f,s}, d_{f,s} \le T^{max} \qquad \forall f, s
\tag{6}
$$

**Rerouting feasibility — rerouting only during the disruption window and only on blocked segments:**
$$
y_{fi} = 0 \qquad \forall f,\; i \notin I^B
\tag{7}
$$
$$
a_{f,s_{i+1}} \ge T^s \;\lor\; d_{f,s_i} \le T^e \;\lor\; y_{fi} = 0
\quad \text{(linearized: } a_{f,s_{i+1}} \ge T^s - M(1-y_{fi}),\; d_{f,s_i} \le T^e + M(1-y_{fi})\text{)}
\tag{8}
$$

**Rerouting switch-over time:** if train $f$ is rerouted on segment $i$, extra time $\tau^{sw}$ is added at the boundary:
$$
a_{f,s_{i+1}} \ge d_{f,s_i} + \sum_{p} r_{fi}^p x_{fi}^p + \tau^{sw}\, y_{fi} \qquad \forall f,\; i \in I^B
\tag{9}
$$

**Same-direction headway on the same track.** For trains $f, f'$ of the same direction on segment $i$, if both use the same track (i.e., $y_{fi} = y_{f'i}$), one must precede the other by at least $h$:
$$
a_{f',s_{i+1}} \ge d_{f,s_i} + h - M(1 - z_{f'i,f}) - M\,|y_{fi} - y_{f'i}|
\tag{10}
$$
$$
a_{f,s_{i+1}} \ge d_{f',s_i} + h - M\, z_{f'i,f} - M\,|y_{fi} - y_{f'i}|
\tag{11}
$$
(The term $|y_{fi}-y_{f'i}|$ is linearized with an auxiliary binary $u_{ff',i} \ge y_{fi} - y_{f'i}$, $u_{ff',i} \ge y_{f'i} - y_{fi}$.)

**Opposite-direction headway on a shared (rerouted) track.** If $f \in F^{up}$ is rerouted ($y_{fi}=1$) and $f' \in F^{down}$ is not ($y_{f'i}=0$), they share track $i$; separation $h^{op}$ applies:
$$
a_{f',s_{i+1}} \ge d_{f,s_i} + h^{op} - M(1 - z_{f'i,f}) - M(1 - y_{fi}) - M\, y_{f'i}
\tag{12}
$$
$$
a_{f,s_{i+1}} \ge d_{f',s_i} + h^{op} - M\, z_{f'i,f} - M(1 - y_{fi}) - M\, y_{f'i}
\tag{13}
$$
Analogous constraints (with roles of $y$ swapped) cover the case $f$ non-rerouted, $f'$ rerouted.

**Station overtaking / ordering consistency:** ordering variables must be consistent along the corridor (no crossing of two trains between stations unless they overtake at a station):
$$
z_{f'i,i} \ge z_{f'i,i+1} \quad \text{unless an overtaking station lies between } i \text{ and } i+1
\tag{14}
$$

**Variable domains:**
$$
a_{f,s}, d_{f,s}, \Delta_{f,s}^{arr}, \Delta_{f,s}^{dep} \ge 0; \qquad x_{fi}^p,\, y_{fi},\, z_{f'i,f} \in \{0,1\}
\tag{15}
$$

## 6. Remarks

- Constraints (2)–(3) couple the **timetable level** (TRP) with the **control level** (TSMP): the chosen speed profile determines the feasible running time, so the rescheduled timetable is guaranteed executable — this is the core integration.
- Constraints (7)–(9) restrict rerouting to the disruption time window on blocked segments and account for switch-over time.
- Constraints (10)–(13) ensure conflict-free operation, including the bidirectional conflicts arising when trains share the opposite track during partial blockage.
- The model is a valid MILP: all big-M terms are linearized with auxiliary binaries as indicated. As stated in the paper, this MILP can be decomposed into an IP over train interactions plus single-train plan subproblems, with plan granularity refined adaptively; with sufficiently fine profile sets $P_{fi}$, the IP is equivalent to this MILP.
