Text:
# Final Model: MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Assumptions

- **A1**: Each train *i* travels a fixed route through an ordered sequence of segments *S*; segment *s\** is the partially blocked segment.
- **A2**: For each train and segment, a finite, pre-generated set of speed profiles *K_{i,s}* is given with known running times *r_{i,s,k}* and energy consumptions *e_{i,s,k}*.
- **A3**: A train may be **cancelled** (*u_i = 1*), in which case all its scheduling constraints are relaxed and it occupies no infrastructure.
- **A4**: Segment *s\** is blocked during window [T1, T2]; each non-cancelled train must either pass **before T1**, wait and pass **after T2**, or be **rerouted** to the opposite track with entry within [T1, T2].
- **A5**: Headway separations are enforced on segment entry (departure) times.
- **A6**: Big-M constants are chosen validly (larger than any relevant time difference).
- **A7**: Delays are measured against ideal arrival times *a⁰_i* at the final segment; all parameters are deterministic and the planning horizon contains all movements.

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *I* | set of trains, indices *i, j* |
| *S* | ordered set of segments, index *s*; *s\** = disrupted segment |
| *K_{i,s}* | set of speed profiles for train *i* on segment *s*, index *k* |

## 3. Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *w_i* | delay weight of train *i* |
| *α* | energy cost scaling factor |
| *C^u* | cancellation penalty |
| *e_{i,s,k}* | energy consumption of profile *k* on segment *s* |
| *r_{i,s,k}* | running time of profile *k* on segment *s* |
| *a⁰_i* | ideal arrival time of train *i* at the final segment |
| *h_{i,j,s}* | minimum headway between trains *i* and *j* entering segment *s* |
| *T1, T2* | disruption window bounds on *s\** |
| *M* | sufficiently large constant |

## 4. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Domain | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| *t^dep_{i,s}* | ≥ 0 | departure (entry) time of train *i* onto segment *s* |
| *t^arr_{i,s}* | ≥ 0 | arrival time of train *i* at the end of segment *s* |
| *x_{i,s,k}* | binary | 1 if profile *k* is chosen on segment *s* |
| *u_i* | binary | 1 if train *i* is **cancelled** |
| *y^s_i* | binary | 1 if train *i* passes *s\** **before T1** |
| *y^o_i* | binary | 1 if train *i* waits and passes *s\** **after T2** |
| *z_i* | binary | 1 if train *i* is **rerouted** (uses the opposite track on *s\** within [T1, T2]) |

## 5. Objective Function

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I} w_i \left( t^{arr}_{i,|S|} - a^0_i \right)}_{\text{weighted final-arrival delay}} \;+\; \underbrace{\alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S}\sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} e_{i,s,k}\, x_{i,s,k}}_{\text{energy consumption}} \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{i \in I} C^u\, u_i}_{\text{cancellation penalties}}
$$

## 6. Constraints

**(1) Profile selection** (at most one profile per segment; none if cancelled):
$$
\sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} x_{i,s,k} \le 1 \qquad \forall i \in I,\ \forall s \in S \tag{1}
$$

**(2) Running time linking** (travel time equals the chosen profile's running time):
$$
t^{arr}_{i,s} - t^{dep}_{i,s} - \sum_{k \in K_{i,s}} r_{i,s,k}\, x_{i,s,k} \ge -M u_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s \tag{2}
$$

**(3) Continuity between consecutive segments**:
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s+1} - t^{arr}_{i,s} \ge -M u_i \qquad \forall i,\ \forall s < |S| \tag{3}
$$

**(4) Initial departure time**:
$$
t^{dep}_{i,1} \ge a^0_i - M u_i \qquad \forall i \tag{4}
$$

**(5) Delay nonnegativity** (arrival no earlier than ideal):
$$
t^{arr}_{i,|S|} \ge a^0_i - M u_i \qquad \forall i \tag{5}
$$

**(6) Closure blockage on *s\*** — non-rerouted trains must avoid [T1, T2]; rerouted trains (*z_i = 1*) are exempt via the *+M z_i* terms:

(6a) entry before closure (or exempt):
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s^*} \le T1 + M\left( y^o_i + z_i \right) + M u_i \qquad \forall i \tag{6a}
$$

(6b) entry after closure (or exempt):
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s^*} \ge T2 - M\left( y^s_i + z_i \right) - M u_i \qquad \forall i \tag{6b}
$$

**(7)–(10) Headways on entry times** (relaxed if either train is cancelled or rerouted, since rerouted trains use the opposite track):
$$
t^{dep}_{j,s} - t^{dep}_{i,s} \ge h_{i,j,s} - M\left( u_i + u_j + z_i + z_j \right) \qquad \forall i \ne j,\ \forall s \tag{7}
$$
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s} - t^{dep}_{j,s} \ge h_{j,i,s} - M\left( u_i + u_j + z_i + z_j \right) \qquad \forall i \ne j,\ \forall s \tag{8}
$$
(9)–(10): analogous constraints for the remaining ordered pairs *(i, j)* covering all combinations.

**(11) Reroute entry window** — rerouted trains must enter *s\** within the disruption window:
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s^*} \ge T1 - M(1 - z_i), \qquad t^{dep}_{i,s^*} \le T2 + M(1 - z_i) \qquad \forall i \tag{11}
$$

**(12) Nonnegative delay**:
$$
t^{arr}_{i,|S|} - a^0_i \ge 0 \qquad \forall i \tag{12}
$$

**(13)–(14) Option selection logic** — each non-cancelled train chooses exactly one of the three options on *s\**; cancelled trains choose none:
$$
y^s_i + y^o_i + z_i \le 1 - u_i \qquad \forall i \tag{13}
$$
$$
y^s_i + y^o_i + z_i \ge 1 - u_i \qquad \forall i \tag{14}
$$

**(15) Variable domains**:
$$
t^{dep}_{i,s},\ t^{arr}_{i,s} \ge 0;\quad x_{i,s,k},\ u_i,\ y^s_i,\ y^o_i,\ z_i \in \{0,1\} \qquad \forall i, s, k \tag{15}
$$

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Objective**: trades off passenger-weighted delay, total traction energy (via profile choice — slower profiles save energy but increase delay), and cancellation penalties.
- **(2)–(5)**: propagate each train along its route; the *−M u_i* terms make all timing constraints vacuous for cancelled trains, so a cancelled train contributes only *C^u*.
- **(6a)–(6b) vs (11)**: a non-rerouted train (*z_i = 0*) is forced around the closure window by (6); a rerouted train (*z_i = 1*) is exempt from (6) by the *+M z_i* terms and instead forced *into* [T1, T2] by (11).
- **(7)–(10)**: enforce pairwise headways on segment entry times, relaxed when either train is cancelled or rerouted (rerouted trains use the opposite track, so headways on the original track do not apply).
- **(13)–(14)**: force each active train to pick exactly one of the three routing options, and cancelled trains to pick none.

## 8. Model Summary — Three Disjoint Options on Segment *s\**

| Option | *z_i* | *y^s_i* | *y^o_i* | Entry time *t^dep_{i,s\*}* | Enforced by |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pass before T1** | 0 | 1 | 0 | ≤ T1 | (6a), (13)–(14) |
| **Wait, pass after T2** | 0 | 0 | 1 | ≥ T2 | (6b), (13)–(14) |
| **Reroute (opposite track)** | 1 | 0 | 0 | ∈ [T1, T2] | (11); (6a)–(6b) exempt via *+M z* |
| *(Cancelled)* | 0 | 0 | 0 | unconstrained | *u_i = 1* relaxes all |

**Linearity note**: All constraints are linear; every disjunction (ordering, closure-window logic, rerouting conditions, cancellation) is handled with standard big-M relaxations, so the model is a pure MILP solvable by branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut. Big-M values should be chosen as tight as possible (e.g., based on the planning horizon) to keep the LP relaxation strong.

Text:
# TRSMP — Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Model (MILP)

Below are the equations of the complete linear model, based on the generated formulation. Assumptions are marked where data was missing.

## Sets and Parameters

- **S** = set of stations {S₀, S₁, S₂, S₃}; **E** = set of segments between consecutive stations
- **T** = set of trains, each with direction dir(t) ∈ {+1, −1}
- **K(t,e)** = discrete speed profiles for train t on segment e, each with running time rᵗᵉₖ and energy consumption Eᵗᵉₖ *(assumption: 3 profiles per train–segment, generated around a base running time)*
- **[dˢ, dᵉ]** = disruption time window on disrupted segment e* (partial blockage: one track unusable)
- h = minimum headway on segments; h_s = headway at stations; [d̲ᵗ, d̄ᵗ], [a̲ᵗ, āᵗ] = departure/arrival time windows
- dwell̲, dwell̄ = min/max dwell times at intermediate stations
- wᵃ, wᵈ = arrival/departure delay weights; πᵗ = cancellation penalty; c_e = energy cost coefficient
- C(s) = station capacity *(assumed 2)*; M = big-M constant

## Decision Variables

- a(t,s), d(t,s) ≥ 0 — actual arrival/departure times (retiming)
- x(t,e,k) ∈ {0,1} — speed profile selection
- o(e,i,j) ∈ {0,1} — reordering: train i enters segment e before train j (same direction)
- ρ(t,e) ∈ {0,1} — rerouting: train t uses the opposite track on segment e
- zᵇ(t), zᵃ(t) ∈ {0,1} — entry before disruption start / after disruption end
- b(e,i,j) ∈ {0,1} — occupancy order for bidirectional conflicts
- ov(s,i,j), ovc(s,i,j) ∈ {0,1} — simultaneous station presence indicators
- dᵃ(t,s), dᵈ(t,s) ≥ 0 — positive-part arrival/departure delays
- γ(t) ∈ {0,1} — cancellation of train t
- ent(t,e) ≥ 0 — entry time of train t onto segment e

## Objective Function

Minimize weighted delays + cancellation penalties + energy consumption:

min Σₜ Σₛ ( wᵃ·dᵃ(t,s) + wᵈ·dᵈ(t,s) ) + Σₜ πᵗ·γ(t) + c_e · Σₜ Σₑ Σₖ Eᵗᵉₖ · x(t,e,k)

## Constraints

**1. Delay definition (positive part, deactivated if cancelled):**
- dᵃ(t,s) ≥ a(t,s) − aᵖˡ(t,s) − M·γ(t)
- dᵃ(t,s) ≤ a(t,s) − aᵖˡ(t,s) + M·(1−γ(t));  dᵃ(t,s) ≤ M·(1−γ(t))
- (analogously for dᵈ(t,s) with d(t,s) and dᵖˡ(t,s))

**2. Timetable–speed-profile consistency (running-time chain):**
- a(t, s⁺) = d(t, s) + Σₖ rᵗᵉₖ · x(t,e,k)  for each segment e = (s, s⁺)
- ent(t,e) = d(t, s)

**3. Speed profile selection:**
- Σₖ x(t,e,k) = 1 − γ(t)  ∀ t, e (exactly one profile if not cancelled)

**4. Dwell time bounds (intermediate stations):**
- dwell̲ − M·γ(t) ≤ d(t,s) − a(t,s) ≤ dwell̄ + M·γ(t)

**5. Departure/arrival time windows:**
- d̲ᵗ − M·γ(t) ≤ d(t, s₀) ≤ d̄ᵗ + M·γ(t)
- a̲ᵗ − M·γ(t) ≤ a(t, s_N) ≤ āᵗ + M·γ(t)

**6. Disruption blocking (partial blockage disjunction):** for each train t on disrupted segment e*:
- zᵇ(t) + zᵃ(t) + ρ(t,e*) ≥ 1 − γ(t)
- ent(t,e*) ≤ dˢ + M·(1 − zᵇ(t))
- ent(t,e*) ≥ dᵉ − M·(1 − zᵃ(t))

i.e., a train either passes before the disruption, after it, or reroutes onto the opposite track.

**7. Rerouting restriction:**
- ρ(t,e) = 0 ∀ e ≠ e* (rerouting only on the disrupted segment)

**8. Same-direction headway (same track):** for trains i, j with dir(i)=dir(j) on segment e, with σᵢⱼ = 1 − ρ(i,e)·ρ(j,e) (both on own track):
- ent(j,e) − ent(i,e) ≥ h − M·(2 − o(e,i,j) − σᵢⱼ) − M·γ(i) − M·γ(j)
- ent(i,e) − ent(j,e) ≥ h − M·(1 + o(e,i,j) − σᵢⱼ) − M·γ(i) − M·γ(j)

**9. Bidirectional conflicts on shared track** (dir(i) ≠ dir(j), segment e): non-overlapping occupancy intervals [ent, ent + running time]:
- ent(j,e) − (ent(i,e) + Σₖ rⁱᵉₖ·x(i,e,k)) ≥ h − M·(1 − b(e,i,j)) − M·(1 − ρ(i,e)) − M·γ(i) − M·γ(j)
- ent(i,e) − (ent(j,e) + Σₖ rʲᵉₖ·x(j,e,k)) ≥ h − M·b(e,i,j) − M·(1 − ρ(i,e)) − M·γ(i) − M·γ(j)

**10. Station capacity:** pairwise overlap binaries ov(s,i,j) = 1 if trains i and j are simultaneously at station s:
- a(i,s) − d(j,s) ≤ M·(1 − ov(s,i,j)) − M·γ(i)
- a(j,s) − d(i,s) ≤ M·ov(s,i,j) − M·γ(j)
- Σ_{(i,j)} ovc(s,i,j) ≤ C(C(s), 2), with ovc(s,i,j) = ov(s,i,j)

**11. Cancellation limit:**
- Σₜ γ(t) ≤ Γ_max *(assumed 1)*

## Notes and Assumptions

- **Assumed data:** 3 speed profiles per train–segment (fast/high-energy to slow/low-energy), station capacity 2, max 1 cancellation, uniform headways, big-M = 500 exceeding the planning horizon.
- The model is fully linear: running times and energy are linearized through the binary profile-selection variables x(t,e,k); all sequencing/disjunction constraints use big-M formulations.
- Cancelled trains (γ(t)=1) are exempted from timetable, headway, disruption, and dwell constraints via big-M relaxation, and incur penalty πᵗ in the objective.
- The formulation matches the paper's structure: simultaneous retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation, and speed-profile optimization yielding a conflict-free, control-level-executable timetable.

Text:
# MILP: Conflict Detection and Resolution for Railway Traffic under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

Based on the input (a CDR model for ETCS L2 with trackside train detection, extending RECIFE-MILP), the following model is presented. Assumptions are explicitly marked.

---

## 1. Problem Description

Given:
- A railway corridor partitioned into fixed track sections (TDSs), with a distinction between **switch areas** and **open-line/station sections** (Assumption A1).
- A set of trains $T$, a set of sections $S$, and a reference (scheduled) timetable with planned passage times.
- A disruption causing initial delays.
- A set of **speed profile options** per train (Assumption A2), each with train- and speed-dependent running times and braking distances.

Find: a rescheduled timetable (retiming, reordering, local rerouting) such that all conflicts (section occupancy, headway, route conflicts) are resolved and total delay is minimised.

**Assumptions**
- **A1:** The network is a linear corridor; rerouting is modelled via alternative routes (sequences of sections) per train where available; otherwise a single route.
- **A2:** Each train $t$ has a finite set $P_t$ of speed profile options; each option $p$ prescribes a fixed running time on each section and a braking distance to the EoA. This linearises the speed-dependent braking (no nonlinear dynamics).
- **A3:** Minimum headway between consecutive trains on a section equals the blocking time of the follower, which depends on the follower's speed profile option (speed-dependent separation under DTG).
- **A4:** Dwell times are within given bounds; initial delays are known constants.
- **A5:** Rolling stock circulation is unchanged (no re-assignment of units).

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T$ | set of trains |
| $S$ | set of track sections (TDSs) |
| $R_t$ | set of feasible routes for train $t$; each route $r$ is an ordered subset of $S$ |
| $P_t$ | set of speed profile options for train $t$ |
| $a_t$ | scheduled arrival time of train $t$ at destination |
| $d_t$ | scheduled departure time of train $t$ at origin |
| $\tau^{run}_{tsp}$ | running time of train $t$ on section $s$ with speed profile $p$ |
| $\tau^{dwell,min}_t, \tau^{dwell,max}_t$ | min/max dwell time of train $t$ at intermediate stations |
| $h_{tp}$ | minimum headway (blocking time incl. speed-dependent approach/braking distance) that train $t$ with profile $p$ imposes on the preceding train on a section |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $\delta_t \ge 0$ | initial delay of train $t$ (constant) |
| $H$ | scheduling horizon |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $x_{ts}$ | actual passage (entry) time of train $t$ at section $s$ (continuous, $\ge 0$) |
| $y_{tr} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses route $r \in R_t$ |
| $z_{tp} \in \{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $p \in P_t$ |
| $o_{ts} \in \{0,1\}$ | ordering variable: 1 if train $t$ passes section $s$ before train $t'$ (for each unordered pair on shared sections) |
| $D_t \ge 0$ | final delay of train $t$ at destination |

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total train delay:

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{t \in T} D_t$$

(Alternative objectives, e.g. weighted delay $\sum_t w_t D_t$, are possible.)

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route and profile choice (exactly one each):**
$$\sum_{r \in R_t} y_{tr} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T$$
$$\sum_{p \in P_t} z_{tp} = 1 \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(C2) Delay definition (final delay at destination $s^{end}_t$):**
$$D_t \ge x_{t,s^{end}_t} + \tau^{run}_{t,s^{end}_t,p} - a_t - M(1 - z_{tp}) \qquad \forall t \in T,\; p \in P_t$$
$$D_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(C3) Running time propagation along the chosen route:** for consecutive sections $s, s'$ on route $r$ of train $t$:
$$x_{t,s'} \ge x_{t,s} + \tau^{run}_{t,s,p} + \tau^{dwell,min}_t \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\{s \text{ station}\}} - M\big(2 - y_{tr} - z_{tp}\big)$$
$$x_{t,s'} \le x_{t,s} + \tau^{run}_{t,s,p} + \tau^{dwell,max}_t \cdot \mathbb{1}_{\{s \text{ station}\}} + M\big(2 - y_{tr} - z_{tp}\big)$$
$$\forall t \in T,\; r \in R_t,\; p \in P_t,\; (s,s') \text{ consecutive on } r$$

**(C4) Initial delay at origin:**
$$x_{t,s^{orig}_t} \ge d_t + \delta_t \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(C5) Headway / conflict-free section occupancy (DTG speed-dependent separation):** for each pair $(t, t')$ sharing section $s$ (i.e., $s \in r \cap r'$ for some $r \in R_t, r' \in R_{t'}$), with $t$ following $t'$:
$$x_{t,s} \ge x_{t',s} + \sum_{p \in P_t} h_{tp}\, z_{tp} - M(1 - o_{ts,t'})$$
$$x_{t',s} \ge x_{t,s} + \sum_{p \in P_{t'}} h_{t'p}\, z_{t'p} - M\, o_{ts,t'}$$

Here $h_{tp}$ includes the speed-dependent approach distance to the first occupied section, i.e., the braking distance from the brake indication point to the EoA under profile $p$ (Assumption A3). This is the key DTG enhancement: the headway is train- and speed-dependent rather than a fixed number of blocks.

**(C6) Switch-area exclusivity (no simultaneous route locking):** for trains $t \ne t'$ whose routes overlap on a switch area $w \subset S$, the entire traversal must be separated:
$$x_{t', s^{first}_w} \ge x_{t, s^{last}_w} + \tau^{run}_{t,s^{last}_w,p} + \epsilon - M(1 - o_{tw,t'}) - M(2-y_{tr} - z_{tp})$$
$$x_{t, s^{first}_w} \ge x_{t', s^{last}_w} + \tau^{run}_{t',s^{last}_w,p'} + \epsilon - M\, o_{tw,t'} - M(2-y_{t'r'} - z_{t'p'})$$
for all feasible $(r,p)$, $(r',p')$ combinations, where $s^{first}_w, s^{last}_w$ are the first/last sections of switch area $w$ and $\epsilon$ is a minimum switching margin. (Big-M terms deactivate the constraint if the route/profile is not chosen.)

**(C7) Consistency of ordering across sections (no overtake within a switch area):** if train $t$ precedes $t'$ on the first section of a shared route segment, it precedes on all its sections (linear ordering consistency, standard in RECIFE-MILP):
$$o_{ts,t'} \ge o_{t,s^{first},t'} - M \cdot \big(\text{route divergence indicator}\big)$$
simplified (Assumption A6: overtaking only at stations):
$$o_{ts,t'} = o_{t,s^{first},t'} \qquad \forall s \text{ on the shared open-line segment}$$

**(C8) Variable bounds:**
$$0 \le x_{ts} \le H \qquad \forall t \in T,\; s \in S$$
$$D_t \ge 0,\quad y_{tr}, z_{tp}, o_{ts,t'} \in \{0,1\}$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

- **Continuous variables:** passage times $x_{ts}$, delays $D_t$.
- **Binary variables:** route choice $y_{tr}$, speed-profile choice $z_{tp}$, ordering $o_{ts,t'}$.
- **Objective:** minimise total final delay $\sum_t D_t$.
- **Key DTG features:** (i) speed-profile options $z_{tp}$ allowing retiming with adjusted speed profiles; (ii) train- and speed-dependent headways $h_{tp}$ replacing fixed-block separation; (iii) explicit switch-area constraints (C6).

The model is a standard big-M MILP, solvable by branch-and-bound; it generalises RECIFE-MILP by replacing fixed blocking times with profile-dependent ones and adding the profile-selection dimension.

Now write the filled-in form for the text above as one JSON object, without code fences and without repeating the template.

# MILP: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Infrastructure Feasibility

Below is a complete linear model combining the **composition model** (rolling stock assignment, based on Fioole et al., 2006) with an **infrastructure feasibility check** handled via Combinatorial Benders–style cuts. Missing details are marked as assumptions.

---

## 1. Sets and indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $T$ | Train trips in the (timetabled) passenger service; index $t$ |
| $S$ | Stations; index $s$ |
| $U$ | Train unit types (e.g., VIRM-4, ICM-3); index $u$ |
| $D$ | Shunting movements at considered stations; index $d$ |
| $K$ | Tracks at station $s$; index $k \in K_s$ |
| $E$ | Infrastructure events (train passages and shunting movements) on a track; index $e$ |
| $C$ | Set of infeasible combinations of shunting movements found so far (Benders cuts); index $c$ |

Assumption: the disruption has a known start and end time; the planning horizon covers the disruption period plus recovery.

## 2. Parameters

- $n_u$: number of available units of type $u$.
- $cap_u$, $seats_u$: capacity and number of seats of a unit of type $u$.
- $q_t$: required seat capacity on trip $t$ (forecast demand).
- $a_{t}, b_t$: arrival / departure station of trip $t$.
- $\tau_t$: scheduled duration of trip $t$.
- $w^{cap}, w^{dev}, w^{shunt}, w^{delay}$: weights for capacity shortage, deviation from plan, number of shunting movements, and delay.
- $\Delta^{max}$: maximum allowed delay of a train to enable a shunting movement (assumption: a few minutes, e.g., 5).
- $I_{dt}$: = 1 if shunting movement $d$ supports the composition change needed around trip $t$ (e.g., coupling/uncoupling at a station).
- $\sigma_{es}$: start time of event $e$ at station $s$; $l_e$: duration.
- $M$: big constant (e.g., horizon length).

## 3. Variables

**Rolling stock (composition) variables**

- $x_{tu} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $u$ on trip $t$.
- $y_{tu} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if type $u$ is used on trip $t$ (composition change indicator).
- $z_{d} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if shunting movement $d$ is performed.
- $r_{su} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: number of units of type $u$ present (buffered) at station $s$ at the end of the horizon.

**Infrastructure variables**

- $\delta_e \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: delay (minutes) assigned to event $e$, $\delta_e \le \Delta^{max}$.
- $o_{ee'} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if event $e$ is ordered before event $e'$ on the same track.
- $p_{ek} \in \{0,1\}$: = 1 if event $e$ uses track $k$.

## 4. Objective function

$$
\min \; w^{cap}\sum_{t\in T}\, q^{short}_t \;+\; w^{dev}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{u\in U} c^{dev}_{tu}\, y_{tu} \;+\; w^{shunt}\sum_{d\in D} z_d \;+\; w^{delay}\sum_{e\in E} \delta_e
$$

where $q^{short}_t \ge 0$ is a slack variable for capacity shortage on trip $t$, and $c^{dev}_{tu}$ measures deviation of the composition from the original plan (assumption: derived from the original rolling stock plan).

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Composition constraints

**(C1) Seat capacity**

$$
\sum_{u \in U} seats_u \, x_{tu} + q^{short}_t \ge q_t \qquad \forall t \in T
$$

**(C2) Composition consistency**

$$
x_{tu} \le n_u \, y_{tu} \qquad \forall t \in T,\; u \in U
$$

**(C3) Rolling stock balance per station and time** (flow conservation; units arriving on trips plus shunt-in movements equal units departing plus shunt-out movements):

$$
\sum_{t:\, b_t = s} x_{tu} + \sum_{d:\, dest(d)=s} z_d \, m_{du}
=
\sum_{t:\, a_t = s,\, \tau_t \le \tau_{t'}} x_{t'u} + \sum_{d:\, orig(d)=s} z_d \, m_{du} + r_{su}
\qquad \forall s \in S,\; u \in U
$$

where $m_{du}$ is the number of units of type $u$ moved by shunt $d$ (assumption: $m_{du} \in \{0,1\}$).

**(C4) Fleet size**

$$
\sum_{s \in S} r_{su} + \sum_{t \in T} x_{tu} \;\le\; n_u \qquad \forall u \in U
$$

**(C5) Shunting only if needed**

$$
z_d \le \sum_{t \in T} I_{dt}\, y_{tu} \qquad \forall d \in D,\; u \in U
$$

### 5.2 Infrastructure constraints (feasibility of shunting movements)

**(I1) Each event uses exactly one track at its station**

$$
\sum_{k \in K_s} p_{ek} = 1 \qquad \forall e \in E_s
$$

**(I2) No overlap on a track** (disjunctive ordering; for events $e, e'$ that could share a track):

$$
\sigma_e + l_e + \delta_e \;\le\; \sigma_{e'} + \delta_{e'} + M(1 - o_{ee'}) + M(2 - p_{ek} - p_{e'k})
\qquad \forall e<e',\; k \in K_s
$$

$$
\sigma_{e'} + l_{e'} + \delta_{e'} \;\le\; \sigma_e + \delta_e + M\, o_{ee'} + M(2 - p_{ek} - p_{e'k})
\qquad \forall e<e',\; k \in K_s
$$

**(I3) Shunting movement performed only if infrastructure-feasible** — link: if $z_d = 1$, the corresponding event must be scheduled without excessive delay:

$$
\delta_{e(d)} \le \Delta^{max} + M(1 - z_d) \qquad \forall d \in D
$$

**(I4) Delay limits**

$$
0 \le \delta_e \le \Delta^{max} \qquad \forall e \in E
$$

### 5.3 Combinatorial Benders cuts

After solving the composition model, the infrastructure model checks the suggested set $Z = \{d : z_d = 1\}$. If infeasible, add a **no-good cut**:

$$
\sum_{d \in Z} z_d - \sum_{d \notin Z} z_d \;\le\; |Z| - 1 \qquad (c \in C)
$$

More refined cuts (assumption: derived from the conflict set $F_c \subseteq Z$ of mutually infeasible shunts identified by the infrastructure model):

$$
\sum_{d \in F_c} z_d \;\le\; |F_c| - 1 \qquad \forall c \in C
$$

The algorithm iterates: solve composition model → check infrastructure → add cuts → repeat until no infeasibility is found.

## 6. Assumptions (explicit)

1. Demand $q_t$ and the original plan are known; deviation costs $c^{dev}_{tu}$ are precomputed.
2. Delays of at most $\Delta^{max}$ minutes are absorbed by timetable buffers and thus allowed.
3. Shunting durations $l_e$ are fixed and known.
4. Each shunting movement moves at most one unit ($m_{du} \in \{0,1\}$).
5. Crew availability for shunting is assumed sufficient (not modeled).
6. The heuristic variant feeds shunting movements one by one to the infrastructure model, mimicking the split between rolling stock and infrastructure dispatchers; the MILP above represents the exact combined model.

# MILP for Conflict Detection and Resolution under Distance-to-Go (DTG) Signalling

An enhanced RECIFE-MILP formulation. Missing information is replaced by assumptions, marked **[A]**.

---

## 1. Assumptions

- **[A1]** The network is a set of *routes* (paths through the infrastructure). Each train traverses exactly one pre-defined route; local rerouting is modelled by allowing a choice among a small set of alternative routes per train.
- **[A2]** Track resources are: TTD sections (blocks) `s ∈ S` and switches `w ∈ W`. A route `r` occupies a set `S(r)` of sections and `W(r)` of switches.
- **[A3]** Each train `t ∈ T` has a set of *speed profile options* `p ∈ P_t` on each route, each with a fixed running time `τ_{t,r,p}` and a *speed-dependent* blocking time `b_{t,r,p,s}` on section `s` (including the DTG braking/approach distance, which depends on the train's speed at the brake indication point).
- **[A4]** The timetable is periodic-free (single planning horizon `[0, H]`); delays are non-negative deviations from scheduled passing times.
- **[A5]** Rolling-stock, dwell-time and driver-behaviour variations are captured by an initial (primary) delay `δ⁰_t` per train.
- **[A6]** Headway times between consecutive trains on the same resource are aggregated into the blocking times (no separate headway constraints).

---

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `T` | trains; `R_t` alternative routes of train `t`; `P_{t,r}` speed profiles |
| `S, W` | TTD sections, switches |
| `d_t` | scheduled exit time of train `t` from the network |
| `δ⁰_t` | initial delay of train `t` |
| `τ_{t,r,p}` | running time of train `t` on route `r` with profile `p` |
| `b_{t,r,p,s}` | blocking time of section `s` (DTG: speed-dependent, includes braking distance) |
| `b_{t,r,p,w}` | blocking time of switch `w` |
| `M` | big-M (e.g., `H + max δ⁰`) |
| `L_t` | minimum connection/turnaround time of train `t` to its successor (if any) |

---

## 3. Variables

**Binary**

- `x_{t,r,p} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train `t` uses route `r` with speed profile `p`.
- `y_{t,t',r,r',p,p',s} ∈ {0,1}` — 1 if train `t` (route `r`, profile `p`) passes section `s` **before** train `t'` (route `r'`, profile `p'`); defined for pairs of trains sharing at least one resource.
- `z_{t,t',r,r',p,p',w} ∈ {0,1}` — analogous ordering variable for switches.

**Continuous**

- `e_t ≥ 0` — exit (passing) time of train `t` at the end of its route.
- `δ_t ≥ 0` — final delay of train `t`.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimise total delay:

```
min  Σ_{t∈T} δ_t
```

*(Alternative: weighted delay `Σ w_t δ_t`, or max-plus second term `M' Σ δ_t` for lexicographic robustness.)*

---

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route/profile choice — exactly one option per train:**

```
Σ_{r∈R_t} Σ_{p∈P_{t,r}} x_{t,r,p} = 1        ∀ t ∈ T
```

**(C2) Exit time definition:**

```
e_t = d_t + δ⁰_t + δ_t
    + Σ_{r,p} x_{t,r,p} · τ_{t,r,p}          ∀ t ∈ T
```

i.e., the exit time equals scheduled time plus initial delay plus rescheduled delay plus running time of the chosen profile.

**(C3) Non-negativity of rescheduled delay:**

```
δ_t ≥ 0        ∀ t ∈ T
```

**(C4) No-overlap on TTD sections (DTG blocking times).** For every pair of trains `t, t'` sharing section `s`, for every combination of routes and profiles:

```
e_t − Σ_{r,p} x_{t,r,p}·b_{t,r,p,s}
      − e_{t'} + Σ_{r',p'} x_{t',r',p',s}·b_{t',r',p',s}
      + M · y_{t,t',r,r',p,p',s}  ≤  M − b_{t',r',p',s} − b_{t,r,p,s}
```

and symmetrically with `y` flipped:

```
e_{t'} − ... − e_t + ... + M(1 − y_{...}) ≤ M − b_{t,r,p,s} − b_{t',r',p',s}
```

In compact standard form (as in RECIFE-MILP), for each conflicting pair on resource `s`:

```
e_{t'} − e_t ≥ b_{t,r,p,s} − M(1 − y_{t,t',...,s}) − M(2 − x_{t,r,p} − x_{t',r',p'})
e_t − e_{t'} ≥ b_{t',r',p',s} − M·y_{t,t',...,s}   − M(2 − x_{t,r,p} − x_{t',r',p'})
```

These ensure that if `t` precedes `t'` on `s`, the exit-time gap covers the (speed-dependent) blocking time of the follower — this is where DTG enters: `b` grows with braking distance, hence with speed profile choice.

**(C5) No-overlap on switches** — identical structure to (C4) with `b_{t,r,p,w}` and variables `z_{t,t',r,r',p,p',w}`, distinguishing switches from plain sections (different blocking/locking times).

**(C6) Consistency of ordering across shared resources (optional, tightens formulation):** for trains `t, t'` sharing two consecutive resources `s₁, s₂`, forbid crossing orders:

```
y_{t,t',...,s₁} = y_{t,t',...,s₂}        (valid inequality)
```

**(C7) Minimum turnaround/connection time** (if train `t'` is the scheduled successor of `t`):

```
e_{t'} ≥ e_t + L_{t,t'} − M(1 − x_{t',r',p'}) ... (linearised over chosen options)
```

**(C8) Variable domains:**

```
x ∈ {0,1},  y ∈ {0,1},  z ∈ {0,1},  e_t ≥ 0,  δ_t ≥ 0
```

---

## 6. DTG-Specific Enhancement (summary)

The key deviation from conventional fixed-block RECIFE-MILP:

1. **Speed profile options** `p` appear as first-class binary decisions, changing both running times `τ` and blocking times `b`.
2. **Blocking times are train- and speed-dependent**: `b_{t,r,p,s} = t_block,base + v_p²/(2·a_brake,t·k_conv)` — the approach/braking distance to the first occupied section depends on the train's entry speed under profile `p`, so the brake indication point may lie anywhere on the track rather than at a fixed signal.

All constraints remain linear; the model is a MILP solvable by standard branch-and-bound.

# MILP: Rolling Stock Rescheduling with Shunting Feasibility

Based on the paper, I formulate the **composition model** (based on Fioole et al., 2006) with an integrated infrastructure-feasibility mechanism handled via Combinatorial Benders' cuts. Sets, parameters, and assumptions not given in the text are marked as *(assumption)*.

---

## 1. Sets and indices

| Set | Description |
|---|---|
| $S$ | stations; $s \in S$ |
| $T$ | train trips (timetabled passenger services); $t \in T$ |
| $V$ | train unit types (e.g., VIRM-4, VIRM-6, ICM-4); $v \in V$ |
| $D$ | shunting tasks (deadheading, parking, repositioning) at station $s$; $d \in D_s$ |
| $K$ | shunting movements at considered stations; $k \in K$ *(assumption: each $k$ is a movement of one train unit at Utrecht Centraal or Rotterdam Centraal)* |
| $P$ | paths through the infrastructure network of a station; $p \in P_s$ *(assumption: pre-enumerated conflict-free route/track paths per station)* |
| $E$ | events (arrivals, departures, shunting movements) at considered stations; $e \in E$ |
| $\mathcal{C}$ | set of generated infeasibility cuts (initially empty) |

## 2. Parameters

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| $c_v$ | fixed capital cost of using a train unit of type $v$ *(assumption)* |
| $m_v$ | number of available units of type $v$ |
| $\kappa_v$ | capacity (seats) of type $v$ |
| $q_t$ | required seat capacity on trip $t$ (expected demand) |
| $\ell_t, u_t$ | min/max number of units allowed on trip $t$ (composition length limits) |
| $a_{tv}$ | allowed (1) / forbidden (0) composition of type $v$ on trip $t$ |
| $M$ | big-M constant |
| $\delta^{\max}$ | maximum allowed delay (minutes) for passenger trains *(assumption: a few minutes, e.g., 5)* |
| $\pi_e$ | planned time of event $e$ |
| $w_p$ | set of events occupying path $p$; event $e$ occupies path $p$ if $e \in w_p$ |
| $\beta_e$ | weight of delay of event $e$ in the objective |
| $o_k$ | penalty for canceling shunting movement $k$ |
| $\sigma_{kt}$ | 1 if shunting movement $k$ supports trip $t$'s composition, else 0 *(assumption)* |

## 3. Variables

**Composition variables**
- $x_{tv} \in \mathbb{Z}_+$: number of units of type $v$ assigned to trip $t$.
- $y_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trip $t$ is operated, 0 if canceled.
- $n_v \in \mathbb{Z}_+$: number of units of type $v$ used in the circulation.

**Shunting variables**
- $z_k \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if shunting movement $k$ is performed.
- $z_{kp} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if movement $k$ uses path $p$.

**Infrastructure / timing variables**
- $\delta_e \ge 0$: delay (minutes) of event $e$; $\delta_e \le \delta^{\max}$.
- $\tau_e \ge 0$: realized time of event $e$: $\tau_e = \pi_e + \delta_e$.

---

## 4. Objective function

Minimize total cost = capital cost + delay cost + cancellation + shunting cancellation + deviation from plan:

$$
\min \; \underbrace{\sum_{v \in V} c_v n_v}_{\text{capital}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{e \in E} \beta_e \delta_e}_{\text{delays}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T} C^{canc}(1 - y_t)}_{\text{cancellations}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{k \in K} o_k (1 - z_k)}_{\text{canceled shunting}}
+ \underbrace{\sum_{t \in T}\sum_{v \in V} \gamma_{tv}\,|x_{tv} - \bar{x}_{tv}|}_{\text{stick-to-plan}}
$$

where $\bar{x}_{tv}$ is the original plan and $\gamma_{tv}$ a deviation weight. Linearize $|x_{tv}-\bar{x}_{tv}|$ with auxiliary variables $\Delta_{tv} \ge x_{tv}-\bar{x}_{tv}$, $\Delta_{tv} \ge \bar{x}_{tv}-x_{tv}$. *(Weights $C^{canc}, \gamma_{tv}$ are assumptions.)*

## 5. Composition constraints

**(C1) Capacity per trip:**
$$\sum_{v \in V} \kappa_v x_{tv} \ge q_t\, y_t \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(C2) Composition length limits:**
$$\ell_t\, y_t \le \sum_{v \in V} x_{tv} \le u_t\, y_t \qquad \forall t \in T$$

**(C3) Allowed compositions:**
$$x_{tv} \le a_{tv}\, u_t\, y_t \qquad \forall t \in T, v \in V$$

**(C4) Fleet balance (flow conservation per station and time node):** for each station $s$ and event node $e$ (ordered in time),
$$\sum_{t:\, t \text{ arrives at } s \text{ before } e} x_{tv} - \sum_{t:\, t \text{ departs } s \text{ before } e} x_{tv} + \sum_{k \in K_s \text{ ending at } e} z_k - \sum_{k \in K_s \text{ starting at } e} z_k \ge 0 \qquad \forall s, e, v$$
*(assumption: shunting movements transfer one unit; initial inventory $N_{sv}$ added at start of day).*

**(C5) Fleet size:**
$$\sum_{s \in S} N_{sv} \le n_v \le m_v \qquad \forall v \in V$$

## 6. Infrastructure constraints

**(I1) Path selection:**
$$\sum_{p \in P_s} z_{kp} = z_k \qquad \forall k \in K_s$$

**(I2) Event timing:** $\tau_e = \pi_e + \delta_e$, $\;0 \le \delta_e \le \delta^{\max}$.

**(I3) No-conflict on paths (big-M disjunction):** for events $e, e'$ on the same path $p$ with $\pi_e < \pi_{e'}$ and minimum headway $h_{ee'}$:
$$\tau_{e'} - \tau_e \ge h_{ee'} - M(2 - u_{ep} - u_{e'p}) \qquad \forall e<e' \in w_p,\; p \in P_s$$
where $u_{ep} \in \{0,1\}$ indicates event $e$ uses path $p$ (for shunting events $u_{ep}=z_{kp}$; for passenger events $u_{ep}=1$ on their fixed path). *(assumption: headways precomputed; alternative paths modeled by parallel track groups.)*

## 7. Combinatorial Benders' cuts

The infrastructure subproblem is solved for a fixed composition/shunting vector $(\hat x, \hat z)$. If infeasible, it returns a minimal infeasible set $I \subseteq K$ of shunting movements that cannot coexist. Add the cut:

$$\sum_{k \in I} z_k \le |I| - 1$$

More generally, with delay relief: if set $I$ is feasible only with delays exceeding $\delta^{\max}$, add:

$$\sum_{k \in I} z_k \le |I| - 1 \quad \text{or} \quad \sum_{e \in E_I} \delta_e \ge \Delta_I \left(|I| - \sum_{k\in I} z_k + 1\right)$$

*(assumption: $\Delta_I$ is the extra delay needed if one fewer movement is dropped — derived from the subproblem dual/infeasibility analysis.)*

## 8. Algorithm (exact, Combinatorial Benders)

1. Solve the master (composition model with cuts accumulated so far), relaxing integrality of infrastructure checks.
2. Fix $(\hat x, \hat z)$; solve the infrastructure feasibility subproblem per station (Van Aken-style TTAP model) for the shunting movements $\hat z_k = 1$.
3. If feasible → optimal solution found. If infeasible → add cut $\sum_{k \in I} z_k \le |I|-1$ and go to 1.

**Iterative heuristic variant:** feed shunting movements to the infrastructure model one at a time (in order of penalty $o_k$); if movement $k$ is infeasible, set $z_k = 0$ permanently, re-solve the master, and repeat. This mimics the split between rolling stock dispatchers (operator) and infrastructure dispatchers (ProRail).

## 9. Assumptions summary

1. Shunting movements move single units and occur only at Utrecht Centraal and Rotterdam Centraal during the disruption.
2. Paths through station infrastructure are pre-enumerated and conflict-free individually; conflicts arise only between simultaneous occupations.
3. Delays of passenger trains are capped at $\delta^{\max}$ minutes and absorbed by timetable buffers.
4. Costs/weights ($c_v$, $o_k$, $\gamma_{tv}$, $C^{canc}$, $\beta_e$) are given exogenously.
5. Fleet balance is checked at discrete time nodes per station; overnight repositioning is out of scope but penalized via the stick-to-plan term.

# MILP Model: Passenger-Oriented Real-Time Train Rescheduling with Flexible Train Composition and Rolling Stock Circulation

## 1. Problem Description and Assumptions

We consider a single urban rail transit line with stations $i \in \mathcal{S} = \{1, \dots, S\}$ and trains $j \in \mathcal{T} = \{1, \dots, N\}$ operating in one direction. The prediction horizon is divided into time intervals $k \in \mathcal{K} = \{1, \dots, K\}$ of equal length $\Delta t$; passenger demand is piecewise constant per interval.

**Assumptions (marked where not given in the input):**
- (A1) Single-track-direction line, no overtaking; train order is fixed (as in Liu et al., 2023a).
- (A2) Passenger demand $d_{i,k}$ (arrivals at station $i$ during interval $k$) is deterministic and piecewise constant.
- (A3) Rolling stock: trains are composed of train units; each train $j$'s composition (number of units $u_j \in \{1, \dots, U^{\max}\}$) is chosen at the depot and fixed for the whole circulation.
- (A4) All trains start and end at the depot; each train performs exactly one complete run (simplification; multiple circulations per train can be added by indexing over trips).
- (A5) Passengers board the first arriving train with sufficient residual capacity; left-behind passengers wait (no abandonment).
- (A6) Running times between stations are fixed; dwell times are decision variables.
- (A7) Linear waiting-time approximation: waiting passengers accumulate linearly within an interval.

## 2. Sets and Parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{K}$ | stations, trains, time intervals |
| $r_i$ | running time from station $i$ to $i+1$ |
| $d_i^{\min}, d_i^{\max}$ | min/max dwell time at station $i$ |
| $h^{\min}$ | minimum headway between consecutive trains |
| $c_1$ | capacity per train unit (passengers) |
| $U^{\max}$ | max number of units per train |
| $d_{i,k}$ | passenger arrivals at station $i$ in interval $k$ |
| $\alpha_i$ | alighting fraction at station $i$ (assumed; A5) |
| $w_1, w_2, w_3$ | weights: waiting time, deviation, operation cost |
| $a_j^{nom}, d_j^{nom}$ | nominal arrival/departure reference times |
| $T^{open}, T^{close}$ | operational time window boundaries |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{i,j} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $j$ at station $i$
- $x_{i,j} \ge 0$: dwell time of train $j$ at station $i$
- $b_{i,j,k} \ge 0$: passengers boarding train $j$ at station $i$ from interval-$k$ demand
- $n_{i,j} \ge 0$: in-vehicle passengers of train $j$ on section $(i, i+1)$
- $q_{i,j} \ge 0$: passengers left behind by train $j$ at station $i$
- $W \ge 0$: total passenger waiting time (auxiliary)

**Integer/Binary:**
- $u_j \in \{1, \dots, U^{\max}\}$: number of train units of train $j$ (flexible composition)
- $z_{j,u} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $j$ has $u$ units ($\sum_u z_{j,u} = 1$, $u_j = \sum_u u\, z_{j,u}$)
- $\delta_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $j$ departs station $i$ during interval $k$ (needed to link piecewise demand to trains)

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize weighted sum of passenger waiting time, timetable deviation, and operational cost (units of composition):

$$
\min \; Z = w_1 W + w_2 \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}} \left( |a_{S,j} - a_j^{nom}| + |d_{1,j} - d_j^{nom}| \right) + w_3 \sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}} u_j
$$

**Linearization:** with $\sigma_j^+, \sigma_j^- \ge 0$:
$$
a_{S,j} - a_j^{nom} = \sigma_j^+ - \sigma_j^- , \quad d_{1,j} - d_j^{nom} = \pi_j^+ - \pi_j^-
$$

so the objective becomes:
$$
\min \; w_1 W + w_2 \sum_{j} (\sigma_j^+ + \sigma_j^- + \pi_j^+ + \pi_j^-) + w_3 \sum_j \sum_{u=1}^{U^{\max}} u\, z_{j,u}
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Timetable dynamics (running and dwell times):**
$$
d_{i,j} = a_{i,j} + x_{i,j} \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\},\; \forall j
$$
$$
a_{i+1,j} = d_{i,j} + r_i \qquad \forall i \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{S\},\; \forall j
$$

**(C2) Dwell time bounds:**
$$
d_i^{\min} \le x_{i,j} \le d_i^{\max} \qquad \forall i \neq S,\; \forall j
$$

**(C3) Headway (fixed train order, no overtaking):**
$$
a_{i,j+1} - a_{i,j} \ge h^{\min} \qquad \forall i,\; \forall j = 1, \dots, N-1
$$

**(C4) Time window:**
$$
T^{open} \le a_{1,j} \le a_{S,j} \le T^{close} \qquad \forall j
$$

**(C5) Composition selection:**
$$
\sum_{u=1}^{U^{\max}} z_{j,u} = 1 \qquad \forall j
$$
$$
u_j = \sum_{u=1}^{U^{\max}} u\, z_{j,u} \qquad \forall j
$$

**(C6) Departure-interval assignment:** each train departs each station in exactly one interval:
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \delta_{i,j,k} = 1 \qquad \forall i \neq S,\; \forall j
$$
Linking (big-$M$, with $M = T^{close}-T^{open}$):
$$
d_{i,j} \ge \sum_k (k-1)\Delta t \,\delta_{i,j,k}, \qquad d_{i,j} \le \sum_k k \Delta t\, \delta_{i,j,k} + M(1 - \delta_{i,j,k}) \quad \forall k
$$

**(C7) Passenger flow — boarding allocation:** demand at station $i$ in interval $k$ is served by trains departing in interval $k$ or later; passengers board the earliest feasible train. With $F_{i,k} = \sum_j \delta_{i,j,k}$:
$$
\sum_{j} b_{i,j,k} + q_{i,k}^{carry} = d_{i,k} + \sum_{j} q_{i,j,k-1} \quad\text{(demand + carry-over of left-behinds)}
$$
implemented as: boarding from interval $k$ demand only on trains with $\delta_{i,j,k'}$, $k' \ge k$:
$$
b_{i,j,k} \le d_{i,k} \sum_{k' \ge k} \delta_{i,j,k'} \qquad \forall i, j, k
$$
$$
\sum_{j} b_{i,j,k} \le d_{i,k} + Q_{i,k-1}, \qquad Q_{i,k} = d_{i,k} + Q_{i,k-1} - \sum_j b_{i,j,k} \qquad \forall i,k
$$
with $Q_{i,0} = 0$, where $Q_{i,k}$ is the queue at the end of interval $k$ (linear queue dynamics, A7).

**(C8) Train capacity:**
$$
n_{i,j} \le c_1 \sum_u u\, z_{j,u} \qquad \forall i \neq S,\; \forall j
$$

**(C9) On-board passenger dynamics:** alighting fraction $\alpha_i$ at station $i$:
$$
n_{i,j} = (1 - \alpha_i)\, n_{i-1,j} + \sum_k b_{i,j,k} \qquad \forall i \neq S,\; \forall j
$$
with $n_{0,j} = 0$.

**(C10) Left-behind passengers per train:**
$$
q_{i,j} \ge Q_{i,k} - \sum_{k'} b_{i,j,k'} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,k}) \qquad \forall i, j, k \quad (\text{optional tightening})
$$

**(C11) Total waiting time (linear approximation):** passengers arriving in interval $k$ at station $i$ wait on average until the representative departure of the first train serving them; approximated linearly:
$$
W = \sum_{i} \sum_{k} \left( Q_{i,k} \cdot \Delta t + \sum_j q_{i,j} \right)
$$
*(Assumption A7: linear accumulation; a tighter piecewise version can be substituted.)*

**(C12) Rolling stock circulation / fleet size:**
$$
\sum_{j \in \mathcal{T}} u_j \le U^{fleet} \qquad \text{(available train units)}
$$
$$
a_{S,j} + r_{return} \le a_{1,j'} \quad \text{if train } j' \text{ reuses units of } j \;(\text{handled via fixed circulation order } j' = j + \lfloor N/2 \rfloor)
$$
*(A4 simplification: one run per train; circulation constraint ensures units return before reuse if multiple trips are modeled.)*

**(C13) Variable domains:**
$$
a_{i,j}, x_{i,j}, b_{i,j,k}, n_{i,j}, Q_{i,k}, \sigma^\pm, \pi^\pm \ge 0; \quad z_{j,u}, \delta_{i,j,k} \in \{0,1\}; \quad u_j \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}
$$

## 6. Remarks

- The model is a **pure MILP**: the nonlinear waiting/capacity couplings of the literature (e.g., Wu et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2021) are linearized via the queue variables $Q_{i,k}$, the boarding assignment variables $b_{i,j,k}$, and big-$M$ constraints (C6), (C10).
- In the **MPC scheme**, at each control step the model is solved over a receding horizon $\mathcal{K}$ with measured/forecast demands $d_{i,k}$; only the first train departures are applied.
- In the **learning-based MPC scheme**, the integer variables ($z_{j,u}$, $\delta_{i,j,k}$, after presolve pruning) are predicted by an LSTM network; with integers fixed, constraints (C1)–(C4), (C7)–(C11) reduce to a linear program (LP) solved online, guaranteeing feasibility (constraint satisfaction) while keeping computation fast.

Here is the final, cleaned-up MILP (with two small corrections applied: the redundant constraint (6) is removed, and (8a)–(8b) now partition the single $(p,t)$ choice on $e^*$ between the two directions).

---

# TRSMP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage

## 1. Sets and Parameters

**Sets**
- $K$: trains; $K_e \subseteq K$: trains traversing segment $e$
- $E$: track segments; $e^* \in E$: disrupted segment (one direction blocked during $[T_0, T_1]$)
- $P$: speed (make-up) profiles; $T = \{0,\dots,T_{max}\}$: discretized time horizon
- $\text{Sched}(k,e)$: feasible (profile, entry-time) combinations $(p,t)$ for train $k$ on $e$

**Parameters**
- $\rho_{k,e,p}$, $\gamma_{k,e,p}$: running time and energy of train $k$ on $e$ with profile $p$
- $h_e$: minimum headway on $e$; $\sigma_{k,e}$: scheduled exit time; $[a_{k,e}, b_{k,e}]$: feasible entry window
- $\alpha_{k,p,t} \in \{0,1\}$ (precomputed): $=1$ iff $[t, t+\rho_{k,e^*,p})$ intersects $[T_0, T_1]$
- $\lambda^{\text{fix}}_{e,kk'}$: given ordering constant on fixed-direction segments ($1$ if $k$ precedes $k'$)
- $w^{\text{del}}_k, w^{\text{en}}_k$: delay/energy weights; $M = T_{max} + \max_p \rho$: big-$M$

**Assumptions**
1. (A1) Times are integer on the discretized horizon; occupation interval of $(k,e,p,t)$ is $[t,\, t+\rho_{k,e,p})$.
2. (A2) Each train uses exactly one profile and one entry time per segment.
3. (A3) The blocked direction of $e^*$ is usable only for traversals avoiding $[T_0,T_1]$ (enforced via $\alpha$); the open direction is always usable. No cancellations.
4. (A4) At most one train occupies $e^*$ at any instant during the blockage (joint capacity, (7)); hence for opposite-direction pairs ($w_{kk'}=0$) the pairwise headway is safely dropped — separation is guaranteed by (7).
5. (A5) Profiles are pre-generated, linearizing train dynamics.

## 2. Variables

- $x_{k,e,p} \in \{0,1\}$: train $k$ uses profile $p$ on $e$
- $s_{k,e,p,t} \in \{0,1\}$: train $k$ enters $e$ at time $t$ with profile $p$
- $y_k \in \{0,1\}$: $=1$ iff train $k$ uses the open direction of $e^*$
- $w_{kk'} \in \{0,1\}$: $=1$ iff $k,k'$ use the same direction on $e^*$
- $d_{k,e} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$: exit time of $k$ from $e$; $D_{k,e} \ge 0$: linearized delay

## 3. Objective

$$\min \; Z = \sum_{k \in K}\sum_{e \in E_k} w^{\text{del}}_k D_{k,e} \;+\; \sum_{k}\sum_{e}\sum_{p \in P} w^{\text{en}}_k \gamma_{k,e,p}\, x_{k,e,p} \tag{1}$$

## 4. Constraints

**(2) Entry-time window:**
$$a_{k,e} \le \sum_{(p,t)\in \text{Sched}(k,e)} t\, s_{k,e,p,t} \le b_{k,e} \qquad \forall k \in K_e,\; e \in E \tag{2}$$

**(3) Exit-time consistency:**
$$d_{k,e} = \sum_{(p,t)\in \text{Sched}(k,e)} (t + \rho_{k,e,p})\, s_{k,e,p,t} \qquad \forall k \in K_e \tag{3}$$

**(4) One profile per segment:** $\;\sum_{p \in P} x_{k,e,p} = 1 \qquad \forall k \in K_e \tag{4}$

**(5) Path–schedule linking:** $\;\sum_{t:(p,t)\in\text{Sched}(k,e)} s_{k,e,p,t} = x_{k,e,p} \qquad \forall k, e, p \tag{5}$

**(6) Direction partition at $e^*$** (exactly one of the two directions is used):
$$\sum_{(p,t)\in \text{Sched}(k,e^{*}_{\text{open}})} s_{k,e^{*}_{\text{open}},p,t} = y_k, \qquad \sum_{(p,t)\in \text{Sched}(k,e^{*}_{\text{blocked}})} s_{k,e^{*}_{\text{blocked}},p,t} = 1 - y_k \qquad \forall k \ni e^* \tag{6}$$
with the blocked-direction feasibility constraint:
$$s_{k,e^{*}_{\text{blocked}},p,t} \le 1 - \alpha_{k,p,t} \qquad \forall k,\; p,\; t \tag{7}$$

**(8) Joint capacity on $e^*$ (single-track operation during the blockage):**
$$s_{k,e^*,p,t} + s_{k',e^*,p',t'} \le 1 \qquad \forall k \ne k' \text{ on } e^*,\; \forall (p,t),(p',t') \text{ with } [t,t+\rho_{k,e^*,p}) \cap [t',t'+\rho_{k',e^*,p'}) \ne \emptyset \tag{8}$$
Per-direction capacity on all other segments $e \ne e^*$:
$$\sum_{k}\sum_{p}\sum_{t'=t-\rho_{k,e,p}+1}^{t} s_{k,e,p,t'} \le 1 \qquad \forall e \ne e^*,\; t \in T \tag{9}$$

**(10) Uniform headway/ordering constraints** (all $k<k'$ on the same segment $e$):
$$d_{k',e} \ge d_{k,e} + \sum_{p} \rho_{k,e,p}\, x_{k,e,p} + h_e - M(1 - \lambda_{e,kk'}) \tag{10}$$
where $\lambda_{e,kk'} = \lambda^{\text{fix}}_{e,kk'}$ for $e \ne e^*$, and $\lambda_{e^*,kk'} = w_{kk'}$ for $e = e^*$ (headway relaxed exactly for opposite-direction pairs, whose separation is guaranteed by (8)).

**(11) Linearization of $w_{kk'} = 1 \Leftrightarrow y_k = y_{k'}$:**
$$w_{kk'} \ge y_k - y_{k'}, \quad w_{kk'} \ge y_{k'} - y_k, \quad w_{kk'} \le 2 - y_k - y_{k'}, \quad w_{kk'} \le y_k + y_{k'} \tag{11}$$

**(12) Delay linearization:**
$$D_{k,e} \ge d_{k,e} - \sigma_{k,e}, \qquad D_{k,e} \ge 0 \tag{12}$$

**(13) Domains:**
$$x, s, y, w \in \{0,1\}; \quad d_{k,e} \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}; \quad D_{k,e} \ge 0 \tag{13}$$

## 5. Structure and Decomposition Note

For fixed $(y_k, p)$, the variables $(s_{k,e,p,t})_t$ reduce to one integer entry time per segment, so each train's feasible set $\{(x,s,y)\}$ is a small enumerable set of **train plans** (a plan fixes profiles, entry times, and direction choices). Inter-train coupling occurs only through constraints (8)–(10). Enumerating train-plan candidates and introducing binary selection variables per plan yields the equivalent IP reformulation (exact for sufficiently fine time discretization), which can be solved with an adaptive iterative refinement / local-branching scheme instead of the full MILP.

The model is fully linear: train dynamics are linearized through discrete speed profiles, disruption feasibility through the precomputed parameter $\alpha$, and bidirectional conflict resolution through the joint capacity (8) plus the big-M headway form (10) with the linearized same-direction indicator $w$.

# MILP: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management under Partial Segment Blockage (TRSMP)

## Sets and Indices
- $i, j \in \mathcal{I}$ — trains, with scheduled direction $\text{dir}(i) \in \{up, down\}$
- $s \in \{0,\dots,S\}$ — stations (segment $(s,s+1)$ between consecutive stations)
- $k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}$ — precomputed feasible speed profiles for train $i$ on segment $(s,s+1)$
- $b \in \mathcal{B}$ — blocked segments, each with blocked direction $\text{dir}(b)$

## Parameters
| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $T_{start}, T_{end}$ | disruption time window |
| $\bar{a}[i,s], \bar{d}[i,s]$ | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $r[i,s,k],\ e[i,s,k]$ | running time / energy of profile $k$ |
| $\tau_{min}[i,s], \tau_{max}[i,s]$ | min/max dwell times |
| $W_{early}, W_{late}$ | allowed earliness / max delay (retiming window) |
| $\Delta_{late}$ | maximum allowed delay |
| $H,\ H_{cross}$ | same-direction headway / opposite-direction crossing separation |
| $\alpha_{delay}[i,s],\ \alpha_{energy},\ \alpha_{canc}[i],\ \alpha_{rer}[i,s]$ | objective weights |
| $M$ | big-M (larger than planning horizon + max running time) |

## Variables
- $A[i,s], D[i,s] \ge 0$ — actual arrival/departure times
- $\delta[i,s] \ge 0$ — arrival delay
- $x[i,s,k] \in \{0,1\}$ — speed-profile selection
- $y[i,s] \in \{0,1\}$ — rerouting to opposite track on segment $(s,s+1)$
- $c[i] \in \{0,1\}$ — cancellation
- $o[i,j,s] \in \{0,1\}$ — train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$
- $\beta[i,b] \in \{0,1\}$ — train waits until disruption ends at blocked segment $b$

## Objective
$$\min\ \sum_{i,s}\alpha_{delay}[i,s]\,\delta[i,s] \;+\; \alpha_{energy}\sum_{i}\sum_{s=0}^{S-1}\sum_{k} e[i,s,k]\,x[i,s,k] \;+\; \sum_i \alpha_{canc}[i]\,c[i] \;+\; \sum_{i,s}\alpha_{rer}[i,s]\,y[i,s]$$

## Constraints

**(1) Retiming windows** (relaxed if cancelled):
$$\bar{a}[i,s] - W_{early} - M c[i] \le A[i,s] \le \bar{a}[i,s] + W_{late} + M c[i] \qquad \forall i,s$$
(analogously for $D[i,s]$ with $\bar{d}[i,s]$).

**(2) Speed-profile selection and running time:**
$$\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}_{i,s}} x[i,s,k] = 1 - c[i] \qquad \forall i,\ s=0,\dots,S-1$$
$$D[i,s] + \sum_{k} r[i,s,k]\,x[i,s,k] \le A[i,s+1] \qquad \forall i,\ s=0,\dots,S-1$$

**(3) Dwell times:**
$$\tau_{min}[i,s](1-c[i]) \le D[i,s] - A[i,s] \le \tau_{max}[i,s] + M c[i] \qquad \forall i,\ s=1,\dots,S-1$$

**(4) Same-direction headways** (six variants; shown for entry/entry, others analogous with $A[i,s+1]$, $D[i,s]$, $A[i,s]$):
$$D[j,s] \ge D[i,s] + H - M(1-o[i,j,s]) - M c[i] - M c[j] \qquad \forall (i,j),\ s$$
$$D[i,s] \ge D[j,s] + H - M\,o[i,j,s] - M c[i] - M c[j] \qquad \forall (i,j),\ s$$

**(5) Disruption disjunction** — for each blocked $(b,\text{dir}(b))$ and each train $i$ with $\text{dir}(i)=\text{dir}(b)$, with $t_{in}[i,b] = D[i,b]$:
$$t_{in}[i,b] \le T_{start} + M\,(y[i,b] + c[i] + \beta[i,b])$$
$$t_{in}[i,b] \ge T_{end} - M\,(3 - y[i,b] - c[i] - \beta[i,b])$$
*Logic:* if $y=c=\beta=0$, the train must enter before $T_{start}$ (or, via $\beta=1$, after $T_{end}$); entering during the window is only possible if rerouted ($y=1$) or cancelled ($c=1$).

**(6) Opposite-direction crossing on shared single-track segments:**
$$A[j,s] \ge A[i,s] + H_{cross} - M(1-o[i,j,s]) - M c[i] - M c[j] \qquad \forall i<j \text{ opposite dir},\ s$$
$$A[i,s] \ge A[j,s] + H_{cross} - M\,o[i,j,s] - M c[i] - M c[j] \qquad \forall i<j \text{ opposite dir},\ s$$

**(7) Delay definition and bound:**
$$\delta[i,s] \ge A[i,s] - \bar{a}[i,s], \qquad \delta[i,s] \ge 0, \qquad \delta[i,s] \le \Delta_{late}(1-c[i]) \qquad \forall i,s$$

**(8) Rerouting consistency:**
$$y[i,s] \le 1 - c[i] \qquad \forall i,\ s \in \mathcal{B}$$

**(9) Turnaround (optional):**
$$D[i,S] \ge A[i,0] + T_{turn}[i] \qquad \forall i \text{ with a return service}$$

## Assumptions
1. Disruption is deterministic and known: blocked segments and $[T_{start},T_{end}]$ are input data; the opposite track remains operational.
2. Speed profiles are precomputed offline from train dynamics; exactly one is chosen per run unless the train is cancelled.
3. Cancellation removes a train from all timing/headway/resource interactions via the $M c$ relaxation terms; its delay variables are forced to zero and it incurs penalty $\alpha_{canc}$.
4. Rerouting means using the opposite track of the blocked segment; bidirectional sharing is coordinated by ordering variables $o$ and crossing constraints (6).
5. Uniform headways $H$ and $H_{cross}$; retiming bounded by $[W_{early}, W_{late}]$; delays beyond $\Delta_{late}$ force cancellation.
6. Fixed stop pattern; only dwell durations may change; no overtaking within segments.
7. $M$ exceeds the planning horizon so relaxed constraints are non-binding.
8. Station track/platform capacity is assumed sufficient; segment occupancy is represented by entry/exit times.

All constraints are linear; binaries are $x, y, c, o, \beta$, making this a valid MILP that jointly optimizes train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles (minimizing delay, energy, cancellations, and rerouting cost) under a partial segment blockage.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## Sets and Parameters

- Stations $i = 1,\dots,S$; segments (blocks) $k = 1,\dots,S-1$ connecting station $k$ and $k+1$
- Trains $t \in T$ with direction $\mathrm{dir}(t) \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$
- Disrupted segments $k \in K$ with disruption time window $[T_0, T_1]$
- $a^{sched}_{t,i}, d^{sched}_{t,i}$: original scheduled arrival/departure times
- $P_{t,k}$: set of feasible speed profiles for train $t$ on segment $k$, with running time $\tau_{t,k,p}$ and energy consumption $E_{t,k,p}$
- $[\underline{w}, \bar{w}]$: min/max dwell time; $h$: minimum headway; $H$: time horizon; $M$: big-M
- Weights $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$; cancellation penalty $\pi_t$

## Decision Variables

- $x_{t,i} \in [0,H]$: rescheduled arrival time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $y_{t,i} \in [0,H]$: rescheduled departure time of train $t$ at station $i$
- $r_{t,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ reroutes to the opposite track on segment $k$
- $z_{t,t',k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ enters segment $k$ before train $t'$
- $v_{t,k,p} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $k$
- $c_t \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $t$ is cancelled
- $u_{t,t',k} \in \{0,1\}$: XOR auxiliary, 1 iff $r_{t,k} \neq r_{t',k}$ (different physical tracks)

## Objective Function

$$\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{t}\sum_{i} (x_{t,i} - a^{sched}_{t,i}) \;+\; \beta \sum_{t}\sum_{k}\sum_{p \in P_{t,k}} E_{t,k,p}\, v_{t,k,p} \;+\; \gamma \sum_{t} \pi_t\, c_t$$

(total weighted delay + total energy consumption + cancellation penalties)

## Constraints

**(1) Speed-profile selection** — exactly one profile per segment unless cancelled:
$$\sum_{p \in P_{t,k}} v_{t,k,p} + c_t = 1 \qquad \forall t, \forall k$$

**(2) Running-time consistency** — timetable matches the selected speed profile:
$$y_{t,k+1} - x_{t,k} \le \tau_{t,k,p} + M(1 - v_{t,k,p}) + M c_t \qquad \forall t, \forall k, \forall p$$
$$y_{t,k+1} - x_{t,k} \ge \tau_{t,k,p} - M(1 - v_{t,k,p}) - M c_t \qquad \forall t, \forall k, \forall p$$

**(3) Dwell-time bounds:**
$$\underline{w} - M c_t \le y_{t,i} - x_{t,i} \le \bar{w} + M c_t \qquad \forall t, \forall i$$

**(4) Disruption constraint** — entry into a disrupted segment during $[T_0,T_1]$ only if rerouted:
$$e_{t,k} \le T_0 + M(r_{t,k} + c_t) \qquad \forall t, \forall k \in K$$
$$e_{t,k} \ge T_1 - M(1 - r_{t,k}) - M c_t \qquad \forall t, \forall k \in K$$
where $e_{t,k}$ is the entry time (departure from station $k$, or arrival if no stop).

**(5) Reroute consistency** across adjacent segments (single-track entry/exit coordination):
$$r_{t,k+1} - r_{t,k} \ge -M c_t \qquad \forall t, \forall k = 1,\dots,S-2$$

**(6) XOR linearization** (same-track indicator: $u=0$ iff $r_{t,k} = r_{t',k}$):
$$u_{t,t',k} \ge r_{t,k} - r_{t',k}, \quad u_{t,t',k} \ge r_{t',k} - r_{t,k}$$
$$u_{t,t',k} \le r_{t,k} + r_{t',k}, \quad u_{t,t',k} \le 2 - r_{t,k} - r_{t',k}$$

**(7) Headway / conflict-free constraints** — enforced only when both trains use the same physical track ($u_{t,t',k}=0$) and neither is cancelled; ordering determined by $z$:

Departure (entry) separation:
$$y_{t',k} - y_{t,k} \ge h - M(1 - z_{t,t',k}) - M u_{t,t',k} - M(c_t + c_{t'})$$
$$y_{t,k} - y_{t',k} \ge h - M z_{t,t',k} - M u_{t,t',k} - M(c_t + c_{t'})$$

Arrival (exit) separation:
$$x_{t',k+1} - x_{t,k+1} \ge h - M(1 - z_{t,t',k}) - M u_{t,t',k} - M(c_t + c_{t'})$$
$$x_{t,k+1} - x_{t',k+1} \ge h - M z_{t,t',k} - M u_{t,t',k} - M(c_t + c_{t'})$$

These constraints cover both same-direction conflicts and opposite-direction (rerouted) conflicts on the shared single track.

**(8) Cancellation logic** — cancelled trains have no timetable presence:
$$x_{t,i} \le H(1 - c_t), \quad y_{t,i} \le H(1 - c_t) \qquad \forall t, \forall i$$

**(9) Time horizon bounds:**
$$0 \le x_{t,i} \le H, \quad 0 \le y_{t,i} \le H \qquad \forall t, \forall i$$

## Assumptions (made where information was missing)

1. Delay is measured as arrival deviation from the original timetable (linear, non-negative implicitly since rescheduled times can only be pushed later under disruption; otherwise an absolute-value linearization could be added).
2. Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set per (train, segment), each with fixed running time and energy — this keeps the model linear.
3. Rerouting is all-or-nothing per segment per train, and propagates to adjacent segments for single-track entry/exit coordination.
4. Headway is uniform ($h$) for all train pairs and enforced on both segment entry and exit.
5. Cancellation fully removes a train from the network and incurs a fixed penalty $\pi_t$.

# MILP for the Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Assumptions

- A double-track line with stations S = {1,…,|S|} and segments between consecutive stations. Each segment has two directed tracks: the **normal track** and the **opposite track**.
- A disruption blocks the normal track of segment s* during time window [T^dis_start, T^dis_end]. Trains may cross s* on the opposite track (single-track operation) if rerouted.
- For each train i and segment s, a discrete set of precomputed feasible speed profiles P_{i,s} = {1,…,|P_{i,s}|}, each with running time τ_{i,s,p} and energy consumption e_{i,s,p}.
- Trains may be retimed, reordered, rerouted, or cancelled. Cancellation removes the train's path entirely.
- Headway h is the minimum separation on a track (segment or station).
- Time horizon T (continuous time variables).

## 2. Sets and Indices

- I: set of trains, i ∈ I
- S: set of stations, s ∈ S; segments indexed by s = 1,…,|S|−1 (segment s connects stations s and s+1)
- K_i: ordered sequence of stations visited by train i (fixed route; rerouting only affects which track is used on segments)
- P_{i,s}: speed profiles for train i on segment s
- T: time horizon

## 3. Parameters

- a⁰_{i,s}, d⁰_{i,s}: original scheduled arrival/departure of train i at station s
- τ^min_{i,s}: minimum dwell time of train i at station s
- τ_{i,s,p}: running time of train i on segment s under profile p
- e_{i,s,p}: energy consumption of profile p
- h: minimum headway (same for stations and segments; can be differentiated)
- [T^dis_s, T^dis_e]: disruption window on affected segment s*
- w_i: delay weight of train i
- π_i: cancellation penalty of train i
- α, β: weights for delay and energy in the objective
- M: sufficiently large constant (Big-M, e.g., M = T)
- L_{i,s}: latest allowed arrival slack (time-window bound)

## 4. Variables

**Continuous:**
- a_{i,s} ∈ [0, T]: actual arrival time of train i at station s
- d_{i,s} ∈ [0, T]: actual departure time of train i at station s
- u_{i,s}, v_{i,s} ≥ 0: positive-part arrival/departure delays

**Binary:**
- x_{i,s,j} ∈ {0,1}: ordering variable = 1 if train i passes segment s before train j
- y_{i,s} ∈ {0,1}: = 1 if train i uses the **opposite track** on segment s (only meaningful on s*)
- c_i ∈ {0,1}: = 1 if train i is cancelled
- z_{i,s,p} ∈ {0,1}: = 1 if train i uses speed profile p on segment s
- δ_{i,s,j} ∈ {0,1}: ordering variable for station headway (train i before train j at station s)
- b_i ∈ {0,1}: auxiliary variable (traversal of s* starts after disruption ends)

## 5. Objective Function

Minimize weighted total delay + cancellation penalties + energy:

$$
\min \; \alpha \sum_{i \in I} w_i \sum_{s \in K_i} (u_{i,s} + v_{i,s}) + \sum_{i \in I} \pi_i c_i + \beta \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s} \sum_{p \in P_{i,s}} e_{i,s,p}\, z_{i,s,p}
$$

with delay linearization:

$$
u_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^0_{i,s}, \quad u_{i,s} \ge 0, \qquad v_{i,s} \ge d_{i,s} - d^0_{i,s}, \quad v_{i,s} \ge 0
$$

## 6. Constraints

**(C1) Speed-profile selection (exactly one profile if running, none if cancelled):**

$$
\sum_{p \in P_{i,s}} z_{i,s,p} = 1 - c_i \quad \forall i, \forall s
$$

**(C2) Running-time consistency (link profiles to timetable):**

$$
d_{i,s} + \sum_p \tau_{i,s,p}\, z_{i,s,p} \le a_{i,s+1} + M c_i \quad \forall i, \forall s \in K_i \setminus \{\text{last}\}
$$

**(C3) Dwell time:**

$$
d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \ge \tau^min_{i,s} (1 - c_i) \quad \forall i, \forall s
$$

**(C4) Flow/continuity (arrival at next station equals departure from previous when not cancelled):**

$$
a_{i,s+1} \le d_{i,s} + M c_i \quad \text{and} \quad a_{i,s+1} \ge d_{i,s} - M c_i \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C5) Time-window feasibility:**

$$
0 \le a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \le T, \qquad a_{i,s} \le a^0_{i,s} + L_{i,s} + M c_i
$$

**(C6) Disruption blockage:** On the affected segment s*, the normal track is unusable during [T^dis_s, T^dis_e]. A train either is rerouted (y_{i,s*} = 1) or its traversal avoids the window:

$$
d_{i,s^*} \ge T^{dis}_e \cdot (1 - y_{i,s^*}) - M\, b_i - M c_i
$$

$$
d_{i,s^*} + \sum_p \tau_{i,s^*,p} z_{i,s^*,p} \le T^{dis}_s + M y_{i,s^*} + M(1 - b_i) - M c_i
$$

Interpretation: if not rerouted (y=0), the train either enters after T^dis_e (b_i=1) or completes traversal before T^dis_s (b_i=0). If rerouted, both are relaxed.

**(C7) Segment headway / ordering (same track):** For each pair (i, j), i < j, on segment s, with x_{i,s,j} = 1 if i precedes j:

$$
d_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s+1} + h - M(1 - x_{i,s,j}) - M y_{i,s} - M y_{j,s} - M c_i - M c_j
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{j,s+1} + h - M x_{i,s,j} - M y_{i,s} - M y_{j,s} - M c_i - M c_j
$$

If i precedes j on the same track (x=1), j cannot enter the segment until i has cleared it plus headway h; symmetric for j preceding i.

**(C8) Opposite-track (single-track) exclusivity on disrupted segment s*:** For each pair (i,j), both rerouted:

$$
d_{j,s^*} \ge a_{i,s^*+1} + h - M(1 - x_{i,s^*,j}) - M(1 - y_{i,s^*}) - M(1 - y_{j,s^*}) - M c_i - M c_j
$$

$$
d_{i,s^*} \ge a_{j,s^*+1} + h - M x_{i,s^*,j} - M(1 - y_{i,s^*}) - M(1 - y_{j,s^*}) - M c_i - M c_j
$$

When both y=1, exactly one ordering holds and headway is enforced on the single available track.

**(C9) Station headway:** For each pair (i,j), i < j, at station s, with δ_{i,s,j} = 1 if i occupies the station before j:

$$
d_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h - M(1 - \delta_{i,s,j}) - M c_i - M c_j
$$

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{j,s} + h - M \delta_{i,s,j} - M c_i - M c_j
$$

**(C10) Rerouting only allowed on disrupted segment:**

$$
y_{i,s} = 0 \quad \forall i, \forall s \neq s^*
$$

**(C11) Variable domains:**

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s} \in [0, T]; \quad u_{i,s}, v_{i,s} \ge 0
$$

$$
x_{i,s,j},\, \delta_{i,s,j},\, y_{i,s},\, c_i,\, z_{i,s,p},\, b_i \in \{0,1\}
$$

## 7. Explanation of Model Elements

- **Timetable variables (a, d):** continuous arrival/departure times allow retiming; the original timetable enters only through the delay terms.
- **Ordering variables (x, δ):** Big-M disjunctions linearize the "who goes first" decision, guaranteeing conflict-free headways on segments (C7–C8) and at stations (C9).
- **Rerouting variables (y):** permit using the opposite track on the blocked segment; C6 ensures no train uses the blocked normal track during the disruption window unless rerouted, and C8 serializes trains on the single available opposite track.
- **Cancellation variables (c):** when c_i = 1, all of train i's timing constraints are relaxed via Big-M terms, its profile-selection constraint (C1) forces z = 0, and the penalty π_i is charged.
- **Speed-profile variables (z):** select exactly one precomputed profile per train-segment; C2 links the chosen profile's running time τ to the timetable, and the objective charges its energy e. This couples speed management with rescheduling: slower profiles may reduce delays of following trains at the cost of energy.
- **Objective:** trades off passenger-weighted delays (α w_i), service cancellation (π_i), and energy consumption (β), reflecting the integrated nature of the TRSMP.

The model is a mixed-integer linear program solvable by branch-and-bound/branch-and-cut; Big-M should be set to T (horizon length) for tightness.

Text:
# MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Problem setting and assumptions

**Physical setting (Assumptions marked A):**

- **A1.** A double-track high-speed railway corridor with stations $s \in S$ and segments $f \in F$ connecting consecutive stations. Each segment has two physical tracks, one per direction $r \in R = \{u, d\}$ (up/down).
- **A2.** A set of trains $i \in I$ operates according to a planned timetable $\{\bar a_{i,s}, \bar d_{i,s}\}$ (scheduled arrival/departure at station $s$).
- **A3.** A disruption partially blocks one track of a segment set $F^D \subseteq F$ during time window $[T_1, T_2]$. Trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track of the disrupted segment(s) during this window, subject to bidirectional conflict resolution.
- **A4.** For every train–segment pair $(i,f)$ there is a finite set of **speed profiles** $p \in P_{i,f}$, each with running time $\tau^{p}_{if}$ and energy consumption $e^{p}_{if}$, precomputed from train dynamics (this linearizes the nonlinear dynamics; profiles must satisfy acceleration/braking/speed limits by construction).
- **A5.** All running times, headways, dwell times, and the disruption window are deterministic and known; time is discretized in seconds.
- **A6.** Trains may be cancelled; the number of cancellations is bounded by dispatching policy.

## 2. Sets and parameters

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| $I$ | trains; $S$ stations; $F$ segments; $F^D$ disrupted segments |
| $P_{i,f}$ | admissible speed profiles of train $i$ on segment $f$ |
| $\tau^{p}_{if}, e^{p}_{if}$ | running time / energy of profile $p$ |
| $\bar a_{i,s}, \bar d_{i,s}$ | scheduled arrival/departure times |
| $h^{sec}, h^{run}$ | safety headways (station section / running track), seconds |
| $\underline{w}_{i,s}, \overline{w}_{i,s}$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ at $s$ |
| $H_{max}$ | maximum admissible delay per train |
| $T_1, T_2$ | disruption start / end |
| $M$ | sufficiently large constant |
| $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ | weights for delay, energy, cancellations |
| $r^*(f)$ | the blocked track of segment $f \in F^D$ |

## 3. Decision variables

**Continuous:**
- $a_{i,s} \ge 0$ — actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$ — actual departure time of train $i$ at station $s$
- $E_i \ge 0$ — energy consumption of train $i$

**Binary:**
- $x^{p}_{if} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p$ on segment $f$
- $y^{r}_{if} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $f$ on track of direction $r$
- $z_{ij,f} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ passes segment $f$ before train $j$ (ordering)
- $b_{if} \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ traverses disrupted segment $f$ **before** $T_1$ (0: after $T_2$)
- $c_i \in \{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

## 4. Objective function

Minimize total weighted delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{s \in S}\big[(a_{i,s} - \bar a_{i,s}) + (d_{i,s} - \bar d_{i,s})\big] \;+\; \beta \sum_{i \in I} E_i \;+\; \gamma \sum_{i \in I} c_i
$$

(Only positive deviations count; delays can be linearized by $del_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s}-\bar a_{i,s}$, $del_{i,s}\ge 0$ if negative delays should not be rewarded.)

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Speed-profile selection (each train–segment gets exactly one profile, unless cancelled):**
$$\sum_{p \in P_{i,f}} x^{p}_{if} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; f \in F$$

**(C2) Timetable–speed-profile coupling (running time consistency):**
$$a_{i,s'} - d_{i,s} = \sum_{p \in P_{i,f}} \tau^{p}_{if}\, x^{p}_{if} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; f=(s,s')\in F$$

**(C3) Energy accounting:**
$$E_i = \sum_{f \in F}\sum_{p \in P_{i,f}} e^{p}_{if}\, x^{p}_{if} \qquad \forall i \in I$$

**(C4) Route selection (exactly one track per segment, unless cancelled):**
$$\sum_{r \in R} y^{r}_{if} = 1 - c_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; f \in F$$

**(C5) Rerouting restriction — on undisrupted segments, only the scheduled track may be used:**
$$y^{r}_{if} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in I,\; f \notin F^D,\; r \neq r_{scheduled}(f)$$

**(C6) Disruption time window: a train using the blocked track must pass entirely before $T_1$ or entirely after $T_2$.**

If $y^{r^*(f)}_{if}=1$ and $b_{if}=1$ (before the window):
$$d_{i,s} + \sum_{p \in P_{i,f}} \tau^{p}_{if}\, x^{p}_{if} \;\le\; T_1 + M\big(2 - y^{r^*(f)}_{if} - b_{if}\big) \qquad \forall i,\; f=(s,s') \in F^D$$

If $y^{r^*(f)}_{if}=1$ and $b_{if}=0$ (after the window):
$$a_{i,s'} \;\ge\; T_2 - M\big(1 - y^{r^*(f)}_{if}\big) - M\big(1 - b_{if}\big) \qquad \forall i,\; f \in F^D$$

(On the *opposite* track $r \neq r^*(f)$ these constraints are inactive, enabling rerouting through the disruption area.)

**(C7) Conflict-free operation on each physical track (big-M disjunctive headway).** For all ordered pairs $(i,j)$, $i \ne j$, each segment $f=(s,s')$ and each track $r$:
$$a_{j,s'} \;\ge\; d_{i,s} + h^{run} - M\big(1 - z_{ij,f}\big) - M\big(2 - y^{r}_{if} - y^{r}_{jf}\big)$$
$$a_{i,s'} \;\ge\; d_{j,s} + h^{run} - M\, z_{ij,f} - M\big(2 - y^{r}_{if} - y^{r}_{jf}\big)$$

These constraints ensure that two trains sharing the same track — in particular bidirectional trains rerouted onto the same opposite track — never occupy the segment simultaneously; $z_{ij,f}$ selects the pass order.

**(C8) Dwell time bounds at stations:**
$$\underline{w}_{i,s} \le d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \overline{w}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S \setminus \{\text{terminals}\}$$

**(C9) Station headway (arrival and departure separation on station tracks):** for all pairs $(i,j)$ and stations $s$:
$$|a_{i,s} - a_{j,s}| \ge h^{sec} \;\Longleftrightarrow\; a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h^{sec} - M\, u_{ij,s},\quad a_{i,s} \ge a_{j,s} + h^{sec} - M(1-u_{ij,s})$$
with auxiliary binaries $u_{ij,s}$ (analogous constraints for $d_{i,s}$).

**(C10) Maximum delay / recovery horizon:**
$$a_{i,s} \le \bar a_{i,s} + H_{max} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S$$

**(C11) Cancellation policy and consistency:**
$$\sum_{i \in I} c_i \le C_{max}, \qquad c_i \in \{0,1\}$$
If $c_i = 1$, all times of train $i$ are freed from headway constraints via the $y$-terms in (C7), which vanish since $\sum_r y^r_{if}=0$.

**(C12) Variable domains:**
$$a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, E_i \ge 0; \quad x^{p}_{if}, y^{r}_{if}, z_{ij,f}, b_{if}, c_i \in \{0,1\}$$

## 6. Remarks
